methods.name: MaLoRA / MaRA
methods.full_name: MaLoRA: Mamba-modulated Low-Rank Adaptation, with the MaRA Mamba Retrieval Adapter
methods.paper_title: Selective State-Space Adaptation and Retrieval for Language Model Reasoning
methods.formula_latex: h_t=W_0x_t+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\,\lambda_t\,BAx_t,\ \ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ (\text{the paper's Eq. 3 writes }(W_0+B\lambda_tA)x_t\text{ with the LoRA scale absorbed; released code: }\alpha/r=32/16=2);\ \ \lambda_t=\operatorname{softplus}\big(w_\phi^{\top}o_t+b_\phi\big)\in\mathbb{R}_{>0};\ \ (o_1,\dots,o_t)=\mathrm{Mamba}\big(Px_1,\dots,Px_t\big),\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ \ \text{one Mamba-1 block of width }r\text{: }[u_t';z_t]=W_{\mathrm{up}}Px_t\in\mathbb{R}^{4r},\ u_t=\mathrm{SiLU}(\mathrm{conv}_4(u'_{1:t})_t),\ s_t=\bar A_t s_{t-1}+\bar B_t u_t,\ y_t=C_t s_t+D\odot u_t\ (\bar A_t,\bar B_t,C_t\text{ computed from }u_t;\ d_s=16),\ o_t=W_{\mathrm{dn}}\big(y_t\odot\mathrm{SiLU}(z_t)\big);\ \ \text{i.e. }\Delta W_t=\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\,\lambda(x_{1:t})\,BA;\ \ \text{frozen: }W_0;\ \text{trained jointly: }A,B,P,\text{ the Mamba block},w_\phi,b_\phi;\ B_0=0,\ b_\phi\approx\operatorname{softplus}^{-1}(1);\ \ \text{MaRA (separate stage, LM frozen): }H_i=\mathrm{LM}_{1:K}(Q\Vert C_i),\ p_i=\textstyle\sum_j\operatorname{softmax}_j\big(q_a^{\top}\tanh(W_kH_{i,j})\big)H_{i,j},\ (s_1,\dots,s_N)=\mathrm{Mamba}_{2\text{ layers}}(W_{in}p_1,\dots,W_{in}p_N),\ r_i=\mathbf w_\ell^{\top}s_i,\ \tilde{\mathbf r}=W_gs_N\ (\text{training only}),\ \text{keep the top-}k\text{ segments by }r_i
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ (\text{LoRA})+r\,d_{in}\ (P)+6r^2+6r\,d_s+4r\lceil r/16\rceil+16r\ (\text{Mamba-1 block of width }r,\text{ expand }2,\text{ conv }4,\ d_s=16,\text{ plus the }r\to1\text{ readout and an }r\text{-vector bias of which one entry is used})\ \text{per adapted matrix}\ (=3{,}392\text{ beyond }P\text{ at }r=d_s=16);\ \text{totals: }42.45\text{M (Qwen-2.5-7B)},\ 44.58\text{M (Llama-3.1-8B; }44{,}582{,}912\text{ exactly as in the released metrics)},\ 56.79\text{M (Gemma-2-9B)},\ \text{mean }47.9\text{M vs }30.7\text{M for LoRA }(\approx+56\%);\ \text{MaRA: }\approx2.9\text{–}3.1\text{M per model}
methods.locus: q_proj, k_proj, v_proj, up_proj and down_proj of every decoder layer of Qwen-2.5-7B, Llama-3.1-8B and Gemma-2-9B (also Qwen-2.5-3B). Each projection in each layer has its own modulator, which reads that projection's input \(x_t\) and runs causally over the token sequence. MaRA reads the hidden states of the first \(K\) frozen layers (\(K=12\) to \(20\)) for each (query, paragraph) pair and acts on the context before generation.
methods.structure: A rank-\(r\) LoRA delta whose magnitude is a positive scalar gate that depends on the token history, \(\Delta W_t=\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\lambda(x_{1:t})BA\): the direction \(BA\) is static and only the strength changes per token. The gate is a causal, stateful function of the prefix: a selective state-space (Mamba/S6) recurrence of width \(r\) over the projected inputs \(Px_1,\dots,Px_t\), read out by a linear head and a softplus. It can therefore both suppress (\(\lambda<1\)) and amplify (\(\lambda>1\)) the update. The TopLoRA baseline instead inserts a stateless per-token diagonal \(\Lambda(x_t)=\mathrm{diag}(\exp(\mathrm{RMSNorm}(Px_t)))\). MaLoRA trades the diagonal for a scalar (a stateful diagonal variant gave no consistent gain, Appendix C) and gives the gate memory across tokens. READ and SSMLoRA also use recurrence, but across layers; MaLoRA's runs across tokens. At the token level, GRU and LSTM gates perform about the same as the Mamba gate, so recurrence itself is what matters there. The paper notes that with KV caching the recurrence is restarted at each generated position, so only the prompt is modulated with its full history. MaRA is a separate adapter at the retrieval level, not a weight update. It combines an attention pool over frozen early-layer states, a two-layer Mamba that runs over paragraphs rather than tokens, and linear local and global scoring heads. It selects the top-\(k\) paragraphs (\(k=12\) on MuSiQue, \(k=4\) on 2WikiMultihopQA) over \(N_p=4\) chained passes and is trained on supporting-paragraph labels against the unadapted backbone, separately from MaLoRA.
methods.mergeable_reason: The effective delta \(\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\lambda(x_{1:t})BA\) changes from token to token, so it cannot be folded into \(W_0\). The modulator must run at inference: one \(d_{in}\to r\) projection plus a width-\(r\), \(d_s=16\) Mamba step per token. Folding is possible only if \(\lambda\) is frozen to a constant \(c\), giving \(W_0+c\,\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA\), and that changes the model.
methods.identity_at_init: \(B_0=0\) gives \(\Delta W_t=0\) and \(h_t=W_0x_t\) for every token. In the released code the gate bias starts at \(\operatorname{softplus}^{-1}(1)\approx0.54\) (plus small noise) and the readout weights are small, so \(\lambda_t\approx1\) and training starts as plain LoRA. The paper notes that its Eq. 3 reduces to LoRA when \(\lambda\equiv1\).
methods.key_idea: LoRA applies one static update to every token. MaLoRA rescales that update per token with a gate \(\lambda(x_{1:t})\) produced by a Mamba recurrence over the prefix, so the adapter's strength depends on the whole trajectory up to token \(t\), not only on \(x_t\). The learned gate is mostly suppressive and separates token roles (markers and query versus content), but it does not separate supporting from distractor paragraphs. That limit motivates MaRA, which applies the same state-space idea one level up as a paragraph selector of about 3M parameters.
methods.results_note: At \(r=16\), MaLoRA alone raises MuSiQue F1 over LoRA from 51.1/54.4/59.8 to 56.4/62.3/63.7 on Qwen-2.5-7B/Llama-3.1-8B/Gemma-2-9B (ahead of stateless TopLoRA in every cell, Table 1). Adding MaRA gives +6.4 F1 over LoRA on average across the \(3\times2\) backbone-dataset grid (+2.1 to +8.1 per cell, Table 4).

relations.note: Setting \(\lambda_t\equiv1\) recovers LoRA (the paper's Eq. 3 reduces to Eq. 1).

Not cited (no Activated LoRA reference in the paper). aLoRA also makes the LoRA contribution depend on token position, through a hard causal switch that turns on at the invocation token. MaLoRA learns a soft, content-dependent causal gate that is active on prompt tokens too, so it gives up aLoRA's reuse of the base model's KV cache.
Static baseline in Tables 4 and 6. DoRA trains 1.90x slower than LoRA (20.3 h vs 10.8 h), MaLoRA 1.16x slower.

methods.name: Model Soups
methods.full_name: Model soups (uniform / greedy weight averaging of fine-tuned models)
methods.paper_title: Model soups: averaging weights of multiple fine-tuned models improves accuracy without increasing inference time
methods.formula_latex: W^{\mathrm{soup}}=\tfrac{1}{|\mathcal{S}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}W_i=W_0+\tfrac{1}{|\mathcal{S}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\Delta W_i,\ \ \mathcal{S}\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\};\ \text{uniform soup: }\mathcal{S}=\{1,\dots,N\};\ \text{greedy soup: add models in order of validation accuracy, keep }i\text{ only if held-out accuracy does not drop};\ \text{all }W_i\text{ frozen, nothing trained}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(post-hoc average of }N\text{ fine-tuned models sharing one pre-trained initialization)}
methods.locus: all parameters of fully fine-tuned models that share a pre-trained initialization
methods.structure: Equal-weight barycentre (convex combination) of N points in weight space that share the base point W_0; the greedy soup is the barycentre of a validation-selected subset.
methods.mergeable_reason: The soup is a single weight vector of the original architecture, so inference costs exactly one model.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free); a soup of a single model returns that model.
methods.key_idea: Models fine-tuned from the same pre-trained weights with different hyper-parameters tend to lie in one low-error basin, so averaging their weights gives ensemble-like accuracy and robustness at single-model cost.
methods.results_note: A greedy soup of fine-tuned ViT-G/14 models reached 90.94% ImageNet top-1, above the best single model of the sweep (90.78%).

methods.name: Fisher Merging
methods.paper_title: Merging Models with Fisher-Weighted Averaging
methods.formula_latex: W^{\star}_{[p]}=\frac{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i\,F_{i,[p]}\,W_{i,[p]}}{\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i\,F_{i,[p]}}\ \ (\text{per coordinate }p),\quad F_i=\mathbb{E}_{x}\,\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p_{\theta_i}(y\mid x)}\big[(\nabla_{\theta}\log p_{\theta_i}(y\mid x))^{2}\big],\ \lambda_i\ge0,\ \textstyle\sum_i\lambda_i=1;\ \text{models frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(one diagonal Fisher estimate per model, same size as the model)}

methods.structure: Per-coordinate precision-weighted mean: the maximizer of \sum_i\lambda_i\log\mathcal{N}(\theta;\theta_i,F_i^{-1}) under a diagonal Laplace approximation of each posterior; isotropic averaging is the case F_i=I.
methods.mergeable_reason: The output is one set of weights for the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: View merging as maximizing the joint likelihood of the models' posteriors; using each model's diagonal Fisher information as its posterior precision lets every coordinate be dominated by the model that is most certain about it.
methods.results_note: Fisher merging beats isotropic averaging for robust fine-tuning and model ensembling and is competitive with intermediate-task transfer and domain-adaptive pre-training at much lower cost.

methods.paper_title: Dataless Knowledge Fusion by Merging Weights of Language Models

methods.structure: Layer-wise least-squares merge: the merged linear map is the Gram-weighted matrix mean of the individual maps; equals simple averaging when all G_i are equal, and the off-diagonal shrinkage \alpha (\approx0.9) acts as a pull toward the individual weights.

methods.key_idea: Merge each linear layer so that on every model's own training inputs it reproduces that model's outputs as closely as possible; this regression has a closed form that needs only inner-product statistics of the inputs, not the data itself.
methods.results_note: Across GLUE-style merging settings RegMean significantly outperforms Fisher-weighted averaging and model ensembling baselines and can preserve or improve individual-model performance without training data.

methods.paper_title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic

methods.mergeable_reason: The edited model is a single weight vector of the original architecture; only element-wise operations on weights are used.

methods.name: TIES-Merging
methods.paper_title: TIES-Merging: Resolving Interference When Merging Models
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraModel.add_weighted_adapter(combination_type='ties' | 'ties_svd', density=k, majority_sign_method='total' | 'frequency'); 'ties' trims and elects signs on the lora_A and lora_B factors separately, 'ties_svd' on the dense Delta W followed by SVD truncation; also IA3 vectors via merge_utils.ties
methods.formula_latex: \hat\tau_i=\operatorname{TopK}_{k\%}(\tau_i)\ (\text{trim});\quad \gamma^{p}=\operatorname{sgn}\Big(\textstyle\sum_{i}\hat\tau_i^{p}\Big)\ (\text{elect});\quad \tau_m^{p}=\frac{1}{|\mathcal{A}^{p}|}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{A}^{p}}\hat\tau_i^{p},\ \mathcal{A}^{p}=\{i:\operatorname{sgn}(\hat\tau_i^{p})=\gamma^{p}\}\ (\text{disjoint merge});\quad \theta_m=\theta_0+\lambda\,\tau_m
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(hyper-parameters }k\approx20\%,\ \lambda\approx1)
methods.locus: task vectors of full fine-tuning or of PEFT parameters (e.g. (IA)^3 vectors, LoRA factors in HF PEFT)
methods.structure: Coordinate-wise non-linear aggregation: magnitude sparsification, sign election by total mass, and a mean over agreeing non-zero entries only; not a linear combination of task vectors.
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged task vector is added to the base weights once, giving a standard model.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: Merging interference comes from redundant small updates and sign conflicts; trimming small entries, electing one sign per parameter and averaging only agreeing values recovers much of the accuracy lost by plain averaging.
methods.results_note: With validation-tuned hyper-parameters, TIES outperforms averaging, Fisher merging, RegMean and Task Arithmetic across T5, ViT and (IA)^3-PEFT merges, in-domain and out-of-domain. Without a validation set, the fixed recipe (k = 20%, lambda = 1) is weaker than Task Arithmetic for the T5-base (IA)^3 merge (69.7 vs 73.2).

methods.name: DARE
methods.paper_title: Language Models are Super Mario: Absorbing Abilities from Homologous Models as a Free Lunch
methods.formula_latex: m_i\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p)\ \text{elementwise},\quad \hat\tau_i=\frac{(\mathbf{1}-m_i)\odot\tau_i}{1-p};\quad \theta_m=\theta_0+\lambda\textstyle\sum_i\hat\tau_i\ (\text{DARE+TA})\ \text{or TIES on }\{\hat\tau_i\};\ \text{no training}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(drop rate }p\text{, up to }0.9\text{--}0.99)
methods.locus: delta parameters (fine-tuned minus pre-trained) of homologous SFT models; LoRA factors in HF PEFT
methods.structure: Random sparse coordinate mask with inverted-dropout rescaling 1/(1-p), which preserves the expectation of each delta and of its action on inputs; a pre-processing operator applied before any merge rule.
methods.mergeable_reason: Sparsified deltas are added back to the base weights, giving one ordinary model.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: SFT deltas of language models are extremely redundant: randomly dropping 90-99% of them and rescaling the rest barely changes behaviour, and sparsified deltas of several homologous models interfere less when merged.
methods.results_note: DARE removes 90% or even 99% of delta parameters with little performance loss, and a DARE-merged 7B model ranked first among 7B models on the Open LLM Leaderboard at the time.

relations.note: commonly used as DARE-TIES
DARE+Task Arithmetic is the basic merge

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2311.03099 (Yu, 2023); ICML 2024 per arXiv comment and PMLR v235. Bernoulli(p) drop with 1/(1-p) rescaling, 90-99% drop rates and the top-ranked 7B merged model on the Open LLM Leaderboard confirmed. PEFT random_pruning keeps a fraction density = 1 - p and rescales by 1/density.

methods.name: AdaMerging
methods.paper_title: AdaMerging: Adaptive Model Merging for Multi-Task Learning
methods.formula_latex: \theta_m^{l}=\theta_0^{l}+\sum_{i=1}^{N}\lambda_i^{l}\,\tau_i^{l}\ \ (\text{layer-wise; task-wise uses one }\lambda_i\text{ per model});\quad \{\lambda\}=\arg\min_{\lambda}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{D}^{\mathrm{unlab}}_{\mathrm{test}}}H\big(f_{\theta_m(\lambda)}(x)\big),\ H=\text{prediction entropy};\ \text{task vectors frozen}
methods.trainable_params: N\ \text{per layer (layer-wise) or }N\text{ in total (task-wise)}
methods.locus: task vectors of all layers (CLIP ViT image encoders in the paper)
methods.structure: Learned layer-wise linear combination of task vectors, fitted by test-time entropy minimization on unlabeled multi-task inputs.
methods.mergeable_reason: After learning the coefficients the merged weights form one ordinary model.
methods.identity_at_init: Coefficients initialized to the task-arithmetic default \lambda=0.3 (not an identity initialization).
methods.key_idea: Merging coefficients matter a lot; they can be learned per task and per layer without labels by minimizing the entropy of the merged model's predictions on unlabeled test inputs.
methods.results_note: Merging eight ViT task models, AdaMerging improves average accuracy by about 11% over Task Arithmetic and generalizes better to unseen tasks and distribution shift.

methods.name: TSV-Merge
methods.full_name: Task Singular Vectors Merge (TSV-M) and Compress (TSV-C)
methods.paper_title: Task Singular Vectors: Reducing Task Interference in Model Merging
methods.formula_latex: \Delta_i=U_i\Sigma_iV_i^{\top}\ (\text{keep top }1/N\text{ components});\ U=[U_1|\cdots|U_N],\ \Sigma=\operatorname{blockdiag}(\Sigma_1,\dots,\Sigma_N),\ V=[V_1|\cdots|V_N];\ U=P_UD_UQ_U^{\top}\Rightarrow U_\perp=P_UQ_U^{\top}\ (\text{same for }V);\ W=W_0+\alpha\,U_\perp\Sigma V_\perp^{\top}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(one scaling }\alpha\text{; the paper finds }\alpha=1\text{ best, so no tuning is needed)}
methods.locus: per-layer task matrices of all weight matrices (ViT CLIP encoders in the paper)
methods.structure: Per-layer low-rank truncation of each task matrix, then orthogonalization (whitening, equivalently orthogonal Procrustes) of the concatenated singular-vector bases to remove cross-task overlap measured by the Singular Task Interference \|(U^{\top}U-I)\Sigma(V^{\top}V-I)\|_1.
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged matrix is added once to the pre-trained weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: Layer task matrices are low-rank, so each can be kept as its top singular vectors; interference appears as overlap between different tasks' singular vectors and can be removed by orthogonalizing the stacked bases before summation.
methods.results_note: TSV-C compresses task matrices to 10% of their size while retaining 99% of accuracy, and TSV-M significantly outperforms prior merging methods on 8/14/20-task ViT benchmarks.

relations.note: replaces flat task vectors with per-layer SVD structure
both merge in an SVD basis; KnOTS shares U Sigma across LoRAs, TSV orthogonalizes per-task bases

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2412.00081 (Gargiulo, 2024); CVPR 2025 per arXiv comment and IEEE DOI 10.1109/CVPR52734.2025.01742. Per-layer SVD truncation to a 1/T share per task, whitening X(X^T X)^{-1/2} = PQ^T (Procrustes, Prop. 1), the STI score (Eq. 6), and TSV-C's 10% size with 99% accuracy confirmed.
corrections: trainable_params: added that alpha = 1 works best in the paper (Sec. 6.3, Fig. 7), so TSV-M needs no coefficient tuning.

methods.name: KnOTS
methods.paper_title: Model merging with SVD to tie the Knots
methods.formula_latex: \big[\Delta W^{(1)}\ \cdots\ \Delta W^{(N)}\big]=U\Sigma\,\big[V^{(1)};\dots;V^{(N)}\big]^{\top}\ \ (\Delta W^{(i)}=B_iA_i);\quad V^{(m)}=\operatorname{Merge}\big(V^{(1)},\dots,V^{(N)}\big)\ (\text{TA, TIES, DARE},\dots);\quad W=W_0+U\Sigma\,V^{(m)\top}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(data-free, gradient-free)}
methods.locus: LoRA-adapted attention projections (q, k, v, o) of ViT-B/32, ViT-L/16 and Llama3-8B LoRA models in the paper (rank 16)
methods.structure: Joint SVD of the column-concatenated LoRA updates: a shared orthonormal output basis U\Sigma (rank \le N r) and task-specific input-side factors V^{(i)}; any existing merge rule is applied in this aligned coordinate system.
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged update U Sigma V^(m)T is a dense matrix added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: LoRA updates of different tasks are much less aligned than full fine-tuning deltas; re-expressing them in a common SVD basis aligns them so that standard merging rules stop destroying each other's information.
methods.results_note: KnOTS improves LoRA merging by up to 4.3% across vision and language benchmarks, including a new joint-task benchmark for general models.

relations.note: TIES/DARE/TA are applied to the aligned V factors
designed for merging LoRA-finetuned models

methods.name: PEM Arithmetic
methods.full_name: Composing parameter-efficient modules with arithmetic operations
methods.paper_title: Composing Parameter-Efficient Modules with Arithmetic Operations
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraModel.add_weighted_adapter(combination_type='linear'): PEFT scales each factor by sqrt(|w_i| * scaling_i) and puts the sign on lora_A only, so weights w_i = lambda_i^2 reproduce PEM addition and a negative weight reproduces PEM negation; IA3Model.add_weighted_adapter gives (IA)^3 addition, but the affine negation l -> 2 - l is not built in
methods.formula_latex: \theta^{\mathrm{add}}=\lambda\theta^{(1)}\oplus(1-\lambda)\theta^{(2)}:=\lambda\theta^{(1)}+(1-\lambda)\theta^{(2)}\ \ (\text{component-wise on }(A,B)\text{ or on }l);\quad \ominus\theta_{\mathrm{LoRA}}=\{A,-B\}\ \Rightarrow\ \Delta h=BAx\mapsto-\Delta h;\quad \ominus l_{(IA)^3}=\mathbf{2}-l;\ \text{e.g. domain transfer }\theta^{(1)}\ominus\theta^{(2)}\oplus\theta^{(3)};\ \text{no training}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(weight }\lambda\text{ tuned on validation)}
methods.locus: LoRA factors or (IA)^3 scaling vectors of modules trained from the same base model
methods.structure: Addition is defined on module parameters (for LoRA (A_1+A_2),(B_1+B_2), which creates cross terms B_1A_2+B_2A_1), whereas negation is defined through the induced hidden-state change \Delta h: negate only B for LoRA, l\mapsto 2-l for (IA)^3, because negating both factors leaves BA unchanged.
methods.mergeable_reason: The composed module is again a LoRA/(IA)^3 module, which can be folded into the base weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: PEFT modules trained from one base model can be composed by weight-space arithmetic; the subtle part is negation, which must flip the module's effect on hidden states rather than its raw parameters.
methods.results_note: Arithmetic compositions of LoRA/(IA)^3 modules (RoBERTa-base, T5-base) beat the individual modules for distribution generalization, multi-tasking, unlearning and domain transfer, and LoRA negation detoxifies Alpaca-LoRA.

The PDF footnote gives the code at github.com/hkust-nlp/PEM_composition (the arXiv comment's SJTU-LIT URL also resolves).
corrections: hf_peft_config: explained how PEFT's sqrt-weight convention maps onto PEM (weights lambda^2, sign on one factor). Added that IA3Model.add_weighted_adapter covers (IA)^3 addition only, not the 2 - l negation.

methods.name: AdapterSoup
methods.full_name: AdapterSoup: weight averaging of domain adapters
methods.paper_title: AdapterSoup: Weight Averaging to Improve Generalization of Pretrained Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \theta_{\mathrm{soup}}=\tfrac{1}{l}\sum_{i\in\mathcal{S}}\theta_i,\ |\mathcal{S}|=l\le k;\quad y=f\big(x;\theta_m,\theta_{\mathrm{soup}}\big);\ \mathcal{S}\text{ chosen by sentence-BERT similarity or domain clustering on a little novel-domain text};\ \text{PLM }\theta_m\text{ and all adapters frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{for the novel domain (}k\text{ domain adapters are trained beforehand, each a bottleneck adapter of }\approx2rd\text{ per layer)}
methods.locus: Bapna and Firat (2019)-style bottleneck adapters (bottleneck size 64) in every Transformer layer of GPT-2
methods.structure: Uniform average (a model soup) of a retrieved subset of adapter parameter vectors; one averaged adapter is executed at test time.
methods.mergeable_reason: The soup collapses the selected adapters into one adapter, so inference costs a single adapter. That adapter is a nonlinear bottleneck module and cannot fold into W_0. The same recipe applied to LoRAs (mentioned only as future work) would be foldable.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free combination of trained adapters).
methods.key_idea: For an unseen domain, rather than picking one related-domain adapter, average the weights of several selected domain adapters to obtain ensemble-like gains at the cost of a single adapter.
methods.results_note: On 10 held-out web domains with GPT-2, AdapterSoup with clustering-based selection gives the best average out-of-domain perplexity among single-adapter-cost methods.

LoraHub learns signed weights instead of uniform averaging

No official code link found.
corrections: locus: named the adapter architecture used (Bapna and Firat 2019, bottleneck 64; Sec. 4), not generic 'bottleneck adapters'.

mergeable_reason: rewritten to match the 'no' verdict.

methods.name: LoraHub
methods.paper_title: LoraHub: Efficient Cross-Task Generalization via Dynamic LoRA Composition
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_iB_i\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{N}w_iA_i\Big),\ \ w\in\mathbb{R}^{N}\ (\text{signed});\quad w^{\star}=\arg\min_{w}\ \mathcal{L}_{Q}(w)+\alpha\textstyle\sum_i|w_i|\ \text{by gradient-free CMA-ES (Nevergrad Shiwa)};\ W=W_0+\Delta W;\ \text{base model and all }(A_i,B_i)\text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: N\ \text{scalars in total (e.g. }N=20\text{ randomly sampled LoRAs), shared by all layers}
methods.locus: all LoRA-adapted matrices of the base model (Flan-T5 in the paper)
methods.structure: Element-wise linear combination of the factor matrices (a product of sums, which introduces cross terms B_iA_j), with one global coefficient per module found by black-box optimization on a few examples.
methods.mergeable_reason: The composed LoRA has fixed weights and can be merged into W_0 like any LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (only composition weights are searched; modules are pre-trained).
methods.key_idea: Given a hub of task LoRAs, an unseen task can be handled by searching, without gradients, for a weighted combination of existing LoRAs that minimizes loss on a handful of examples.
methods.results_note: On Big-Bench Hard with Flan-T5-large and 20 candidate LoRAs, LoraHub approaches few-shot in-context learning while using far fewer tokens per example at inference.

Not in HF PEFT: PEFT's 'linear' only reproduces LoraHub's composition for non-negative weights (passed as w_i^2), and it has no search.

methods.name: LoRA Soups (CAT)
methods.paper_title: LoRA Soups: Merging LoRAs for Practical Skill Composition Tasks
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W^{l}=\sum_{i=1}^{N}\alpha_i^{l}\,B_iA_i=\big[\alpha_1^{l}B_1\ \cdots\ \alpha_N^{l}B_N\big]\begin{bmatrix}A_1\\ \vdots\\ A_N\end{bmatrix};\ \ \alpha_i^{l}\text{ trained per layer on a small data mixture};\ W_0\text{ and all }(A_i,B_i)\text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: N\ \text{per layer}
methods.locus: all LoRA-adapted matrices (Llama-family models in the paper)
methods.structure: Rank-concatenation (direct sum along the rank axis) of LoRA factors with learned layer-wise scalars: a weighted sum of the LoRA updates without the cross terms of factor averaging; merged rank \sum_i r_i. methods.mergeable_reason: Coefficients are input-independent, so the concatenated LoRA is a fixed low-rank update that can be folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable; only the merging coefficients are trained after the skill LoRAs exist.
methods.key_idea: For skill composition (e.g. hard math word problems solved by writing code), concatenating independently trained skill LoRAs and learning only per-layer mixing weights beats both data mixing and parameter-averaging merges.
methods.results_note: On GSM-Hard, CAT beats existing model-merging and data-mixing baselines by 43% and 12% on average and shows super-linear gains over the individual skill LoRAs.

compared as linear-merging baseline

both build a merged LoRA from rank units without factor averaging; LoRA-LEGO with k = sum r_i returns the static concatenation scaled by sqrt(r/k), whereas CAT learns per-layer weights, so CAT is not a special case

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.13025 (Prabhakar, 2024); COLING 2025 Industry Track confirmed (ACL Anthology 2025.coling-industry.55). The CAT definition Delta W^l = alpha_1^l B_1A_1^T + alpha_2^l B_2A_2^T, with trainable alpha in [0,1] (Sec. 4), the contrast with linear merging (cross terms), and the 43%/12% GSM-Hard gains confirmed.

methods.name: LoRA-LEGO
methods.full_name: LoRA-LEGO: rank-wise clustering of minimal semantic units
methods.paper_title: Merging LoRAs like Playing LEGO: Pushing the Modularity of LoRA to Extremes Through Rank-Wise Clustering
methods.formula_latex: s_{ij}=[a_{ij},b_{ij}]\ (a_{ij}\text{: row }j\text{ of }A_i,\ b_{ij}\text{: column }j\text{ of }B_i);\ \Phi=\textstyle\bigcup_i\{s_{i1},\dots,s_{ir_i}\};\ \{\mu_c\}_{c=1}^{k}=\operatorname{KMeans}_k(\Phi);\ \mu'_c=\frac{\overline{\|s\|}_{\mathbb{C}_c}}{\|\mu_c\|}\mu_c;\ A'=[a'_1;\dots;a'_k],\ B'=[b'_1\cdots b'_k];\ \Delta W=\tfrac{\sqrt{r}}{\sqrt{k}}\,B'A'
methods.trainable_params: 0\ \text{(merged rank }k,\ 1\le k\le\textstyle\sum_i r_i)
methods.locus: all LoRA-adapted matrices
methods.structure: Decomposes each LoRA into rank-1 'minimal semantic units' b_ja_j and uses two algebraic facts: permutation invariance BA=(BP^{\top})(PA) and concatenation-summation equivalence [B_1\ B_2][A_1;A_2]=B_1A_1+B_2A_2; units from all LoRAs are clustered and k centroids (norm- and variance-rescaled) form the merged LoRA.
methods.mergeable_reason: The result is an ordinary rank-k LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: A LoRA is an unordered bag of rank-1 units, so merging should regroup similar units across LoRAs instead of averaging factor matrices position by position, which mixes misaligned units.
methods.results_note: Outperforms existing LoRA merging approaches on multi-task and mixed-task benchmarks.

methods.name: ZipLoRA
methods.full_name: ZipLoRA: merging subject and style LoRAs
methods.paper_title: ZipLoRA: Any Subject in Any Style by Effectively Merging LoRAs
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W_m=\Delta W_c\operatorname{diag}(m_c)+\Delta W_s\operatorname{diag}(m_s)\ (\text{one coefficient per column});\ \min_{m_c,m_s}\ \|(D\oplus L_m)(x_c,p_c)-(D\oplus L_c)(x_c,p_c)\|_2+\|(D\oplus L_m)(x_s,p_s)-(D\oplus L_s)(x_s,p_s)\|_2+\lambda\sum_{l}|m_c^{(l)}\cdot m_s^{(l)}|;\ W_0,\Delta W_c,\Delta W_s\text{ frozen}

methods.formula_latex: \Delta W_i=B_iA_i,\ B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen: }r\text{ rows drawn at random from a shared orthogonal basis }O\in O(d_{in});\quad \text{merge (FedAvg-style): }W=W_0+\sum_i\lambda_i\Delta W_i\ (\lambda=0.6);\quad A_jA_i^{\top}\approx0\Rightarrow\Delta W_j\,A_i^{\top}A_i\approx0\ \text{(concept }j\text{ is blind to the subspace concept }i\text{ reads)};\ \text{paper's notation: }\Delta\theta_i=A_iB_i^{\top},\ B_i\text{ frozen}

methods.locus: customizable linear layers of a text-to-image diffusion model
methods.structure: LoRA whose input-side factor is frozen and (approximately) mutually orthogonal across independently trained concepts, so each concept's update reads a nearly disjoint input subspace; merging is plain summation with little crosstalk.
methods.mergeable_reason: Each concept update is a fixed low-rank matrix and the merge is a sum, foldable into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: The frozen factor is a random orthonormal slice; the update is zero at init only if the trainable factor starts at zero (as in LoRA), which the paper does not stress.
methods.key_idea: Make LoRAs mergeable by construction: if each user's update reads its input through a random slice of a shared orthogonal basis, independently trained concept residuals barely interfere when added.
methods.results_note: Merged multi-concept Stable Diffusion models preserve identity better than FedAvg-style summation and match Mix-of-Show gradient fusion while merging almost instantly instead of ~15 minutes.

Delta theta_i = A_i B_i^T with B_i fixed and only A_i optimized (Eq. 4), B_i as random columns of a shared orthogonal basis (Sec. 3.5), r = 20, lambda = 0.6, and parity with Mix-of-Show gradient fusion (~15 min) at near-instant merging confirmed. The init of the trained factor is not stated in the paper, and no official code was found.

methods.name: LoRA Switch / LoRA Composite
methods.paper_title: Multi-LoRA Composition for Image Generation
methods.formula_latex: \text{Switch: }i(t)=\big\lfloor((t-1)\bmod k\tau)/\tau\big\rfloor+1,\ W_t=W_0+w_{i(t)}B_{i(t)}A_{i(t)};\quad \text{Composite: }\tilde\epsilon(z_t,c)=\tfrac{1}{k}\sum_{i=1}^{k}w_i\big[\epsilon_{\theta_i'}(z_t)+s\,(\epsilon_{\theta_i'}(z_t,c)-\epsilon_{\theta_i'}(z_t))\big];\ \text{training-free, LoRA weights untouched}
methods.locus: denoising trajectory of a text-to-image diffusion model
methods.structure: Composition in time (round-robin activation of one LoRA every \tau denoising steps) or in score space (averaging classifier-free-guided noise predictions of k LoRA-adapted models) instead of in weight space.
methods.mergeable_reason: LoRA Switch runs one merged LoRA at a time (original cost, weights swapped every tau steps). LoRA Composite runs 2k UNet evaluations per denoising step (conditional and unconditional for each of the k LoRA-adapted models), so it never reduces to one set of weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: Instead of merging LoRA weights, compose LoRAs during decoding, either alternating them across denoising steps or averaging their guided scores, which scales to many LoRAs without weight interference.
methods.results_note: On the ComposLoRA testbed (480 composition sets), both methods beat weight-space LoRA merging in GPT-4V and human evaluations, increasingly so as more LoRAs are composed.

methods.name: Polytropon (Poly)
methods.full_name: Polytropon: latent-skill routing over parameter-efficient modules
methods.paper_title: Combining Parameter-efficient Modules for Task-level Generalisation
methods.formula_latex: \hat z_{\tau,j}\sim\text{Gumbel-sigmoid}(Z_{\tau,j}),\ \alpha_j=\frac{\hat z_{\tau,j}}{\sum_{j'}\hat z_{\tau,j'}};\ A^{\tau}=\sum_{j=1}^{|\mathcal{S}|}\alpha_jA_j,\ B^{\tau}=\sum_{j}\alpha_jB_j;\ h=W_0x+s\,B^{\tau}A^{\tau}x;\ \text{trained: skill inventory }\{A_j,B_j\}\text{ and task-skill logits }Z\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{T}|\times|\mathcal{S}|}\text{ per layer}
methods.trainable_params: |\mathcal{S}|\,r(d_{in}+d_{out})+|\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{S}|\ \text{per adapted matrix}
methods.locus: LoRA skills on attention projections (q, k, v, o) of T5; sparse LT-SFT skills also studied
methods.structure: Task-conditioned normalized combination of a small inventory of LoRA skills; the task-skill allocation is a relaxed binary soft partition (optional Indian Buffet Process prior); factors are mixed separately (product of sums).
methods.mergeable_reason: For a known task the mixed (A^tau, B^tau) is fixed and can be folded into W_0 (one merged copy per task). Mixed-task batches need per-task routing. HF PEFT's Poly layer implements no merge/unmerge.
methods.identity_at_init: HF PEFT: routing logits ~U(-1e-3, 1e-3) (near uniform) and LoRA up-projections zero-initialized, so the model starts unchanged.
methods.key_idea: Assume tasks share a small inventory of latent skills; jointly learn which skills each task uses and the skills themselves, so new tasks can be few-shot adapted by recombining skills. (arXiv title: 'Combining Modular Skills in Multitask Learning'.)
methods.results_note: Improves sample efficiency on 8 BabyAI levels and few-shot generalization on CrossFit (160 NLP tasks) over fully shared, task-specific and hypernetwork-generated baselines.

methods.name: MHR
methods.paper_title: Multi-Head Adapter Routing for Cross-Task Generalization
methods.formula_latex: A^{\tau}=\operatorname{concat}_{k=1}^{h}\Big(\sum_{j}\frac{\hat{\mathsf{Z}}_{\tau,j,k}}{\sum_{j'}\hat{\mathsf{Z}}_{\tau,j',k}}\,A_j[k]\Big)\ (\text{same for }B^{\tau}),\ A_j[k]:\ k\text{-th of }h\text{ disjoint blocks of the factor};\ h_{out}=W_0x+s\,B^{\tau}A^{\tau}x;\ \mathsf{Z}\in\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{T}|\times|\mathcal{M}|\times h}
methods.trainable_params: |\mathcal{M}|\,r(d_{in}+d_{out})+|\mathcal{T}||\mathcal{M}|h\ \text{per adapted matrix; MHR-}z\text{ fine-tunes only }|\mathcal{M}|h\text{ routing logits per new task}
methods.locus: LoRA modules on attention projections (T5 / T0 backbones)
methods.structure: Block-wise task-conditioned mixing: a separate Polytropon routing for each of h disjoint blocks of the factor matrices (in HF PEFT, A is split along d_in and B along d_out), with the routed blocks concatenated.
methods.mergeable_reason: For a known task the routed factors are fixed and the LoRA can be merged; routing must be resolved per task.
methods.identity_at_init: As Polytropon (near-uniform routing logits; zero-initialized up-projections in HF PEFT).
methods.key_idea: Finer-grained routing is more expressive: letting different blocks of each adapter come from different modules beats whole-module mixing at equal budget, and the benefit of routing lies mostly in multi-task pre-training.
methods.results_note: MHR outperforms Poly at comparable budget; routing-only MHR-z is competitive with extreme parameter efficiency, and MHR-mu (fine-tuning the averaged adapters) shows routing matters chiefly during multi-task pre-training.

methods.name: SMEAR
methods.full_name: Soft Merging of Experts with Adaptive Routing
methods.paper_title: Soft Merging of Experts with Adaptive Routing
methods.formula_latex: y=\bar f\Big(u;\ \sum_{i=1}^{N}R(v)_i\,\theta_i\Big),\ \ R(v)=\operatorname{softmax}(W_rv);\ \theta_i:\text{ parameters of expert }i\text{ (adapters)};\ \text{experts and router trained end-to-end, backbone frozen}
methods.trainable_params: N\cdot(2rd+r+d)+dN\ \text{per routing block (}N\text{ bottleneck-adapter experts plus a linear router), plus router/expert LayerNorms and the backbone LayerNorms}
methods.locus: expert routing blocks inserted after self-attention, feed-forward and cross-attention (T5) or after residual groups (ResNet)
methods.structure: Per-example soft parameter merging: the router's distribution averages expert parameters and the input passes through the single merged expert, keeping routing fully differentiable at the cost of one expert.
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged expert changes with every input, so it cannot be folded into fixed weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Experts are randomly initialized with different values to break symmetry; no identity guarantee.
methods.key_idea: Learned discrete routing underperforms because of poor gradient estimators; averaging expert parameters with the router's probabilities makes routing differentiable without extra compute.
methods.results_note: On T5-GLUE and ResNet-DomainNet, SMEAR outperforms metadata-based routing and routing learned with gradient estimators at similar inference cost.

Router-weighted parameter averaging into a single expert, per-example routing on average-pooled hidden states, random expert init to break symmetry, and blocks after self-attention, FFN and cross-attention (60 blocks in T5.1.1-Base) confirmed.

methods.name: MoV / MoLoRA
methods.full_name: Mixture of (IA)^3 Vectors / Mixture of LoRA experts
methods.paper_title: Pushing Mixture of Experts to the Limit: Extremely Parameter Efficient MoE for Instruction Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{MoV: }E_{\mathrm{mix}}(x)=\sum_{i=1}^{N}s_i(x)\,l_i,\ s(x)=\operatorname{softmax}(W_gx),\ h\leftarrow E_{\mathrm{mix}}(x)\odot h\ \text{at each (IA)}^3\text{ site};\quad \text{MoLoRA: }\Delta W(x)=\sum_{i}s_i(x)\,B_iA_i;\ W_0\text{ frozen, experts and router trained}
methods.trainable_params: \text{MoV: }N\,d_{site}+N\,d_{model}\ \text{per (IA)}^3\text{ site (}N\text{ scaling vectors of the site's width plus a }d_{model}\times N\text{ router)};\ \text{MoLoRA: }N\,r(d_{in}+d_{out})+N\,d_{in}\ \text{per matrix}
methods.locus: (IA)^3 rescaling sites (keys, values, FFN intermediate) for MoV; linear layers for MoLoRA; T5 encoder-decoder
methods.structure: Token-level soft merging of lightweight experts: a router-weighted average of diagonal (IA)^3 scaling vectors (multiplicative) or of LoRA experts, applied as one merged expert.
methods.mergeable_reason: The merged scaling vector / LoRA depends on each token through the router.
methods.identity_at_init: MoV expert vectors initialized to ones (identity scaling), so the network is unchanged at init.
methods.key_idea: Mixture-of-experts can be pushed to extreme parameter efficiency by making each expert an (IA)^3 vector or a LoRA and merging experts softly, which also generalizes to unseen tasks without task metadata.
methods.results_note: Instruction-tuning T5 on P3 with <1% of parameters updated, MoV matches full fine-tuning on unseen tasks at scale and improves over standard (IA)^3 by up to 14.57% (3B) and 8.39% (11B).

methods.name: LoRAMoE
methods.full_name: LoRAMoE: MoE-style LoRA plugin with localized balancing
methods.paper_title: LoRAMoE: Alleviating World Knowledge Forgetting in Large Language Models via MoE-Style Plugin
methods.formula_latex: o=W_0x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\sum_{i=1}^{N}\omega_i(x)\,B_iA_ix,\ \ \omega(x)=\operatorname{softmax}(W_g^{\top}x);\quad \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{task}}+\beta\,\frac{\sigma^2(I\circ Q)}{\mu(I\circ Q)},\ I_{n,m}=1\pm\delta\ \text{(localized balancing constraint)};\ W_0\text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: N\,r(d_{in}+d_{out})+N\,d_{in}\ \text{per adapted FFN matrix}
methods.locus: linear layers of the feed-forward block
methods.structure: Dense softmax mixture of N LoRA experts per FFN linear layer, with a soft balancing loss that dedicates one expert group to world-knowledge tasks and another to other downstream tasks.
methods.mergeable_reason: Expert weights are computed per token by the router.
methods.identity_at_init: Not discussed in the paper. The official code (Ablustrund/LoRAMoE, peft/tuners/lora.py) initializes every B_i to zero (A_i and router Kaiming-uniform), so the plugin starts as the identity regardless of the router.
methods.key_idea: Large-scale SFT erodes world knowledge stored in the backbone; freezing it and adding router-mixed LoRA experts, part of which are pushed toward knowledge tasks, keeps that knowledge while still learning downstream tasks.
methods.results_note: Compared with vanilla SFT, LoRAMoE avoids the knowledge collapse and improves world-knowledge benchmarks by up to 63.9% (35.3% on average) while matching or beating SFT on other tasks.

methods.name: MoLE
methods.paper_title: Mixture of LoRA Experts
methods.formula_latex: E_{\Omega}(x)=\operatorname{Norm}\big(E_{\Delta\theta_0}(x)\oplus\cdots\oplus E_{\Delta\theta_{N-1}}(x)\big),\ \varepsilon=\operatorname{Flatten}(E_{\Omega}(x))^{\top}e,\ G_i=\frac{\exp(\varepsilon_i/\tau)}{\sum_j\exp(\varepsilon_j/\tau)},\ O(x)=F_{\theta}(x)+\sum_iG_i\,E_{\Delta\theta_i}(x);\ \text{trained LoRAs frozen; per-layer gate }e\text{ and temperature }\tau\text{ trained with }\mathcal{L}_D+\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{balance}}

methods.structure: Hierarchical, layer-wise learned gating over the outputs of N frozen pre-trained LoRAs, with a gate-balancing loss -\log\prod_i q^{(i)} against collapse onto one LoRA.

methods.name: Doc-to-LoRA (D2L)
methods.full_name: Doc-to-LoRA: meta-learned context distillation into LoRA
methods.paper_title: Doc-to-LoRA: Learning to Instantly Internalize Contexts
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W_l=B_lA_l=h_{\phi}(Z_{l-1}),\ \ U_l=\operatorname{XAttn}\big(Q_m,K(Z_{l-1}),V(Z_{l-1})\big)\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_u}\ (\text{each latent}\to\text{a row of }A_l\text{ and a column of }B_l),\ W'_l=W_l+\alpha_lB_lA_l;\quad \min_{\phi}\mathbb{E}\,\mathrm{KL}\big(p_{\theta}(y\mid x,c)\,\|\,p_{\theta+H_{\phi}(c)}(y\mid x)\big);\ \text{chunks: }A_l=[A_l^{(1)};\dots;A_l^{(K)}],\ B_l=[B_l^{(1)}\cdots B_l^{(K)}]
methods.trainable_params: \text{hypernetwork only (Perceiver with 8 cross-attention blocks, }309\text{M parameters for Gemma-2-2b-it, Sec. 5); learnable per-layer scales }\alpha_l;\ \text{zero training per document; generated adapter }Kr(d_{in}+d_{out})\text{ per down-projection for }K\text{ chunks}
methods.locus: the down-projection of every MLP block of the target LLM (rank-8 LoRAs per chunk); per-layer context activations of the frozen LLM feed the hypernetwork
methods.structure: Meta-learned context distillation: a Perceiver hypernetwork reads the frozen LLM's per-layer activations of a document and emits rank-r LoRA factors; long documents are composed by rank-concatenation (direct sum) of per-chunk adapters, giving rank rK.
methods.mergeable_reason: The generated adapter is an ordinary LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (generated weights); a learnable per-layer scale alpha_l modulates the update.
methods.key_idea: Amortize context distillation: instead of distilling each document into weights by gradient descent, train a hypernetwork once so that any new document is internalized into a LoRA in one sub-second forward pass, removing it from the context window.
methods.results_note: Achieves near-perfect zero-shot needle-in-a-haystack accuracy at lengths more than 4x the target LLM's native context window and outperforms standard context distillation on QA with much lower memory and update latency.

relations.note: extends T2L-style hypernetworks from task descriptions to documents
App. D shows the same hypernetwork can instead emit a compressed KV cache (prefix-tuning parametrization): weight-space vs KV-space internalization of one context
Both map a context to a parameter delta in one forward pass.
Cartridges also stores a document in trainable parameters (a KV prefix), but trains per document by self-study.
Concurrent context-to-LoRA hypernetwork.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2602.15902 (Charakorn, 2026). ICML 2026 confirmed by the official README citation (booktitle 'Forty-third International Conference on Machine Learning'). It is not yet in PMLR, and Semantic Scholar still lists arXiv. W'_l = W_l + alpha_l B_l A_l (Eq. 5), KL context-distillation objective, Perceiver latents mapped to rows of A and columns of B, rank concatenation over chunks (rank rK), and NIAH beyond 4x the native context confirmed.

trainable_params: sourced the 309M figure from the paper (Sec. 5, 'only 309M trainable parameters'), not only the project page. Added the generated adapter size Kr(d_in + d_out).
relations: removed 'competes-with lora-soups'. D2L neither cites nor competes with LoRA Soups. The shared rank-concatenation operator is a structural fact, already stated in the structure field.
relations: cited App. D for the prefix-tuning duality.

methods.name: Tina
methods.paper_title: Tina: Tiny Reasoning Models via LoRA
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(r=32, lora_alpha=128, lora_dropout=0.05, target_modules=["q_proj","k_proj","v_proj","o_proj","gate_proj","up_proj","down_proj"])  # plain LoRA (no dedicated tuner), trained with GRPO / Dr.GRPO via TRL
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r} B A,\ \ r=32,\ \alpha=128;\quad \max_{A,B}\ \mathcal{J}_{\mathrm{GRPO}}\big(\pi_{W_0+\frac{\alpha}{r}BA}\big)\ \text{with verifiable math rewards};\ W_0 \text{ frozen},\ A,B \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per adapted projection } (r=32)
methods.locus: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen-1.5B; the paper's Table 5 lists "query, key, value, dense", while the released training recipes target q/k/v/o and gate/up/down projections
methods.structure: Plain rank-r LoRA factorization \Delta W = BA; the contribution is the objective: on-policy GRPO / Dr.GRPO reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards on a 1.5B distilled reasoning model, instead of SFT.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter is ordinary LoRA, so BA folds into W_0 after training.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (standard LoRA initialization), so RL starts exactly at the distilled base policy.
methods.key_idea: Low-rank RL on a tiny distilled model recovers most of the reasoning gain of full RL at a few dollars per run; the authors attribute this to 'rapid format adaptation': LoRA learns the structure/format that RL rewards while leaving base knowledge intact.
methods.results_note: Best Tina checkpoint reaches 43.33% Pass@1 on AIME24 (>20% reasoning improvement over the base) for about $9 of post-training and evaluation compute.

relations.note: Uses unmodified LoRA as the policy parameterization for RL.
TinyLoRA pushes the same 'RL needs very few parameters' thesis to ~13 trainable parameters.
QeRL is another recipe for cheap LoRA-based RL, adding NVFP4 quantization and noise.

corrections: hf_peft_config: added target_modules from the released recipes (e.g. recipes/.../train_model_open_rs3.yaml) and noted there is no dedicated tuner.
locus: paper Table 5 says attention-only, but the official recipes also adapt the MLP projections; both are now recorded.
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2504.15777 (Wang, 2025) confirmed; ICLR 2026 confirmed via mlanthology and OpenReview (P2OXYO3bEe). r=32, alpha=128, dropout=0.05, GRPO, $9 and 43.33% AIME24 confirmed from the paper. Uses the default PEFT LoraConfig (paper App. B.2).

methods.name: QeRL
methods.paper_title: QeRL: Beyond Efficiency -- Quantization-enhanced Reinforcement Learning for LLMs
methods.formula_latex: y = \mathrm{Dequant}(\tilde W_0)\,x + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}BAx,\ \ \mathrm{Dequant}(\tilde W)=S_{\mathrm{FP32}}\cdot(S_{\mathrm{E4M3}}\odot \tilde W)\ (\text{NVFP4, frozen});\ \ \text{AQN: } w_{\mathrm{noise}} = w_{\mathrm{RMSNorm}} + Z,\ Z\sim\mathcal{N}(0,\sigma_k^2 I),\ \sigma_k=\sigma_{\mathrm{start}}\big(\tfrac{\sigma_{\mathrm{end}}}{\sigma_{\mathrm{start}}}\big)^{\frac{k-1}{K-1}};\ A,B \text{ trained by GRPO/DAPO}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per adapted matrix } (r=32 \text{ default})
methods.locus: LoRA on the linear layers of an NVFP4-quantized LLM (Qwen2.5 3B-32B); exploration noise injected through RMSNorm gains
methods.structure: QLoRA-type composite: additive rank-r delta on a frozen 4-bit (NVFP4) base, plus a scheduled channel-wise Gaussian noise vector added to the RMSNorm scale. This is equivalent to row-wise multiplicative noise (Z/w + 1) on the following W_q, W_k, W_v (shared norm) and W_gate, W_up (shared norm).
methods.mergeable_reason: BA can be merged into the dequantized weights (giving up the NVFP4 format) or kept as a side adapter; the noise is used only during training.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0, but the starting policy is the NVFP4-quantized base, not the exact bf16 model. In stage 0 only the inherent quantization noise acts (sigma = 0); AQN then starts at sigma_start (1e-2 in the main text, range 5e-2 to 5e-4 in experiments) and decays exponentially over K stages.
methods.key_idea: In RL, quantization noise helps: it raises policy entropy and so aids exploration. QeRL schedules it with Adaptive Quantization Noise and combines it with fast NVFP4 rollouts and LoRA.
methods.results_note: First RL training of a 32B LLM on a single H100-80GB, >1.5x rollout speedup, and Qwen2.5-7B reaching 90.8% GSM8K / 77.4% MATH500, matching full-parameter RL.

relations.note: Frozen low-bit base + LoRA, here with NVFP4 and for RL rather than SFT.
Trainable part is standard LoRA.
Alternative low-cost LoRA-RL recipe.

corrections: identity_at_init: stage 0 uses only quantization noise (sigma=0) before AQN starts at sigma_start (Alg. 1).
structure: specified which matrices receive the AQN noise (q/k/v and gate/up, App. G).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2510.11696 (Huang, 2025) confirmed; ICLR 2026 confirmed (mlanthology). Dequant formula, AQN RMSNorm form, exponential schedule, rank 32 and 90.8 GSM8K / 77.4 MATH500 checked against Sec. 3 and App. G. No PEFT tuner (NVFP4 base is not supported by PEFT LoRA).

methods.name: PLoP
methods.paper_title: PLoP: Precise LoRA Placement for Efficient Finetuning of Large Models
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{NFN}(W,x)=\frac{\|W z_{\mathrm{in}}(x)\|}{\|W \tilde z_{\mathrm{in}}(x)\|},\ \tilde z_{\mathrm{in}}(x)\ \text{i.i.d. centered Gaussian, same dimension and norm as } z_{\mathrm{in}}(x);\ \ \mathrm{NFN}(W,\mathcal{D})=\tfrac{1}{|\mathcal{D}|}\sum_{x\in\mathcal{D}}\frac{\|W z_{\mathrm{in}}(x)\|^2}{\|W \tilde z_{\mathrm{in}}(x)\|^2},\ \ \mathrm{NFN}(T,\mathcal{D})=\tfrac{1}{|N_T|}\sum_{W\in T}\mathrm{NFN}(W,\mathcal{D});\ \ W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \text{ inserted only in the module types } T \text{ with the lowest } \mathrm{NFN}(T,\mathcal{D})
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per selected matrix; total depends on the selected module types}
methods.locus: data-dependent subset of module types (e.g. V, O, down-projection), chosen per model and dataset before training
methods.structure: A placement rule that chooses the support (set of module types) of an otherwise standard LoRA, scored by how aligned each frozen W_0 is with its real inputs relative to random inputs of the same norm.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapters placed are ordinary LoRA and merge as usual.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 as in LoRA; the placement is computed from the frozen model before training starts.
methods.key_idea: From infinite-width feature-learning analysis, modules whose weights are least aligned with the fine-tuning data (low normalized feature norm) gain most from adaptation, so LoRA should be placed there instead of a fixed attention or MLP default.
methods.results_note: SFT on MetaMathQA -> GSM8K with Qwen3-0.6B: PLoP (Down-Up-Value, r=76, 21.8M params) reaches 63.8%, vs 63.3% for MLP-only (r=64, 22.0M) and 58.6% for attention-only (r=64, 12.8M); also evaluated with GRPO on Qwen3-1.7B.

relations.note: Changes only where LoRA is inserted.
Gives a different placement prescription (data-driven NFN versus all layers / MLP-first).
Both allocate adaptation budget across modules, AdaLoRA during training, PLoP before training.

corrections: venue: arXiv -> ICLR 2026 (mlanthology /iclr/2026/hayou2026iclr-plop/).
formula_latex: the dataset-level score in PLoP Step 1 averages the SQUARED norm ratio; aggregation is a mean over modules of type T (Sec. 3).
results_note: the 63.8% vs 58.6% comparison is NOT at equal parameter count (21.8M vs 12.8M); the matched-budget comparison is MLP-only at 63.3% (Table 1).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2506.20629 (Hayou, 2025) confirmed; venue corrected to ICLR 2026. NFN definition and PLoP steps 1-3 checked against Sec. 3; Table 1 numbers re-read.

methods.name: LoRI
methods.paper_title: LoRI: Reducing Cross-Task Interference in Multi-Task Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + (B_t\odot M_t)\,A_t,\ \ A_t\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} \text{ frozen random (Kaiming-uniform)},\ B_t\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ trained},\ M_t=\mathbb{1}\big(|B_t|\ge\tau_t\big),\ \tau_t=\mathrm{Quantile}_s\big(\textstyle\bigcup_{\text{layers}}|B_t|\big);\ \ \text{merge: } W=W_0+\sum_t\alpha_t (B_t\odot M_t)A_t
methods.trainable_params: r\,d_{out} \text{ per adapted matrix (LoRI-D)};\ \ (1-s)\sum_{\text{adapted matrices}} r\,d_{out} \text{ in total (LoRI-S, global mask, } s=0.9\text{)}
methods.locus: any linear layer (attention and MLP projections of Llama-3-8B / Mistral-7B in the paper)
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through a fixed random r-dimensional projection of the input; only the up-projection is learned, and only on a sparse coordinate mask. Independent random A_t per task give nearly orthogonal row spaces, so merged adapters interfere little.
methods.mergeable_reason: Each task delta is a fixed matrix (B_t odot M_t)A_t, and multi-task merging is a weighted sum, all foldable into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B_t = 0 with A_t random (Kaiming-uniform) and frozen. Masks M_t come from a calibration run that trains B_t unmasked (A_t frozen); B_t is then reset to zero and retrained under the fixed mask.
methods.key_idea: LoRA's down-projection can be a frozen random map and its up-projection can be about 90% sparse. Random task-specific projections make adapters nearly orthogonal (easy merging), and sparse masks protect earlier adapters, such as a safety adapter, in continual learning.
methods.results_note: Up to 95% fewer trainable parameters than LoRA while matching or beating it, e.g. LoRI-D reaches 63.2% HumanEval pass@10 vs 50.8% for LoRA on Llama-3-8B.

relations.note: LoRA-FA also freezes a random A; LoRI adds task-specific sparse masks on B.
Restricts both factors of LoRA.
Both rely on frozen random projections to cut parameters.
Reduces merge interference by construction (orthogonal subspaces + sparsity) rather than post hoc.
Alternative fix for cross-task interference when merging LoRAs.

corrections: trainable_params: the LoRI-S mask is a single global (model-wise) quantile, so the (1-s) budget applies to the total, not to each matrix.
identity_at_init: clarified that B_t is reset to zero after mask calibration (Sec. 2.1).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2504.07448 (Zhang, 2025); COLM 2025 confirmed (arXiv comment + OpenReview). The paper writes Delta = A(B odot M) in row-vector convention; the entry's column form (B odot M)A matches. HumanEval 63.2 vs 50.8 confirmed. Reduces to LoRA-FA for a single task with zero sparsity (paper).

methods.name: SingLoRA
methods.paper_title: SingLoRA: Low Rank Adaptation Using a Single Matrix
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}\,u(t)\,A A^{\top},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},\ u(t)=\min(t/T,1)\ \ (d_{in}=d_{out}=d);\ \ \text{rectangular: } \Delta W=\tfrac{\alpha}{r}u(t)\,A_{[1:d_{out}]}A_{[1:d_{in}]}^{\top},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{\max(d_{in},d_{out})\times r};\ W_0 \text{ frozen},\ A \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: r\,\max(d_{in},d_{out})
methods.locus: any linear layer (attention projections in the LLM and Stable Diffusion experiments)
methods.structure: Gram-type update from a single factor: for square W_0, \Delta W = AA^\top is symmetric positive semidefinite of rank at most r; rectangular layers use a row-truncated copy of the same factor. The reparameterization symmetry shrinks from LoRA's GL(r) (B\mapsto BG, A\mapsto G^{-1}A) to O(r) (A\mapsto AQ).
methods.mergeable_reason: AA^T (or its truncated version) is a fixed matrix after training and adds to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Ramp u(0)=0 with Kaiming-initialized A, so the update is zero at step 0 and phased in over T steps (T = 1% of training steps in the main experiments, 10^3 steps for RoBERTa/GPT-2; robust for T from 0.5% to 8%).
methods.key_idea: Replacing LoRA's two factors by one matrix and its transpose removes the scale imbalance between factors. The authors prove stable feature learning at infinite width and transformation-invariance of standard optimizers, while halving parameters. For square layers the symmetric-PSD form restricts expressivity, which the paper argues the transformer architecture compensates for.
methods.results_note: Llama-7B on MNLI: 91.3% vs 89.1% (LoRA) and 90.2% (LoRA+) with about 60% of their parameters; DreamBooth DINO 0.151 vs 0.148 (DoRA) and 0.143 (LoRA).

relations.note: Same additive low-rank role with one factor instead of two.
LoRA+ fixes factor imbalance with separate learning rates; SingLoRA removes the second factor.
Both target transformation-invariant optimization of low-rank adapters.
Alternative route to scale-stable LoRA training.

corrections: identity_at_init: T is 1% of steps in the main experiments and 10^3 steps for the GLUE runs, not specifically "for LLMs" (App. A).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2507.05566 (Bensaid, 2025). Venue: ICLR 2026 DeLTa Workshop poster (OpenReview xjksemsy11); no main-track acceptance found. Formula W0 + (alpha/r) u(t) A A^T and the truncation rule for non-square layers (Sec. 4.4) confirmed. No public code (paper: "will be released").

methods.name: SHINE
methods.paper_title: SHINE: A Scalable In-Context Hypernetwork for Mapping Context to LoRA in a Single Pass
methods.formula_latex: \mathcal{M}=\mathrm{LLM}_{\theta_0+\Delta_{\mathrm{meta}}}\big([c;\,m_{1:M}]\big)\big|_{\text{last } M \text{ tokens of all } L \text{ layers}}\in\mathbb{R}^{L\times M\times H},\ \ \{(A_l,B_l)\}_{l}=\mathrm{M2P}_\psi(\mathcal{M}),\ \ W_l=W_{0,l}+B_lA_l;\ \theta_0 \text{ frozen},\ \Delta_{\mathrm{meta}},\,m,\,\psi \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: \text{meta-LoRA (rank 128) + } M=\lceil rD/H\rceil \text{ memory embeddings + 4-layer M2P Transformer (shared); generated adapter has rank } r=8
methods.locus: all linear layers of each backbone layer (Qwen3-8B; generated rank-8 LoRA); D is the summed input and output width of those linear layers
methods.structure: In-context hypernetwork: the frozen LLM itself (with a meta-LoRA and learnable memory tokens) encodes the context into an L x M memory grid, which an axial (row/column) attention Transformer maps jointly to every LoRA factor. The deployed modification is additive low-rank.
methods.mergeable_reason: Generated per context; it can be merged for a fixed context but is normally kept as a swappable adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity guarantee for the generated adapter; base weights are untouched.
methods.key_idea: Reuse the LLM as its own hypernetwork encoder so that context-to-LoRA generation scales with the backbone, producing an adapter for an arbitrary context in one pass, pretrained with reconstruction/completion objectives and then instruction-tuned on QA.
methods.results_note: About 0.3 s to generate an adapter in one forward pass. On SQuAD it beats test-time-training baselines such as SEAL (58.2) and PaST, and perplexity improves with backbone size, M2P depth, meta-LoRA rank and generated LoRA rank.

relations.note: Both are self-supervised context-to-adapter generators; SHINE generates all layers jointly.
Concurrent context-to-LoRA hypernetwork.
Extends the text-to-adapter hypernetwork idea to arbitrary contexts.
Amortized one-pass alternative to iterative test-time LoRA training.

corrections: locus: added the backbone (Qwen3-8B) and made clear all linear layers in each block are generated.
sources: replaced github.com/Yewei-Liu/SHINE (redirect) with the canonical github.com/MuLabPKU/SHINE given in the paper; added OpenReview.
results_note: added the reported 0.3 s generation time and the SEAL comparison figure (Table 3).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2602.06358 (Liu, 2026); ICML 2026 confirmed (OpenReview ZMexYcAibv). Meta-LoRA rank 128, generated rank 8, M = ceil(rD/H) = 148 memory tokens, 4-layer M2P with alternating row/column attention confirmed.

methods.name: GenerativeAdapter
methods.paper_title: Generative Adapter: Contextualizing Language Models in Parameters with A Single Forward Pass
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W_l = A_1\,\mathrm{norm}_r\big(A_2 H_{l-1}^{\top}H_{l-1} B_1\big)\,B_2,\ \ H_{l-1}^{\top}H_{l-1}=\textstyle\sum_{m=1}^{M} h_m h_m^{\top}\ (\text{context hidden states from block } l-1),\ \ \mathrm{norm}_r(S)=U_rV_r^{\top}\ (\text{rank-}r \text{ SVD } S\approx U_r\Sigma_rV_r^{\top},\ r=128);\ \ \text{streaming: } S_t\leftarrow S_{t-1}+A_2H_t^{\top}H_tB_1;\ A_1\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_r},A_2\in\mathbb{R}^{d_r\times d_h},B_1\in\mathbb{R}^{d_h\times d_r},B_2\in\mathbb{R}^{d_r\times d_{in}};\ \text{base LM frozen, generator trained}
methods.trainable_params: d_r(d_{in}+d_{out}+2d_h) \text{ generator parameters per adapted layer (about 500M total for 7B models, } d_r=1024\text{)}; \text{ generated adapter rank } 128 \text{ (about 32M parameters)}
methods.locus: attention output projections of every layer (Mistral-7B-Instruct, Llama2-7B-Chat)
methods.structure: Bilinear, linear-attention-like map from context hidden states to a parameter delta: the context enters only through its second-moment matrix \sum_m h_m h_m^\top, compressed into a d_r x d_r state that accumulates additively over streamed chunks, then SVD-normalized (singular values reset to 1).
methods.mergeable_reason: A generated delta can be added to W_o for a fixed context, but it is context-specific and regenerated per context.
methods.identity_at_init: Not identity by construction; the base LM is frozen and recovered by dropping the delta.
methods.key_idea: A lightweight generator, trained self-supervised (reconstruction + completion), turns any context into a parameter delta in one forward pass, giving test-time knowledge injection, in-context learning and personalization without fine-tuning or long prompts.
methods.results_note: StreamingQA F1 rises from 19.5 (SFT) to 31.5 for contexts up to 32K tokens; 44.9 average accuracy on 26 MetaICL tasks.

relations.note: Both generate adapters with a forward pass; GenerativeAdapter conditions on raw context rather than task descriptions.
Both put context into parameters; Cartridges trains per document.

corrections: formula_latex: SVD normalization is a rank-r truncated SVD (r=128), so the generated delta has rank 128; hidden states come from block l-1 (Eqs. 1-9).
trainable_params: re-derived the generator size from the four matrices.
relations: removed hyperformer builds-on; the paper does not cite HyperFormer or hypernetworks (lineage reaches HyperFormer via text-to-lora).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2411.05877 (Chen, 2024); ICLR 2025 poster confirmed (OpenReview bc3sUsS6ck, DBLP). Bilinear generator, streaming update, SVD normalization, attention output-projection placement, d_r=1024, r=128 and StreamingQA 19.5 -> 31.5 confirmed.

methods.name: GOAT
methods.full_name: Great LoRA Mixture-of-Experts (adaptive SVD priors + optimization alignment)
methods.paper_title: Make LoRA Great Again: Boosting LoRA with Adaptive Singular Values and Mixture-of-Experts Optimization Alignment
methods.formula_latex: h=(W_0-W_{\mathrm{res}})x+\sum_{i=1}^{E} w^{i}(x)\,s\,B^{i}A^{i}x,\ \ w(x)=\mathrm{softmax}\ \text{over the top-}k \text{ router logits } W_z^{\top}x \ (0 \text{ elsewhere}),\ \ B_0^{i}=\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{s\rho}}\,U_i\Sigma_i^{1/2},\ A_0^{i}=\sqrt{\tfrac{1}{s\rho}}\,\Sigma_i^{1/2}V_i^{\top},\ \ W_{\mathrm{res}}=\tfrac{s}{E}\sum_{i}B_0^{i}A_0^{i},\ \ s=\sqrt{3n\eta/r}
methods.trainable_params: E\cdot\tfrac{r}{E}(d_{in}+d_{out})+E\,d_{in}=r(d_{in}+d_{out})+E\,d_{in}\ \ (E=8,\ \text{top-}2)
methods.locus: linear layers of ViT-B/32, RoBERTa-large and LLaMA-2-7B (MoE-LoRA in place of a single LoRA)
methods.structure: Mixture of E rank-(r/E) LoRA experts with input-dependent top-k gating; expert i is initialized on the i-th contiguous segment of the SVD of W_0 (segments tile the whole spectrum: U_i\Sigma_iV_i^\top with start index (i-1)\min(d_{in},d_{out})/E), and a closed-form scale s aligns MoE-LoRA gradients with full fine-tuning of an upcycled MoE.
methods.mergeable_reason: Expert weights depend on the input through the router, so no single static matrix reproduces the layer.
methods.identity_at_init: The residual (s/E) sum_i B_0^i A_0^i is subtracted from W_0; the initial layer equals W_0 exactly only when routing weights are uniform (1/E), so identity holds approximately, not pointwise.
methods.key_idea: Give each LoRA expert a different SVD-derived starting subspace spread across the whole spectrum, and derive the scaling factor that makes MoE-LoRA optimization mimic full-parameter MoE fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: Across 25 datasets (image classification, GLUE, NLG, commonsense reasoning) GOAT beats LoRA and MoE-LoRA baselines and closes most of the gap to full fine-tuning.

relations.note: Uses SVD of W_0 to initialize adapters, distributed across experts and the whole spectrum.
Both align low-rank updates with full fine-tuning dynamics.
Mixture of adaptation modules.
Learned gating over several LoRA experts.
Main LoRA-MoE baseline in the paper; GOAT beats it on IC and commonsense reasoning.

corrections: formula_latex: renamed so that W_res is the subtracted constant (s/E) sum B_0 A_0, as in the paper (Eq. 15, Thm. 3.4); the previous entry used W_res for the residual base, which clashes with the paper.
relations: added hydralora (directly compared baseline).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2502.16894 (Fan, 2025); ICML 2025 confirmed. GOAT = "Great LoRA Mixture-of-Expert" (abstract). Segment init, 1/(s rho) scaling, W_res = (s/E) sum B0A0 and s = sqrt(3 n eta / r) confirmed; 8 experts with top-2 in the main setting.

methods.name: Core Space
methods.full_name: Core Space merging of low-rank adapters
methods.paper_title: Accurate and Efficient Low-Rank Model Merging in Core Space
methods.formula_latex: \big[A^{(1)};\dots;A^{(T)}\big]=U_A\Sigma_AV_A^{\top},\ \ \big[B^{(1)},\dots,B^{(T)}\big]=U_B\Sigma_BV_B^{\top},\ \ M^{(t)}=\big(U_B^{\top}B^{(t)}\big)\big(A^{(t)}V_A\big)\in\mathbb{R}^{Tr\times Tr},\ \ W=W_0+U_B\,\mathcal{M}\big(\{M^{(t)}\}_{t}\big)\,V_A^{\top}
methods.trainable_params: 0 \text{ (training-free merging)}
methods.locus: every LoRA-adapted layer (Llama-3-8B, ViT-B/32, ViT-L/14)
methods.structure: All rank-r task updates lie in the span of the union of their factor spaces; shared orthonormal bases of the stacked A's (row space) and concatenated B's (column space) map each update losslessly to a small Tr x Tr core matrix, where any merging operator acts before mapping back.
methods.mergeable_reason: The reconstructed merged update is a single static matrix added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free).
methods.key_idea: Merge LoRAs in their joint core space rather than at full size: the projection is provably lossless, aligns the tasks, and costs far less than full-matrix or KnOTS-style SVD merging.
methods.results_note: State-of-the-art merging accuracy on Llama-3-8B NLI and ViT-B/32 / ViT-L/14 vision benchmarks, with up to 600x faster merging than merging in full space or KnOTS space.

relations.note: Same alignment-before-merging idea, done in a lossless reduced space.
Off-the-shelf merging operators are applied inside the core space.

corrections: results_note: the 600x speed-up is relative to full-space or KnOTS-space merging (Sec. 5).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2509.17786 (Panariello, 2025); NeurIPS 2025 confirmed (arXiv comment, OpenReview y1z7SAS8q8). Reference bases from SVD of stacked A and B, core matrix M^(t) = (U_B^T B)(A V_A) in R^{Tr x Tr} and zero alignment error confirmed (Alg. 1).

methods.name: K-LoRA
methods.paper_title: K-LoRA: Unlocking Training-Free Fusion of Any Subject and Style LoRAs
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W^{l}(t)=\begin{cases}\Delta W_c^{l} & \text{if } S_c^{l}\ \ge\ \gamma\,\mathcal{S}(t)\,S_s^{l}\\ \Delta W_s^{l} & \text{otherwise}\end{cases},\ \ S_\bullet^{l}=\sum_{i\in\mathrm{TopK}(|\Delta W_\bullet^{l}|)}|\Delta W_\bullet^{l}|_i,\ K=r_cr_s,\ \ \mathcal{S}(t)=\alpha\tfrac{t_{\mathrm{now}}}{t_{\mathrm{all}}}+\beta,\ \ \gamma=\frac{\sum_l\sum_i|\Delta W_c^{l}|_i}{\sum_l\sum_j|\Delta W_s^{l}|_j}
methods.trainable_params: 0 \text{ (training-free)}
methods.locus: attention-layer LoRA weights of SDXL and FLUX diffusion models
methods.structure: Layer-wise, timestep-dependent hard selection between two pretrained LoRA deltas (content vs style), decided by comparing their Top-K l1 mass with a time-ramped scale (alpha=1.5, beta=0.5): content dominates early denoising steps, style later ones.
methods.mergeable_reason: At each timestep the selected LoRA per layer can be merged, but the selection changes over timesteps, so no single static merged weight reproduces it.
methods.identity_at_init: Not applicable (training-free; no new parameters).
methods.key_idea: Only the few largest LoRA entries matter, and early denoising steps set content while later ones set style; so at each attention layer use whichever LoRA has more Top-K mass, rescaled over time, with no training.
methods.results_note: Highest subject similarity among compared methods (CLIP score 69.4% vs 64.4% ZipLoRA and 63.8% B-LoRA; DINO 46.9% vs 35.7%), with style similarity 58.7% (ZipLoRA 60.4%, B-LoRA 58.0%); preferred in user studies.

relations.note: Operates on community LoRAs.
Different training-free answer to combining LoRAs (selection vs aligned merging).
Main baseline: ZipLoRA learns merge coefficients, whereas K-LoRA selects per layer without training.

corrections: results_note: the 69.4% figure is SUBJECT similarity; on style similarity K-LoRA trails ZipLoRA (58.7 vs 60.4), so "outperforms" overall was inaccurate (Table 1).
relations: added ziplora (directly compared baseline).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2502.18461 (Ouyang, 2025); CVPR 2025 confirmed (arXiv comment, DBLP). The Top-K l1 rule with K = r_c r_s, gamma and alpha=1.5, beta=0.5 are from Eqs. 1-8. The paper's Algorithm 1 writes scale = alpha + beta t/T, which is inconsistent with Eq. 7 (alpha t/T + beta); the entry follows Eq. 7.

methods.name: OminiControl
methods.full_name: Minimal and Universal Control for Diffusion Transformer
methods.paper_title: OminiControl: Minimal and Universal Control for Diffusion Transformer
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{MMA}\big([X;C_T;C_I]\big)=\mathrm{softmax}\Big(\tfrac{QK^{\top}}{\sqrt d}+B(\gamma)\Big)V,\ \ C_I=\mathrm{VAE}(\text{condition image}),\ \ B(\gamma)=\log\gamma \text{ on the } X\leftrightarrow C_I \text{ blocks, } 0 \text{ elsewhere};\ \ \text{per token } z:\ (W_0+\mathbb{1}[z\in C_I]\,BA)\,z \text{ (rank-4 LoRA, scale 0 on non-condition tokens)};\ W_0,\ \mathrm{VAE} \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 0.1\% \text{ of FLUX.1 } (\approx 14.5\mathrm{M} \text{ LoRA parameters for 12B})
methods.locus: all FLUX.1 DiT blocks (attention projections and norms matter most) plus condition-image tokens appended to the token sequence
methods.structure: Input augmentation plus a token-restricted low-rank update: VAE-encoded condition tokens are concatenated into the multimodal attention sequence (shared RoPE positions for spatially aligned tasks, shifted positions for subject-driven tasks). A rank-4 LoRA in the shared DiT blocks acts only on condition tokens, and condition strength is a log-gamma attention-bias block.
methods.mergeable_reason: The LoRA is applied only to condition tokens, so merging it into the shared weights would change text and image tokens; inference must also process the extra condition tokens.
methods.identity_at_init: LoRA uses B = 0 and is off on text and noise tokens, but appending condition tokens changes attention outputs from the start; gamma = 0 (bias of minus infinity) removes the condition's influence.
methods.key_idea: A DiT can serve as its own condition encoder: pass the condition image through the same VAE and transformer as extra tokens and train only a tiny LoRA, giving one mechanism for both spatial and subject-driven control.
methods.results_note: With about 0.1% extra parameters on FLUX.1 it outperforms ControlNet / T2I-Adapter on spatially aligned control and IP-Adapter on subject-driven generation; releases the Subjects200K dataset.

relations.note: Replaces ControlNet's trainable encoder copy with token concatenation + LoRA.
Alternative lightweight conditioning of diffusion models.
Subject/image-prompt conditioning without a separate image encoder.
The only trainable weights are LoRA.

corrections: formula_latex: the paper sets the LoRA scale to 0 on non-condition tokens (Sec. 4, implementation details), so the LoRA is token-restricted to condition tokens rather than applied to the whole sequence.
structure: LoRA acts only on condition tokens (LoRA scale 0 for text/noise tokens).
mergeable_reason: rewritten to reflect token-restricted LoRA.
identity_at_init: noted that the LoRA is off on non-condition tokens.
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2411.15098 (Tan, 2024); ICCV 2025 confirmed (arXiv comment). Attention-bias formula, rank 4, 14.5M parameters (~0.1% of 12B FLUX.1) and the LoRA scale of 0 on non-condition tokens are confirmed from the current (v6) text.

methods.name: EasyControl
methods.paper_title: EasyControl: Adding Efficient and Flexible Control for Diffusion Transformer
methods.formula_latex: Q_c'=Q_c+B_QA_QZ_c,\ \ K_c'=K_c+B_KA_KZ_c,\ \ V_c'=V_c+B_VA_VZ_c;\ \ Q,K,V \text{ of text and noise tokens computed with frozen } W_0;\ \ \mathrm{Attn}\big([Z_t;Z_n;Z_{c_1};\dots]\big) \text{ under a causal mutual-attention mask}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 15\mathrm{M} \text{ per condition (FLUX.1-dev): } 3r(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per block for the condition branch}
methods.locus: Q/K/V projections applied only to condition-image tokens in the FLUX.1-dev DiT
methods.structure: Token-restricted LoRA: the low-rank delta acts only on condition tokens, so the map on text and noise tokens is exactly W_0; conditions interact with generation only through masked attention (separate conditions do not attend to each other), and condition K/V are computed once and cached across denoising steps.
methods.mergeable_reason: The LoRA applies only to condition tokens, so folding it into shared weights would alter text/noise tokens; inference also processes extra condition tokens.
methods.identity_at_init: Condition-branch LoRA starts at B = 0, but the frozen base still attends to condition tokens, so outputs change once a condition is added.
methods.key_idea: Keep the control signal in its own LoRA-adapted token branch so that conditions are plug-and-play, compose zero-shot across condition types, stay compatible with community style LoRAs, and can be KV-cached.
methods.results_note: About 15M parameters per condition. Combining the position-aware training paradigm (resolution-normalized conditions) with KV caching cuts 1024x1024 / 25-step inference time by 58% for a single condition (16.3 s) and 75% for two conditions (18.3 s), relative to the variant without both; KV caching alone gives -36% / -50%.

relations.note: Same token-concatenation conditioning on FLUX with condition-token LoRA. EasyControl adds a causal (mutual) attention mask so condition K/V can be cached and several conditions composed; it compares directly with OminiControl.
Lightweight alternative for spatial control.
Structural analogue in LLMs: aLoRA also applies its adapter to only some tokens so the base computation stays intact and cacheable.

corrections: results_note: the 58%/75% reductions come from PATP + KV cache together, not KV caching alone (Table 1).
relations[ominicontrol]: note corrected, since OminiControl already restricts its LoRA to condition tokens; the difference is the causal mask, KV cache and multi-condition composition.
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2503.07027 (Zhang, 2025); ICCV 2025 confirmed (mlanthology, pp. 19513-19524). Condition-branch-only QKV LoRA (Eqs. 2-4), causal conditional/mutual attention masks and 15M parameters per condition confirmed.

methods.name: ICEdit
methods.paper_title: In-Context Edit: Enabling Instructional Image Editing with In-Context Generation in Large Scale Diffusion Transformer
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{Out}(x)=W_0x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\sum_{i=1}^{N}G(x)_i\,B_iA_ix \ \text{(attention output projection)},\ \ G(x)=\mathrm{softmax}\big(\mathrm{TopK}(g(x),k)\big),\ N=4,\ r=\alpha=32,\ k=1;\ \ \text{other DiT modules: standard LoRA } W_0+BA \ (r=\alpha=32);\ \ \text{input: diptych [source | masked target] with the prompt ``A diptych with two side-by-side images of the same scene. On the right, the scene is exactly the same as on the left but \{instruction\}''}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 0.2\mathrm{B} \text{ (Table 1; about 1.7\% of the 12B FLUX.1 Fill, the abstract rounds to }\sim 1\%\text{): LoRA-MoE experts, router and standard LoRAs}
methods.locus: FLUX.1 Fill (inpainting DiT): LoRA-MoE in the output projection of the multimodal attention blocks, standard LoRA in the other modules
methods.structure: In-context input augmentation (an edit is inpainting the right half of a diptych conditioned on the left half) combined with a top-1 routed mixture of four rank-32 LoRA experts.
methods.mergeable_reason: Routing over experts is input-dependent and the diptych doubles the image sequence at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Experts presumably start at B_i = 0 (standard LoRA initialization; not stated). The training-free diptych prompt already produces edits, which the LoRA-MoE then sharpens.
methods.key_idea: Instruction-based editing can be posed as in-context inpainting of a diptych in a large DiT. A small LoRA-MoE trained on 50K pairs (about 0.1% of prior methods' data) is enough, and VLM-guided early filtering of noise seeds improves results at inference.
methods.results_note: Strong results on Emu Edit (CLIP-I 0.907, DINO 0.866) and MagicBrush with about 0.1% of the training data of prior methods.

relations.note: Both use mixtures of LoRA experts with top-k routing.
Both reuse the DiT's own attention over concatenated image tokens for conditioning.
Experts are LoRA modules.
