methods.name: BEFT
methods.paper_title: BEFT: Bias-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Language Models in Low-Data Regimes
methods.formula_latex: h = W_v x + b_v + \Delta b_v,\ \ \Delta b_v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}} \text{ trained, all weights frozen};\ \ a(V+\mathbf{1}b_v^\top)=aV+\mathbf{1}b_v^\top \text{ (rows of } a \text{ sum to 1)}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out} \text{ per value projection } (\approx 0.01\% \text{ of parameters})
methods.locus: bias of the value projection W_v in every attention block (bias added, zero-initialized, for bias-free LLMs)
methods.structure: additive shift of the value-projection output; because attention rows sum to one, the shift passes straight to the attention output
methods.mergeable_reason: Delta b_v adds to an existing value-projection bias after training. PEFT raises an error when merging into a bias-free layer (for example LLaMA-style projections), so merging is only possible when the base layer has a bias.
methods.identity_at_init: PEFT adds a separate zero-initialized Delta b_v (init_weights=True), so the function is unchanged at init.
methods.key_idea: Among q/k/v biases, fine-tuning only the value bias b_v gives the best accuracy per parameter in low-data regimes.
methods.results_note: Paper reports b_v fine-tuning consistently beating b_q and b_k fine-tuning across encoder- and decoder-only LLMs up to 6.7B, with about 9x fewer parameters than tuning all biases.

relations.note: Restricts BitFit to a single bias term (value projection).
Both are vector-sized interventions on attention; IA3 scales, BEFT shifts.
The paper also applies LoRA/VeRA/DoRA-style reparameterizations to the bias terms.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv id/title/first author/year checked by batch arXiv API query; arXiv 2509.15974; ACL 2026 main (long) confirmed in the ACL Anthology (2026.acl-long.1799) and the PDF header. Formula and value-bias-only scope match the paper; PEFT beft/layer.py checked.
corrections: mergeable_reason: PEFT refuses to merge into bias-free layers (it raises an error); it does not create a new bias as the old text said
identity_at_init: PEFT trains a separate zero-initialized delta, not the pretrained bias
trainable_params: the count is the value projection's output width d_v, which is smaller than d under grouped-query attention (e.g. LLaMA-3), so dL was replaced by d_v L.
mergeable_reason: added the paper's equivalence Delta b_v ~ output bias W_o Delta b_v, which is why folding still needs a bias somewhere.

methods.name: BOFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Orthogonal Finetuning via Butterfly Factorization
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 R(m,b)^{\top},\quad R(m,b)=\prod_{i=1}^{m}\tilde{B}^{b}_{(d_{in},i)},\ \big(\tilde{B}^{b}_{(d_{in},i)}\big)^{\top}\tilde{B}^{b}_{(d_{in},i)}=I,\ \text{each factor a permuted block-diagonal matrix of } b\times b \text{ Cayley-parameterized orthogonal blocks};\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \tfrac{1}{2}\,m\,(b-1)\,d_{in}\quad(\mathcal{O}(d_{in}\log d_{in})\ \text{for } b=2,\ m=\log_2 d_{in})
methods.locus: any linear / conv layer (attention and MLP of ViTs, LLMs, SAM, Stable Diffusion); acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of a product of m sparse butterfly factors, each a permutation conjugate of the block-diagonal subgroup O(b)^{d/b}; the product is a dense orthogonal matrix. The paper frames this as information transmission on a butterfly grid graph (a Cooley-Tukey style factorization of an O(d) element).
methods.mergeable_reason: The product R(m,b) is a fixed orthogonal matrix after training, so W_0 R(m,b)^T can be precomputed.
methods.identity_at_init: All skew-symmetric generators start at 0, so every butterfly factor is the identity and R = I.
methods.key_idea: Build a dense orthogonal matrix as a product of sparse butterfly-structured orthogonal factors. OFT then gets dense rotations from O(d log d) parameters. Block-diagonal OFT is the m=1 case.
methods.results_note: Reports higher scores than LoRA and OFT on GLUE (DeBERTaV3), the best VTAB-1K average in its table (77.9% for BOFT m=2, b=8 with DINOv2-large), better Llama-2-7B MMLU and math (GSM8K/MATH) results, HQ-SAM-level segmentation with 3% of its parameters, and better controllable and subject-driven Stable Diffusion generation.

relations.note: BOFT(1,b) is block-diagonal OFT; BOFT(1,d) is full OFT
both build O(d) elements from log-depth sparse factors; GOFT uses one Givens angle per pair and fewer pairs per layer
multiplicative sparse factorization in place of low-rank addition
Alternative structured parameterization of an orthogonal multiplicative update.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2311.06243 (Liu, 2023) matches; ICLR 2024 confirmed (arXiv comment, ICLR 2024 proceedings). Parameter count (1/2)(b-1)dm, BOFT(1,b)=block-diagonal OFT and identity init checked in Sec. 4 of the PDF; BOFTConfig exists in HF PEFT.
corrections: formula: paper's forward pass is z=(R(m,b) W^0)^T x, i.e. W = W_0 R(m,b)^T in the h=Wx convention (mergeable_reason updated to match)
results_note: the LLM experiments use Llama-2-7B, not LLaMA-7B; added the VTAB-1K configuration (m=2, b=8, DINOv2-large)

methods.name: C3A
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Circular Convolution
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Delta W,\quad \Delta W = \big[\,\mathcal{C}(w_{ij})\,\big]_{i\le d_{out}/b,\ j\le d_{in}/b},\ \mathcal{C}(w)\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b}\ \text{circulant with first row } w\in\mathbb{R}^{b}\ (\text{trained});\ \mathcal{C}(w) = F\,\mathrm{diag}\big(\tfrac{1}{b}Fw\big)F^{-1}\ (\text{paper's convention}),\ \text{so } \Delta W x \text{ is computed blockwise with FFTs};\ \text{HF PEFT additionally divides } \Delta W \text{ by } d_{in}
methods.trainable_params: \tfrac{d_{in}\,d_{out}}{b}
methods.locus: any linear layer whose dimensions are divisible by the block size b (paper: RoBERTa, LLaMA-3-8B, ViT)
methods.structure: block-circulant update: each b x b block is a circulant matrix (simultaneously diagonalised by the DFT), so rank can reach min(d_{in}, d_{out}) independently of the parameter count
methods.mergeable_reason: The block-circulant matrix can be materialised and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: HF default initialises the kernels with xavier_uniform (non-zero, so not an exact identity); init_weights=True sets them to zero (no-op)
methods.key_idea: Use circular convolution (a circulant matrix) as the update: rank is decoupled from parameter count, and FFTs make forward and backward passes fast and memory-light; block-circulant structure handles non-square weights and tunes the budget.
methods.results_note: Consistently outperforms LoRA and its variants across fine-tuning tasks (e.g. on LLaMA-3-8B) while being efficient in compute and memory.

relations.note: both use the DFT; C3A makes Delta W DFT-diagonalisable rather than sparse in the 2-D spectrum
high-rank update with LoRA-like efficiency
positioned as more efficient than random-projection methods

methods.name: Cartridges
methods.paper_title: Cartridges: Lightweight and general-purpose long context representations via self-study
methods.formula_latex: \forall l:\ K_l\leftarrow[Z_k^{(l)};K_l],\ V_l\leftarrow[Z_v^{(l)};V_l],\ Z_k^{(l)},Z_v^{(l)}\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times d};\ \ \min_Z\sum_{(x,\tilde c)}\sum_i D_{KL}\big(F(\cdot\mid\tilde c\oplus x_{:i})\,\|\,F_Z(\cdot\mid x_{:i})\big)
methods.trainable_params: 2L\,(p-p_f)\,d_{kv} \ \ (p=\text{num\_virtual\_tokens},\ p_f=\text{num\_frozen\_tokens}=1 \text{ by default},\ d_{kv}=\text{per-layer key/value width})
methods.locus: keys/values at every layer (a directly parameterized KV-cache prefix)
methods.structure: learned key/value vectors prepended at every layer, trained directly (no MLP reparameterization) by context distillation on synthetic self-study conversations about a corpus
methods.mergeable_reason: The cartridge is extra KV state attended by the model, not a weight change.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an identity. The paper recommends initializing Z from the prefill KV cache of the first p corpus tokens (PEFT: initialize_kv_prefix_from_text / initialize_kv_prefix_from_past_key_values). PEFT get_peft_model alone gives random N(0,1) init. The first num_frozen_tokens (default 1) are frozen as an attention sink.
methods.key_idea: Compress a long corpus offline into a small trainable KV cache via self-study distillation, so it can replace in-context documents at inference.
methods.results_note: Paper reports matching ICL quality with 38.6x less memory and 26.4x higher throughput, and extending effective context to 484k tokens.

relations.note: Same serving mechanism (past_key_values), but the KV prefix itself is the parameter and is distilled from a corpus.
Self-described simplified prefix-tuning (direct KV parameterization); new objective and initialization.
The paper finds KV-cache parameterization beats a LoRA parameterization for this use.
Transformer counterpart of learning the recurrence's initial state.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv id/title/first author/year checked by batch arXiv API query; ICLR 2026 confirmed in the ICLR 2026 accepted-paper list (poster). PEFT CartridgeConfig checked: KV prefix trained directly, num_frozen_tokens default 1.
corrections: trainable_params: made the frozen-token subtraction and the KV width explicit (PEFT stores num_frozen_tokens rows as non-trainable)
identity_at_init: PEFT default init is random N(0,1); corpus-prefill init needs a separate PEFT helper
trainable_params: noted the frozen attention-sink token (HF num_frozen_tokens=1 default)

methods.name: CPT
methods.paper_title: Context-aware Prompt Tuning: Advancing In-Context Learning with Adversarial Methods
methods.formula_latex: X_{ctx}=[T_i(x_i),S_{intra},T_o(y_i),S_{inter}]_{i=1}^{N};\ E\leftarrow\Pi_{\|E-E_0\|_2\le\epsilon}\big(E-\eta\nabla_E\mathcal{L}\big);\ \mathcal{L}=\sum_{k=1}^{N}\gamma^{N+1-k}\,\mathrm{CE}(\hat t_O^{(k)},t_O^{(k)})+\mathrm{CE}(\hat t_O^{(N+1)},t_O^{(N+1)})
methods.trainable_params: \ell\,d \ \ (\ell=\text{number of context input/format tokens optimized; label tokens frozen})
methods.locus: input embedding sequence (embeddings of the in-context demonstrations)
methods.structure: soft prompt initialized from real few-shot demonstrations; per-token embedding changes projected onto an L2 ball (projected gradient descent) with a recency-decayed context loss
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimized context tokens are extra inputs, not weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Not a no-op relative to the bare query: at init it equals ordinary in-context learning with the given demonstrations.
methods.key_idea: Treat the in-context demonstrations themselves as trainable soft prompts, but keep them within an epsilon-ball of the real tokens and down-weight early examples to counter recency bias.
methods.results_note: Paper reports gains over LoRA, prompt tuning, IPT and ICL on SST-2, AG News, DBpedia and TREC in 2/4/6-shot settings with BLOOM-1.7B, GPT-J-6B and Llama-3-8B.

relations.note: Soft prompt over demonstration tokens with projected (adversarial-style) updates.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv id/title/first author/year checked by batch arXiv API query; arXiv only (not found in ICLR/ICML/NeurIPS 2024-2026 lists). Per-token epsilon-ball projection and gamma^(N+1-k) decay match the paper (Sec. on loss weighting) and PEFT CPTConfig (opt_projection_epsilon, opt_loss_decay_factor).
corrections: relations: removed 'warp' (CPT does not cite WARP; its adversarial inspiration is Madry-style PGD attacks, so 'builds-on WARP' was unjustified)

methods.name: DEFT
methods.paper_title: DEFT: Decompositional Efficient Fine-Tuning for Text-to-Image Models
methods.formula_latex: W=(I-QQ^\top)W_0+QR,\ \ Q=\mathrm{qr}(P),\ P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ \ \text{(PEFT default 'relu'): } W=(I-P\,\mathrm{relu}(P)^\top)W_0+PR
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{out}+d_{in})
methods.locus: Linear / Conv1D layers (mainly text-to-image diffusion transformers/UNets)
methods.structure: rank-r update that removes an r-dimensional output subspace of W_0 and injects new content into it: \Delta W = Q(R - Q^\top W_0)
methods.mergeable_reason: The update equals a low-rank additive delta Q(R - Q^T W_0) that can be merged into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: PEFT (init_weights=True) draws P ~ N(0, 0.02^2) and sets R so that the injection exactly cancels the removal term, so W = W_0 at init.
methods.key_idea: Split adaptation into 'forget a subspace' (projection) and 'write new content there' (low-rank injection) to personalize while preserving the base model's instruction-following/editability.
methods.results_note: Paper reports DreamBench Plus CLIP-T 0.361 on SDXL vs 0.341 for LoRA and 0.354 for PaRa.

relations.note: Dropping the injection term QR gives PaRa (DeftConfig(para=True)).
Same rank-r parameter budget, different (subspace-replacing) structure.
the injection is a rank-r additive term

methods.verification_notes: arXiv id/title/first author/year checked by batch arXiv API query; NeurIPS 2025 confirmed. Paper Eq. 2: W_reduce = W_0 - P P^T W_0 + P R with P orthonormal (QR); the paper also discusses a ReLU(P)ReLU(P)^T variant. PEFT default decomposition_method="relu" uses P relu(P)^T, as the formula states.
corrections: identity_at_init: dropped the unverified claim that 'the paper initializes P at zero' (Q=qr(0) would be undefined)
formula: the paper's ReLU variant is ReLU(P)ReLU(P)^T; P relu(P)^T is HF PEFT's default 'relu' projector, so both are now attributed separately
hf_peft_config: noted the decomposition_method option of DeftConfig

methods.name: PaRa
methods.paper_title: PaRa: Personalizing Text-to-Image Diffusion via Parameter Rank Reduction
methods.formula_latex: W=(I-QQ^\top)W_0,\ \ Q=\mathrm{qr}(B),\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: r\,d_{out}
methods.locus: attention/linear layers of text-to-image diffusion models
methods.structure: left-multiplication of W_0 by an orthogonal projector of corank r, shrinking the output space of the layer (rank reduction)
methods.mergeable_reason: (I - QQ^T) W_0 is a single dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: Not an identity: PEFT notes PaRa cannot be a no-op at initialization since only the projection is trained.
methods.key_idea: Personalization works by reducing the rank of generation: projecting out a few output directions narrows the model's output space toward the target concept.
methods.results_note: Paper reports about 2x fewer parameters than LoRA and 82-97% human preference over LoRA across tested concepts.

relations.note: DEFT without the injection term.
Subtractive (rank-reducing) instead of additive low-rank adaptation.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv id/title/first author/year checked by batch arXiv API query; ICLR 2025 confirmed (ICLR 2025 list, DBLP via Semantic Scholar). PEFT implements PaRa as pure subspace removal (delta = -P_proj W) inside DeftConfig.
corrections: hf_peft_config: the paper's projector is QR-orthogonal; PEFT's default decomposition_method='relu' would give the non-orthogonal P relu(P)^T
hf_peft_config: DeftConfig defaults to decomposition_method='relu' (non-orthogonal projector); PaRa's QR projector needs decomposition_method='qr'
identity_at_init: added the paper's zero initialization of B and why it still does not give the identity
results_note: human preference over LoRA is 91.18-97.13% across the five single-subject cases (Table 3), not 96-97%; removed the unverified comparison with SVDiff

methods.name: DeLoRA
methods.paper_title: DeLoRA: Decoupling Angles and Strength in Low-rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+\frac{\lambda\|W_0\|}{r}\,B\,\Xi\,A,\ \ \Xi=\mathrm{diag}\Big(\tfrac{1}{\|b_i\|\,\|a_i\|}\Big),\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ \lambda \text{ trainable}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+1
methods.locus: nn.Linear layers only (PEFT)
methods.structure: sum of r unit-Frobenius rank-1 terms with a learnable global strength, so \|\Delta W\|_F\le\lambda\|W_0\| (a Frobenius-ball boundary)
methods.mergeable_reason: The normalized low-rank update is a fixed dense matrix after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Paper: subtract a frozen copy of the initial update from W_0; PEFT default: B = 0 (A Kaiming) with lambda initialized to delora_lambda.
methods.key_idea: Normalize the low-rank directions and learn their strength separately, bounding how far the weights can drift and making training robust to learning rate and length.
methods.results_note: Paper reports GLUE avg 85.6 vs 84.7 for LoRA, parity with LoRA/DoRA on subject-driven generation, and better robustness to learning rate and extended training.

relations.note: Both decouple angle and strength. The paper contrasts itself with DoRA (it normalizes the update, DoRA normalizes the full weight); it does not build on DoRA.

The paper derives DeLoRA as an evolution of ETHER that keeps its bounded, normalized update but adds rank r and a learnable strength. It is not a strict generalization (ETHER is a multiplicative reflection).
derived from ETHER+: its fixed distance bound becomes a learnable bound and the rank becomes arbitrary
normalized LoRA factors with a learnable norm bound

methods.verification_notes: arXiv id/title/first author/year checked by batch arXiv API query; ICLR 2025 confirmed. Formula matches paper Eq. 8 (lambda ||W|| / r * B Xi A). PEFT computes ||W_0|| column-wise (per input feature) and clamps the factor norms at 1e-4, so B = 0 init is allowed.
corrections: relations: 'generalizes -> ether' changed to 'builds-on -> ether' ("generalizes" overstated; the paper frames DeLoRA as built from ETHER)
relations: 'builds-on -> dora' changed to 'competes-with -> dora' (the paper positions DoRA as a competitor, not a basis)

formula: the paper writes the scale as lambda*||W||/r; both the official code (Wnorm = weight.norm(dim=0)) and HF PEFT (delora_w_norm, 'per-input channel') multiply column j of the update by the norm of the j-th input column of W_0, so the formula now shows that, with the paper's form kept as a note
identity_at_init: added how the official code realizes the subtract-a-copy initialization

methods.name: FourierFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Discrete Fourier Transform
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=\alpha\,\mathrm{Re}\big(\mathcal{F}^{-1}_{2D}(F)\big),\ F\in\mathbb{C}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}} \text{ zero except at } n \text{ fixed random frequency locations (shared across layers) holding trainable } c\in\mathbb{R}^{n}
methods.trainable_params: n \ \ (n=\text{n\_frequency})
methods.locus: any linear layer (typically W_q, W_v)
methods.structure: \Delta W is the real part of the inverse 2D DFT of a sparse spectral matrix with n learnable coefficients
methods.mergeable_reason: The spatial-domain Delta W can be computed once and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: PEFT default init_weights=False draws coefficients from N(0,1), so it is NOT an exact identity; init_weights=True zero-initializes for a no-op.
methods.key_idea: Weight updates are compressible in the frequency domain, so learn only a handful of spectral coefficients.
methods.results_note: Paper reports outperforming LoRA on LLaMA2-7B instruction tuning with 0.064M trainable parameters versus LoRA's 33.5M.

relations.note: Both are Fourier-domain parameterizations of Delta W.
Same sparse-transform-coefficient idea with a wavelet instead of Fourier basis.
replaces the low-rank structure with a sparse spectral one
LoCA analyses FourierFT's random-location iDFT and moves to learned locations with iDCT
Hartley transform with energy-based frequency selection

methods.verification_notes: arXiv id/title/first author/year checked by batch arXiv API query; ICML 2024 confirmed. Delta W = scaling * Re(ifft2(F)) with n random locations fixed by random_loc_seed. PEFT init_weights defaults to False, so coefficients start as N(0,1).

methods.name: FRoD
methods.full_name: Full-Rank Efficient Fine-Tuning with Rotational Degrees
methods.paper_title: FRoD: Full-Rank Efficient Fine-Tuning with Rotational Degrees for Fast Convergence

methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+W_0\odot(BA)=W_0\odot(\mathbf{1}\mathbf{1}^{\top}+BA),\quad B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ B,A\ \text{trained}

methods.name: LoHa

methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \gamma\,(B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2),\quad B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ (k=1,2),\ \gamma=\alpha/r;\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_1,A_2,B_1,B_2\ \text{trained}

methods.structure: Hadamard (entrywise) product of two rank-r matrices; \mathrm{rank}(\Delta W)\le r^2 (FedPara Prop. 1) at the parameter cost of a rank-2r LoRA. Equivalently (B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top}: a rank-r^2 factorization through row-wise Khatri-Rao products. Conv kernels can use a Tucker-style core variant (FedPara Prop. 3, use_effective_conv2d).

methods.structure: block-diagonal orthogonal R\in O(d_{in}) (Cayley-parameterized) multiplying W_0, preserving hyperspherical energy (pairwise angles between neurons)

methods.identity_at_init: Q = 0, so R = I.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tune by rotating neurons rather than adding to them, which provably preserves the pairwise angular structure of pretrained weights.

methods.name: OFTv2
methods.full_name: Orthogonal Finetuning v2 (input-centric OFT with Cayley-Neumann parameterization; QOFT for quantized models)
methods.paper_title: Orthogonal Finetuning Made Scalable
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0\,(R^{\top}x),\quad R=\operatorname{diag}(R_1,\dots,R_r),\ R_i=(I+Q_i)\Big(I+\sum_{k=1}^{K}Q_i^{k}\Big)\approx(I+Q_i)(I-Q_i)^{-1},\ Q_i=-Q_i^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times b};\ \text{QOFT: } h=\mathrm{Dequant}(W_q)\,(R^{\top}x);\ W_0 \text{ (or } W_q) \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \tfrac{d_{in}(b-1)}{2},\ b=d_{in}/r
methods.locus: any linear layer (input activations are rotated before the frozen matmul); works on top of quantized base weights
methods.structure: the same block-diagonal (now only approximately) orthogonal action as OFT, evaluated as an action on the input vector x (two matrix-vector products, O(nd + d^2)) instead of on W_0 (matrix-matrix, O(nd^2)). The truncated Neumann series makes the Cayley map only approximately orthogonal.
methods.mergeable_reason: For a full-precision base, R can be folded into the weight (W_0 R^T); for QOFT, merging requires dequantizing and re-quantizing the merged weight.
methods.identity_at_init: Q = 0 gives R = I.
methods.key_idea: Rotate the input instead of the weight, which cuts OFT's cost from cubic to quadratic. Replace the matrix inverse in the Cayley transform with a truncated Neumann series. Because R acts on activations, the method runs on any quantized backbone (QOFT).
methods.results_note: Reports up to 10x faster training and 3x lower GPU memory than the original OFT, and better results than QLoRA when fine-tuning quantized Qwen2.5 models (0.5B-72B) for math reasoning; also applied to Stable Diffusion 3.5.

relations.note: same group action; input-centric evaluation and Cayley-Neumann approximation
QOFT targets the same quantized-base setting as QLoRA

methods.name: OSF
methods.full_name: Orthogonal Subspace Fine-tuning (adaptive-SVD constrained full fine-tuning)
methods.paper_title: Sculpting Subspaces: Constrained Full Fine-Tuning in LLMs for Continual Learning
methods.formula_latex:
W_0=U_{hi}\Sigma_{hi}V_{hi}^	op+U_{lo}\Sigma_{lo}V_{lo}^	op;\ U_{hi},\Sigma_{hi},V_{hi} 	ext{ frozen};\ U_{lo},\Sigma_{lo},V_{lo} 	ext{ trained with projected gradients }

abla_{U_{lo}},\ 
abla_{V_{lo}^	op}\leftarrow
abla_{V_{lo}^	op}(I-V_{hi}V_{hi}^	op)
methods.trainable_params: k(d_{out}+d_{in}+1),\ \ k=\min(d_{in},d_{out})-\text{effective\_rank}
methods.locus: any linear layer ('all-linear' supported)
methods.structure: SVD split of W_0: top singular subspace (important for prior tasks) frozen; minor singular components trained with gradients projected orthogonally to the frozen subspace
methods.mergeable_reason: The frozen and trained SVD components recombine into one dense W.
methods.identity_at_init: Trainable components initialized from W_0's own SVD, so W = W_0 at init.
methods.key_idea: For continual learning, update only directions orthogonal to the dominant singular subspaces of earlier tasks, giving full-rank-capacity updates with little forgetting.
methods.results_note: Paper reports 71.3 vs 69.6 (O-LoRA) on the 15-task T5-Large benchmark and 48.4 vs 41.3 on TRACE with LLaMA-2 7B.

methods.name: P-Tuning
methods.full_name: P-Tuning (continuous prompts with a prompt encoder)
methods.paper_title: GPT Understands, Too
methods.formula_latex: T=\{[P_{0:i}],\,x,\,[P_{i+1:j}],\,y,\,[P_{j+1:k}]\}\ \longmapsto\ \{h_0,\dots,h_i,\,e(x),\,h_{i+1},\dots,h_j,\,e(y),\,h_{j+1},\dots,h_k\},\quad (h_0,\dots,h_k)=f_\psi(P_0,\dots,P_k)\ \ (f_\psi:\ \text{LSTM or MLP prompt encoder});\ \ P,\psi\ \text{trained, LM frozen (or tuned)}
methods.trainable_params: \ell d+|\psi|\ \text{(encoder dropped after training, leaving } \ell d\text{)}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence, at arbitrary template positions interleaved with discrete anchor tokens
methods.structure: Virtual-token embeddings produced by a shared reparametrization network h=f_\psi(P) (bi-LSTM or MLP) that models dependencies between prompt tokens, inserted at template positions and concatenated with discrete prompt/anchor tokens.
methods.mergeable_reason: The continuous prompt tokens lengthen the input; only the encoder can be discarded (its outputs cached as embeddings).
methods.identity_at_init: No identity: the continuous prompt embeddings are freshly (randomly) initialized and concatenated with discrete prompt/anchor tokens, which the paper finds improves performance. The paper ablates LSTM, MLP and identity (EMB) prompt encoders and finds EMB unstable.
methods.key_idea: Make prompts continuous and let a small encoder couple the prompt tokens, which stabilizes training against the large variance of discrete prompts and lets GPT-style models compete with BERT-style models on NLU.
methods.results_note: With a frozen LM on LAMA knowledge probing P-Tuning beats manual prompts by 20+ points and searched prompts by 9 points; with tuned LMs it beats PET on SuperGLUE in both fully supervised and few-shot settings.

relations.note: Prompt tuning = P-Tuning with identity encoder and all virtual tokens at the front.
Both reparametrize prompt embeddings through a shared network; Residual PT adds a skip connection.
Same input-level soft prompt, but reparameterized through an encoder.

methods.name: PEANuT
methods.full_name: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Weight-aware Neural Tweakers
methods.paper_title: PEANuT: Parameter-Efficient Adaptation with Weight-aware Neural Tweakers
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+f(W_0;\theta),\ \ f(W_0;\theta)^\top=\sigma(W_0^\top\Theta_1)\,\Theta_2,\ \Theta_1\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ \Theta_2\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{out}} \ (\text{paper writes } \sigma(W_0\Theta_1)\Theta_2 \text{ with } W_0\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times d_{out}};\ \text{optional depth: extra } r\times r \text{ encoder/decoder layers with residuals})
methods.trainable_params: 2r\,d_{out}+2\,\text{depth}\,r^2
methods.locus: nn.Linear layers
methods.structure: nonlinear weight-conditioned update: a small MLP applied to the columns of W_0 (one d_out-vector per input feature) produces Delta W (rank <= r)
methods.mergeable_reason: f(W_0) is computed once after training and added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Output projection Theta_2 (B) zero-initialized.
methods.key_idea: Generate the update as a nonlinear function of the frozen weight itself instead of a weight-agnostic linear factorization.
methods.results_note: Paper reports consistent gains over strong PEFT baselines on four benchmarks spanning 20+ NLP and vision datasets at comparable or fewer parameters.

relations.note: Paper theorem: with ReLU, PEANuT of rank 2r matches any rank-r LoRA (Theta_1 = [W_0^+A; -W_0^+A] uses sigma(x) - sigma(-x) = x), so its reachable set contains LoRA's.

methods.name: Prefix-Tuning
methods.paper_title: Prefix-Tuning: Optimizing Continuous Prompts for Generation
methods.formula_latex: h_i=\begin{cases}P_\theta[i,:] & i\in P_{\mathrm{idx}}\\ \mathrm{LM}_\phi(z_i,h_{<i}) & \text{otherwise}\end{cases}\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \mathrm{head}^{(l)}=\mathrm{Attn}\big(XW_q^{(l)},\,[P_k^{(l)};XW_k^{(l)}],\,[P_v^{(l)};XW_v^{(l)}]\big),\ \ P_k^{(l)},P_v^{(l)}\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d},\ l=1,\dots,L;\ \ \text{training: } P_\theta[i,:]=\mathrm{MLP}_\theta(P'_\theta[i,:]),\ P'_\theta\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times k};\ \ \phi\ (W_0)\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2L\ell d\ \text{(stored, one key and one value prefix per attention layer of a decoder-only LM; an encoder-decoder prefixes each attention stack)};\ \ \ell k+|\mathrm{MLP}_\theta|\ \text{during training (MLP discarded afterwards)}
methods.locus: keys/values at every attention layer (decoder; encoder and decoder for enc-dec models in the paper)
methods.structure: Learned key/value vectors prepended at every layer, i.e. a learned initial KV-cache state of length \ell. By He et al. (2022) this is equivalently a gated parallel attention-adapter: h \leftarrow (1-\lambda(x))\,h+\lambda(x)\,\mathrm{softmax}(xW_qP_k^\top)P_v, with gate \lambda(x) = attention mass on the prefix.
methods.mergeable_reason: The prefix adds \ell extra key/value slots to every attention layer (extra attention cost per token); it can be served as a cached prefix but not folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No exact identity: any prefix diverts attention mass \lambda(x)>0 away from the content. HF PEFT's init_weights='zero' zeroes keys and values, which still rescales attention outputs by 1-\lambda(x). Li & Liang initialize the prefix with activations of real (preferably task-relevant) words, which substantially helps in low-data settings; direct optimization of P is unstable, hence the MLP reparametrization.
methods.key_idea: Optimize a short continuous 'context' that every token can attend to at every layer, steering a frozen LM like a prompt would but with far more expressive power than input embeddings alone (discrete prompt < embedding-only < prefix-tuning).
methods.results_note: With 0.1% of parameters, GPT-2 prefix-tuning is comparable to fine-tuning on table-to-text (E2E, WebNLG, DART), outperforms it in low-data settings and extrapolates better to unseen categories, but trails full fine-tuning on XSUM summarization with BART.

relations.note: Prompt tuning only frees the layer-0 slice of the prefix.
P-Tuning v2 is the same deep-prompt parameterization with an NLU-oriented recipe (optional reparametrization, classification head).
He et al. (2022) rewrite prefix-tuning as a parallel adapter with W_1=W_qP_k^⊤, W_2=P_v, softmax nonlinearity and input-dependent gate λ(x).
Cartridges are prefix-tuning without the MLP reparametrization, trained by context distillation.
On S4 SSMs every prefix acts only through an initial-state update (Galim et al., Prop. 1); initial-state tuning is an upper bound, equal when \ell \ge H under a genericity condition.
Same KV-prefix mechanism trained by self-study distillation.

methods.name: PSOFT
methods.paper_title: Efficient Orthogonal Fine-Tuning with Principal Subspace Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W=W_{res}+B\,\operatorname{diag}(\beta)\,R^{\top}\operatorname{diag}(\alpha)\,A,\quad W_0=U\Sigma V^{\top},\ A=V_{:,:r}^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{(row-orthonormal)},\ B=U_{:,:r}\Sigma_{:r,:r}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ W_{res}=W_0-BA\ \text{(all frozen)};\ R\in SO(r)\ \text{(Cayley or Cayley-Neumann)},\ \alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{r}\ \text{trained};\ \alpha=\beta=\mathbf{1}\Rightarrow W=W_0\big(I+A^{\top}(R^{\top}-I)A\big)
methods.trainable_params: \tfrac{r(r-1)}{2}+2r
methods.locus: any linear layer; acts on the principal input subspace of W_0
methods.structure: OFT restricted to the r-dimensional principal input subspace. O(r) acts on W_0 from the right through the embedding R -> I + A^T(R-I)A in O(d_in), which is the identity on the orthogonal complement. Two diagonal scalings (alpha, beta) gradually relax exact orthogonality.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapted weight W_res + B diag(beta) R diag(alpha) A is a fixed dense matrix after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Q = 0 (so R = I) and alpha = beta = 1 give W = W_0 exactly.
methods.key_idea: Confine orthogonal fine-tuning to the principal subspace of W_0 found by SVD. An r x r rotation plus two tunable scaling vectors then preserves the subspace geometry the way OFT does, with LoRA-like memory and far fewer parameters.
methods.results_note: Across 35 NLP/CV tasks and four backbones, avoids the out-of-memory failures of BOFT and GOFTv2/qGOFTv2, gives up to 18x higher parameter efficiency than BOFT, OFTv2 and LoRA variants on the smaller models, the best VTAB-1K average (73.4%), +2.28% over LoRA on LLaMA-3.2-3B GSM8K and +1.4% over LoRA on LLaMA-3.1-8B commonsense reasoning.

relations.note: orthogonal action restricted to a principal subspace
uses the Cayley-Neumann parameterization
with alpha=beta=1, PSOFT is mathematically a one-sided (right) Spectral Adapter^R: a rotation of the top-r right singular subspace
both use the top-r SVD (principal subspace) of W_0; PiSSA is a baseline in the PSOFT paper (+1.02% on MATH)
Uses the principal SVD subspace of W_0 like PiSSA.
Implemented as the additive low-rank update B(R-I)A, but with frozen principal-subspace bases and an r x r orthogonal core it is strictly more constrained than LoRA, not equivalent.

methods.name: PVeRA
methods.paper_title: PVeRA: Probabilistic Vector-Based Random Matrix Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0x + \alpha\,\Lambda_b B\, z,\quad z = \mu + \epsilon\odot\sigma,\ \epsilon\sim\mathcal{N}(0,I),\quad [\mu;\sigma] = \Lambda_d A x;\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{2r\times d_{in}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{frozen random shared};\ d\in\mathbb{R}^{2r},\ b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\ \text{trained};\ \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{task}+\beta\sum \mathrm{KL}(\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^2)\,\|\,\mathcal{N}(0,I));\ \text{deterministic inference: } W = W_0 + \alpha\Lambda_b B\,\Lambda_{d_\mu}A_\mu
methods.trainable_params: d_{out} + 2r
methods.locus: linear layers (paper: W_q, W_v of ViT); shared random matrices as in VeRA
methods.structure: VeRA with a stochastic (VAE-style reparameterised) rank-r bottleneck: the r-dim code is sampled from a Gaussian whose mean and std are VeRA-style scaled random projections of x; KL prior on the code (HF PEFT reads the second half of \Lambda_d A x as a log-variance, \sigma = \exp(\tfrac12\log\sigma^2), and adds no explicit \alpha)
methods.mergeable_reason: With mean (deterministic) inference z = mu the update is a fixed matrix that merges like VeRA; Monte-Carlo sampling mode at test time is input-dependent and cannot be merged.
methods.identity_at_init: b = 0 (HF: \lambda_b zeros), d = d_{initial} (0.1); so the adapter output is zero at init
methods.key_idea: Make VeRA's shared-random-basis bottleneck probabilistic so the adapter learns a distribution over adaptations, enabling uncertainty estimates while keeping VeRA's tiny footprint and mergeability.
methods.results_note: Outperforms VeRA and the other benchmarked adapters (seven adapters in total in the comparison) on average on VTAB-1k with ViT backbones; deterministic (mean) inference keeps it mergeable.

relations.note: same frozen shared random A, B and trainable scaling vectors, plus a reparameterised Gaussian bottleneck
Both make low-rank adapters Bayesian/stochastic.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2512.07703 (Fillioux, Dec 2025); WACV 2026 confirmed by arXiv journal-ref and IEEE DOI 10.1109/WACV61042.2026.00243; Eqs. for mu/sigma = xA (.) d, z = eps*sigma + mu, KL loss, merge with A_mu checked; HF pvera/layer.py (lambda_b zeros, lambda_d = 0.1, logvar chunking, mean at eval) checked.

code_url: added official code link from the abstract

methods.name: RandLoRA
methods.full_name: RandLoRA: full-rank PEFT via scaled random bases
methods.paper_title: RandLoRA: Full-rank parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large models
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W=\sum_{j=1}^{n}B_j\Lambda_jA\,\Gamma_j,\ \ B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r} \text{ and shared } A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} \text{ frozen random},\ \Lambda_j\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r},\ \Gamma_j \text{ trainable diagonal},\ n=\lceil\min(d_{in},d_{out})/r\rceil \ (\text{PEFT applies }\Gamma_j\text{ on the smaller dimension})
methods.trainable_params: n\,\big(r+\min(d_{in},d_{out})\big)\ \approx\ \tfrac{d^2}{r}+d \text{ for } d_{in}=d_{out}=d
methods.locus: nn.Linear layers only (PEFT)
methods.structure: sum of n frozen random rank-r bases with trainable diagonal scalings on both sides, reaching full rank; parameter count grows as the basis rank shrinks
methods.mergeable_reason: The scaled sum of bases is a fixed dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: PEFT sets Lambda_j = 0 and Gamma_j to the constant 1/max(n, min(d_in,d_out)) (in practice 1/min(d_in,d_out)), so Delta W = 0.
methods.key_idea: Separate parameter count from rank: combine many frozen random low-rank bases with learned diagonal scalings to get full-rank updates cheaply.
methods.results_note: Paper reports RandLoRA overtaking LoRA as the parameter budget grows on vision (DinoV2, CLIP), vision-language and commonsense reasoning (e.g. LLaMA3-8B).

relations.note: The paper says its formulation is similar to VeRA's (VeRA approximates only the first block of a full-rank update). VeRA scales the output side whereas RandLoRA scales the input side, so VeRA is not literally its n = 1 case.
Full-rank alternative at similar budgets.

methods.paper_title: LoRA-GA: Low-Rank Adaptation with Gradient Approximation
methods.formula_latex: G=\nabla_{W}\mathcal{L}(W_0)=USV^\top,\quad A_0=\tfrac{\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}}{\sqrt{\gamma}}V_{[:,1:r]}^\top,\quad B_0=\tfrac{\sqrt[4]{d_{out}}}{\sqrt{\gamma}}U_{[:,r+1:2r]},\quad W^{res}=W_0-\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}B_0A_0,\qquad h=(W^{res}+\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}BA)\,x;\ W^{res}\text{ frozen},\ A,B\text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: any linear layer
methods.structure: \Delta W factors through an r-dimensional space; A and B are initialized from disjoint blocks of the top-2r singular vectors of a sampled full gradient so that the first LoRA step \eta^2(G A_0^\top A_0+B_0B_0^\top G) best approximates \zeta G
methods.mergeable_reason: W^{res}+\tfrac{\alpha}{\sqrt r}BA is an ordinary dense matrix of the original shape (but the base differs from W_0, so the adapter alone is not a LoRA on W_0).
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: the offset W_0-\eta B_0A_0 cancels the nonzero adapter; initialization is gradient-driven (one sampled batch, layer-by-layer backward for O(1) memory) with the stable scale factor \sqrt[4]{d_{out}}/\sqrt{\gamma} (paired with \eta=\alpha/\sqrt r) chosen so that forward and backward magnitudes stay rank- and width-stable.
methods.key_idea: Choose A and B from the SVD of the full-fine-tuning gradient so that the very first LoRA update is the best low-rank approximation of the full-fine-tuning update, with a rank- and width-stable scale.

methods.name: KaSA
methods.paper_title: KaSA: Knowledge-Aware Singular-Value Adaptation of Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W_0=\sum_{i=1}^{k}\sigma_iu_iv_i^\top,\quad W_{world}=\sum_{i=1}^{k-r}\sigma_iu_iv_i^\top,\qquad W=W_{world}+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B\,\mathrm{diag}(\Delta\sigma)\,A,\qquad \mathcal{L}=\mathcal{L}_{task}+\beta\textstyle\sum_j\Delta\sigma_j^2+\gamma\big(\lVert B^\top B-I_r\rVert_F+\lVert AA^\top-I_r\rVert_F\big);\ W_{world}\text{ frozen},\ B,\Delta\sigma,A\text{ trained}

methods.name: LoRA+
methods.full_name: LoRA+ (decoupled learning rates for A and B)
methods.paper_title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA;\qquad A \leftarrow A - \eta_A\, g_A,\quad B \leftarrow B - \eta_B\, g_B,\quad \eta_B = \lambda\,\eta_A,\ \ \lambda\gg 1\ (\text{e.g. } \lambda=2^4)
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Unchanged rank-r factorization; the optimizer applies a block-diagonal learning-rate operator \mathrm{diag}(\eta_A I,\ \lambda\eta_A I) to (A,B). Infinite-width analysis: efficient feature learning requires \eta_A=\Theta(n^{-1}),\ \eta_B=\Theta(1), i.e. \eta_B/\eta_A=\Theta(n) (n = model width); this explicitly breaks the GL(r) gauge symmetry in favour of B.
methods.mergeable_reason: Only the training procedure changes; the trained adapter is a standard LoRA product that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Delta W = 0 at init under either zero-product scheme analysed in the paper: Init[1] (B = 0, A random with variance Theta(1/n); the standard LoRA/PEFT default) or Init[2] (A = 0, B random with variance Theta(1)). Most of the paper's experiments (and the recommended ratio lambda ~ 2^4 for RoBERTa) use Init[2]; with Init[1] the optimal ratio is smaller (~2^2-2^3).
methods.key_idea: With one shared learning rate, A and B cannot both learn features efficiently as width grows; setting the B learning rate a fixed large multiple of the A learning rate fixes this while keeping a 1-D LR search.
methods.results_note: Reports 1-2% accuracy improvements and up to ~2x faster fine-tuning at the same compute as LoRA (RoBERTa/GPT-2 on GLUE, Llama-7b on MNLI and flan-v2/MMLU); the best ratio is model/task/init dependent: ~2^4 for RoBERTa with Init[2], ~2^2-2^3 with Init[1], ~2^1-2^2 for Llama.
