methods.name: LoRA-Pro
methods.paper_title: LoRA-Pro: Are Low-Rank Adapters Properly Optimized?
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Gradient surgery on the fixed-rank manifold: the 'equivalent gradient' becomes \tilde g = P_BG+(I-P_B)GP_A, the orthogonal projection of the full gradient G onto the tangent space of rank-r matrices at BA (closed-form minimiser of \|\tilde g-G\|_F); the residual r\times r gauge freedom X is fixed by a Sylvester equation keeping (g^A,g^B) closest to the vanilla LoRA gradients. The AdamW variant keeps moments of the full-size equivalent gradient.
methods.mergeable_reason: Only the optimizer changes; the result is a standard LoRA adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA init (B = 0, so Delta W = 0). The closed form assumes full-rank A and B; the paper observes that both factors become full rank after the first update step, so the assumption fails only at step 0. LLM experiments use rsLoRA scaling s = alpha/sqrt(r).
methods.key_idea: Training LoRA is equivalent to full fine-tuning with a low-rank 'equivalent gradient' sBg^A + sg^BA; choosing g^A, g^B to make this as close as possible to the true full gradient (closed form, guaranteed loss decrease) narrows the gap to full fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: On a GLUE subset with T5-base LoRA-Pro beats standard LoRA by 6.36 points on average (above full fine-tuning), and on Llama-2-7B it beats LoRA-GA by 2.85 (GSM8K) and 6.45 (HumanEval) at rank 32, at ~4 GB more GPU memory than LoRA.

relations.note: both precondition LoRA gradients with Gram inverses: scaled GD yields P_BG+GP_A (double-counting P_BGP_A), LoRA-Pro the exact tangent-space projection P_BG+(I-P_B)GP_A; neither update contains the other as a special case
both align LoRA with full fine-tuning gradients: LoRA-GA only at initialization, LoRA-Pro at every step
both approximate full-gradient training with low-rank projected updates

methods.verification_notes: ICLR 2025 Spotlight confirmed (accepted list; arXiv v3 is the camera-ready). Theorems 2.1-2.3 (g^A, g^B, Sylvester equation for X) match the formula exactly; equivalent gradient P_BG+(I-P_B)GP_A re-derived. Results (+6.36 avg over 5 GLUE tasks with T5-base; +2.85 GSM8K / +6.45 HumanEval over LoRA-GA at r=32; ~4 GB extra memory) confirmed. Not in PEFT.
corrections: identity_at_init: replaced 'inverses must be regularized while B is rank-deficient early in training' with the paper's actual observation (factors are full rank after the first step) and added s = alpha/sqrt(r).
relations: 'generalizes riemannian-preconditioned-lora' changed to 'competes-with' - LoRA-Pro's update is P_BG+(I-P_B)GP_A for every X, so it never reproduces scaled GD's P_BG+GP_A.

methods.name: ReLoRA
methods.full_name: Restarted LoRA (high-rank training through low-rank updates)
methods.paper_title: ReLoRA: High-Rank Training Through Low-Rank Updates
methods.formula_latex: W^{(k)} = W^{(k-1)} + s\,B_kA_k\ \ (\text{merge every } T \text{ steps}),\qquad \Delta W_{\text{total}}=\sum_{k=1}^{N} s\,B_kA_k,\ \ \mathrm{rank}\le Nr;\quad \text{after each merge: } B_k\leftarrow 0,\ A_k\ \text{re-init},\ \text{prune most Adam moments, LR re-warm-up}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix at any time (after a short full-rank warm start when training from scratch); in the paper's pre-training runs embeddings and normalization layers are also trained full-rank}
methods.locus: attention and MLP linear layers of Transformer LMs during (pre-)training
methods.structure: Sum of N rank-r increments accumulated by periodic merge-and-reinit: the total update lies in M_{\le r}+\cdots+M_{\le r}=M_{\le Nr} while each phase optimizes only a rank-r chart; uses a jagged cosine schedule and magnitude-pruned (~99%) optimizer state at each restart.
methods.mergeable_reason: LoRA factors are merged into the dense weights at every restart and at the end, leaving a plain dense model.
methods.identity_at_init: Each restart re-initializes B = 0 (A Kaiming) so merge-and-reinit leaves the function unchanged; from-scratch training needs a full-rank warm start (e.g. 5k steps) before switching to ReLoRA.
methods.key_idea: Since rank(X+Y) can exceed rank(X), repeatedly merging low-rank updates into the weights and restarting the adapter yields a high-rank total update with low-rank memory; partial optimizer reset and LR re-warm-up stop the new adapter from relearning the old subspace.
methods.results_note: Pre-training Transformer LMs up to 1.3B parameters on C4, ReLoRA performs comparably to full-rank training while saving up to 5.5 GB RAM per GPU and speeding up training by 9-40% depending on model size and hardware.

relations.note: LoRA plus periodic merge-and-restart
both target memory-efficient high-rank (pre-)training via low-rank updates

methods.verification_notes: ICLR 2024 confirmed (accepted list; earlier arXiv title 'Stack More Layers Differently'). Algorithm 1 (Kaiming re-init of A, B=0, magnitude pruning of optimizer state, jagged cosine schedule), 99% pruning, 5k-step warm start and 1.3B / 5.5 GB / 9-40% claims confirmed. Not in PEFT.
corrections: trainable_params: added that embeddings and normalization layers are trained full-rank in the paper's setup (Sec. 3).

methods.name: Delta-LoRA
methods.full_name: Delta-LoRA (propagating the low-rank delta into the pretrained weight)
methods.paper_title: Delta-LoRA: Fine-Tuning High-Rank Parameters with the Delta of Low-Rank Matrices
methods.formula_latex: h = W^{(t)}x+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}B^{(t)}A^{(t)}x;\quad (A,B)\ \text{updated by AdamW};\quad W^{(t+1)} = W^{(t)} + \lambda\,\tfrac{\alpha}{r}\big(B^{(t+1)}A^{(t+1)}-B^{(t)}A^{(t)}\big)\ \ \text{for } t> K;\ \ \text{no dropout on the LoRA branch}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{with optimizer state; all } d_{out}d_{in} \text{ entries of } W \text{ are also modified (no gradient or moments stored for } W)
methods.locus: same as LoRA (paper: GPT-2, BART, RoBERTa weight matrices)
methods.structure: Every step after K adds \lambda times the increment of the rank-r product (itself of rank \le 2r) to the base weight, so W accumulates an unbounded-rank sum of low-rank increments; the increment acts as a surrogate for -\eta\,\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial W, which is exact only without dropout in the branch.
methods.mergeable_reason: The final model is the dense weight W^(T) + (alpha/r) B A, but the pretrained weight itself is overwritten, so the adaptation cannot be stored or swapped as a small detachable adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 and W-updates only start after K steps, so training starts from the pretrained function.
methods.key_idea: Reuse the change of the low-rank product between consecutive steps as a free (no gradient, no optimizer state) update to the full pretrained weight, giving high-rank adaptation at LoRA's memory cost.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA, DyLoRA and AdaLoRA in the paper's experiments on E2E and WebNLG (GPT-2 medium), XSum (BART-large) and GLUE (RoBERTa-base).

relations.note: LoRA branch plus a delta-driven update of W
both push high-rank updates into W; Delta-LoRA does it continuously every step rather than by periodic merges

methods.verification_notes: arXiv-only (OpenReview record is an unaccepted submission; not in any accepted list). Algorithm 1 (A Kaiming, B=0, update ratio lambda, start steps K, condition t>K) and experiments (GPT-2 medium E2E/WebNLG, BART-large XSum, RoBERTa-base GLUE) confirmed; formula transposed from the paper's AB convention. Not in PEFT.
corrections: formula_latex: start condition is t > K (Algorithm 1), not t >= K.

methods.name: COLA
methods.paper_title: Chain of LoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Language Models via Residual Learning
methods.formula_latex: W^{(i)} = W_0 + \sum_{j=1}^{i} B_jA_j,\qquad (B_i,A_i) \approx \arg\min_{B_i,A_i}\ \mathcal{L}\big(W^{(i-1)} + B_iA_i\big);\quad \text{then merge ('tie a knot'), re-init } B_{i+1}=0,\ A_{i+1}\sim\mathcal{N},\ \text{reset optimizer}
methods.trainable_params: r_i(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{for the active link (ranks may decrease along the chain)}
methods.locus: same as LoRA (OPT-1.3B, Llama-2-7B)
methods.structure: Residual learning: a chain of M rank-r_i corrections, each fitted to the residual \Delta W^\star-\sum_{j<i}B_jA_j on top of the merged weights; analysed as a (stochastic, non-convex) Frank-Wolfe / conditional-gradient method over low-rank atoms.
methods.mergeable_reason: Each link is merged into the frozen weights as training proceeds, so the final model is a dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Each new link starts with B = 0 and Gaussian A, so extending the chain does not change the function.
methods.key_idea: Approximate the optimal high-rank update by a Frank-Wolfe-like sequence of low-rank residual fits (tune LoRA, merge, extend the chain with a fresh LoRA and reset optimizer state), at LoRA's compute and memory.
methods.results_note: Across OPT-1.3B and Llama-2-7B on seven tasks COLA consistently beats LoRA, e.g. a 6.47% relative test-accuracy gain on WSC with OPT-1.3B and up to 4.4% relative gain with Llama-2-7B.

relations.note: same merge-and-reinit idea applied to fine-tuning, with full optimizer reset and a Frank-Wolfe convergence analysis
same periodic-merge mechanism
chain of standard LoRA modules

methods.verification_notes: arXiv-only ('Work in progress'). Tune-LoRA / tie-a-knot / extend-the-chain with Gaussian A, zero B and full optimizer reset, Frank-Wolfe analysis, rank step-down ablation and the 6.47% (WSC, OPT-1.3B) / 4.40% (RTE, Llama-2-7B) relative gains confirmed. Not in PEFT. Relation to ReLoRA is conceptual (COLA does not cite ReLoRA by name).

methods.name: PeriodicLoRA
methods.paper_title: PeriodicLoRA: Breaking the Low-Rank Bottleneck in LoRA Optimization
methods.formula_latex: W_t = W_{t-1} + s\,B_tA_t\ \ (\text{unload at the end of stage } t),\qquad W_T = W_0 + \sum_{t=1}^{T} s\,B_tA_t,\ \ \mathrm{rank}\le Tr;\quad \text{momentum unloading: merge } (1-m)\,sB_tA_t \text{ and keep } (B_t,A_t) \text{ scaled by } m
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: all attention and MLP linear layers (LLaMA-7B experiments)
methods.structure: Periodic merge-and-reinit (unloading point = 4.8k training examples per stage) accumulating a sum of rank-r terms, with a 'momentum' that only partially unloads the adapter to stabilize training. The paper describes momentum only in words ('scaling the BA product by (1-m) and A and B matrices by m'); read literally the retained product is m^2 sBA, so the unload is not exactly function-preserving.
methods.mergeable_reason: Adapters are unloaded into the backbone during training; the final model is dense with the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: Each stage re-initializes B = 0, A Gaussian (when m = 0), together with optimizer and LR-scheduler state.
methods.key_idea: Unload LoRA weights into the backbone after every few hundred steps and restart them, so multiple low-rank updates accumulate into a higher-rank update at constant memory; a momentum-based partial unload prevents collapse across mini-batches.
methods.results_note: With LLaMA-7B instruction tuning PLoRA consistently outperforms LoRA at the same rank (reporting up to ~1.8x LoRA's 'learning ability') without extra memory.

relations.note: same merge-and-restart idea for fine-tuning; PLoRA adds momentum unloading
concurrent periodic-merge method
periodically restarted LoRA

methods.verification_notes: arXiv-only. Unload into backbone + reset of LoRA weights, optimizer and LR-scheduler state, 4.8k-example unloading point, momentum 0.1-0.3, LLaMA-7B on all attention+MLP projections, '~1.8x learning ability' confirmed. Not in PEFT.
corrections: structure: added that the literal momentum rule retains m^2 sBA (not m sBA), so the momentum unload slightly changes the function.

methods.name: LoRA Dropout
methods.full_name: LoRA Dropout (sparsity-regularizing dropout on LoRA factors with test-time ensembling)
methods.paper_title: LoRA Dropout as a Sparsity Regularizer for Overfitting Control
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,\hat B\hat A,\quad \hat A = A\,\mathrm{diag}(m_A),\ \hat B = \mathrm{diag}(m_B)\,B,\quad m_A\in\{0,1\}^{d_{in}},\ m_B\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}}\sim\mathrm{Bern}(1-p);\quad \text{test time: } \bar o(x)=\tfrac{1}{N}\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mathcal{M}\big(x;\,W_0+s\hat B^{(n)}\hat A^{(n)}\big)
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: same as LoRA; also applied to AdaLoRA's P, Q factors
methods.structure: Bernoulli masks on the input columns of A and output rows of B (not on the rank dimension), so each entry of the product is zeroed with probability 2p-p^2; analysed as sparsity-regularized empirical risk minimization with a stability-based generalization bound, plus a Monte-Carlo test-time ensemble.
methods.mergeable_reason: Without test-time ensembling the trained BA merges like LoRA; the proposed test-time ensemble needs several stochastic forward passes and cannot be folded into a single weight.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (B = 0).
methods.key_idea: Even with few trainable parameters LoRA overfits; randomly dropping input/output coordinates of the LoRA factors acts as a sparsity regularizer that trades empirical risk against adaptation complexity, and averaging over dropout masks at test time tightens the bound further.
methods.results_note: Improves accuracy and calibration over LoRA/AdaLoRA on GLUE and SQuAD (DeBERTaV3-base) and on Alpaca instruction tuning of LLaMA2-7B in the paper's experiments.

relations.note: regularizer on the LoRA factors
the paper also applies the masks to AdaLoRA
both are regularizers for LoRA generalization (noise on factors vs. noise in full weight space)

methods.verification_notes: arXiv-only (OpenReview record is a withdrawn submission). Masks on input columns of A and output rows of B (Eq. 3), Bern(2p-p^2) sparsity of the product, AdaLoRA extension, MC test-time ensemble and experiments (DeBERTaV3-base GLUE/SQuAD, LLaMA2-7B Alpaca-clean -> MMLU) confirmed. Not in PEFT (PEFT lora_dropout is plain input dropout).

methods.name: AsyLoRA
methods.full_name: Asymmetric LoRA (random frozen A, train only B)
methods.paper_title: Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,B\,Q,\quad Q\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{random with orthonormal rows (Haar/Stiefel), frozen};\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{trained from } B=0
methods.trainable_params: r\,d_{out}
methods.locus: same as LoRA (RoBERTa, BART, LLaMA-2, ViT experiments)
methods.structure: Linear (not bilinear) parametrization: \Delta W ranges over \mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\otimes\mathrm{row}(Q) for a fixed random r-dim input subspace; freezing A gives least-squares/logistic regression on randomly projected features Qx, whereas freezing B only fits outputs projected onto a random subspace.
methods.mergeable_reason: B Q is an ordinary additive low-rank update that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 with Q random orthogonal and never updated.
methods.key_idea: A and B play asymmetric roles: A extracts input features (and a random A works about as well as a learned one) while B maps them to the task; training only B halves parameters, tightens information-theoretic generalization bounds, and lets one double r at fixed budget.
methods.results_note: Across RoBERTa, BART-Large, LLaMA-2 and ViT, B-only tuning with a random orthogonal A matches or beats standard LoRA at matched parameter count and improves out-of-domain accuracy on DomainBed.

relations.note: LoRA with eta_A = 0 and orthogonal random A
same freeze-A design, LoRA-FA motivated by activation memory
both rely on frozen random projections

methods.verification_notes: ICML 2024 confirmed (accepted list). Random orthonormal A sampled uniformly from the Stiefel manifold, B trained from 0, alpha = 2r, RoBERTa/BART/LLaMA-2/ViT and DomainBed experiments confirmed. Not in PEFT.

methods.name: LoRA Without Regret
methods.full_name: LoRA Without Regret (Thinking Machines Lab recipe and analysis)
methods.paper_title: LoRA Without Regret
methods.hf_peft_config: LoraConfig(lora_alpha=32, target_modules='all-linear')  # same-LR AdamW, LR ~10x the FullFT LR
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA,\ \ \alpha=32,\ \ A_{ij}\sim\mathcal{U}\big(\pm\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{d_{in}}}\big),\ B=0,\ \ \eta_A=\eta_B=\eta_{\text{LoRA}}\approx 10\,\eta_{\text{FullFT}};\ \ \text{apply to all linear layers incl. MLP/MoE}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: all weight matrices, especially MLP and MoE layers (attention-only LoRA underperforms MLP-only LoRA)
methods.structure: Standard LoRA parametrization; of the four hyperparameters (\alpha, \eta_A, \eta_B, init scale of A) only two affect the dynamics, and with the 1/r multiplier and B=0 the expected first update \tfrac{1}{r}\sum_i b_ia_i^{\top} is rank-independent, making the optimal LR approximately independent of r.
methods.mergeable_reason: It is plain LoRA, so the adapter merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 with A uniform of scale 1/sqrt(d_in) (the PEFT default parametrization).
methods.key_idea: LoRA matches full fine-tuning in the regime that matters for post-training when applied to all layers (especially MLPs) with ~10x the FullFT learning rate and when the dataset does not exceed adapter capacity; RL needs very little capacity, so even rank-1 LoRA matches FullFT for policy-gradient training.
methods.results_note: On Llama 3 / Qwen3 models with Tulu3 and OpenThoughts3 SFT, LoRA matches FullFT until capacity is exceeded; on MATH/GSM8K/DeepMath RL even rank-1 LoRA matches FullFT; LoRA is less tolerant of large batch sizes; LoRA costs slightly more than 2/3 of FullFT FLOPs per pass.

relations.note: empirical study and recipe for vanilla LoRA
argues the default 1/r scaling already makes the optimal LR roughly rank-invariant
uses a single LR for A and B and shows two of the four hyperparameters are redundant

methods.verification_notes: Blog post (Sep 29 2025) confirmed at thinkingmachines.ai/blog/lora with the official citation 'Schulman, John and Thinking Machines Lab', DOI 10.64434/tml.20250929. alpha = 32, uniform A with scale 1/sqrt(d_in), B = 0, same LR, optimal LR ~10x FullFT, attention-only < MLP-only, rank-1 RL parity, ~2/3 FLOPs and the two-parameter invariance of the four hyperparameters all confirmed. Plain LoRA, so PEFT LoraConfig applies.

methods.name: Flat-LoRA
methods.full_name: Flat-LoRA (low-rank adaptation over a flat full-space loss landscape)
methods.paper_title: Flat-LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation over a Flat Loss Landscape
methods.formula_latex: \min_{A,B}\ \mathbb{E}_{\varepsilon_W}\,\mathcal{L}\big(W'+\varepsilon_W\big),\quad W'=W_0+sBA,\quad (\varepsilon_W)_{ij}\sim\mathcal{N}\!\big(0,\tfrac{\sigma^2}{d_{in}}\|W'_{i,:}\|_2^2\big)\ \ (\text{fresh noise each step, regenerated from a seed})
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: same as LoRA (LLMs and text-to-image diffusion models)
methods.structure: Random-weight-perturbation (Bayesian expected loss) regularizer applied in the full d_{out}\times d_{in} weight space rather than in the (A,B) space, with filter(row)-norm-scaled Gaussian noise; a cheap relaxation of SAM's min-max over full-space perturbations.
methods.mergeable_reason: Noise is used only during training; the learned BA merges like LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization (B = 0); the perturbation is zero-mean training noise only.
methods.key_idea: A minimum that is flat in LoRA's (A,B) coordinates can still be sharp in the full weight space; averaging the loss over full-space random weight perturbations steers LoRA toward full-space flat minima without SAM's extra gradient step or weight copy.
methods.results_note: Improves in-domain and out-of-domain generalization over LoRA on mathematical reasoning, coding, dialogue, instruction following and text-to-image generation in the paper's experiments.

relations.note: regularized LoRA training objective
alternative regularizer for LoRA generalization

methods.verification_notes: ICML 2025 confirmed (arXiv comment + ICML 2025 list). Objective E L(W+sBA+eps) with filter-wise noise N(0, sigma^2/n ||W'_{i,:}||^2) (n = input dim) regenerated from a seed confirmed. Not in PEFT.

methods.name: AltLoRA
methods.paper_title: AltLoRA: Towards Better Gradient Approximation in Low-Rank Adaptation with Alternating Projections
methods.formula_latex: \text{even } t:\ A\leftarrow A-\eta\,\tfrac{1}{s^2}(B^{\top}B)^{-1}\nabla_A\mathcal{L}\ \ (\delta W=-\eta P_BG);\qquad \text{odd } t:\ B\leftarrow B-\eta\,\tfrac{1}{s^2}\nabla_B\mathcal{L}\,(AA^{\top})^{-1}\ \ (\delta W=-\eta\, G P_A);\quad \tilde M^B = M^BA_tA_{t+1}^{\top}(A_{t+1}A_{t+1}^{\top})^{-1}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Alternating one-sided projections of the full gradient onto col(B) and row(A) (each the exact least-squares solution for the factor being updated), with momentum transported into the new low-rank subspace by an r\times r change-of-basis; avoids LoRA-Pro's non-unique X and full-size optimizer state.
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only change; the result is a standard LoRA adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: Standard LoRA initialization; Gram inverses are damped as (B^T B + lambda I)^{-1} to stay invertible when a factor is rank-deficient.
methods.key_idea: Instead of jointly matching the full gradient (LoRA-Pro), alternately update A and B so each step is an exact projection of the full gradient, and keep momentum aligned with the changing subspace without extra memory; this gives stable feature learning and transformation invariance.
methods.results_note: Outperforms LoRA and its variants (including LoRA-Pro) across SFT and NLU tasks while keeping LoRA-level memory, narrowing the gap to full fine-tuning.

relations.note: same gradient-approximation goal, alternating instead of joint update, low-rank momentum
each half-step uses the same (B^T B)^{-1} / (AA^T)^{-1} preconditioners
concurrent alternating-update optimizer

methods.verification_notes: NeurIPS 2025 poster confirmed (NeurIPS 2025 list). Theorem 1 closed forms, Theorem 2 momentum transport M^B A_t A_{t+1}^T (A_{t+1}A_{t+1}^T)^{-1}, Algorithm 1 (even t: A, odd t: B, s = alpha/r) and weight-decay relaxation of full rank (Corollary 1) confirmed. Not in PEFT.

methods.name: LoFT
methods.full_name: Low-rank adaptation that mimics Full fine-Tuning
methods.paper_title: LoFT: Low-Rank Adaptation That Behaves Like Full Fine-Tuning
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: same as LoRA
methods.structure: Six building blocks (alternating updates, scaled gradients, momentum recalibration across changing subspaces via C_k=(A_{k-1}A_k^{\top})(A_kA_k^{\top})^{-1} [the paper's (V_{k-1}^{\top}V_k)(V_k^{\top}V_k)^{-1} with V=A^{\top}], second-moment alignment with cross terms, reconstruction of the full AdamW update followed by projection, gradient clipping) that make the low-rank step the tightest approximation to the AdamW full-fine-tuning step; alpha is fixed to 1, and LoFT reduces exactly to AdamW when r=\max(d_{in},d_{out}) with full-rank factors.
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only change; the adapter is a standard mergeable low-rank product.
methods.identity_at_init: Inherits LoRA's zero-product initialization; Gram inverses fall back to pseudo-inverses when a factor is rank-deficient.
methods.key_idea: Not only gradients but also Adam's first and second moments are misaligned between LoRA and full fine-tuning; projecting and recalibrating them in the evolving low-rank subspace makes LoRA behave like full fine-tuning and removes the need to tune alpha.
methods.results_note: Substantially narrows the gap to full fine-tuning and consistently outperforms standard LoRA-style methods without increasing inference cost; memory overhead O((d_in+d_out) r^2) for second-moment calibration.

relations.note: concurrent alternating-update optimizers
Building Block 2 (scaled gradients) coincides with the Riemannian preconditioner
both align low-rank updates with full fine-tuning; LoFT also aligns optimizer states

methods.verification_notes: ICLR 2026 poster confirmed (arXiv comment + ICLR 2026 list). Paper parametrizes W = W_0 + UV^T (U = our B, V = our A^T); Building Blocks 1-6, P_V projection, (V^TV)^{-1}/(U^TU)^{-1} scaled gradients, O((m+n)r^2) memory and pseudo-inverse fallback confirmed. Not in PEFT (PEFT 'LoftQ' is unrelated).
corrections: structure: rewrote the momentum calibration matrix C_k in the catalog's notation (it used the paper's undefined V) and noted alpha = 1.

methods.name: PoLAR
methods.paper_title: PoLAR: Polar-Decomposed Low-Rank Adapter Representation
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0+X\,\Theta\,Y^{\top},\quad X\in\mathrm{St}(d_{out},r),\ Y\in\mathrm{St}(d_{in},r),\ \Theta\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r};\ \text{retraction-free landing field } \Gamma(X)=\psi(X)X+\lambda\nabla\mathcal{N}(X);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+r^2
methods.locus: any linear layer
methods.structure: rank-r additive update in polar form: two direction factors on Stiefel manifolds (orthonormal r-frames, i.e. points of O(d)/O(d-r)) and an unconstrained r x r scale/core matrix, optimized by Riemannian 'landing' without retractions
methods.mergeable_reason: X Theta Y^T is a fixed rank-r matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Theta_0 = 0, with X_0 and Y_0 drawn uniformly at random from the Stiefel manifolds.
methods.key_idea: LoRA updates collapse to a very low stable rank. Writing the update as two orthonormal direction frames times a free core, and training with GPU-friendly Riemannian landing, keeps the directions diverse and provably speeds up convergence on a canonical low-rank problem.
methods.results_note: Reports gains over LoRA on GLUE (DeBERTa-v3-base 88.94 vs 88.18), commonsense reasoning (Llama-2-7B, 73.71 vs 72.18) and math (Gemma-3-27B) across models from 350M to 27B parameters.

relations.note: the same rank-r update, polar-decomposed
orthogonality over the whole factor instead of DoRA's per-neuron normalization
an SVD-shaped P Lambda Q update, with hard Stiefel constraints instead of an orthogonality penalty

both use Riemannian geometry for LoRA optimization, but PoLAR optimizes Stiefel-manifold factors with the landing field, whereas Zhang & Pilanci precondition unconstrained factors with a quotient metric; PoLAR cites them only for the matrix-factorization reduction

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2506.03133 (Lion, 2025) matches; NeurIPS 2025 confirmed in the NeurIPS 2025 accepted-paper data. Delta W = X Theta Y^T with Stiefel X, Y, free Theta, landing field Gamma(X)=psi(X)X+lambda grad N(X), Theta_0=0 with random Stiefel X_0, Y_0, and the GLUE (88.94 vs 88.18) and commonsense (73.71 vs 72.18) averages checked in the PDF. No official code link found in the paper. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: relations: 'builds-on riemannian-preconditioned-lora' changed to 'competes-with' - PoLAR's Stiefel/landing optimizer is not built on the Zhang & Pilanci preconditioner.

methods.name: GOFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter Efficient Quasi-Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Givens Rotation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 R^{\top},\quad R=\prod_{\ell=1}^{\log_2 d_{in}}P_\ell,\ P_\ell=\prod_{k=0}^{d_{in}/2^{\ell}-1}G\big(2^{\ell}k,\ 2^{\ell-1}(2k+1);\ \theta_k^{\ell}\big),\ G(i,j;\theta) \text{ a Givens rotation in the } (i,j) \text{ plane};\ W_0 \text{ frozen, angles } \theta \text{ trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer; acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of SO(d_in), with the group element written as a product of d-1 Givens rotations (one-parameter subgroups SO(2) embedded in coordinate planes) arranged in log2(d) parallel layers of non-overlapping rotations, a butterfly-like layout
methods.mergeable_reason: The product of Givens rotations is a fixed orthogonal matrix that can be multiplied into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: All angles start at 0 (each rotation initialized to the identity).
methods.key_idea: d-1 Givens rotations can map any vector to any other vector on the same sphere, so OFT-level expressiveness only needs O(d) angles instead of O(d^2) parameters. A parallel arrangement keeps the depth at O(log d) sequential layers.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with DeBERTaV3-base, GOFT with 0.08M parameters matches OFT (b=8, 0.66M parameters) at an 88.78 average; also evaluated on LLaMA-2-7B instruction tuning and VTAB-1K.

relations.note: same orthogonal right action; far sparser parameterization

up to factor-ordering and permutation conventions, GOFT's parallel layer P_l keeps only the first 2x2 rotation of each stride-2^{l-1} butterfly block, so it is a sparser instance of BOFT(log2 d, 2) with the other rotations fixed to the identity (a function-class inclusion, not a statement made in either paper)
qGOFT relaxes each Givens block to a general 2x2 matrix

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2404.04316 (Ma, 2024) matches; ICML 2024 confirmed by arXiv comment and DBLP. Forward pass h=(RW)^T x with R=prod P_r, P_r = prod G(2^r k, 2^{r-1}(2k+1)), d-1 angles, zero-angle init, and the GLUE numbers (GOFT 0.08M 88.78 = OFT b=8 0.66M 88.78) checked in the PDF.
corrections: code_url: added the official repository linked in the paper (github.com/ArthurLeoM/peft-givens)
relations: clarified that the boft special-case-of link is a function-class inclusion derived here, not a claim of either paper

methods.name: qGOFT
methods.paper_title: Parameter Efficient Quasi-Orthogonal Fine-Tuning via Givens Rotation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0\tilde{R}^{\top},\quad \tilde{R}=\prod_{\ell}\tilde{P}_\ell,\ \text{each Givens block replaced by a free } \tilde{G}_i=[\alpha_i\ \beta_i]\in\mathbb{R}^{2\times 2};\ \min\ \mathcal{L}+\lambda\sum_i\langle\alpha_i,\beta_i\rangle^2;\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.locus: any linear layer; acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of a product of embedded free 2x2 blocks (singular ones included) laid out like GOFT. Leaving SO(d) lets the update change neuron norms and angles, and a soft column-orthogonality penalty keeps it near the orthogonal group.
methods.mergeable_reason: The product of 2x2 blocks is a fixed matrix that can be multiplied into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Every quasi-Givens block is initialized to the 2x2 identity.
methods.key_idea: Relax each Givens rotation to an arbitrary 2x2 linear map, so fine-tuning can also rescale neurons and shift their angles. A soft regularizer keeps the map close to orthogonal.
methods.results_note: Reports an 89.35 GLUE average on DeBERTaV3-base with 0.33M parameters (above OFT b=8 with 0.66M) and a 79.4% VTAB-1K average.

relations.note: Givens rotations relaxed to general 2x2 blocks with a soft orthogonality penalty
structural analogue: both act with 2x2 blocks (qGOFT on the input side with butterfly-style mixing, RoAd with scaled rotations on fixed output pairs); neither paper compares against the other

methods.verification_notes: Same paper as GOFT (arXiv 2404.04316, ICML 2024). Quasi-Givens 2x2 blocks (alpha_i, beta_i), the lambda * sum <alpha_i,beta_i>^2 regularizer, identity init of each block, the 89.35 GLUE (0.33M) and 79.4 VTAB-1K numbers checked in the PDF.
corrections: code_url: added the official repository linked in the paper
relations: road note clarified as a structural analogy (neither paper compares against the other)

methods.name: ETHER
methods.paper_title: ETHER: Efficient Finetuning of Large-Scale Models with Hyperplane Reflections
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 H^{B},\quad H^{B}=\operatorname{diag}(H_1,\dots,H_n),\ H_j=I-2u_ju_j^{\top},\ \|u_j\|=1,\ u_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}/n};\ \|H_j-I\|_F=2;\ W_0 \text{ frozen, } u_j \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: d_{in}
methods.locus: any linear layer (diffusion attention, LLM projections); acts on the input side of W_0
methods.structure: right action of a block-diagonal product of n hyperplane reflections, an element of O(d_in) that lies at fixed distance ||H_j - I||_F = 2 from the identity in every block
methods.mergeable_reason: H^B is a fixed orthogonal matrix that can be multiplied into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No. A Householder reflection is never the identity (||H - I||_F = 2 per block), and the official code initializes u with Kaiming-uniform random values, so the model is moved by a bounded reflection at step 0. Training only re-orients the reflection hyperplanes.
methods.key_idea: Restricting the multiplicative update to hyperplane reflections bounds how far the fine-tuned weights can move from the pretrained ones, whatever the learning rate. The result needs very few parameters and is robust to hyperparameters.
methods.results_note: Reports performance matching or beating LoRA and OFT with about 10-100x fewer parameters on subject-driven and controllable Stable Diffusion generation, GLUE and LLaMA instruction tuning.

relations.note: block-diagonal orthogonal action with each block restricted to a single reflection

diag(H_1,...,H_n) is a product of n reflections with disjoint-support vectors, i.e. HRA with r=n orthogonal reflection vectors and without the identity-preserving pairing (the two methods were concurrent)

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2405.20271 (Bini, 2024) matches; ICML 2024 confirmed (arXiv comment, PMLR 235 header). Paper convention (Q W)^T x with W in R^{d x f}; H is symmetric so W_0 H is exact. Block-diagonal form, ||H-I||_F=2, O(Ld) parameters and the 120x/30x fewer-than-OFT statements checked in the PDF. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: identity_at_init: confirmed from the official code (ether-instruct/lit_gpt/ether.py: Kaiming-random u, H = I - 2uu^T/||u||^2) that ETHER does not start at the identity; removed the 'not confirmed' hedge
confidence: medium -> high after checking the paper and official code

methods.name: ETHER+
methods.full_name: ETHER+ (relaxed two-hyperplane transformation applied on both sides)
methods.paper_title: ETHER: Efficient Finetuning of Large-Scale Models with Hyperplane Reflections
methods.formula_latex: W=\tilde{H}^{+}\,W_0\,H^{+},\quad H^{+}=I-uu^{\top}+vv^{\top}\ (u,v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}}\ \text{unit, block-diagonal}),\ \tilde{H}^{+}=I-\tilde u\tilde u^{\top}+\tilde v\tilde v^{\top}\ (\tilde u,\tilde v\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}});\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: any linear layer; acts on both the input and the output side of W_0
methods.structure: two-sided action (left on R^{d_out}, right on R^{d_in}) by rank<=2 perturbations of the identity. These are not orthogonal in general, so they leave the group O(d), but their distance to I is bounded by ETHER's.
methods.mergeable_reason: Both transforms are fixed matrices after training, so H~+ W_0 H+ can be precomputed.
methods.identity_at_init: Yes. The official code initializes the second vector as the negative copy of the first (v = -u), so vv^T = uu^T and H+ = I on both sides; the paper notes that H+ returns the identity when the two hyperplanes coincide.
methods.key_idea: Relax the Householder reflection to I - uu^T + vv^T so that two hyperplanes can interact or cancel. Applied on both sides of W_0, this gives finer, still norm-bounded updates.
methods.results_note: Reports e.g. 0.666 DINO for subject-driven generation with 0.4M parameters vs OFT's 0.652 with 11.6M, and 27.3 mIoU vs 24.5 for controllable generation.

relations.note: a two-hyperplane relaxation of the reflection that can reach the identity
DeLoRA is derived from ETHER+ by making the bound on the deviation learnable and the rank arbitrary

methods.verification_notes: Same paper as ETHER. H+ = I - uu^T + vv^T, two-sided forward (H+ W H~+)^T x (which is H~+ W_0 H+ in the h=Wx convention), ||H+ - I||_F <= 2, O(L(d+f)) parameters and the 0.666 vs 0.652 DINO and 27.3 vs 24.5 mIoU numbers checked in the PDF.
corrections: identity_at_init: confirmed from the official code (ether_R2 = -ether_R, also for the two-sided etherplusHH variant) that ETHER+ starts exactly at the identity
confidence: medium -> high after checking the paper and official code

methods.name: Spectral Adapter^R
methods.paper_title: Spectral Adapter: Fine-Tuning in Spectral Space
methods.formula_latex: W=[U_1R_U,\ U_2]\,S\,[V_1R_V,\ V_2]^{\top}=\tilde{U}\,W_0\,\tilde{V}^{\top},\quad \tilde{U}=I+U_1(R_U-I)U_1^{\top},\ \tilde{V}=I+V_1(R_V-I)V_1^{\top};\ W_0=USV^{\top}\ \text{frozen},\ R_U,R_V\in O(r)\ \text{(Cayley) trained}
methods.trainable_params: 2r^2\ \ (r(r-1)\ \text{with skew-symmetric Cayley generators})
methods.locus: any linear layer (top-r spectral space of each pretrained weight)
methods.structure: two-sided orthogonal action of O(r) x O(r), embedded in O(d_out) x O(d_in) as rotations of the top-r left and right singular subspaces of W_0 (identity on their complements). Singular values are unchanged and only the principal singular frames are rotated.
methods.mergeable_reason: The rotated singular factors recombine into one dense matrix of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: R_U = R_V = I.
methods.key_idea: Run the SVD of each pretrained weight and fine-tune only by rotating its top singular vectors. The adapter is very compact, and keeping the adapted subspaces orthogonal helps when several adapters are fused.

relations.note: OFT-style orthogonal action restricted to the principal spectral subspace
same paper; rotational vs additive tuning of the top singular vectors

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2405.13952 (Zhang, 2024) matches; NeurIPS 2024 confirmed in the NeurIPS 2024 accepted-paper data. Definition [U_1 R_U, U_2] S [V_1 R_V, V_2]^T, identity init, Cayley with Q=(A-A^T)/2 (so 2r^2 stored parameters) checked in Sec. 2 and 4.3 of the PDF. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: Spectral Adapter^A
methods.paper_title: Spectral Adapter: Fine-Tuning in Spectral Space
methods.formula_latex: W=[U_1+A_U,\ U_2]\,S\,[V_1+A_V,\ V_2]^{\top},\quad A_U\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_V\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r}\ \text{trained};\ W_0=USV^{\top}\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: any linear layer (top-r singular vectors)
methods.structure: additive perturbation of the top-r singular-vector factors: Delta W = A_U S_1 V_1^T + U_1 S_1 A_V^T + A_U S_1 A_V^T. This has rank <= 2r for LoRA's parameter budget (the paper's 'twice the rank capacity' lemma).
methods.mergeable_reason: The perturbed factors recombine into a single dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: A_U = A_V = 0.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tune the top singular vectors of the pretrained weight additively. For the same number of trainable parameters this doubles LoRA's rank capacity and uses the pretrained spectrum.
methods.results_note: Reports 49.73 on GSM8K with Mistral-7B vs 44.81 for LoRA and 43.82 for DoRA (r=8), and an 88.03 GLUE average on DeBERTaV3-base, above LoRA, DoRA, OFT and AdaLoRA.

relations.note: same parameter budget, twice the rank capacity
both adapt the principal singular subspace of W_0 (concurrent work)
same paper; additive vs rotational

methods.verification_notes: Same paper as Spectral Adapter^R (arXiv 2405.13952, NeurIPS 2024). Zero init of A_U, A_V, the rank-capacity lemma (2r) and Tables 1-2 checked in the PDF.
corrections: results_note: the GSM8K experiment (49.73 vs 44.81) uses Mistral-7B, not Llama-3-8B (Llama3-8B appears only in the Figure 1 loss curves)

methods.name: SVDiff
methods.paper_title: SVDiff: Compact Parameter Space for Diffusion Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W=U\,\operatorname{diag}\big(\mathrm{ReLU}(\sigma+\delta)\big)\,V^{\top},\quad W_0=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma)V^{\top}\ \text{(SVD, frozen)},\ \delta\in\mathbb{R}^{\min(d_{in},d_{out})}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: \min(d_{in},d_{out})
methods.locus: 2-D linear weights and reshaped 4-D conv kernels of the diffusion UNet (1-D weights such as biases and norms are not decomposed and are tuned directly); optimizing the cross-attention layers gives the best subject preservation in the paper's layer ablation
methods.structure: the singular values are adjusted by a diagonal (torus) map while the singular vectors stay fixed. For sigma > 0 this equals W = U diag(s/sigma) U^T W_0 with s = ReLU(sigma+delta) >= 0, a positive-semidefinite rescaling that commutes with W_0 W_0^T.
methods.mergeable_reason: U diag(ReLU(sigma+delta)) V^T is a fixed dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: delta = 0.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tune only the singular values of every weight matrix (spectral shifts). The tiny parameter space resists overfitting in personalization and supports multi-subject training (Cut-Mix-Unmix) and single-image editing (CoSINE).
methods.results_note: About 1.7MB of parameters for Stable Diffusion vs 3.66GB for full DreamBooth (roughly 2,200x smaller) and 1/2-1/3 of a LoRA checkpoint.

relations.note: SVF scales singular values multiplicatively; SVDiff shifts them additively (equivalent reparameterizations for sigma > 0)
SVFT with a diagonal mask is a spectral shift without the ReLU
much smaller checkpoint for diffusion personalization

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2303.11305 (Han, 2023) matches; ICCV 2023 confirmed (DBLP conf/iccv, Semantic Scholar). W_delta = U diag(ReLU(sigma+delta)) V^T, the 1.7MB vs 3.66GB and ~2,200x figures and the 1/2-1/3 of LoRA checkpoint size checked in the PDF. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: locus: removed 'optionally the text encoder' (not found in the paper); added that 1-D weights are tuned directly and rephrased the cross-attention finding as reported in the layer ablation

methods.name: SVF (Transformer²)
methods.paper_title: Transformer-Squared: Self-adaptive LLMs
methods.formula_latex: W=U\big(\Sigma\otimes\operatorname{diag}(z)\big)V^{\top}=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma\odot z)V^{\top}\ \Big(\times\tfrac{\sum_i\sigma_i}{\sum_i\sigma_iz_i}\ \text{in the official code}\Big),\quad W_0=U\operatorname{diag}(\sigma)V^{\top}\ \text{frozen},\ z\in\mathbb{R}^{\min(d_{in},d_{out})}\ \text{trained (REINFORCE + KL)};\ \text{test time: } z'=\sum_k\alpha_kz_k
methods.trainable_params: \min(d_{in},d_{out})
methods.locus: weight matrices of the LLM (the official code adapts the MLP matrices)
methods.structure: multiplicative diagonal (torus) action on the singular values with fixed singular vectors. Trained expert vectors z_k can be linearly mixed at inference.
methods.mergeable_reason: Once z (or the mixture z') is chosen, W is a fixed dense matrix; self-adaptation is a two-pass procedure that sets z before the second pass.
methods.identity_at_init: z starts near a constant value (the paper's hyperparameter table lists an initial mean of 0.1). The official code passes z through a sigmoid and renormalizes by sum(sigma)/sum(sigma*z), so a uniform z leaves W_0 unchanged up to this normalization (approximately the identity).
methods.key_idea: Train one scaling vector over each weight's singular values with RL to get compact, composable 'expert' vectors. At test time a dispatcher identifies the task and mixes the experts, so the LLM adapts itself.
methods.results_note: On Llama-3-8B-Instruct, SVF beats LoRA on GSM8K (79.15 vs 77.18) and ARC-Easy while training less than 10% of LoRA's parameters.

relations.note: multiplicative instead of additive adjustment of singular values
far fewer parameters; experts can be mixed

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2501.06252 (Sun, 2025) matches; ICLR 2025 confirmed (arXiv comment, ICLR 2025 accepted-paper data). W'=U(Sigma (x) diag(z))V^T, REINFORCE with KL penalty, z init mean 0.1 (Table 6), test-time mixing z'=sum alpha_k z_k, the 79.15 vs 77.18 GSM8K result and <10% of LoRA's parameters checked; sigmoid and sum(sigma)/sum(sigma*z) renormalization confirmed in the official utils.py/policy/base.py. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: SVFT
methods.paper_title: SVFT: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning with Singular Vectors
methods.formula_latex: W=U(\Sigma+M)V^{\top}=W_0+UMV^{\top},\quad U,\Sigma,V\ \text{from the SVD of frozen } W_0,\ M\ \text{sparse with fixed pattern } \Omega\ \text{(plain/diagonal, banded, random, top-}k\text{)};\ \text{only } M_{\Omega} \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: |\Omega|\ (+1\ \text{gate scalar per layer in the official code});\ \ \min(d_{in},d_{out})\ \text{for SVFT}^{P}
methods.locus: any linear layer
methods.structure: sparse additive update in the singular-vector basis of W_0: Delta W = sum over (i,j) in Omega of m_ij u_i v_j^T, a fixed dictionary that depends on the weight rather than a free low-rank factorization. A diagonal Omega reduces it to a spectral shift.
methods.mergeable_reason: U M V^T is a fixed dense matrix after training.
methods.identity_at_init: Not exactly in the official code: the coefficients of M are Kaiming-normal initialized and multiplied by a learnable gate sigmoid(g) with g = 0, so Delta W = U (0.5 M_init) V^T is non-zero at step 0. The paper does not state an initialization.
methods.key_idea: Use the outer products of W_0's own singular vectors as a fixed dictionary and learn sparse coefficients for it, including off-diagonal ones. This trades parameters against expressivity smoothly.
methods.results_note: Recovers up to 96% of full fine-tuning performance while training 0.006-0.25% of parameters (e.g. Gemma-2B and LLaMA-3-8B on GSM8K/MATH); baselines reach at most 85% with 0.03-0.8%.

relations.note: a diagonal mask gives SVDiff's spectral shift without the ReLU
weight-dependent fixed basis instead of learned low-rank factors
our observation: a dense top-left r x r block of M gives the LoRA-XS form
Plain SVFT (diagonal M) shifts singular values like SVDiff, but SVDiff clamps with ReLU(Sigma + delta) and SVFT does not, so neither strictly contains the other; SVFT does not cite SVDiff
both train O(d) parameters per matrix; SVFT uses weight-derived rather than random bases
FRoD builds on the U(Sigma+S)V^T form with a basis shared across layers

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2405.19597 (Lingam, 2024) matches; NeurIPS 2024 confirmed in the NeurIPS 2024 accepted-paper data. h = U(Sigma+M)V^T x, the Plain/Banded/Random/Top-k patterns and the 96% / 0.006-0.25% abstract claim checked in the PDF. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: identity_at_init: the official svft_layers.py initializes the sparse coefficients with kaiming_normal_ (times sigmoid(gate)=0.5), not M=0
trainable_params: added the per-layer gate scalar used in the official code
identity_at_init: noted that the code's gate is itself a trainable scalar (one extra parameter per module)
relations[svdiff]: type generalizes -> competes-with, note rewritten (SVDiff's ReLU clamp means SVFT-Plain is not an exact generalisation)

methods.name: BiDoRA
methods.paper_title: BiDoRA: Bi-level Optimization-Based Weight-Decomposed Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W=\operatorname{diag}(m)\,\frac{W_0+BA}{\|W_0+BA\|_{row}};\quad \min_{m}\ \mathcal{L}_{val}\big(\mathcal{V}^{*}(m),m\big)\ \ \text{s.t.}\ \ \mathcal{V}^{*}(m)=\arg\min_{\mathcal{V}=\{B,A\}}\ \mathcal{L}_{tr}(\mathcal{V},m)+\gamma\sum_k\big\|(V_k+\Delta V_k)^{\top}(V_k+\Delta V_k)-I\big\|_F^2
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+d_{out}
methods.locus: any linear layer (as DoRA)
methods.structure: DoRA's magnitude-direction parameterization, with magnitude and direction optimized at different levels of a bi-level program (hypergradient for the magnitude) and an orthogonality regularizer on the direction
methods.mergeable_reason: Same final parameterization as DoRA, so it folds into a single dense matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: As DoRA: B = 0 and m = ||W_0|| per neuron.
methods.key_idea: Train DoRA's magnitude and direction asynchronously: the direction on the training split and the magnitude on a validation split via hypergradients, then refit the direction. This decouples the two further and reduces overfitting.
methods.results_note: Reports an 85.2 GLUE average on RoBERTa-base vs 84.6 for DoRA, a smaller train-test gap, and consistent gains over DoRA on NLU, NLG, token classification and extremely small biomedical datasets (Wilcoxon p = 2.4e-4 on GLUE).

relations.note: same parameterization, bi-level training

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.09758 (Qin, 2024) matches; TMLR (07/2025, OpenReview v2xCm3VYl4) confirmed on the PDF header. DoRA parameterization, Gram regularizer on V+Delta V, upper-level magnitude on the validation split, and Table 1 (85.2 vs 84.6) checked. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: code_url: added the official repository from the abstract
results_note: removed the unverified '14 datasets' count; restated the evaluated task families from the abstract
confidence: medium -> high (TMLR 07/2025 confirmed on the paper's first page)

methods.name: SSF
methods.paper_title: Scaling & Shifting Your Features: A New Baseline for Efficient Model Tuning
methods.formula_latex: y=\gamma\odot x+\beta\ \text{after each operation (MSA, MLP, LayerNorm)};\ \text{after a linear op: } W=\operatorname{diag}(\gamma)\,W_0,\ b=\gamma\odot b_0+\beta;\ W_0,b_0\ \text{frozen},\ \gamma,\beta\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: 2d\ \text{per SSF-wrapped operation}
methods.locus: after every operation of a ViT block (attention, MLP, LayerNorm)
methods.structure: a per-channel affine map (diagonal scaling plus shift), i.e. an action of the diagonal affine group (R^x)^d semidirect R^d on output channels, re-parameterizable into the preceding linear layer
methods.mergeable_reason: The paper re-parameterizes (gamma, beta) into the preceding linear/conv weight and bias, so inference runs the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: gamma ~ N(1, 0.02) and beta ~ N(0, 0.02) in the official code (init_ssf_scale_shift): close to, but not exactly, the identity.
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning a pretrained vision backbone can be reduced to learning a per-channel scale and shift of its features. These fold back into the weights, so there is no inference overhead.
methods.results_note: With ViT-B/16, reports 90.72% on FGVC and 73.10% on VTAB-1k (about 0.3M trainable parameters), above full fine-tuning (88.54% and 65.57%).

relations.note: per-channel scaling, plus a shift, for vision models
SSF's shift is a bias update; SSF adds a multiplicative scale
GLoRA reports SSF as a special case of its unified formulation

Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: RED
methods.paper_title: Advancing Parameter Efficiency in Fine-tuning via Representation Editing
methods.formula_latex: h_2=l_{scaling}\odot h_1+l_{bias},\ h_1=\text{output of each FFN sub-layer};\ \text{equivalently } W_{down}=\operatorname{diag}(l_{scaling})\,W_{down}^{0},\ b=l_{scaling}\odot b^{0}+l_{bias};\ \text{model frozen},\ l_{scaling},l_{bias}\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: 2dL
methods.locus: outputs of the FFN sub-layer in every Transformer layer (ablations also edit Q, K, V)
methods.structure: per-channel affine edit (diagonal scaling plus shift) of each FFN's contribution to the residual stream; the same algebraic form as SSF, applied to LLM FFN outputs
methods.mergeable_reason: The scaling always folds into the FFN down-projection; the shift folds into its bias only if that layer has one (LLaMA-style down-projections have no bias, so a bias term must be added).
methods.identity_at_init: l_scaling = 1 and l_bias = 0.
methods.key_idea: Instead of adding modules, edit hidden representations directly with one scaling vector and one bias vector per layer. This uses about 25,700x fewer parameters than full fine-tuning and about 32x fewer than LoRA, with no rank to tune.
methods.results_note: Comparable to or better than full fine-tuning and other PEFT methods on GLUE (RoBERTa, T5), E2E NLG (GPT-2) and LLaMA-2 instruction tuning (AlpacaEval) with far fewer parameters.

Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: DiffFit
methods.full_name: DiffFit (bias tuning plus learnable residual scaling for diffusion transformers)
methods.paper_title: DiffFit: Unlocking Transferability of Large Diffusion Models via Simple Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: x\leftarrow x+\gamma_1\odot\mathrm{Attn}(x),\quad x\leftarrow x+\gamma_2\odot\mathrm{FFN}(x),\ \gamma_1,\gamma_2\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ (\text{init } \mathbf{1});\ \text{trained: } \gamma,\ \text{biases, normalization parameters, class embedding; all other weights frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 0.12\%\ \text{of DiT-XL/2 (0.83M of 673.8M)}
methods.locus: learnable scales gamma on the residual branches of the first 14 DiT-XL/2 blocks, plus QKV-linear and final layers; all biases, normalization parameters and the class embedding are also tuned
methods.structure: diagonal scaling of each residual branch's output (foldable into the branch's output projection) combined with BitFit-style selective tuning of biases and normalization parameters
methods.mergeable_reason: gamma folds into the output projection weight and bias of the attention/FFN branch; the tuned biases and norms replace the old ones.
methods.identity_at_init: gamma = 1, and biases and norms start from their pretrained values.
methods.key_idea: For diffusion transformers, tuning the biases plus a learnable per-channel scale on each residual branch is enough to transfer quickly to new domains and resolutions.
methods.results_note: About 2x faster training than full fine-tuning, storing about 0.12% of the parameters; FID 3.02 on ImageNet 512x512 after 25 epochs from a 256x256 checkpoint.

relations.note: bias tuning plus added scaling factors
per-channel scaling of features in vision transformers
