methods.name: LieRA
methods.full_name: Lie-group Rank Adaptation (Lie-group-based generalized tensor PEFT)
methods.paper_title: Generalized Tensor-based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Lie Group Transformations
methods.formula_latex: W=W_0\odot\exp_{\odot}(\Delta W)\approx W_0+W_0\odot\Delta W\ \ (\text{first-order form used in all experiments}),\quad \Delta W=BA\ (\text{LoRA-factorized; conv kernels are treated as tensors}),\ \exp_{\odot}\ \text{entry-wise};\ W_0\ \text{frozen (non-zero entries)},\ B,A\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: linear layers and higher-order (convolutional) kernels
methods.structure: action of the abelian Lie group of entry-wise non-zero tensors under the Hadamard product (identity = all-ones tensor) on W_0. The update lives in its Lie algebra (all real tensors) and is mapped back through the entry-wise exponential; truncating at first order gives W_0 + W_0 ⊙ Delta W.
methods.mergeable_reason: The trained first-order update W_0 + W_0 (.) BA (or W_0 (.) exp(BA)) is a fixed tensor of the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (A Gaussian), so exp(0) = 1 and W = W_0.
methods.key_idea: Treat parameters as elements of a Lie group under element-wise multiplication. Matrix PEFT updates (LoRA-style) then lift to high-dimensional (conv) tensors without flattening, via the exponential map from the Lie algebra.
methods.results_note: Reports gains over LoRA, e.g. a 75.5 vs 74.1 VTAB-1K average with ConvNeXt-V2-B (r=16), plus improvements on COCO detection, LLaMA commonsense reasoning and GLUE.

relations.note: LieRA's evaluated first-order form W_0 + W_0 (.) BA is HiRA's parameterization (concurrent work)
Delta W in the Lie algebra is LoRA-factorized

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2504.00851 (Si, 2025) matches; ICCV 2025 confirmed (arXiv comment, CVF proceedings per Semantic Scholar). Hadamard Lie group, entry-wise exponential, the first-order approximation W + W (.) Delta W and B=0/A Gaussian init checked in Sec. 4. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: code_url: added the repository linked in the abstract (github.com/Chongjie-Si/Subspace-Tuning)
formula: stated that the paper integrates the first-order approximation (Eq. 8) with LoRA for all experiments
results_note: the VTAB-1K numbers are for ConvNeXt-V2-B
relations: hira type generalizes -> equivalent-to
mergeable_reason: now refers to the first-order update that is actually trained

methods.name: FLoRA
methods.full_name: Fast LoRA (batched, example-specific multiplicative low-rank adaptation)
methods.paper_title: Batched Low-Rank Adaptation of Foundation Models
methods.formula_latex: W_i=W_0\odot(B_iA_i),\quad h_i=\operatorname{reduce}_{j=1..r}\Big[b^{(i)}_j\odot\big(W_0\,(a^{(i)}_j\odot x_i)\big)\Big]\ (\text{the paper uses a reduction such as torch.mean over the } r \text{ terms}),\ B_i=[b^{(i)}_1,\dots,b^{(i)}_r]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_i^{\top}=[a^{(i)}_1,\dots,a^{(i)}_r]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{in}\times r}\ \text{per example/adapter } i;\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapter}
methods.locus: linear layers, with per-request adapters in multi-tenant serving
methods.structure: entry-wise (Hadamard) modulation of W_0 by a rank-r matrix. The rank-1 case is a two-sided diagonal scaling diag(b) W_0 diag(a), an action of the torus (R^x)^{d_out} x (R^x)^{d_in}; rank r is a sum of r such scalings, so a batch with different adapters needs only element-wise operations around one shared matmul.
methods.mergeable_reason: For a fixed adapter, W_0 ⊙ BA can be precomputed; the point of the method is to keep it unmerged so different examples in a batch can use different adapters.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified in the method section read. The parameterization reproduces W_0 only when B_iA_i is the all-ones matrix (e.g. rank-1 all-ones vectors), not with LoRA's B = 0.
methods.key_idea: Make each request's adapter multiply W_0 entry-wise. A minibatch with heterogeneous adapters can then be served with cheap element-wise operations around one shared matmul, giving better throughput and latency than batched LoRA.
methods.results_note: Reports about 2x throughput over LoRA on StarCoder-15B when each request needs a different low-rank adapter, while keeping LoRA-level accuracy on MultiPL-E multilingual code generation and on multilingual speech recognition (Whisper).

relations.note: the paper describes IA3 as a 'rank 0.5' special case that rescales only columns
same parameter count, multiplicative instead of additive, built for heterogeneous batching
HiRA's J + BA modulation is a FLoRA modulation of rank <= r+1

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2312.05677 (Wen & Chaudhuri, 2023) matches; ICLR 2024 (oral) confirmed in the ICLR 2024 accepted-paper data. W_i = Delta W_i o W_0 with Delta W_i = B_i A_i and the 'rank 0.5' IA3 connection checked in Sec. 3. No initialization is stated. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: formula: the paper combines the r rank-one terms with a dimension reduction such as torch.mean, not a plain sum
results_note: added the 2x StarCoder-15B throughput figure and the speech-recognition experiment from the paper

methods.name: Quantum-PEFT
methods.paper_title: Quantum-PEFT: Ultra parameter-efficient fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + U\Lambda V^{\top},\quad U=Q_P(\theta_U)\,I_{d_{out}\times K},\ V=Q_P(\theta_V)\,I_{d_{in}\times K},\ \Lambda=\mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\in\mathbb{R}^{K\times K},\ Q_P=\prod_{l=1}^{L}\Big(\big(I\otimes\mathrm{CZ}^{\otimes\frac{q-1}{2}}\textstyle\bigotimes_{k=2}^{q}\mathrm{RY}(\theta_{k,2l+1})\big)\big(\mathrm{CZ}^{\otimes\frac{q-1}{2}}\textstyle\bigotimes_{k=1}^{q-1}\mathrm{RY}(\theta_{k,2l})\otimes I\big)\Big)\textstyle\bigotimes_{k=1}^{q}\mathrm{RY}(\theta_{k,1}),\ q=\log_2 d;\ \theta_U,\theta_V,\lambda\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: (2L+1)(\log_2 d_{in}+\log_2 d_{out})-4L+K\ \ \text{(Pauli parameterization: } (2L+1)\log_2 N-2L \text{ per unitary, plus } K \text{ diagonal entries)}
methods.locus: same targets as LoRA (attention/linear layers of language and vision transformers)
methods.structure: SVD-form update whose orthogonal factors are quantum-circuit (Pauli) parameterizations: Kronecker products of 2 x 2 RY rotations interleaved with diagonal \pm1 CZ entanglers, so parameters grow logarithmically in d.
methods.mergeable_reason: U Λ V^T is a dense matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not stated explicitly in the sections consulted (AdaLoRA-style SVD form; a zero diagonal Λ would give ΔW = 0).
methods.key_idea: Parameterize the singular-vector frames by a small quantum circuit, so trainable parameters scale like log d instead of d.
methods.results_note: Reports orders of magnitude fewer trainable parameters than the lowest-rank LoRA with competitive accuracy on language and vision transfer benchmarks.

relations.note: same UΛV^T SVD-form update
both build orthogonal matrices from products of sparse/Kronecker-structured factors
both quantum-circuit-inspired tensor networks
logarithmic instead of linear parameter growth
both use Stiefel-frame x core factorizations; Quantum-PEFT generates the frames from a small Lie-group parameterization
both use an SVD-shaped P Lambda Q additive update

methods.verification_notes: ICLR 2025 Poster confirmed (arXiv comment, OpenReview, proceedings); Eq. 2 and parameter count checked from the arXiv HTML; init not stated in the paper.
corrections: formula_latex: replaced the simplified circuit by the paper's Eq. 2 (two RY layers per entangling layer plus an initial RY layer)
trainable_params: exact count from Sec. 4.1 instead of an O(.) bound

methods.name: P-Tuning v2
methods.full_name: P-Tuning v2 (deep prompt tuning for NLU)
methods.paper_title: P-Tuning v2: Prompt Tuning Can Be Comparable to Fine-tuning Universally Across Scales and Tasks
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{head}^{(l)}=\mathrm{Attn}\big(XW_q^{(l)},\,[P_k^{(l)};XW_k^{(l)}],\,[P_v^{(l)};XW_v^{(l)}]\big)\ \ \forall l\le L,\quad \hat y=\mathrm{softmax}(W_{\mathrm{cls}}\,h_{\mathrm{tok}});\ \ P^{(l)}\ (\text{optionally } \mathrm{MLP}\text{-reparametrized}),\ W_{\mathrm{cls}}\ \text{trained};\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2L\ell d+d\,|\mathcal{Y}|\ \ (\approx 0.1\%\text{--}3\%\ \text{of the model})
methods.locus: keys/values at every layer (deep prompts) plus a randomly initialized linear head on token representations
methods.structure: Learned key/value vectors prepended at every layer (identical parameter shape to prefix-tuning), with a linear classification head instead of a verbalizer, task-dependent prompt length (short for classification, ~100 for sequence labeling) and optional reparametrization / multitask initialization.
methods.mergeable_reason: Same as prefix-tuning: \ell extra key/value slots per layer that cannot be folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; random initialization, optionally a multitask-pretrained prompt as initialization.
methods.key_idea: Inserting prompts at every layer (not just the input) gives more capacity and more direct influence on predictions, making prompt tuning match fine-tuning even for 300M-scale models and for hard sequence-labeling tasks.
methods.results_note: Matches fine-tuning across model scales from 300M to 10B parameters and on hard sequence tagging (NER, extractive QA, SRL) while tuning 0.1%-3% of parameters.

relations.note: Self-described implementation of deep prompt tuning (Li & Liang 2021; Qin & Eisner 2021) adapted to NLU.
Prompt tuning is the input-layer-only special case.
Alternative PEFT method for NLU (not compared in the P-Tuning v2 paper; prefix-tuning vs. LoRA is compared by He et al. 2022).

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.07602 confirmed; published as ACL 2022 short paper 2022.acl-short.8 under the shortened title 'P-Tuning: Prompt Tuning Can Be Comparable to Fine-tuning Across Scales and Tasks'. HF has no separate P-Tuning v2 class: deep prompts are PrefixTuningConfig (its PrefixEncoder is adapted from THUDM/P-tuning-v2, and the PEFT v0.4.0 README listed P-Tuning v2 under Prefix Tuning); the linear classification head is not part of the PEFT config.
corrections: hf_peft_config: normalized to the bare config class name (deep-prompt detail moved to verification_notes)
relations[lora]: note corrected: P-Tuning v2 does not compare against LoRA; kept as a generic PEFT competitor

methods.name: WARP
methods.paper_title: WARP: Word-level Adversarial ReProgramming
methods.formula_latex: P_\Theta(y\mid x)=\frac{\exp\big(\Theta^{V}_{y}\cdot f(T_{\Theta^P}(x))\big)}{\sum_{i\in C}\exp\big(\Theta^{V}_{i}\cdot f(T_{\Theta^P}(x))\big)},\quad \Theta^P\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{(prompt embeddings inserted by template } T\text{ around a [MASK])},\ \Theta^V\in\mathbb{R}^{|C|\times d}\ \text{(verbalizer embeddings)}\ \text{trained; MLM body frozen}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence (template positions around a [MASK] token) and the output verbalizer vectors of the MLM head
methods.structure: Adversarial reprogramming in word-embedding space: learned input embeddings at template positions plus learned class vectors that replace output-embedding rows of the masked-LM head (an input-side and an output-side reprogramming map around a frozen body).
methods.mergeable_reason: Prompt embeddings lengthen the input; only the verbalizer vectors act like a (new) linear head.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; prompt tokens initialized with the [MASK] embedding or embeddings similar to the vocabulary; verbalizers from the MLM head.
methods.key_idea: Treat task adaptation as adversarial reprogramming: search continuous prompt and verbalizer embeddings by SGD so a frozen masked LM's [MASK] prediction solves the task.
methods.results_note: With up to 25K trainable parameters per task on RoBERTa-large it reaches 81.6 on the GLUE test leaderboard, beating submissions with up to three orders of magnitude more trainable parameters; strong few-shot SuperGLUE results with ALBERT.

relations.note: Concurrent continuous-prompt method; adds learned output verbalizers.
Same adversarial-reprogramming principle in text embedding space vs. pixel space.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2101.00121 and 2021.acl-long.381 confirmed; probability formula with f(T_{Theta^P}(x)) and verbalizer embeddings Theta^V checked against Sec. 3; initialization ([MASK] or word-like embeddings; verbalizers from the MLM head) checked in Sec. 3.2. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: PPT
methods.paper_title: PPT: Pre-trained Prompt Tuning for Few-shot Learning
methods.formula_latex: P^\star=\arg\min_{P}\ \sum_{(X,Y)\in\mathcal{D}_{\text{self-sup}}}-\log\Pr_\theta\big(Y\mid[P;X]\big)\ \text{(unified pre-training tasks built from unlabeled text)};\ \ \text{then prompt tuning on the target task initialized at } P^\star;\ \theta\ \text{frozen throughout}
methods.trainable_params: \ell d
methods.locus: input embedding sequence
methods.structure: Vanilla soft prompt whose initialization is obtained by pre-training the prompt alone on self-supervised tasks cast in the same formats as downstream tasks (sentence-pair, multiple-choice, single-sentence classification, or a unified multiple-choice format).
methods.mergeable_reason: At inference it is an ordinary soft prompt that lengthens the input.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; the contribution is the initialization itself (a prompt pre-trained on the PLM's own pre-training-style objective).
methods.key_idea: Prompt tuning fails in few-shot regimes mainly because of poor initialization, so pre-train the soft prompt on large unlabeled corpora using task formats that mirror downstream classification.
methods.results_note: With T5-XXL and CPM-2 (~11B), tuning pre-trained prompts reaches or exceeds full-model fine-tuning in both full-data and few-shot settings, far above vanilla prompt tuning in few-shot.

relations.note: Same parameterization; adds prompt pre-training as initialization.
Self-supervised prompt pre-training versus supervised source-task transfer.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2109.04332 and 2022.acl-long.576 confirmed; the three pre-training formats and the unified multiple-choice format are in Sec. 3; results claim matches the abstract (full-data and few-shot). Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: SPoT
methods.paper_title: SPoT: Better Frozen Model Adaptation through Soft Prompt Transfer
methods.formula_latex: P_{s}=\arg\min_P\mathcal{L}_{s}\big([P;X]\big),\quad P_{t}^{(0)}\leftarrow P_{s^\star},\quad P_t^\star=\arg\min_P\mathcal{L}_{t}\big([P;X]\big);\ \ s^\star=\arg\max_s\cos\Big(\tfrac1\ell\textstyle\sum_i e^{s}_i,\ \tfrac1\ell\sum_j e^{t}_j\Big)\ \text{(early-checkpoint prompts as task embeddings; a per-token average cosine is the alternative metric)};\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \ell d
methods.locus: input embedding sequence
methods.structure: Vanilla soft prompt initialized from a prompt trained on a source task (or multi-task mixture); early-checkpoint prompts double as task embeddings whose cosine similarity predicts transferability for source retrieval.
methods.mergeable_reason: At inference it is an ordinary soft prompt.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; initialization from a source-task prompt is the method.
methods.key_idea: Soft prompts are transferable task representations: train them on source tasks, use them to initialize target prompts, and use prompt similarity as a cheap task-similarity metric to choose sources.
methods.results_note: Across all T5 sizes, SPoT matches or outperforms full model tuning on SuperGLUE while using up to 27,000x fewer task-specific parameters; a 26-task, 160-pair transfer study shows widespread positive transfer.

relations.note: Same parameterization; adds source-to-target prompt initialization.
ATTEMPT mixes many source prompts per instance instead of picking one for initialization.
MPT distils many source prompts into one shared prompt.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.07904 and 2022.acl-long.346 confirmed; task similarity uses either the cosine of average-pooled prompt tokens (shown in the formula) or the per-token average cosine (Sec. 4); 27,000x and 26-task/160-pair figures confirmed. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: formula_latex: noted the paper's second similarity metric (per-token average cosine)

methods.name: ATTEMPT
methods.paper_title: ATTEMPT: Parameter-Efficient Multi-task Tuning via Attentional Mixtures of Soft Prompts
methods.formula_latex: P_{\mathrm{inst}}(X)=P_{\mathrm{tgt}}+\sum_{j=1}^{t+1}a_j(X)\,P_j,\quad a_j=\frac{\exp(\hat P_j^{\top}H_{\mathrm{out}}/T)}{\sum_{k=1}^{t+1}\exp(\hat P_k^{\top}H_{\mathrm{out}}/T)},\quad H_{\mathrm{out}}=\mathrm{LN}\big(W_{up}^{\top}\,\mathrm{SiLU}(W_{down}^{\top}\hat X)\big),\ P_{t+1}=P_{\mathrm{tgt}};\ \ \text{input }[P_{\mathrm{inst}}(X);X];\ \text{train } P_{\mathrm{tgt}},W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r},W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d};\ \text{source prompts } P_{1..t}\ \text{and LM frozen}
methods.trainable_params: d\big(\ell+2(r+1)/N\big)\ \text{per task (attention module shared across } N \text{ target tasks)}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence (instance-specific prompt)
methods.structure: Instance-wise softmax mixture (a point of the simplex) over a library of frozen source prompts plus the trainable target prompt, added to the target prompt; mixture weights come from a bottleneck network on the max-pooled input (\hat X, \hat P_j are max-pooled).
methods.mergeable_reason: The prompt depends on the input instance and lengthens the sequence; it can never be folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; source prompts pre-trained by prompt tuning on large source tasks, target prompt newly initialized.
methods.key_idea: Treat pre-trained soft prompts as modular knowledge units and learn, per input, an attention-weighted interpolation of them with a new target prompt, sharing the router across tasks.
methods.results_note: On 21 datasets with T5-base, significantly outperforms prompt tuning and matches or beats full fine-tuning and other PEFT methods that use over 10x more parameters, while updating ~2,300x fewer parameters than fine-tuning.

relations.note: SPoT picks one source prompt for initialization; ATTEMPT mixes all sources per instance.
Source and target prompts are vanilla soft prompts.
Alternative multitask prompt-transfer scheme.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2205.11961 and 2022.emnlp-main.446 confirmed; Eqs. (3)-(4), the max-pooled inputs, SiLU, LayerNorm, and the per-task parameter count d(m+2(r+1)/N) checked in Sec. 3.2-3.4. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: relations: removed 'l2p' (no head-to-head comparison or citation; different problem settings (multi-task NLP transfer vs. rehearsal-free continual learning), so 'competes-with' was unjustified)

methods.name: DePT
methods.paper_title: DePT: Decomposed Prompt Tuning for Parameter-Efficient Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{input } \big[P_s;\ E_X+AB\big],\quad P_s\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell'\times d},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times r},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ E_X\in\mathbb{R}^{s\times d}\ \text{frozen word embeddings of the input padded to the maximum length } s;\ \ \ell' d+(s+d)r=\ell d;\ \ A\sim\mathcal{N},\ B=0;\ \text{learning rates } \alpha_1(P_s)\gg\alpha_2(A,B);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \ell' d+(s+d)\,r
methods.locus: input embedding sequence: a shorter soft prompt plus a position-wise offset to the input token embeddings
methods.structure: Short soft prompt (concatenation) plus a rank-r additive, position-indexed offset AB to the frozen s\times d input-embedding matrix, i.e. a LoRA-style low-rank update applied to the input activation matrix rather than to a weight (the paper writes the product as BA; dimensionally it is the s\times d matrix A B).
methods.mergeable_reason: The short prompt still lengthens the input; the positional offset AB could only be folded into absolute position embeddings, which T5-style relative-position models lack.
methods.identity_at_init: The low-rank offset is zero at init (B=0); the short prompt is not an identity.
methods.key_idea: Trade prompt length for a low-rank update of the input embeddings: same parameter budget, shorter sequences, so lower time/memory, trained with two learning rates.
methods.results_note: Across 23 NLP and vision-language tasks, outperforms vanilla prompt tuning and other PEFT methods (sometimes full fine-tuning) while saving over 20% training/inference time and memory relative to prompt tuning with T5-Base.

relations.note: Splits the prompt budget between a shorter prompt and a low-rank embedding offset.
Imports the BA low-rank, zero-initialized update, applied to the input embedding matrix.
Both are low-rank prompt decompositions evaluated on the same 23-task suite.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2309.05173 confirmed, ICLR 2024 per arXiv comment. Eq. (2) is written W_i + BA with A in R^{s x r}, B in R^{r x d}; dimensionally the s x d update is AB (kept). Budget l x d = m x d + (s+d) x r, Gaussian A / zero B, and two learning rates checked in Sec. 2.2. Code repo moved to github.com/ShiZhengyan/DePT. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: formula_latex: s is the maximum (padded) sequence length in the paper, not the length of a given input
code_url: repository was renamed; GitHub redirects ZhengxiangShi/DePT to ShiZhengyan/DePT

methods.name: Residual Prompt Tuning
methods.paper_title: Residual Prompt Tuning: Improving Prompt Tuning with Residual Reparameterization
methods.formula_latex: P'_i=\Phi(P_i)=\mathrm{LN}\big(\mathrm{ReLU}(P_iW_{down})\,W_{up}\big)+P_i,\ \ i=1,\dots,\ell\ \ (P_i\ \text{a row vector});\ \ \text{input }[P';X];\ \ \text{train } P\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d},\ W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times m},\ W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d},\ \mathrm{LN};\ \text{after training store only } P'=\Phi(P);\ W_0\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \ell d+2dm+2d\ \text{(training: prompt, } W_{down},W_{up}\text{ and LayerNorm, as counted in the paper)};\ \ \ell d\ \text{(stored)}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence
methods.structure: Soft prompt reparametrized through a shared bottleneck MLP with LayerNorm and a residual skip, applied token-wise; the reparametrization is discarded after training (an over-parameterization that only changes the optimization geometry).
methods.mergeable_reason: At inference only the projected prompt P' remains, which still lengthens the input.
methods.identity_at_init: No model-level identity; the residual skip lets each virtual token choose between its free embedding and the shared projection, improving robustness to learning rate and initialization.
methods.key_idea: Prompt tuning is unstable because prompt tokens are optimized independently; a shared residual MLP couples them and speeds and stabilizes training at no inference cost.
methods.results_note: Significantly outperforms prompt tuning on SuperGLUE with T5-Large, T5-Base and BERT-Base (e.g., +7 points with T5-Base), allows 10x shorter prompts without loss, and helps in few-shot settings.

relations.note: Same inference-time object; different training parameterization.
Prompt-encoder reparametrization, with an added skip connection.
Inherits the MLP-reparametrization trick used for prefixes.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.03937 and 2023.findings-acl.421 confirmed. Paper writes W_down in R^{d x m}, W_up in R^{m x d} (row-vector convention) and counts 2dm+2d reparametrization parameters (Appendix A.6). Baselines include PT w/ MLP (Li & Liang) and PT w/ LSTM (P-Tuning), SPoT and ATTEMPT. Not in HF PEFT.
corrections: formula_latex: matched the paper's shapes W_down in R^{d x m}, W_up in R^{m x d} (row-vector convention) and listed the trainable LayerNorm
trainable_params: added the 2d LayerNorm parameters counted in the paper (Appendix A.6)

methods.name: LPT
methods.paper_title: Late Prompt Tuning: A Late Prompt Could Be Better Than Many Prompts
methods.formula_latex: h^{(l^\ast)}\leftarrow\big[p(x);\,h^{(l^\ast)}\big],\quad p(x)=W_2\,\mathrm{ReLU}\big(\mathrm{Pool}_{n\to\ell}(W_1h^{(l^\ast)}+b_1)\big)+b_2\ \ (\text{pooling generator}),\ \ \text{or}\ \ p(x)=\mathrm{Reshape}\big(W_2\,\mathrm{ReLU}(W_1h_{[\mathrm{CLS}]}+b_1)+b_2\big)\ (\text{naive});\ \ W_1\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times d};\ \text{single insertion layer } l^\ast\ (\text{e.g. 13 of 24});\ \text{backbone frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 2dm+m+d\ \ \text{(pooling generator)};\ \ \approx dm+\ell dm\ \ \text{(naive generator)}
methods.locus: hidden-state sequence at a single intermediate layer
methods.structure: Instance-dependent prompt generated by a bottleneck MLP (with optional pooling from input length n to prompt length ℓ) from the hidden states just below the insertion layer, inserted once at an intermediate layer.
methods.mergeable_reason: The prompt is input-dependent and adds tokens to the upper half of the network.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity.
methods.key_idea: There is a trade-off between how far the label signal must propagate back to the prompt and how much the prompt can influence outputs; a single 'late' prompt in a middle layer, generated from the instance's own hidden states, balances both and skips backprop through the lower layers.
methods.results_note: Competitive with full model tuning and other PEFT methods in full-data and few-shot settings (RoBERTa-large among backbones), with faster training and lower memory than prompt tuning.

relations.note: Instance-dependent prompt generation, moved to an intermediate layer and fed by in-network hidden states.
Same budget class; inserts later to shorten the gradient path.
One late prompt instead of prompts at every layer.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2210.11292 and 2022.findings-emnlp.95 confirmed; naive (Eqs. 1-2) and pooling (Eqs. 3-4) prompt generators with W_1 in R^{m x d} checked; insertion at layer 13 of RoBERTa-large confirmed; S-IDPG-PHM is a baseline. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: IDPG
methods.paper_title: IDPG: An Instance-Dependent Prompt Generation Method
methods.formula_latex: W_p(T,x)=G\big(M(x),T\big)=W_2\,\sigma\big(W_1M(x)+b_1\big)+b_2\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d},\quad \hat y=\mathrm{softmax}(W h_{[\mathrm{CLS}]}),\ h_{[\mathrm{CLS}]}=M\big(\mathrm{concat}[x,W_p(T,x)]\big);\ \ W_{1,2}\ \text{PHM-factorised as } \textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes B_i;\ M\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: m(d+1)+\ell d(m+1)\ \text{(dense generator)}+\text{classification head};\ \ \text{generator reduced by }\approx n\times\text{ with PHM layers (e.g. 1.5M}\to\text{105K)}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence (optionally multiple layers, M-IDPG)
methods.structure: Two-layer bottleneck hypernetwork mapping a frozen sentence embedding M(x) to an ℓ-token prompt; its second-layer bias is exactly a task-level soft prompt, so the generated prompt = task prompt + instance-dependent part; weights parameterized as sums of Kronecker products (PHM).
methods.mergeable_reason: The prompt is input-dependent and requires an extra forward pass to compute M(x).
methods.identity_at_init: No identity.
methods.key_idea: Condition the soft prompt on each input sentence through a lightweight generator, recovering vanilla prompt tuning as the bias term.
methods.results_note: On ten NLU tasks with RoBERTa-large, consistently outperforms prompt-tuning baselines and is on par with Compacter while tuning far fewer parameters.

relations.note: The generator's second-layer bias is a task-specific prompt; zero first layer recovers prompt tuning.
Uses PHM (Kronecker-sum) layers from Compacter to compress the generator.
Both generate instance-dependent prompts.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2204.04497 and 2022.naacl-main.403 confirmed; Eqs. (1)-(3), the dense generator count m(d+1)+td(m+1), the bias-as-task-prompt remark, PHM compression (1.5M to 105K) and the trainable classification head W checked in Sec. 3. No code found. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.trainable_params: \rho\,\ell d,\ \ \rho<1\ \text{(fraction of tokens/pieces kept)}

methods.structure: Structured sparse mask on a soft prompt at two granularities (whole tokens, then equal-size pieces of each token embedding), found by gradient-sensitivity importance scores and lottery-ticket weight rewinding.
methods.mergeable_reason: The pruned prompt is still a prompt that lengthens the input.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; starts from a fully trained vanilla prompt (stage 1), then prunes and rewinds.
methods.key_idea: Some trained prompt tokens hurt the task; finding a 'winning ticket' sub-prompt by hierarchical structured pruning gives a smaller and better prompt.

methods.name: BBT
methods.paper_title: Black-Box Tuning for Language-Model-as-a-Service
methods.formula_latex: p=Az+p_0,\quad z^\star=\arg\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^{k}}\ \mathcal{L}\big(f(Az+p_0;\tilde X),\tilde Y\big),\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell d\times k}\ \text{fixed random},\ p_0\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell d}\ \text{(random vocab embeddings or an MNLI-pretrained prompt)};\ z\ \text{searched by CMA-ES with forward (API) queries only; model frozen, no gradients}

methods.structure: Soft prompt restricted to a random k-dimensional affine subspace p_0+\mathrm{col}(A) (intrinsic-dimension reparametrization), optimized by derivative-free CMA-ES.
methods.mergeable_reason: The result is a soft prompt that lengthens the input.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; z=0 gives the initial prompt p_0.
methods.key_idea: Because large PLMs have low intrinsic dimension, a soft prompt can be optimized in a small random subspace by gradient-free evolution strategies, using only inference API access (Language-Model-as-a-Service).

methods.name: VPT
methods.paper_title: Visual Prompt Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{Shallow: } [x_1,Z_1,E_1]=L_1([x_0,P,E_0]),\ [x_i,Z_i,E_i]=L_i([x_{i-1},Z_{i-1},E_{i-1}]);\quad \text{Deep: } [x_i,\_\,,E_i]=L_i([x_{i-1},P_{i-1},E_{i-1}]),\ i=1,\dots,L;\quad y=\mathrm{Head}(x_L);\ \ P,P_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{and Head trained; ViT frozen}

methods.locus: token sequence after the patch embedding (shallow) / input of every Transformer layer (deep)
methods.structure: Learned tokens inserted into the residual stream of a ViT. In VPT-Deep the prompt outputs are discarded after each layer, so their only effect on image tokens is as extra keys/values \mathrm{LN}(P_{i-1})W_k,\ \mathrm{LN}(P_{i-1})W_v: a prefix tied through the frozen projections (derived from the equations here).

methods.identity_at_init: No identity; prompts initialized with Xavier-uniform (class-prototype initialization was not better).
methods.key_idea: Transfer NLP prompt tuning to vision Transformers: a handful of learnable tokens per layer plus a head adapts a frozen ViT, often better than full fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: With ViT-B/16 (ImageNet-21k), VPT-Deep outperforms full fine-tuning on 20 of 24 tasks (FGVC + VTAB-1k) and all other PEFT protocols, while storing 0.04%/0.53% extra parameters per task (shallow/deep).

relations.note: VPT-Shallow is input-level prompt tuning transplanted to vision Transformers.
VPT-Deep equals a deep prefix whose keys/values are constrained to the image of the frozen LN+W_k, W_v projections.
VPT-Deep transfers deep prompt tuning (Li & Liang; P-Tuning v2, both cited) to vision Transformers.

methods.name: Visual Prompting
methods.paper_title: Exploring Visual Prompts for Adapting Large-Scale Models
methods.formula_latex: \max_{\phi}\ \log P_{\theta;\phi}\big(y\mid x+v_\phi\big),\quad v_\phi\ \text{a single pixel-space perturbation shared by all images (padding frame of width } p\text{, or a patch)};\ \ \theta\ \text{frozen; labels via CLIP text prompts}
methods.trainable_params: 2Cp(H+W-2p)\ \text{(padding)};\ \ Cp^{2}\ \text{(patch)}
methods.locus: input pixels
methods.structure: An additive translation of input space, x\mapsto x+v_\phi, supported on a border frame (or a patch).
methods.mergeable_reason: For a ViT with a fixed-location prompt (padding or fixed patch) the patch embedding E is linear, so E(x+v)=Ex+Ev and the per-patch constant Ev folds exactly into the positional embeddings (derived here, not claimed in the paper); the random-location patch variant cannot be merged, and CNN backbones would need a per-position bias map after the first convolution, which is not a standard parameter.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity at initialization: the official code initializes v_\phi with a standard normal (torch.randn); v_\phi=0 would recover the frozen model exactly.
methods.key_idea: Adapt a frozen vision model by learning a single input perturbation (adversarial reprogramming as prompting), with the output mapped to labels through text prompts for CLIP.
methods.results_note: Particularly effective for CLIP, where a padding prompt (p=30 best) is competitive with linear probing and robust to distribution shift.

relations.note: Adversarial reprogramming lineage, in pixel space.
Pixel-space prompts vs. token-space prompts.
Image-side vs. text-side learned prompting of a frozen CLIP for the same classification task (not compared head-to-head in Bahng et al.).

methods.name: CoOp
methods.paper_title: Learning to Prompt for Vision-Language Models
methods.formula_latex: t_i=[V]_1[V]_2\cdots[V]_{\ell}[\mathrm{CLASS}_i],\qquad p(y=i\mid x)=\frac{\exp\big(\cos(g(t_i),f(x))/\tau\big)}{\sum_{j=1}^{K}\exp\big(\cos(g(t_j),f(x))/\tau\big)};\ \ [V]_m\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{trained (unified or class-specific)};\ \text{CLIP encoders } f,g\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \ell d\ \text{(unified context)};\ \ K\ell d\ \text{(class-specific context)}
methods.locus: input embedding sequence of the CLIP text encoder
methods.structure: Soft prompt (shared or per-class context vectors) prepended to each class-name token sequence; the classifier weights are the frozen text encoder's images g(t_i) of the prompted class names.
methods.mergeable_reason: In closed-set classification the K prompted class embeddings g(t_i) are computed once after training and cached as a linear classifier, so inference costs exactly as much as zero-shot CLIP; the learned context itself cannot be folded into the text encoder's weights, and any new class name requires re-running the text encoder with the prompt.
methods.identity_at_init: Can be initialized from the embedding of a hand-crafted context such as 'a photo of a' (starting at the zero-shot classifier) or randomly.
methods.key_idea: Replace hand-engineered CLIP prompts by learnable context vectors optimized end-to-end through the frozen text encoder.
methods.results_note: On 11 image-recognition datasets, one or two shots suffice to beat hand-crafted prompts, and with 16 shots the average gain is around 15%.

relations.note: Prompt tuning applied to the text tower of a contrastive vision-language model.
CoCoOp with the meta-net output fixed to zero.
MaPLe with prompt depth J=1 and no vision prompts degenerates to CoOp.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2109.01134 confirmed; journal version IJCV 130:2337-2348 (2022), DOI 10.1007/s11263-022-01653-1 via Crossref. Prompt t_i=[V]_1...[V]_M[CLASS] and the cosine-softmax classifier checked. mergeable_reason: rewritten to separate the cached-classifier case from weight merging

methods.name: CoCoOp
methods.paper_title: Conditional Prompt Learning for Vision-Language Models
methods.formula_latex: v_m(x)=v_m+h_\theta\big(f(x)\big),\ \ t_i(x)=\{v_1(x),\dots,v_\ell(x),c_i\},\qquad p(y\mid x)=\frac{\exp\big(\mathrm{sim}(f(x),g(t_y(x)))/\tau\big)}{\sum_{i=1}^{K}\exp\big(\mathrm{sim}(f(x),g(t_i(x)))/\tau\big)};\ \ h_\theta=\text{Linear-ReLU-Linear (16}\times\text{ bottleneck)};\ \text{train } v_{1..\ell},\theta;\ \text{CLIP frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \ell d+\tfrac{d_v}{16}\,(d_v+d)\ \ (\text{plus biases; } d_v=\text{image-feature width})
methods.locus: input embedding sequence of the CLIP text encoder, conditioned on the image feature
methods.structure: Context vectors shifted by one image-conditioned token π=h_θ(f(x)) produced by a lightweight meta-network (an input-dependent translation of the shared prompt).
methods.mergeable_reason: Class embeddings depend on the image, so the text encoder must be re-run for all K classes per image (much higher inference cost than CoOp).
methods.identity_at_init: No identity; reduces to CoOp when h_θ outputs zero.
methods.key_idea: Static learned prompts overfit to base classes; making the prompt conditional on each image improves generalization to unseen classes and domains.
methods.results_note: Generalizes much better than CoOp to unseen classes within a dataset, and improves cross-dataset transfer and domain generalization across 11 datasets.

relations.note: Adds an instance-conditional shift to CoOp's context vectors.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2203.05557 confirmed (CVPR 2022 per arXiv comment). Meta-Net Linear-ReLU-Linear with a 16x bottleneck on the image feature and v_m(x)=v_m+pi checked in Sec. 3.2. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: MaPLe
methods.paper_title: MaPLe: Multi-modal Prompt Learning
methods.formula_latex: [\_\,,W_i]=L_i([P_{i-1},W_{i-1}]),\quad [c_i,E_i,\_\,]=V_i\big([c_{i-1},E_{i-1},F_{i-1}(P_{i-1})]\big),\ \ i=1,\dots,J;\quad \tilde P_k=F_k(P_k),\ F_k:\mathbb{R}^{d_l}\to\mathbb{R}^{d_v}\ \text{linear};\ \ \text{train } \{P_i\},\{F_i\};\ \text{CLIP frozen}
methods.trainable_params: J\ell d_l+J\,(d_ld_v+d_v)
methods.locus: token sequences of both the text and image encoders up to depth J (deep prompts)
methods.structure: Deep prompts in the language branch, with vision-branch prompts obtained as linear images F_k(P_k) of the language prompts (one shared parameter pushed forward into both modalities, coupling their gradients).
methods.mergeable_reason: Vision-branch prompts add tokens to every image forward pass (the text side alone could be cached).
methods.identity_at_init: No identity.

Deep vision prompts (VPT-style) coupled to deep language prompts.
Main baseline.

(1)-(3) and the coupling P~_k = F_k(P_k) (linear d_l -> d_v, a separate F per layer) checked; with J=9, b=2, d_l=512, d_v=768 the parameter formula gives about 3.55M, matching the paper's Table 6. methods.name: L2P
methods.full_name: Learning to Prompt (prompt pool for continual learning)
methods.paper_title: Learning to Prompt for Continual Learning
methods.formula_latex: K_x=\arg\min_{\{s_i\}_{i=1}^{N}\subseteq[1,M]}\ \sum_{i=1}^{N}\gamma\big(q(x),k_{s_i}\big),\ \ q(x)=f(x)[0]\ \text{(frozen ViT [CLS])};\ \ x_p=[P_{s_1};\dots;P_{s_N};x_e];\ \ \min_{P,K,\phi}\ \mathcal{L}\Big(g_\phi\big(\mathrm{AvgPool}(f_r(x_p)[0{:}N\ell])\big),y\Big)+\lambda\sum_{s_i\in K_x}\gamma\big(q(x),k_{s_i}\big)
methods.trainable_params: M(\ell d+d_k)+\text{head}
methods.locus: input token sequence of a frozen ViT (prompts selected from a pool)
methods.structure: Key-value prompt memory \{(k_j,P_j)\}_{j=1}^M: input-conditioned hard top-N retrieval by cosine matching between a frozen-model query and learnable keys; the selected prompts are concatenated.
methods.mergeable_reason: Prompts are selected per input and lengthen the token sequence; the query also costs an extra frozen forward pass.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity.
methods.key_idea: For rehearsal-free continual learning, keep the backbone frozen and store knowledge in a pool of prompts that are retrieved per instance, so tasks share or separate prompts automatically without task identity at test time.
methods.results_note: Consistently outperforms prior state of the art in class-incremental, domain-incremental and task-agnostic continual learning (e.g., Split CIFAR-100, 5-datasets) and is competitive with rehearsal-based methods without any buffer.

relations.note: Each pool element is a soft prompt.
DualPrompt (same group) refines L2P with a shared G-prompt and task-specific prefix E-prompts at chosen layers.

corrections: relations: removed 'attempt' (no comparison or citation between L2P and ATTEMPT; 'competes-with' was unjustified)

methods.name: DualPrompt
methods.paper_title: DualPrompt: Complementary Prompting for Rehearsal-free Continual Learning
methods.formula_latex: h_g^{(i)}=f_{\mathrm{prompt}}\big(g,h^{(i)}\big),\ \ h_e^{(j)}=f_{\mathrm{prompt}}\big(e_t,h^{(j)}\big),\ \ f^{\mathrm{Pre\text{-}T}}_{\mathrm{prompt}}(p,h)=\mathrm{MSA}\big(h_Q,[p_k;h_K],[p_v;h_V]\big);\ \ t^\star=\arg\min_t\gamma\big(q(x),k_t\big);\ \ \min_{g,e_t,k_t,\phi}\ \mathcal{L}\big(f_\phi(f_{g,e_t}(x)),y\big)+\lambda\,\gamma\big(q(x),k_t\big)
methods.trainable_params: n_g\ell_g d+T\,(n_e\ell_e d+d)+\text{head}\ \ (n_g,n_e=\text{number of layers carrying G/E prompts};\ \ell_g,\ell_e\ \text{total prompt lengths, split into } \ell/2 \text{ key and } \ell/2 \text{ value vectors in prefix form})
methods.locus: keys/values (prefix form) of a few shallow (G-prompt) and middle (E-prompt) ViT layers
methods.structure: A task-invariant prefix g shared by all tasks at shallow layers plus a pool of task-specific prefixes e_t at deeper layers, the latter retrieved by key matching against a frozen-model query.
methods.mergeable_reason: Extra prefix key/value slots and input-dependent selection at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: No identity.
methods.key_idea: Split continual-learning knowledge into a general prompt and expert prompts attached at different depths, using prefix-style (key/value) attachment, which works better than prompt-token insertion for this purpose.
methods.results_note: Sets state of the art for rehearsal-free class-incremental learning and even outperforms methods with sizable rehearsal buffers; introduces the Split ImageNet-R benchmark.

relations.note: Adds a complementary shared G-prompt, prefix-style attachment and decoupled attachment depths to the L2P prompt-pool idea.
Uses prefix-tuning (Pre-T) as the attachment function and compares it with prompt-token insertion (Pro-T).

methods.name: Initial State Tuning
methods.full_name: Initial State Tuning (for state space models)
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of State Space Models
methods.formula_latex: h_t=\bar A_t h_{t-1}+\bar B_t x_t,\ \ y_t=C_th_t\ \ \text{run from } h_0=h'\ \text{instead of } 0\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \hat y_t=y_t+C_t\Big(\prod_{i=1}^{t}\bar A_i\Big)h',\quad h'\in\mathbb{R}^{H}\ \text{per channel trained; all SSM weights frozen}
methods.trainable_params: DH\ \text{per SSM layer}
methods.locus: initial hidden state of each SSM (e.g. Mamba S6) layer
methods.structure: Learned initial state of a linear recurrence. On S4, any prefix of virtual tokens acts only through h_{\mathrm{prefix}}=\sum_{i=0}^{\ell-1}\bar A^{i}\bar Bx_{-i}, so prefix-tuning is exactly an initial-state update (Prop. 1); conversely every initial state is realizable by a prefix iff \ell\ge H (under a genericity condition).
methods.mergeable_reason: No weight changes and per-token cost is unchanged, since SSM scan kernels accept an initial state natively, but the state is injected per sequence (in S6 its effect C_t(\prod_i\bar A_i)h' is input-dependent) and cannot be folded into W_0, exactly like a cached prefix.
methods.identity_at_init: h'=0 recovers the base model exactly.
methods.key_idea: For SSMs, the whole effect of prompt/prefix tuning is captured by the initial hidden state, so tune that state directly: an upper bound on prefix-tuning's expressivity at the same cost.
methods.results_note: On Mamba with <0.5% trainable parameters, initial state tuning outperforms prefix-tuning and prompt tuning on five of seven tasks, but LoRA consistently outperforms it.

relations.note: Galim et al. Prop. 1: on S4 every prefix acts as an initial-state update; the converse holds iff the prefix length is at least H (genericity assumption), so initial-state tuning upper-bounds prefix-tuning.
State-offset tuning removes the decaying coefficient ∏ A_i.
LoRA outperforms state-based tuning in Galim et al.'s benchmarks.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.09016 confirmed (ICML 2025 per arXiv comment). Prop. 1 (S4): every prefix equals an initial-state update, converse iff M >= H under a genericity assumption; initial-state tuning results in Table 14 (beats prefix/prompt tuning on 5 of 7 GLUE tasks, LoRA better). The S6 output formula with prod_i A_i is the form given in Kang et al. (2025) Table 1. Mergeability changed to no for consistency with prefix-tuning and Cartridges. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: State-offset Tuning
methods.paper_title: State-offset Tuning: State-based Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for State Space Models
methods.formula_latex: \hat y_t=y_t+C_t\,h'\ \ \text{(State-offset (h))},\qquad \hat y_t=y_t+y'\ \ \text{(State-offset (y))},\qquad h'\in\mathbb{R}^{H}\ \text{per channel},\ y'\in\mathbb{R}^{D};\ \text{SSM weights frozen}
methods.trainable_params: DH\ \text{(h variant)};\ \ D\ \text{(y variant) per SSM layer}
methods.locus: state readout at every timestep of each SSM (Mamba S6) layer
methods.structure: A constant learned offset added to the hidden state before readout at every step (Initial State Tuning with the time-varying factor \prod_i\bar A_i removed). In S6, C_th'=(W_Cx_t)^\top h', so the h-variant is a rank-\le H linear term in x_t; the y-variant is a bias on the SSM output.
methods.mergeable_reason: The offset enters before Mamba's multiplicative output gate (and as a linear term in x_t for the h-variant), so it cannot be absorbed into the existing diagonal skip or biases, although its cost is negligible.
methods.identity_at_init: h'=0 (or y'=0) recovers the frozen model exactly; the official code supports zero or Kaiming-uniform initialization of the offset parameters.
methods.key_idea: State-based PEFT for SSMs: instead of injecting external virtual tokens, add a learnable constant to the internal state at every timestep, giving a uniform rather than decaying effect.
methods.results_note: On Mamba-family models, State-offset Tuning (h) outperforms prompt-, prefix- and initial-state tuning and BitFit, and surpasses LoRA on most datasets; the (y) variant beats initial state tuning with 0.01% vs 0.23% of parameters.

Prompt-based methods underperform state-based ones on SSMs.
The y-variant is bias-like; reported to outperform BitFit.
Surpasses LoRA on most reported datasets.

Table 1 formulas y_t + C_t h' (h variant, DH params) and y_t + y' (y variant, D params) checked; 0.01% vs 0.23% parameter claim confirmed; BitFit and LoRA are baselines. methods.name: LQ-LoRA
methods.paper_title: LQ-LoRA: Low-rank Plus Quantized Matrix Decomposition for Efficient Language Model Finetuning
methods.formula_latex: \min_{Q\in\mathbb{Q}_{c},\,B,A}\big\lVert\sqrt{F}\odot\big(W_0-(Q+BA)\big)\big\rVert_F\ \ (F\equiv\mathbf 1\ \text{or diagonal empirical Fisher}):\ \ B^{(t)}A^{(t)}=\mathrm{SVD}_r(W_0-Q^{(t-1)}),\ \ Q^{(t)}=\mathrm{Quantize}_c(W_0-B^{(t)}A^{(t)}),\ Q^{(0)}=0;\ \ c=(\text{bits, block sizes})\ \text{per matrix from an ILP under a global bit budget};\quad h=(Q+BA)x,\ Q\ \text{frozen},\ A,B\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})
methods.locus: all linear layers of the transformer, each with its own NF quantization configuration
methods.structure: robust-PCA-style low-rank-plus-quantized decomposition W_0 \approx Q + BA; Q uses a per-matrix mixed-precision configuration chosen by integer linear programming; data-aware variant uses a row/column-scaled (Fisher-weighted) SVD
methods.mergeable_reason: The low-rank component is high-precision and can be folded only into a dequantized copy of Q; folding into the quantized Q needs re-quantization.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate: Q+BA is the alternating approximation of W_0 (stopped when the error rises). Since Q^{(0)}=0, the first low-rank component is the top-r SVD of W_0 itself, so the adapter starts on W_0's principal subspace rather than at zero.
methods.key_idea: Split each pretrained matrix into a fixed, easily quantized part and a trainable high-variance low-rank part. Integer linear programming then allocates bits across matrices to meet any target memory budget.
methods.results_note: Beats QLoRA and GPTQ-LoRA at matched bit budgets on LLaMA-2 (C4, OpenAssistant) and RoBERTa-large (GLUE). For example, 3.5-bit Fisher LQ-LoRA roughly equals 4.127-bit NF4 QLoRA, and a 2.75-bit LLaMA-2-70B (27GB) stays competitive with 16-bit.

relations.note: same Q+BA objective; differs in starting point (Q^{(0)}=0 vs BA=0), ILP bit allocation and Fisher weighting

methods.name: IR-QLoRA
methods.paper_title: Accurate LoRA-Finetuning Quantization of LLMs via Information Retention

methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})+2
methods.locus: all linear layers of LLaMA/LLaMA2; NF2-NF4 or integer-quantized base
methods.structure: LoRA with parameter-free 'elastic' shortcuts: \Delta W=\alpha(B+\beta_2E)(A+\beta_1P), where P\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}} averages r contiguous input groups and E\in\{0,1\}^{d_{out}\times r} repeats each of the r entries d_{out}/r times; still rank \le r. methods.key_idea: View quantize-then-LoRA through information retention. Calibration Quantization (ICQ) maximizes the entropy of the quantized weights so they keep more information. methods.structure: learned-step-size quantizer composed after a rank-r additive update: W=Q_{s,b}(W_0+\alpha BA); custom backward reuses \partial\mathcal L/\partial W_q so no weight-gradient buffer is stored

methods.name: PEQA
methods.paper_title: Memory-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Compressed Large Language Models via sub-4-bit Integer Quantization
methods.formula_latex: \hat W=\mathrm{diag}(s_0+\Delta s)\,\overline W_0,\quad \overline W_0=\mathrm{clamp}\big(\lfloor W_0/s_0\rceil+z_0,\,0,\,2^b-1\big)-z_0\ \ \text{(frozen integer codes)},\ \ s_0,z_0\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}};\ \ \text{only } s_0+\Delta s \text{ trained}

methods.locus: every linear layer of a weight-only (3-4 bit) quantized LLM
methods.structure: diagonal rescaling of the output rows of a frozen integer matrix: \hat W=\mathrm{diag}(s)\,\overline W_0 (group-wise: one scale per output row and input group); the integer codes never change
methods.mergeable_reason: The trained parameters are the quantization scales themselves, so the result is a standard quantized model with the same integer codes and kernels.
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta s = 0: the model starts as the RTN/OPTQ-quantized model whose scales s_0 minimize \lVert W_0-\hat W_0\rVert_F, so the starting point is close to but not exactly W_0.
methods.key_idea: Treat the quantization step sizes as the PEFT parameters. Freeze the integer codes and fine-tune only per-channel scales, so each task adapter is a tiny scale vector and the deployed model stays quantized.

methods.name: ApiQ
methods.paper_title: ApiQ: Finetuning of 2-Bit Quantized Large Language Model
methods.formula_latex: \min_{Q,A,B}\ \big\lVert W_0X-(Q+BA)X^{q}\big\rVert_F\ \ \text{(layer-wise; block-wise: } \lVert\mathcal F(W_s,X)-\mathcal F(Q_s,A_s,B_s,X^{q})\rVert),\ \ Q=q_b(W_0;\gamma,\beta)\ \text{with learnable clipping }(\gamma,\beta)\ \text{via STE},\ X^{q}=\text{inputs from the already-quantized preceding layers};\ \text{then fine-tune } h=(Q+BA)x,\ Q\ \text{frozen}

methods.structure: the same Q+BA shape as LoftQ, but fitted in activation space with calibration data, sequentially layer-by-layer or block-by-block so that quantization error does not accumulate with depth

methods.name: EfficientQAT
methods.paper_title: EfficientQAT: Efficient Quantization-Aware Training for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \text{Block-AP: }\min_{W,s,z}\lVert\mathcal F_{blk}(W_0,X)-\mathcal F_{blk}(Q_{s,z}(W),X)\rVert\ \text{block by block};\quad \text{E2E-QP: } \hat W=s\odot(\overline W-z),\ \overline W\ \text{frozen integers},\ \text{only step sizes } s \text{ trained end-to-end on the task loss}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}\,d_{in}/g\ \text{step sizes in E2E-QP (group size } g)

methods.structure: two stages: block-wise reconstruction training of all weights plus quantization parameters, then end-to-end training of group-wise multiplicative step sizes only (diagonal-per-group scaling of a frozen integer matrix)

methods.name: LoQT
methods.paper_title: LoQT: Low-Rank Adapters for Quantized Pretraining

methods.locus: all attention and MLP linear layers; used for both pre-training and fine-tuning
methods.structure: one-sided low-rank adapter with a frozen gradient-derived projector, W=W_Q+sPB with P the top-r left singular vectors of \nabla_W\mathcal L; periodically merged into the NF4 weight and re-quantized at exponentially growing intervals
methods.mergeable_reason: PB is periodically merged into the (quantized) full-rank weight, with a final merge at the end, so inference uses a plain dense or quantized matrix.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate: B is initialized to compensate the quantization error (B \approx P^{+}(W-q_{NF4}(W))) instead of 0; without quantization (LoQT-nq), B=0 gives exact identity.
methods.key_idea: Realize GaLore's projected step as a trainable adapter. Freeze a gradient-SVD projector P and train only B in W+PB; since \partial\mathcal L/\partial B=P^{\top}\nabla_W\mathcal L, Adam on B equals GaLore within a window. methods.name: GaLore
methods.paper_title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
methods.formula_latex: G_t=\nabla_W\mathcal L(W_t)\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}},\ \ P_t=U_{[:,1:r]}\ \text{of}\ \mathrm{SVD}(G_{t_0})\ \text{(refreshed every }T\text{ steps)};\ \ R_t=P_t^{\top}G_t\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ (M_t,V_t)=\mathrm{Adam}(R_t),\ N_t=M_t/(\sqrt{V_t}+\epsilon);\quad W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\alpha\,P_tN_t\ \ \text{(all of }W\text{ trained; no adapter; shown for } d_{out}\le d_{in}\text{, else project on the right)}

methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices of attention and MLP blocks (embeddings / LM head usually kept on standard Adam)
methods.structure: each step's update lies in an r-dimensional left subspace: \Delta W_t=-\eta\alpha P_tN_t with P_t\in\mathrm{St}(d_{out},r) the gradient's top singular vectors; the subspace switches every T steps, so the accumulated \sum_t\Delta W_t is high-rank

methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: training starts at W_0 with no reparameterization; the projector is initialized from the SVD of the first gradient.
methods.key_idea: Put the low-rank structure on the gradient rather than the weights. Project each gradient onto a periodically refreshed top-r singular subspace, run Adam there, and project back. This gives full-parameter learning with LoRA-like optimizer memory.

methods.name: Flora
methods.paper_title: Flora: Low-Rank Adapters Are Secretly Gradient Compressors
methods.formula_latex: \text{LoRA dynamics} \approx W_0-\eta\textstyle\sum_t G_tA_0^{\top}A_0\ \ (\text{random } A_0,\ \text{only } B \text{ moving});\ \ \text{Flora: } C_t=G_tA_t^{\top}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_t\sim\mathcal N(0,\tfrac1r)^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{regenerated from a seed, resampled every }\kappa\text{ steps};\ \ M_t=\beta M_{t-1}T_t+(1-\beta)C_t,\ \ T_t=A_{t-1}A_t^{\top}\ \text{at resampling steps (momentum transfer), else } T_t=I_r;\ \ W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\mathcal U(M_tA_t)\ \ (\mathcal U=\text{base optimizer, Adafactor in the paper})
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); compressed state } r\,d_{out}\ \text{per EMA / accumulator (+ a random seed for } A_t)
methods.locus: attention and feed-forward weight matrices (embeddings and vector parameters handled uncompressed); T5, GPT-2 (ViT in the appendix)
methods.structure: random-projection (Johnson-Lindenstrauss) compression of the gradient along its input dimension, C=GA^{\top}, decompressed by CA; resampling A_t makes the accumulated update high-rank; sublinear O(r\,d_{out}) state
methods.mergeable_reason: Flora is an optimizer that writes directly into W; no adapter is created.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: W starts at W_0; only optimizer states are compressed.
methods.key_idea: Under SGD with a small learning rate, LoRA's update is dominated by B moving under a nearly fixed random A_0, i.e. -\eta GA_0^{\top}A_0, which is random-projection compression of the gradient. Resampling the projection breaks LoRA's low-rank ceiling while keeping its sublinear memory for momentum and gradient accumulation.
methods.results_note: With Adafactor as base optimizer, Flora-compressed gradient accumulation matches full-matrix accumulation on T5 (XSum) and GPT-2 (IWSLT17 De-En) at reasonably large r, using only about 30% of its memory overhead for T5-3B / GPT-2-XL at r=256. Compressed momentum recovers or surpasses naive momentum when training from scratch, where LoRA lags badly.

relations.note: shows LoRA updates are approximately random-projection gradient compressors (parameter-side LoRA = optimizer-side compression)

LoRA-FA without its (A_0A_0^{\top})^{-1} gradient correction (v1) under SGD is Flora with a fixed, never-resampled projection; with the correction (v3) the fixed projection becomes the orthogonal projector onto row(A_0)
random (Flora) vs SVD-based (GaLore) gradient projections
APOLLO also relies on random projections, but only to estimate scaling factors

sources: added https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/hao24a.html

Eq. 20 / Thm 2.4 (A ~ N(0,1/r), C=GA^T, decompress CA), Algorithm 2 (transfer only on resampling, kappa interval), Adafactor base optimizer, and '30% of naive accumulation memory at r=256' for T5-3B/GPT-2-XL confirmed.

methods.name: Fira
methods.full_name: Fira (full-rank training under a low-rank constraint)
methods.paper_title: Fira: Can We Achieve Full-rank Training of LLMs Under Low-rank Constraint?
methods.formula_latex: R_t=P_t^{\top}G_t,\ \ W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,P_t\psi_t(R_t)-\eta\,\big(G_t-P_tR_t\big)\,\mathrm{diag}\big(\phi_t(R_t)\big),\ \ \phi_t(R_t)_i=\frac{\lVert\psi_t(R_{t,:,i})\rVert}{\lVert R_{t,:,i}\rVert}\ \text{(column-wise)};\ \ \text{limiter: if } \lVert S_t\rVert/\lVert S_{t-1}\rVert>\gamma,\ S_t\leftarrow\gamma\lVert S_{t-1}\rVert\,S_t/\lVert S_t\rVert,\ \ S_t=(G_t-P_tR_t)\,\mathrm{diag}(\phi_t(R_t))
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight, full-rank gradient); optimizer state } \approx 2r\,d_{in}+r\,d_{out}\ \text{(as GaLore)}
methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices; pre-training and fine-tuning
methods.structure: GaLore's Adam-in-subspace term plus the out-of-subspace gradient residual (I-P_tP_t^{\top})G_t rescaled column-wise by the low-rank Adam norm ratio, with a relative norm-growth limiter
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only method; updates go directly into W.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Adam's effect on gradient norms (the norm ratio before and after correction) is nearly the same in a low-rank subspace and in full rank. Fira reuses the cheap low-rank ratio to scale the discarded residual gradient, giving full-rank updates at low-rank memory, and adds a norm-growth limiter against loss spikes.
methods.results_note: Beats LoRA and GaLore in LLaMA pre-training and fine-tuning, matching or exceeding full-rank training. In LLaMA-7B pre-training it uses 8x less optimizer-state memory than GaLore and outperforms it by a large margin.

relations.note: setting the residual scale \phi_t\equiv0 recovers GaLore
concurrent use of channel-wise l2-norm-ratio scaling; APOLLO derives it from structured learning rates with random projections

corrections: sources: added https://openreview.net/forum?id=7aSBAw7tJf
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.01623 (Chen, 2024) confirmed; NeurIPS 2025 poster (arXiv comment, OpenReview). Eq. 10 (norm-based scaling of G-PR), Eq. 11 (column-wise phi) and Eq. 12 (norm-growth limiter on S_t) match the formula; 8x smaller optimizer-state memory than GaLore for LLaMA 7B confirmed.

methods.name: APOLLO
methods.full_name: Approximated Gradient Scaling for Memory-Efficient LLM Optimization
methods.paper_title: APOLLO: SGD-like Memory, AdamW-level Performance
methods.formula_latex: R_t=P_tG_t,\ P_t\sim\mathcal N_{seed}(0,\tfrac1r)^{r\times d_{out}}\ \text{(resampled every }T);\ \ (M^R_t,V^R_t)=\mathrm{AdamW}(R_t),\ \tilde R_t=M^R_t/(\sqrt{V^R_t}+\epsilon);\ \ s_j=\frac{\lVert\tilde R_t[:,j]\rVert_2}{\lVert R_t[:,j]\rVert_2}\ \text{(APOLLO; APOLLO-Mini: one tensor-wise } s=\lVert\tilde R_t\rVert/\lVert R_t\rVert,\ r=1);\quad W_{t+1}=W_t-\eta\,\alpha\,G_t\,\mathrm{diag}(s)-\eta\lambda W_t
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); optimizer state } 2r\,d_{in}\ \text{(}r=1\text{ for APOLLO-Mini, i.e. } 2d_{in}\text{: SGD-like)}
methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices of attention and MLP (optim_target_modules)
methods.structure: structured (channel-wise or tensor-wise) learning-rate scaling: the raw full-rank gradient is right-multiplied by a diagonal matrix diag(s) whose entries are estimated from Adam states kept in a random r-dimensional sketch
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only method; produces an ordinary dense checkpoint.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: AdamW's element-wise adaptive learning rate is redundant and can be coarsened to one rate per channel or per tensor. Those few scaling factors can be estimated from Adam run inside a cheap random projection without SVD, even of rank 1.
methods.results_note: Matches or beats AdamW in LLaMA 60M-7B pre-training (up to 2.8 lower validation perplexity) at near-SGD memory, with about 3x throughput on 8xA100 from larger batches. APOLLO-Mini plus weight quantization pre-trains LLaMA-7B in 12GB.

relations.note: inherits the low-rank auxiliary space idea, but uses it only to estimate scaling factors and replaces SVD with random projection
same l2-norm-ratio channel scaling form, derived from a different principle
both reduce Adam's second-moment state to block-shared learning rates
both use seed-regenerated random projections of the gradient; APOLLO uses them only to estimate channel-wise scaling factors and lists Flora among baselines with performance trade-offs

corrections: relations: -> flora-opt builds-on -> competes-with (APOLLO cites Flora as a competing optimizer, not as its basis)
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2412.05270 (Zhu, 2024) confirmed; MLSys 2025 (arXiv comment, DBLP conf/mlsys). Algorithm 1 (P ~ N(0,1/r) in R^{r x m}, R=PG, channel-wise s_j=||R~[:,j]||/||R[:,j]||, APOLLO-Mini rank 1 tensor-wise with alpha=sqrt(128), W <- W - eta alpha G S - eta lambda W), state 2nr+2, 2.8 perplexity, ~3x throughput with 4x batch on 8xA100, 7B under 12GB all confirmed. transformers optim='apollo_adamw'.

methods.name: Online Subspace Descent
methods.paper_title: Memory-Efficient LLM Training with Online Subspace Descent
methods.formula_latex: W_{t+1}=W_t+P_t\,\phi_t(\hat S_t),\ \ \hat S_t=\psi_t\big(\hat S_{t-1},P_t^{\top}\nabla\mathcal L(W_t)\big);\ \ P_{t+1}=\mathrm{OptimizerP.step}\big(P_t,\nabla_P\mathcal L_{G_t}(P_t)\big),\ \ \mathcal L_{G}(P)=\lVert PP^{\top}\tilde G-\tilde G\rVert^2+\lambda\lVert P^{\top}P-I_r\rVert^2,\ \tilde G=G/\lVert G\rVert
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{(full weight); optimizer state in the } r\text{-dim subspace plus } P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{(and its optimizer state)}
methods.locus: all 2-D weight matrices; LLaMA pre-training (60M-7B)
methods.structure: projected optimizer whose projector P_t evolves continuously by one online-PCA gradient step per iteration (no SVD); any Hamiltonian-descent optimizer (SGD, momentum, Lion, Adam) can run inside the subspace
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only method; updates go directly into W.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Replace GaLore's periodic SVD with streaming online PCA on the projector. A Hamiltonian-descent (Lyapunov) analysis then gives the first convergence guarantee for arbitrary projector update rules.
methods.results_note: In LLaMA 60M-7B pre-training on C4 it reaches lower perplexity and better downstream scores than other low-rank training methods, narrowing the gap to full-rank baselines.

relations.note: GaLore is the special choice of projector rule P_{t+1}=\chi_t(\cdot)= top-r left singular vectors of the current gradient, recomputed every T steps (paper Sec. 3.2)
SVD-free memory-efficient optimizer

methods.name: Adam-mini
methods.paper_title: Adam-mini: Use Fewer Learning Rates To Gain More
methods.formula_latex: \theta=(\theta_{b})_{b\in\mathcal B}\ \text{(blocks = smallest dense Hessian sub-blocks: q,k by head; v, attn.proj, MLP by output neuron; embed/output by token)};\ \ m_b\leftarrow\beta_1m_b+(1-\beta_1)g_b,\ \ v_b\leftarrow\beta_2v_b+(1-\beta_2)\,\mathrm{mean}(g_b\odot g_b)\in\mathbb{R},\ \ \theta_b\leftarrow\theta_b-\eta\,m_b/(\sqrt{v_b}+\epsilon)
methods.trainable_params: \text{all parameters; second-moment state reduced from } d_{out}d_{in} \text{ to at most } d_{out}\ \text{scalars per matrix (one per block: per head for } W_q,W_k\text{, per output neuron otherwise)}
methods.locus: all parameters; Hessian-structure-aware partition of Transformer weights
methods.structure: block-wise shared adaptive learning rate: Adam's per-coordinate v is replaced by one scalar per Hessian block (more than 99.9% of v removed)
methods.mergeable_reason: Optimizer-only method; trains the original parameters directly.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Transformer Hessians are near block-diagonal, and one good learning rate per dense block is enough. Adam-mini keeps momentum but stores one second-moment scalar per block, halving Adam's optimizer memory.
methods.results_note: On par with or better than AdamW for 39M-13B models in pre-training, SFT and RLHF, with 50% less optimizer memory and 49.6% higher throughput for Llama 2-7B pre-training on 2xA800.

relations.note: both coarsen Adam's element-wise learning rates into structured ones
alternative way to shrink optimizer state for full-parameter training

Partition principle (q,k by heads; v, attn.proj, MLP by output neurons; embed/output by tokens), v_b=(1-beta2) mean(g_b^2)+beta2 v_b (Algorithm 1, with bias correction and decoupled weight decay omitted here), >=99.9% of v removed, 49.6% throughput on 2xA800 confirmed.

methods.name: MeZO
methods.paper_title: Fine-Tuning Language Models with Just Forward Passes
methods.trainable_params: \text{all } d \text{ parameters (or a PEFT subset such as LoRA / prefix); optimizer memory } O(1)\text{: one scalar and one seed}
methods.locus: all parameters (full-parameter) or the parameters of a PEFT module
methods.structure: SPSA zeroth-order estimate: a rank-one random projection zz^{\top}\nabla\mathcal L of the gradient, obtained from a finite difference of two forward passes; perturbations regenerated from a random seed so no extra memory is stored
methods.mergeable_reason: MeZO only changes how updates are computed; the trained parameters are the model's own (or a standard PEFT module).
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Classical ZO-SGD can run in place by regenerating Gaussian perturbations from a seed, so fine-tuning costs only inference memory. Good pre-training gives a low effective Hessian rank, so convergence does not degrade with parameter count.
methods.results_note: With one A100-80GB it fine-tunes a 30B model where backprop fits only 2.7B. It is comparable to backprop fine-tuning on many tasks (OPT up to 66B) with up to 12x memory reduction, works with LoRA and prefix-tuning, and can optimize non-differentiable objectives.

relations.note: MeZO can optimize LoRA parameters (MeZO-LoRA)
MeZO can optimize prefix parameters (MeZO-prefix)
the SPSA estimate zz^{\top}\nabla\mathcal L is a rank-one random projection of the vectorized gradient, a forward-only analogue of Flora's random gradient compression
both target full-parameter fine-tuning at near-inference memory (forward-only vs fused-backward SGD)

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.17333 (Malladi, 2023) confirmed; NeurIPS 2023 oral (arXiv comment). SPSA estimator with z ~ N(0,I) regenerated from a seed, 30B on one A100-80GB vs 2.7B for backprop, up to 12x memory reduction, OPT up to 66B, LoRA/prefix compatibility confirmed.

methods.name: LOMO
methods.paper_title: Full Parameter Fine-tuning for Large Language Models with Limited Resources
methods.formula_latex: \text{during backprop, as soon as } g_i=\nabla_{\theta_i}\mathcal L \text{ is computed: } \theta_i\leftarrow\theta_i-\eta\,g_i,\ \text{then free } g_i\ \ \text{(fused gradient computation + SGD update; no optimizer state; gradient memory } O(\max_i|\theta_i|))
methods.trainable_params: \text{all parameters; optimizer state } 0,\ \text{gradient buffer} = \text{largest single tensor}
methods.locus: all parameters (full-parameter fine-tuning)
methods.structure: plain SGD whose per-tensor update is fused into the backward pass (layer-wise gradient release), plus gradient normalization and dynamic loss scaling for mixed precision
methods.mergeable_reason: Trains the original parameters directly; no extra modules.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: For fine-tuning, SGD works well enough to drop Adam's states entirely. Fusing each tensor's update into backpropagation also removes the full gradient buffer, leaving parameters and activations as the only memory.
methods.results_note: Combined with other memory-saving techniques it cuts memory to 10.8% of the DeepSpeed baseline, enabling full-parameter fine-tuning of a 65B model on one machine with 8x RTX 3090 (24GB).

relations.note: both target full-parameter fine-tuning with minimal memory
alternative memory-efficient full-parameter fine-tuning

methods.name: AdaLomo
methods.full_name: Low-memory Optimization with Adaptive Learning Rate
methods.paper_title: AdaLomo: Low-memory Optimization with Adaptive Learning Rate
methods.formula_latex: \text{fused in backprop, per matrix } \theta_i\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}:\ r_{t}=\beta r_{t-1}+(1-\beta)(g_t^{2})\mathbf 1_n,\ \ c_t=\beta c_{t-1}+(1-\beta)\mathbf 1_m^{\top}(g_t^{2}),\ \ v_t=r_tc_t/(\mathbf 1_m^{\top}r_t);\ \ u_t=g_t/\sqrt{v_t},\ \ \hat u_t=\frac{u_t}{\max(1,\mathrm{RMS}(u_t))}\max(\epsilon,\mathrm{RMS}(\theta_{t-1})),\ \ \theta_t=\theta_{t-1}-\alpha_t\hat u_t
methods.trainable_params: \text{all parameters; optimizer state } d_{out}+d_{in}\ \text{per matrix (factored second moment), no momentum}
methods.locus: all parameters (full-parameter instruction tuning and (further) pre-training)
methods.structure: rank-one non-negative factorization of the second-moment matrix (Adafactor-style row/column statistics) with grouped RMS update normalization, fused into the backward pass
methods.mergeable_reason: Trains the original parameters directly.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Of Adam's two ingredients, the adaptive learning rate matters more than momentum for closing LOMO's gap to AdamW. AdaLomo adds a factored, sublinear-memory second moment and a grouped normalization compatible with fused, single-pass backward updates. (The paper's Algorithm 1 line 10 prints u=g/v; the official implementation lomo_optim/adalomo.py uses g/\sqrt{v} via rsqrt, as written here.)
methods.results_note: Matches AdamW in instruction tuning, further pre-training and from-scratch pre-training of LLaMA models with LOMO-level memory.

relations.note: adds an adaptive learning rate to LOMO's fused update

methods.name: BAdam
methods.paper_title: BAdam: A Memory Efficient Full Parameter Optimization Method for Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \theta=(\theta_{\pi_1},\dots,\theta_{\pi_D})\ \text{(e.g. one block per transformer layer; ascending / descending / random order)};\ \ \theta_{\pi_i}^{t+1}\approx\arg\min_{\theta_{\pi_i}}\mathcal L\big(\theta_{\pi_{<i}}^{t+1},\theta_{\pi_i},\theta_{\pi_{>i}}^{t}\big)\ \text{via } K \text{ Adam steps; other blocks frozen; Adam state of } \theta_{\pi_i} \text{ discarded when switching}
methods.trainable_params: \approx|\theta|/D \text{ active at a time (FP32 copy, gradient, } m,v \text{ only for the active block); all parameters over a block-epoch. Memory } \approx 2M+16M/D \text{ GB for an } M\text{B-parameter model}
methods.locus: all parameters, cycled block by block (typically transformer layers)
methods.structure: block coordinate descent: a time-varying coordinate mask selecting one parameter block, optimized with K Adam steps per block, so the cumulative update is full-parameter and high-rank
methods.mergeable_reason: Trains the original parameters in place; the output is a standard dense model.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: Full-parameter fine-tuning at LoRA-like memory: only one block holds FP32 weights, gradients and Adam states at any time. Backpropagation can stop early at the active block, which also saves compute; convergence is proven in the deterministic case.
methods.results_note: Fine-tunes Llama 3-8B on a single RTX3090-24GB and Llama 3-70B on 4xA100-80GB. It outperforms LoRA on MT-bench and math benchmarks and is comparable to or better than full Adam.

methods.name: LISA
methods.paper_title: LISA: Layerwise Importance Sampling for Memory-Efficient Large Language Model Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{every } K \text{ steps sample active layers with } p=\{1,\tfrac{\gamma}{N_L},\dots,\tfrac{\gamma}{N_L},1\}\ \text{(embedding and LM head always on, } \gamma \text{ of } N_L \text{ middle layers)};\ \ \theta_{\ell}\leftarrow\mathrm{AdamW}(\theta_\ell)\ \text{for active } \ell,\ \text{all other layers frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \text{embedding + head + } \gamma \text{ transformer layers at a time (e.g. } \gamma=2);\ \text{all layers over training}
methods.locus: whole transformer layers (plus embedding and LM head), resampled periodically
methods.structure: stochastic block coordinate descent with a time-varying layer mask drawn by importance sampling; optimizer states exist only for the active layers
methods.mergeable_reason: Updates the original weights in place; no adapter.
methods.identity_at_init: Trivial: no reparameterization.
methods.key_idea: LoRA's update norms are heavily skewed toward the bottom and top layers. LISA mimics this by always training the embedding and head and randomly unfreezing a few middle layers, getting full-rank layer updates at LoRA-level memory.
methods.results_note: Beats LoRA by 10-35% on MT-Bench at similar or lower GPU memory, is on par or better on MMLU, AGIEval and WinoGrande, and beats LoRA on MT-Bench, GSM8K and PubMedQA with LLaMA-2-70B.

relations.note: BAdam is block coordinate descent with Adam and a convergence analysis; LISA is its randomized, importance-sampled counterpart.
Designed as a memory-equivalent but full-rank alternative to LoRA.
Alternative memory-efficient full-parameter optimizer (low-rank gradient projection instead of layer sampling).

methods.name: BitFit
methods.paper_title: BitFit: Simple Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning for Transformer-based Masked Language-models
methods.formula_latex: h = W_0 x + (b_0 + \Delta b),\quad W_0,\ g_{LN}\ \text{frozen};\ \text{trainable: every bias vector } \Delta b\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}} \text{ (Q/K/V/O, MLP and LayerNorm biases) plus the task head}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}\ \text{per linear layer (its bias)};\ \approx 0.08\text{--}0.09\%\ \text{of BERT parameters}
methods.locus: bias vectors only (attention Q/K/V/O, MLP, LayerNorm biases); LayerNorm gains and all weight matrices frozen
methods.structure: \Delta W = 0; only the translation part of each affine map h = Wx + b moves, i.e. a fixed, hand-specified coordinate mask on \theta that selects exactly the bias coordinates
methods.mergeable_reason: The tuned biases are the model's own bias parameters, so the fine-tuned model has exactly the original architecture and cost.
methods.identity_at_init: Biases start at their pretrained values (\Delta b = 0), so the function is unchanged at initialization.
methods.key_idea: Freezing all weights and fine-tuning only the additive bias terms (plus the classifier) of a pretrained Transformer is competitive with full fine-tuning on small and medium datasets; tuning only the query and middle-MLP biases (0.04% of parameters) loses little.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with BERT-base/large, bias-only tuning is comparable to full fine-tuning and to Diff Pruning/Adapters while training under 0.1% of parameters; it is strongest in small-to-medium data regimes.

relations.note: BEFT restricts bias tuning further, to the value-projection bias only.
