methods.name: Diff Pruning
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning with Diff Pruning
methods.formula_latex: \theta_\tau = \theta_0 + \delta_\tau,\quad \delta_\tau = z_\tau\odot w_\tau,\quad \min_{\alpha_\tau,w_\tau}\ \mathbb{E}_{z_\tau\sim p(z;\alpha_\tau)}\big[\mathcal{L}(\theta_0+\delta_\tau)\big] + \lambda\sum_i \sigma\!\big(\alpha_{\tau,i}-\log\tfrac{-l}{r}\big);\ \text{then keep the top } t\% \text{ of } |\delta_\tau| \text{ and re-train with the mask fixed; } \theta_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2\,d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{during training } (w,\alpha);\ \ \|\Delta W\|_0\approx 0.005\,d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{stored (0.5\% target)}
methods.locus: all pretrained parameters (embeddings, weight matrices, biases); structured variant groups gates per weight matrix / bias vector
methods.structure: learned sparse coordinate mask: \Delta W = Z\odot V with Z a stretched Hard-Concrete relaxation of a binary gate (differentiable L_0 penalty), projected onto an L_0 ball by magnitude pruning of the diff; optional group gates z^{g} shared within each weight matrix/bias vector
methods.mergeable_reason: The final diff vector is added to the pretrained parameters, giving an ordinary model of the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: w_\tau initialized to 0 so \delta_\tau = 0; gate logits \alpha_\tau initialized to 5 so that z \approx 1 at the start.
methods.key_idea: Treat fine-tuning as learning a task-specific diff vector added to frozen pretrained weights and make it sparse with a relaxed L0 penalty, so each new task costs only a small sparse vector.
methods.results_note: Structured Diff Pruning matches full fine-tuning of BERT-large on GLUE while modifying only 0.5% of parameters per task.

relations.note: FISH Mask precomputes the support from Fisher information instead of learning it, avoiding Diff Pruning's dense training memory.
LT-SFT obtains the support from the largest changes of a dense fine-tuning pass instead of a relaxed L0 gate.
Masking learns a binary mask on the weights themselves (W_0 \odot M); Diff Pruning learns a masked additive update W_0 + Z \odot V.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2012.07463 (Guo, 2020-12) and ACL 2021 (2021.acl-long.378) confirmed. Objective, stretched Hard-Concrete gate, expected-L0 term sigma(alpha - log(-l/r)) with l=-1.5, r=1.5, init w=0 / alpha=5, L0-ball magnitude projection and fixed-mask re-finetuning all match Sec. 3; structured groups are per matrix/bias vector (393 groups for BERT-large).

methods.name: FISH Mask
methods.paper_title: Training Neural Networks with Fixed Sparse Masks
methods.formula_latex: \hat F_i = \tfrac1N\sum_{n=1}^{N}\mathbb{E}_{y\sim p_\theta(y|x_n)}\big(\partial_{\theta_i}\log p_\theta(y|x_n)\big)^2,\quad M = \mathbb{1}\big[\hat F \ge \mathrm{sort}(\hat F)_k\big],\quad W = W_0 + M\odot\Delta W,\ \ \Delta W_{t+1} = \Delta W_t - \eta\,(M\odot\nabla_W\mathcal{L})
methods.trainable_params: k\ \text{in total (one global top-}k\text{ over all parameters, e.g. } k = 0.005\,|\theta|\text{)};\ \text{per-matrix counts vary because the mask concentrates in some layers}
methods.locus: any parameter; top-k diagonal-Fisher coordinates selected globally across the network (classifier always included)
methods.structure: fixed sparse coordinate mask chosen once before training as the top-k entries of the diagonal (empirical) Fisher information, then reused for all iterations
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing parameters change, so the result is a standard dense model of the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Training starts at the pretrained weights (\Delta W = 0); the Fisher is computed through the randomly initialized classifier before any training.
methods.key_idea: Estimate each parameter's importance by its diagonal Fisher information on a few samples, pick the top-k, and train only those with a mask that never changes.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with BERT, updating 0.5% of parameters with a FISH Mask matches standard training and outperforms Diff Pruning, Adapters and random/bias masks; also reduces communication in distributed training.

relations.note: Precomputed Fisher mask vs. learned L0-relaxed mask; FISH avoids Diff Pruning's extra training memory.
Child-Tuning_D (the task-driven variant) uses the same rule: a fixed mask of the top empirical-Fisher entries; the two papers are concurrent (2021).
PaFi replaces the Fisher criterion by a data-free, task-agnostic smallest-magnitude rule.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2111.09839 (Sung, 2021-11); NeurIPS 2021 confirmed in the proceedings listing. Eq. 3 (diagonal Fisher averaged over N samples, expectation over y ~ p_theta), the top-k rule {theta_i : F_i >= sort(F)_k}, classifier always included and Fisher computed through the random head all match Sec. 2. Selection is a single global top-k.
corrections: trainable_params: k is one global top-k over all parameters, so the per-matrix figure rho*d_out*d_in was not accurate; rewritten as a global count.
relations: restricted the equivalent-to note on child-tuning to its task-driven variant Child-Tuning_D (Child-Tuning_F is a random per-step mask).

methods.name: Child-Tuning
methods.paper_title: Raise a Child in Large Language Model: Towards Effective and Generalizable Fine-tuning
methods.formula_latex: w_{t+1} = w_t - \eta\,\frac{\partial\mathcal{L}(w_t)}{\partial w_t}\odot M_t;\quad \text{Child-Tuning}_F:\ M_t\sim\mathrm{Bernoulli}(p_F)\ \text{(kept gradients scaled by } 1/p_F);\quad \text{Child-Tuning}_D:\ M = \mathbb{1}\big[F^{(i)} \in \text{top-}p_D\big],\ F^{(i)} = \tfrac{1}{|D|}\sum_j\big(\partial_{w^{(i)}}\log p(y_j|x_j;w)\big)^2,\ \text{fixed for all } t
methods.trainable_params: \text{Child-Tuning}_D:\ p_D\,|\theta|\ \text{in total (one global top-}p_D\text{ Fisher threshold; per-matrix counts vary)};\ \ \text{Child-Tuning}_F:\ \text{expected } p_F\,|\theta|\ \text{per step, every entry can change over training}
methods.locus: all pretrained parameters (masks applied to gradients inside the optimizer, e.g. AdamW)
methods.structure: Hadamard gradient mask: a fixed top-p_D diagonal-Fisher mask (task-driven, genuinely selective) or a fresh Bernoulli(p_F) mask every step (task-free); the task-free variant accumulates a dense update and acts as a gradient-noise regularizer rather than a parameter-efficient method
methods.mergeable_reason: It only changes which existing parameters are updated; the fine-tuned network has the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights; no new parameters.
methods.key_idea: Update only a 'child network' of the pretrained model: a random Bernoulli subset each step acts as a variance-increasing regularizer favouring flat minima, while a Fisher-selected fixed subset targets task-relevant parameters.
methods.results_note: On GLUE, Child-Tuning outperforms vanilla fine-tuning by 1.5-8.6 average points across four PLMs (BERT, XLNet, RoBERTa, ELECTRA) and improves out-of-domain generalization.

relations.note: Child-Tuning_D's fixed top empirical-Fisher mask is the FISH Mask rule; concurrent 2021 works.
LT-SFT selects by largest change after dense fine-tuning rather than by Fisher information.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2109.05687 (Xu, 2021-09) and EMNLP 2021 (2021.emnlp-main.749) confirmed. Eq. 3 masked update, Bernoulli(p_F) mask with 1/p_F rescaling, empirical-Fisher Eq. 10 and the fixed C_0 = ... = C_T child network for the D variant all match Sec. 2. The official ChildTuningD.py takes one percentile over all parameters, so selection is global.
corrections: trainable_params: Child-Tuning_D thresholds the Fisher scores of all parameters at one global percentile (official ChildTuningD.py), so the count is p_D*|theta| overall, not p_D*d_out*d_in per matrix.
structure: added that Child-Tuning_F's per-step random mask accumulates a dense update (a training-procedure regularizer), so only Child-Tuning_D is selective in the sense of this family.

methods.name: LT-SFT
methods.paper_title: Composable Sparse Fine-Tuning for Cross-Lingual Transfer
methods.formula_latex: \text{Phase 1: } \theta^{(1)} = \mathrm{FT}(\theta^{(0)}),\ \mu = \mathbb{1}\big[\,|\theta^{(1)}-\theta^{(0)}| \in \text{top-}K\big];\ \ \text{Phase 2: reset to } \theta^{(0)},\ \text{train with } \mu\odot\nabla_\theta\mathcal{L},\ \phi = \theta^{(2)}-\theta^{(0)};\ \ \text{composition: } F(\cdot;\theta^{(0)}+\phi_T+\phi_L)
methods.trainable_params: K\ \text{in total (one global top-}K\text{; e.g. } K \approx 7.6\text{M} = 4.3\%\ \text{of mBERT for language SFTs, 0.25--8\% for task SFTs);\ per-matrix counts vary}
methods.locus: all Transformer parameters, including the input embeddings; for language SFTs the output embedding matrix is decoupled and frozen and LayerNorm parameters are frozen; the task classifier head is trained densely in both phases
methods.structure: sparse difference vector \phi supported on a lottery-ticket mask (top-K largest absolute change after a dense fine-tuning pass); SFTs act on the parameter space by translation, so they compose additively: S_L \circ S_T = translation by \phi_T + \phi_L
methods.mergeable_reason: Each SFT is a sparse vector added to the pretrained weights; any sum of SFTs is again a standard dense model.
methods.identity_at_init: Phase 2 restarts from the pretrained values (\phi = 0); optional L1 penalty \tfrac{\lambda}{N}\sum_i|\theta_i-\theta_i^{(0)}| keeps the deltas small.
methods.key_idea: Borrow the lottery-ticket recipe (train, select, rewind, retrain) to find a sparse set of parameters per language and per task; because the resulting deltas are sparse they can be added together with little interference, giving adapter-like modularity with full expressivity.
methods.results_note: In zero-shot cross-lingual transfer (POS, dependency parsing, NER, NLI) with mBERT/XLM-R, LT-SFT outperforms MAD-X adapters, e.g. +2.5 POS accuracy and +3.7 LAS.

relations.note: Same language-adapter/task-adapter composition scheme, but realised by adding sparse deltas instead of stacking adapters.
Same sparse-difference-vector formulation; the support is chosen by lottery-ticket selection.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.07560 (Ansell, 2021-10) and ACL 2022 (2022.acl-long.125) confirmed. Two-phase procedure, top-K |theta1-theta0| mask, masked-gradient phase 2, optional L1 term lambda/N sum|theta-theta0| and additive composition S_L o S_T all match Sec. 3. Selection is a global top-K.
corrections: locus: the paper does not exclude embeddings; it freezes the decoupled output embedding and LayerNorm parameters during language SFT (Sec. 4) and trains the classifier head densely.
trainable_params: K is a global top-K, so the per-matrix rho*d_out*d_in figure was replaced by the global count and the paper's K values.
relations: removed 'generalizes spiel' (wrong direction: SpIEL is the later method that scales sparse fine-tuning to LLMs; the lineage is already recorded as spiel builds-on lt-sft).

methods.name: SPT
methods.paper_title: Sensitivity-Aware Visual Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: s_n = \textstyle\sum_{c=1}^{C} g_{n,c}^2\ \ (g_{n,c} = \partial E/\partial w_n \text{ on sample } c;\ \text{one-step Taylor estimate of the loss reduction}),\ \ \mathcal{T} = \text{top-}\tau(s),\ M_{ij}=\mathbb{1}[W_{ij}\in\mathcal{T}];\quad W = \begin{cases} W_0 + BA, & \|M\|_0 \ge \sigma_{opt}\ \text{(structured tuning)}\\ W_0 + M\odot\Delta W, & \text{otherwise (unstructured tuning)}\end{cases}
methods.trainable_params: \|M\|_0\ \text{(unstructured) or } r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{(LoRA on sensitive matrices)},\ \text{under a global budget } \tau
methods.locus: ViT weight matrices; positions chosen per task by gradient-squared sensitivity
methods.structure: per-matrix choice between a sparse coordinate mask (top-\tau gradient-squared sensitivity) and a low-rank (LoRA) or adapter update on matrices that contain many sensitive entries
methods.mergeable_reason: SPT-LoRA and the unstructured part merge into W_0; the SPT-Adapter variant keeps inserted adapter modules.
methods.identity_at_init: Unstructured part starts at Delta W = 0; structured part uses the zero-initialized LoRA/adapter of the host method. Sensitivity is accumulated in one pass over C = 800 training samples before training (400 are shown to suffice).
methods.key_idea: Measure, per task and before training, how much tuning each pretrained weight would reduce the loss (approximated by its squared gradient), then spend the parameter budget there, upgrading heavily sensitive matrices to low-rank or adapter tuning.
methods.results_note: With ViT-B/16, SPT-Adapter/SPT-LoRA reach state of the art on FGVC and VTAB-1k (e.g. +4.2% and +1.4% mean top-1 over Adapter) and transfer to MAE/MoCo v3 backbones and segmentation.

relations.note: Structured branch is LoRA (or an adapter) applied only to the sensitive matrices.
GPS also selects by gradient magnitude on ViT but enforces K entries per neuron and stays purely sparse.
SPT's unstructured criterion (sum of squared gradients) is the empirical-Fisher diagonal that FISH Mask ranks by, derived independently via a Taylor argument; SPT does not cite FISH.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2303.08566 (He, Haoyu; 2023-03; comment 'ICCV 2023 Oral') and Crossref (ICCV 2023) confirmed. Sensitivity s_n = sum of squared per-sample gradients (Alg. 1, one-step Taylor argument, Eq. 1-3), top-tau budget, Eq. 5 switch to LoRA/adapter when the count of sensitive entries in a matrix reaches sigma_opt all match Sec. 3. Main experiments use C = 800 samples.
corrections: formula_latex: the sensitivity sums squared gradients over C samples (s_n = sum_c g_{n,c}^2); the old notation sum_c g_n^2 had no sample index.
identity_at_init: main experiments use C = 800 samples for the sensitivity (400 is the ablation showing it suffices), not ~400.
relations: fish-mask builds-on -> competes-with; SPT does not cite FISH Mask, it only arrives at the same squared-gradient score.

methods.name: PaFi
methods.full_name: PaFi (task-agnostic sparse fine-tuning of smallest-magnitude weights)
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning without Introducing New Latency
methods.formula_latex: M = \mathbb{1}\big[\,|W_0| \le \mathrm{sort}(|W_0|)_k\big]\ \text{(per matrix, data-free, shared by all tasks)},\quad W = W_0 + M\odot\Delta W;\ \text{norm-layer parameters fully trained, embeddings frozen}
methods.trainable_params: k\ \text{per matrix};\ \text{default } k = 0.005\,d_{out}d_{in}
methods.locus: every weight matrix and bias vector (group-wise bottom-k), plus all normalization parameters
methods.structure: fixed sparse coordinate mask on the k smallest-magnitude pretrained entries of each matrix; one universal mask for every downstream task
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing entries are changed in place, so inference uses the original dense model with no latency overhead.
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta W = 0 at the start; the mask needs no data or training.
methods.key_idea: The least important pretrained weights (smallest magnitude) are the safest to repurpose, so one data-free mask can be reused for every task, removing the task-specific mask-generation stage of sparse fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with RoBERTa-large, PaFi reaches 89.3 average (equal to full fine-tuning) with 0.5% trainable parameters, at least 1.3 points above Diff Pruning and FISH Mask.

relations.note: Replaces task-specific Fisher selection with a task-agnostic magnitude rule.
Super-Tuning's magnitude-only BottomK support is exactly a PaFi-style mask; its Wanda variant reweights |W| by activation norms.
Both store sparse deltas; PaFi needs only one mask for all tasks.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.16742 (Liao, 2023-05; comment 'ACL2023 camera-ready') and ACL 2023 (2023.acl-long.233) confirmed. Bottom-k |theta| mask chosen group-wise (each weight matrix or bias vector is a group), normalization layers fully trained, token/position embeddings frozen, 0.5% budget and GLUE 89.3 avg (= Full FT, vs 87.9 Diff Pruning / 88.0 FISH) all match Sec. 3-4.
corrections: code_url: canonical GitHub owner casing is BaohaoLiao/pafi_hiwi.

methods.name: SMT
methods.paper_title: SMT: Fine-Tuning Large Language Models with Sparse Matrices
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Delta W_M,\quad \mathrm{supp}(\Delta W_M) = \bigcup_{b\in\mathcal{B}} \text{block}_b,\ \ \mathcal{B} = \text{top-}m\ \text{of } \operatorname{mean}_{(i,j)\in b}\Big|\sum_{t\le T_w}\nabla_W\mathcal{L}_t\Big|_{ij}\ \text{over } l\times l \text{ blocks } (l=256)
methods.trainable_params: m_W\, l^2\ \text{per selected matrix } (m_W \text{ selected } l\times l \text{ blocks, } l=256;\ \text{blocks ranked jointly over all Q/K/V matrices});\ 0.84\%\text{--}4.91\%\ \text{of parameters in the experiments}
methods.locus: attention W_q, W_k, W_v (mainly W_v); MLP layers frozen
methods.structure: block-sparse mask: \Delta W is nonzero only on a set of selected l\times l sub-matrices (tiles), gathered into a dense m\times l\times l tensor so compute stays dense
methods.mergeable_reason: Updated sub-matrices are slices of the original weights; the fine-tuned model is a standard dense model.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights; blocks are chosen after a short gradient warm-up (about 25-100 iterations).
methods.key_idea: Select whole sub-matrices with the largest accumulated gradients during a short warm-up and update only those blocks, which keeps the sparsity hardware-friendly and avoids the rank plateau of low-rank methods.
methods.results_note: On commonsense and arithmetic reasoning with LLaMA-7B/13B, LLaMA2-7B and LLaMA3-8B, SMT outperforms DoRA (e.g. +3.0/+2.8 on commonsense for LLaMA-7B/13B) and does not plateau as the trainable budget grows.

relations.note: Block-sparse instead of low-rank update at matched budget; avoids LoRA's performance plateau at large rank.
Main baseline; SMT reports consistent gains over DoRA.
Both select by gradient magnitude; SMT selects contiguous blocks, SIFT individual entries.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2405.15525 (He, Haoze; 2024-05) exists under the title 'Sparse Matrix in Large Language Model Fine-tuning'; the ICLR 2025 camera-ready title used here is confirmed on the ICLR 2025 virtual site (poster 30274), which links OpenReview GbgCRJedQ7. Block score (mean |summed warm-up gradient| over 256x256 tiles), Q/K/V-only with MLP frozen, 100 (commonsense) / 25 (Math10K) warm-up steps match Sec. 3-4.
corrections: trainable_params: replaced 'typically <5%' with the budgets actually reported (0.84%-4.91%) and noted that blocks are ranked jointly across Q/K/V matrices.

methods.name: SpIEL
methods.full_name: Sparse Iterative Efficient Learning (sparse fine-tuning with drop-and-grow)
methods.paper_title: Scaling Sparse Fine-Tuning to Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \theta' = \theta + \mathrm{scatter}(\eta,\phi,d_\theta),\ \ \Delta W = \mathrm{reshape}(\mathrm{scatter}(\eta,\phi));\ \text{every } S \text{ steps: drop } \arg\mathrm{top}k(-|\phi|),\ \text{grow } \arg\mathrm{top}k\,\big|\hat{\mathbb{E}}_{x}[\nabla_\theta\mathcal{L}(x;\theta')]\big|\ \text{(SpIEL-AG) or by SM3 momenta (SpIEL-MA)}
methods.trainable_params: d_\phi = \rho\,d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{per matrix (same density for every tensor) plus } d_\phi \text{ indices}
methods.locus: all linear-layer weight tensors of an LLM (embeddings excluded)
methods.structure: dynamic sparse coordinate set: an index vector \eta and value vector \phi, updated by RigL-style drop (smallest |\phi|) and grow (largest accumulated gradient or approximate momentum); memory O(d_\phi)
methods.mergeable_reason: The final delta is scatter-added into the pretrained weights, producing a standard dense model.
methods.identity_at_init: \phi = 0 and \eta a random index subset (all of it is replaced at the first update).
methods.key_idea: Make sparse fine-tuning memory-efficient for LLMs by storing only indices and deltas and letting the support evolve during training through drop-and-grow, instead of computing a dense mask up front.
methods.results_note: Instruction-tuning LLaMA 2 7B/13B on Flan v2, GPT4-Alpaca and Tulu v2, SpIEL is often better than LoRA and (IA)^3 at comparable run time and is compatible with 4-bit quantization and SM3.

relations.note: Same group and sparse-delta formulation; removes the need for a dense first fine-tuning phase.
Main LLM-scale baseline.
SHiRA is concurrent; it uses a static mask whereas SpIEL's mask is dynamic.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2401.16405 (Ansell, 2024-01) confirmed. No venue found (not in ICML 2024/2025, NeurIPS 2024, ICLR 2024/2025 listings; Semantic Scholar lists arXiv), so venue stays arXiv. scatter-add parametrization (Eq. 5), equal density per parameter tensor, drop argtopk(-|phi|), grow by gamma-step accumulated gradients (AG) or SM3 momenta (MA), random initial eta fully replaced at the first update match Sec. 3. Embeddings are not adapted (listed as future work).

methods.name: GPS
methods.paper_title: Gradient-based Parameter Selection for Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: M_{ij} = \mathbb{1}\Big[j\in\text{top-}K_{j'}\ \big|\partial\mathcal{L}_{SCL}/\partial W_{0,ij'}\big|\Big]\ \text{for every output neuron (row) } i,\qquad W = W_0 + M\odot\Delta W,\ \ \Delta W_{t+1} = \Delta W_t - \epsilon\,\nabla_W\mathcal{L}\odot M
methods.trainable_params: K\,d_{out}\ \text{per matrix (K input connections per neuron; } \approx 0.36\%\ \text{on average)}
methods.locus: every weight matrix of the backbone (ViT, Swin, ConvNeXt), all layers; gradients computed with a supervised contrastive loss
methods.structure: row-balanced sparse mask: exactly K nonzeros in every row of \Delta W, so each neuron's activation can be adjusted through its K most gradient-relevant input connections
methods.mergeable_reason: Only selected entries of existing weights change; inference uses the unchanged architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights (\Delta W = 0); selection uses a supervised contrastive loss so that no randomly initialized head biases the gradients.
methods.key_idea: Pick, for every neuron, the few incoming weights with the largest task gradient, which spreads the budget over all layers instead of concentrating it at the top, and train only those.
methods.results_note: On FGVC and VTAB-1k with ViT-B/16, GPS improves over full fine-tuning by 3.33% and 9.61% mean accuracy while tuning 0.36% of parameters on average.

relations.note: Both are gradient-based selections for vision transformers; GPS stays purely sparse with per-neuron balancing.
FISH selects globally by squared gradients; GPS selects per neuron by gradient magnitude.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2312.10136 (Zhang, Zhi; 2023-12; journal-ref CVPR2024) and Crossref (CVPR 2024) confirmed. Per-neuron top-K input connections by |gradient| from a supervised contrastive loss (no random head), 0.36% average and +3.33 / +9.61 over full FT match Sec. 3-4.

methods.name: S²FT
methods.paper_title: S²FT: Efficient, Scalable and Generalizable LLM Fine-tuning by Structured Sparsity
methods.formula_latex: \Delta W = U_S V^{\top},\ \ U_S = [e_{a_1},\dots,e_{a_s}]\ \text{a frozen one-hot channel selector},\ V \text{ trainable};\ \text{in practice: the slices of } W_O \text{ belonging to selected heads } S_{MHA} \text{ and of } W_{down} \text{ belonging to selected FFN channels } S_{FFN}, \text{ co-permuted to be contiguous}
methods.trainable_params: s\cdot d\ \text{per adapted matrix (s selected channels, i.e. selected heads}\times d_h\text{ or FFN channels)}
methods.locus: output projection W_O (rows of the selected attention heads) and FFN down projection (selected channels) in every block; for LLaMA3-8B and Mistral-7B only the down projection is tuned because of grouped-query attention
methods.structure: structured (row/column-block) sparsity: \Delta W = U_S V^\top with U_S a fixed coordinate projection, i.e. a LoRA whose one factor is a frozen selection matrix; permutation invariance of coupled head/channel structures makes the trainable slice a dense block
methods.mergeable_reason: Updates are in-place on existing weight slices; alternatively the sparse delta can be kept as an unmerged adapter for fast switching and fusion.
methods.identity_at_init: Selected slices start at their pretrained values (\Delta W = 0); selection is random by default (S²FT-R) or by weight, activation, weight×activation or gradient magnitude.
methods.key_idea: Select sparsely but compute densely: choose a few attention heads and FFN channels, permute coupled weight matrices so they are contiguous, and back-propagate only through that dense slice.
methods.results_note: On LLaMA and Mistral models S²FT improves over other PEFT methods by 1.2-4.1% on commonsense and 0.6-1.9% on arithmetic reasoning, while saving up to 3x training memory and running 1.5-2.7x faster than full fine-tuning.

relations.note: Formally S²FT is rank-s adaptation \Delta W = U V^\top with U fixed to a coordinate selector instead of being learned.
Both are hardware-friendly structured sparse updates; SMT uses gradient-selected l\times l tiles, S²FT whole head/channel slices.
Reports better OOD generalization and serving scalability than LoRA.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2412.06289 (Yang, Xinyu; 2024-12) confirmed; NeurIPS 2024 confirmed in the proceedings listing. Delta W = U_S V^T with a frozen one-hot U_S (Sec. 4, 'a LoRA variant that fixes U_S'), random selection by default (S2FT-R), co-permutation of coupled structures, and the choice of the output and down projections all match the paper.
corrections: locus: added that for LLaMA3-8B and Mistral-7B the paper tunes only the down projection (multi-query/GQA attention).

methods.name: SIFT
methods.paper_title: Sparse is Enough in Fine-tuning Pre-trained Large Language Models
methods.formula_latex: \mathcal{S} = \text{top-}x\%\ \text{coordinates of } |g_1|\ (\text{gradient of the first batch(es)}),\quad W = W_0 + \Delta W,\ \ \mathrm{supp}(\Delta W)\subseteq\mathcal{S},\ \ \Delta W_{t+1} = \Delta W_t - \eta\,P_{\mathcal{S}}(\nabla_W\mathcal{L}_t)
methods.trainable_params: x\%\cdot d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{per adapted matrix (stored as values + indices)}
methods.locus: attention W_q, W_k, W_v, W_o by default
methods.structure: coordinate-subspace update: the gradient is projected onto the span of the top-|g| standard basis directions, and the increment is stored as a sparse (value, index) tensor filled via backward hooks
methods.mergeable_reason: The sparse increment is added into the existing weights.
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta W = 0; support fixed after the first batch.
methods.key_idea: Pre-training shifts the PAC-Bayes prior so that fine-tuning gradients become quasi-sparse (a few components carry most of the norm); hence updating only the top-gradient components is enough, implemented memory-efficiently with gradient hooks.
methods.results_note: With RoBERTa-large on GLUE (0.8% sparsity on Q/K/V/O) SIFT is competitive with LoRA and adapters, and when instruction-tuning LLaMA on Alpaca it is competitive with full fine-tuning and LoRA on MMLU and HumanEval.

relations.note: Both fix a gradient-statistics mask early; SIFT uses raw gradient magnitude from the first batch.
Entry-level vs. block-level gradient selection.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2312.11875 (Song, Weixi; 2023-12; comment 'ICML 2024 Spotlight') confirmed; PMLR v235 (song24e). Top-x% |gradient| support from the first batch(es), subspace update, hook-based (value, index) storage and Q/K/V/O targets at 0.8% on GLUE match Sec. 4-5.

methods.name: HiFT
methods.paper_title: HiFT: A Hierarchical Full Parameter Fine-Tuning Strategy
methods.formula_latex: \theta = (\theta_{G_1},\dots,\theta_{G_k})\ \text{(k groups of m layers)};\ \text{at step } t \text{ update only } \theta_{G_{\pi(t \bmod k)}} \text{ with any optimizer (others frozen, their optimizer states offloaded)};\ \text{learning rate advanced once per full cycle}
methods.trainable_params: \approx|\theta|/k\ \text{per step};\ \text{all parameters over one cycle}
methods.locus: groups of consecutive layers (embedding = bottom, head = top), iterated bottom2up, top2down or in a fixed random order
methods.structure: cyclic block-coordinate update over layer groups with delayed learning-rate schedule; accumulated \Delta W is dense
methods.mergeable_reason: It is full-parameter fine-tuning of the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained weights; no new parameters.
methods.key_idea: Achieve full-parameter fine-tuning with PEFT-like memory by updating one group of layers per step in a fixed cyclic order, keeping only that group's gradients and optimizer states on the GPU.
methods.results_note: HiFT matches PEFT and standard full fine-tuning across six models, reduces per-step trainable parameters by about 89% on average and fits full fine-tuning of 7B models in 24GB.

relations.note: Deterministic cyclic vs. randomized layer selection.

Both are block-coordinate full-parameter methods, but HiFT switches group every step and keeps the inactive groups' optimizer states (offloaded to CPU), whereas BAdam runs K Adam steps per block and discards the states when it switches.
Alternative memory-saving route (zeroth-order) that HiFT argues converges worse.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2401.15207 (Liu, Yongkang; 2024-01; arXiv comment still 'under progress') and EMNLP 2024 (2024.emnlp-main.1015) confirmed. One group per step, bottom2up/top2down/random orders, delayed learning-rate update, optimizer states moved to CPU, 89.18% fewer trainable parameters per step and 7B on 24 GB (mixed precision) match the ACL Anthology abstract and Sec. 3.
corrections: relations: badam equivalent-to -> competes-with; the update schedules and optimizer-state handling differ (1 step per group with offloaded states vs K Adam steps per block with states cleared).

methods.name: Surgical FT
methods.paper_title: Surgical Fine-Tuning Improves Adaptation to Distribution Shifts
methods.formula_latex: \theta = (\theta_{B_1},\dots,\theta_{B_n});\ \text{fine-tune only } \theta_{B_j} \text{ (one contiguous block), others frozen};\ \text{Auto-RGN: per-tensor learning rate } \propto \mathrm{RGN} = \|g\|_2/\|\theta\|_2 \text{ normalized to } [0,1]
methods.trainable_params: |\theta_{B_j}|\ \text{(one block of layers)}
methods.locus: one contiguous block of layers: first block for input-level shift, middle blocks for feature-level shift, last layer for output-level shift
methods.structure: layer-block coordinate mask: \Delta W nonzero only on the weights of one contiguous block (soft version: per-tensor learning rates from relative gradient norms)
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing layers are fine-tuned; architecture unchanged.
methods.identity_at_init: Starts from the pretrained (source) model; no new parameters.
methods.key_idea: Which layers to fine-tune should depend on where the distribution shift lives: tuning only early layers fixes input-level shifts, middle layers feature-level shifts, and the head output-level shifts, often beating full fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: Across seven real distribution shifts (e.g. CIFAR-C, ImageNet-C, Living-17, Entity-30, Waterbirds, CelebA) tuning a single block outperforms full fine-tuning, and Auto-RGN beats full fine-tuning without per-block search.

relations.note: Both choose layers to train; surgical FT fixes one block by shift type, LISA resamples layers during training.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2210.11466 (Lee, Yoonho; 2022-10; comment 'ICLR 2023') confirmed; listed on the ICLR 2023 virtual site. Single-block tuning, Auto-RGN (per-tensor RGN normalized to [0,1] times the base learning rate) and the input/feature/output-shift findings match Sec. 2-4. No official code link in the paper.
corrections: relations: removed competes-with bitfit; the paper targets distribution shift, never compares with BitFit, and the two share only 'tune a hand-picked subset'.

methods.name: Masking
methods.full_name: Learning binary weight masks instead of fine-tuning
methods.paper_title: Masking as an Efficient Alternative to Finetuning for Pretrained Language Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0\odot M_{bin},\quad (M_{bin})_{ij} = \mathbb{1}[m_{ij}\ge\tau],\quad m\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times d_{in}} \text{ trained with the straight-through estimator};\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{real-valued scores during training};\ d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{bits stored}
methods.locus: linear layers of selected Transformer blocks (top-down masking works best); biases and the classifier handled separately
methods.structure: Hadamard product with a learned binary mask, i.e. selection of a sub-network of pretrained connections; equivalently the additive update \Delta W = -(\mathbf{1}-M_{bin})\odot W_0 is constrained to zeroing coordinates
methods.mergeable_reason: The masked weight W_0 \odot M_{bin} is an ordinary dense (or sparse) matrix with the original shape.
methods.identity_at_init: No: scores are drawn from a uniform distribution tuned so that a target fraction of weights starts masked (5% for BERT/RoBERTa/DistilBERT; 3-10% works well), so the initial function differs from the pretrained one.
methods.key_idea: Instead of changing pretrained weights, learn which ones to switch off for each task; a 1-bit mask per weight suffices to reach fine-tuning-level accuracy.
methods.results_note: Masking BERT, RoBERTa and DistilBERT on eleven NLP tasks performs comparably to fine-tuning, and masked and fine-tuned solutions are linearly connected with nearly constant accuracy.

relations.note: Transfers Piggyback's thresholded real-valued mask training from CNNs to pretrained Transformers.
Masks the weights themselves rather than an additive update.
Lottery-ticket selection of a sparse update vs. selection of a sparse sub-network of weights.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2004.12406 (Zhao, Mengjie; 2020-04; comment 'EMNLP 2020') and EMNLP 2020 (2020.emnlp-main.174) confirmed. Real-valued scores, hard threshold tau, straight-through estimator, W_0 frozen, embeddings unmasked and top-down masking best match Sec. 3-5.
corrections: identity_at_init: made the default initial sparsity explicit (5%, Appendix) instead of 'a few %'.

methods.name: Piggyback
methods.full_name: Piggyback (learning to mask weights of a fixed backbone)
methods.paper_title: Piggyback: Adapting a Single Network to Multiple Tasks by Learning to Mask Weights
methods.formula_latex: y = (W_0\odot m)\,x,\quad m_{ji} = \mathbb{1}[m^{r}_{ji}\ge\tau],\quad \partial E/\partial m = (\delta y\,x^{\top})\odot W_0 \text{ used as straight-through gradient for } m^{r};\ W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: d_{out}d_{in}\ \text{real-valued mask weights during training};\ 1\ \text{bit per weight stored}
methods.locus: all convolutional and fully-connected layers of a fixed ImageNet backbone (VGG-16, ResNet, DenseNet)
methods.structure: Hadamard product with a learned binary mask (task-specific sub-network of a fixed backbone)
methods.mergeable_reason: The masked weights form an ordinary network of the original architecture.
methods.identity_at_init: m^r initialized to 1e-2 with threshold \tau = 5e-3, so the mask starts as all ones and the network equals the backbone.
methods.key_idea: Add new tasks to one frozen network by learning only a binary mask over its weights, at 1 bit per parameter per task.
methods.results_note: With ImageNet-pretrained VGG-16/ResNet-50 backbones, Piggyback approaches individually fine-tuned networks on fine-grained and large-shift classification tasks (e.g. within 0.36% top-1 error on Places365).
methods.verification_notes: arXiv 1801.06519 (Mallya, 2018-01) confirmed; ECCV 2018 confirmed via Crossref (LNCS, doi 10.1007/978-3-030-01225-0_5) and the CVF open-access page. Thresholded real-valued mask m^r (init 1e-2, tau = 5e-3 so the mask starts all ones), gradient (delta y x^T) . W used as straight-through, 1 bit per weight match Sec. 3.
corrections: relations: removed 'generalizes masking'. Masking is the same thresholded-score mechanism carried over to Transformers (recorded as masking builds-on piggyback), not a special case of Piggyback.

methods.name: SAM (sparse)
methods.full_name: Second-order Approximation Method for parameter selection
methods.paper_title: On the Effectiveness of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex:
heta = 	heta^0 + M\Delta	heta,\ \ \min_{\Delta	heta}\ 
abla\mathcal{L}(	heta^0)^{	op}M\Delta	heta + 	frac12(M\Delta	heta)^{	op}H(M\Delta	heta)\ \ 	ext{s.t.}\ \|M\|_0 = \lfloor mpfloor;\ \ H\preceq|\lambda_{max}|I \Rightarrow \hat M_{ii} = \mathbb{1} ig[
abla\mathcal{L}(	heta^0)_i^2 \in 	ext{top-}\lfloor mpfloor ig],\ 
abla\mathcal{L}(	heta^0) 	ext{ summed over burn-in steps};\ 	ext{mask fixed during training}
methods.trainable_params: \lfloor mp \rfloor\ \text{in total over all } m \text{ parameters (global selection; } p = 0.005 \text{ in experiments);\ per-matrix counts vary}
methods.locus: all parameters; gradients accumulated over a burn-in period
methods.structure: fixed diagonal 0/1 mask matrix M on parameter space, chosen as the analytic optimum of a second-order (upper-bounded) surrogate, which reduces to top squared-gradient selection
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing parameters change.
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta\theta = 0; mask computed from the gradient accumulated over 500-2000 burn-in steps (tuned per task) before training.
methods.key_idea: Casting every PEFT method as a sparse fine-tuned model, choose the sparse support that optimally decreases a second-order approximation of the loss, which under an isotropic Hessian bound means keeping the coordinates with the largest squared gradient.
methods.results_note: With RoBERTa on GLUE/SuperGLUE tasks (CoLA, STS-B, MRPC, RTE, CB, COPA, WSC) at 0.5% sparsity, SAM outperforms random, rule-based and projection-based PEFT baselines.

relations.note: Both fix a mask from gradient statistics before training, but SAM squares the accumulated gradient while FISH sums squared per-sample gradients (diagonal Fisher), so the rankings differ.
SAM avoids the 'projection discontinuity' of methods that re-select the support during training.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2211.15583 (Fu, Zihao; 2022-11) confirmed; AAAI 2023 confirmed via Crossref (doi 10.1609/aaai.v37i11.26505). Problem (8), Theorem 3 (rank by grad_i^2/h_i), replacement of the Hessian by |lambda_max| I, sparsity 0.005 and burn-in steps 500-2000 match Sec. 4-5. The gradient is accumulated (summed) over burn-in steps and then squared, so the score ranks |E[g]|, not E[g^2].
corrections: formula_latex: stated that grad L(theta^0) is the gradient summed over burn-in steps before squaring, which separates SAM's score from a Fisher (sum of squared gradients) score.
trainable_params: the mask M is chosen over all m parameters at once, so the count is floor(mp) overall, not p*d_out*d_in per matrix.
identity_at_init: burn-in is 500-2000 steps (chosen per task), not 'a few hundred'.
relations: fish-mask equivalent-to -> competes-with; the scores differ ((sum g)^2 vs sum g^2).

methods.name: LIFT
methods.paper_title: LIFT the Veil for the Truth: Principal Weights Emerge after Rank Reduction for Reasoning-Focused Supervised Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: W_t' = \mathrm{SVD}_r(W_t)\ \text{(best rank-}r\text{ approximation of the current weight; } W_0 \text{ at the start)},\quad M_t = \mathbb{1}\big[\,|W'_t| \in \text{top-}k\big],\quad W_{t+1} = W_t - \eta\,(M_t\odot \hat g_t);\ M_t \text{ recomputed every } \texttt{update\_mask\_interval} \text{ steps}
methods.trainable_params: k\ \text{per matrix active at any time (top } 5\%\text{ Principal Weights)};\ \text{the accumulated } \Delta W \text{ is supported on the union of successive masks}
methods.locus: LLM linear layers (attention and MLP)
methods.structure: sparse coordinate mask given by the largest-magnitude entries of the rank-r truncation of W_0 ('Principal Weights'), refreshed at fixed intervals; the resulting update is high-rank
methods.mergeable_reason: Only existing entries are updated in place.
methods.identity_at_init: \Delta W = 0; the mask is data-free (SVD of the pretrained weight).
methods.key_idea: Plain magnitude selection works poorly for LLM sparse fine-tuning, but after discarding small singular directions the largest remaining entries identify the weights that carry reasoning-relevant knowledge, so tuning only those beats full fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: Updating the top 5% Principal Weights, LIFT outperforms full fine-tuning on reasoning tasks (arithmetic and commonsense) with LoRA-level memory, and retains up to 20% more source-domain knowledge than full fine-tuning and LoRA.

relations.note: Opposite magnitude rules for a static-structure sparse mask: PaFi tunes the smallest |W_0|, LIFT the largest entries of a rank-r truncation.
Memory comparable to LoRA but high-rank sparse updates.
Both refresh the mask during training; LIFT uses a spectral criterion.
LIFT compares against SIFT (and SpIEL) as sparse fine-tuning baselines (App. F).

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2506.00772 (Liu, Zihang; 2025-06; comment 'ICML 2025') confirmed; PMLR v267 (liu25ba). Rank-r SVD truncation, top-k magnitude mask per matrix, top 5% Principal Weights, periodic mask refresh from the current weights (Alg. 1 calc_mask(theta_t)) match Sec. 4 and App. B.
corrections: formula_latex: the mask is recomputed from the rank-r approximation of the current weights theta_t (Alg. 1), not from W_0 only.
trainable_params: noted that with periodic mask refresh the final delta lives on the union of masks, so it can exceed k nonzeros.
relations: added competes-with sift (direct comparison in App. F).

methods.name: RoSA
methods.paper_title: RoSA: Accurate Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning via Robust Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA + S,\quad \mathrm{supp}(S)\subseteq M,\ \ M = \mathrm{TopK}\Big(\textstyle\sum_{s\in\mathcal{D}_M}(\nabla_W\mathcal{L}_s)^{\alpha}\big|_{W_0+\tilde B\tilde A},\ d\cdot d_{out}d_{in}\Big),\ \alpha\in\{1,2\},\ \ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}};\ W_0 \text{ frozen};\ \tilde B\tilde A = \text{LoRA after a 64-batch warm-up}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out}) + d\cdot d_{out}d_{in}\ \ (d = \text{mask density})
methods.locus: all fully connected layers of the LLM
methods.structure: robust-PCA-style decomposition of the update: low-rank BA plus a sparse S on a fixed gradient-statistics mask (accumulated squared gradients, i.e. a diagonal-Fisher mask for alpha=2)
methods.mergeable_reason: Both the low-rank and the sparse components are additive and can be folded into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: LoRA is first trained alone for 64 batches to compute the mask, then training restarts with both adapters at BA = 0 (B = 0) and S = 0; the mask is fixed from then on.
methods.key_idea: Full fine-tuning updates are not low-rank but are well approximated by low-rank plus sparse, so train both components jointly with system support for sparse adapters.
methods.results_note: Fine-tuning LLaMA2-7B on GSM8K, ViGGO and SQL generation, RoSA outperforms LoRA and pure sparse adaptation at equal budget and can match full fine-tuning.

relations.note: Adds a sparse component to LoRA.
Sparse component uses a FISH-like accumulated-gradient mask.
SPT chooses sparse or low-rank per matrix; RoSA uses both on every matrix.
with no low-rank part RoSA is gradient-masked sparse adaptation as in SHiRA-Grad
DSEE picks its sparse support by robust PCA of W_0 rather than gradients

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2401.04679 (Nikdan, 2024-01) confirmed; ICML 2024 confirmed in PMLR v235 (nikdan24a). Eq. 5 (rank <= r plus ||S||_0 <= d m n), Alg. 1 mask (32 samples, alpha in {1,2}, per-matrix TopK), 64-batch LoRA-only warm-up, then restart with LoRA + sparse adapter, densities 0.15-2.4% match Sec. 3 and 5.
corrections: formula_latex: mask gradients are taken at W_0 plus a briefly warmed-up LoRA (64 batches) and alpha is in {1,2}; both were missing.
identity_at_init: described the LoRA-only warm-up used for mask generation and the restart of training with both adapters at zero.
structure: added the LoRA warm-up step that precedes mask generation

methods.name: ABBA
methods.full_name: ABBA-Adapters (learnable Hadamard product of two low-rank matrices)
methods.paper_title: ABBA-Adapters: Efficient and Expressive Fine-Tuning of Foundation Models
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r_1r_2}}\,(B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2) = W_0 + \frac{\alpha}{\sqrt{r_1r_2}}\,(B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top},\quad B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r_k},\ A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{r_k\times d_{in}};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ B_1,A_1,B_2,A_2\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: any linear layer of an LLM
methods.structure: Hadamard product of two independently learnable rank-r_1 and rank-r_2 matrices (rank \le r_1r_2), executed without materialising \Delta W via the row-wise Khatri-Rao identity (B_1A_1)\odot(B_2A_2)=(B_1\odot_r B_2)(A_1^{\top}\odot_r A_2^{\top})^{\top}; rank-stabilised scale \alpha/\sqrt{r_1r_2}.
methods.mergeable_reason: The product is an ordinary dense matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: (B_1,A_1) initialised from the top-r_1 truncated SVD of W_0; B_2 = 0 and A_2 Kaiming-uniform, so ΔW = 0 at init.
methods.key_idea: Make both Hadamard factors learnable (HiRA fixes one to W_0), anchor one to the principal subspace of W_0, and use a rank-stabilising scale; the Khatri-Rao trick keeps memory at LoRA level.
methods.results_note: Reports state-of-the-art results on arithmetic and commonsense reasoning benchmarks across multiple LLMs, outperforming LoRA, HiRA and other PEFT baselines.

relations.note: ABBA makes both Hadamard factors learnable low-rank products; HiRA fixes one factor to the full-rank frozen W_0. ABBA's SVD init of B_1A_1 approximates W_0, so it starts near a HiRA-like update, but HiRA is not an instance of ABBA's rank-r_1 class
same function class (B_1A_1)⊙(B_2A_2) as LoHa; differs in SVD-anchored init and √(r1 r2) scaling
matched parameter budget, rank up to r_1 r_2

methods.verification_notes: arXiv v4 comment and OpenReview (ICLR 2026 Poster) confirm venue; scale alpha/sqrt(r1 r2) (Eq. 7), Khatri-Rao Theorem 1 and hybrid SVD+LoRA init (Sec. 3, Table 3) checked; ABBA cites FedPara; not in HF PEFT tuners.
corrections: relations[hira]: type generalizes -> competes-with, note rewritten ('generalizes' was wrong: W_0 is full-rank and frozen, so HiRA is not a special case of a learnable rank-r_1 factor)

methods.name: KronA
methods.paper_title: KronA: Parameter Efficient Tuning with Kronecker Adapter
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + s\,(A_k\otimes B_k),\quad A_k\in\mathbb{R}^{a_1\times a_2},\ B_k\in\mathbb{R}^{b_1\times b_2},\ a_1b_1=d_{out},\ a_2b_2=d_{in};\quad \Delta W x = s\,\mathrm{vec}(B_k X A_k^{\top}),\ X=\mathrm{mat}(x)\in\mathbb{R}^{b_2\times a_2};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_k,B_k\ \text{trained}
methods.locus: parallel to attention/FFN weight matrices (KronA); KronA^B and KronA^B_res sit parallel to the whole FFN block
methods.structure: Single Kronecker product of two dense small factors; \mathrm{rank}(A_k\otimes B_k)=\mathrm{rank}(A_k)\,\mathrm{rank}(B_k), reaching full rank with O(\sqrt{d_{in}d_{out}}) parameters; forward pass by the vec-trick without materialising \Delta W.
methods.mergeable_reason: The weight-parallel KronA merges into W_0 like LoRA (zero added latency in the paper's Table 2); KronA^B / KronA^B_res are linear branches placed in parallel to the whole (nonlinear) FFN block, Y = FFN(X) + sX[A_k ⊗ B_k] (+ s_res X), so there is no single existing weight to fold them into (127%/136% latency).
methods.identity_at_init: One factor zero-initialized and the other Kaiming-uniform (a = sqrt(5)); the paper reports zero-init of one factor markedly improves results.
methods.key_idea: Replace LoRA's low-rank product by a Kronecker product, which is full-rank-capable for the same tiny budget and cheap to apply via reshaping.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, KronA variants outperform LoRA, adapters and Compacter at comparable budgets, with KronA^B_res the strongest (at extra inference latency).

relations.note: LoKr with an unfactorized right factor
rank-unbounded alternative at similar parameter count
Compacter uses a sum of n Kronecker products inside adapters

methods.verification_notes: arXiv metadata checked; venue corrected to the NeurIPS 2023 ENLSP-III workshop; Eq. 2-6, zero+Kaiming init and GLUE/latency tables checked.
corrections: venue: the paper was presented as a poster at the Third Workshop on Efficient Natural Language and Speech Processing, NeurIPS 2023 (nips.cc/virtual/2023/81174); no archival main-track venue
mergeable_reason: corrected 'wrap a nonlinear FFN block': the branches are parallel to the FFN block, which is why they cannot be merged

methods.name: PHM-Adapter
methods.paper_title: Compacter: Efficient Low-Rank Hypercomplex Adapter Layers
methods.formula_latex: h \leftarrow h + U\,\mathrm{GeLU}(Dh),\quad D=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i^{D}\otimes B_i^{D},\ U=\sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i^{U}\otimes B_i^{U},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n},\ B_i^{D}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{r}{n}\times\frac{d}{n}},\ B_i^{U}\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d}{n}\times\frac{r}{n}};\ \text{backbone frozen, adapters trained}
methods.trainable_params: 2\left(\tfrac{dr}{n}+n^{3}\right)\ \text{per adapter}
methods.locus: bottleneck adapters after the attention and feed-forward sublayers (Houlsby placement)
methods.structure: Bottleneck MLP inserted serially with residual connection whose down/up projections are PHM layers: sums of n Kronecker products (Kronecker rank \le n, i.e. rank \le n after Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement), reducing parameters by about 1/n.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter contains a GeLU nonlinearity in a new serial branch, so it cannot be folded into existing weights.
methods.identity_at_init: No exact zero-init guarantee is stated in the method section; like Houlsby adapters it relies on the residual connection with small-initialized adapter weights.
methods.key_idea: Learn the 'multiplication rule' of an n-dimensional hypercomplex algebra: a dense projection becomes a sum of n Kronecker products, cutting adapter parameters by ~n.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, PHM-Adapter (n = 12) trains 0.179% of parameters and is competitive with full fine-tuning and standard adapters.

relations.note: replaces the adapter's dense projections by PHM layers
Compacter shares A_i across layers and makes B_i low-rank

methods.verification_notes: Compacter paper Eq. 4 and Sec. 4 parameter count 2(kd/n + n^3) per adapter (k=hidden, d=bottleneck in the paper; here d, r) checked; NeurIPS 2021 proceedings confirmed. Exact init not stated in the paper (kept as stated).

methods.name: KAdaptation
methods.paper_title: Parameter-efficient Model Adaptation for Vision Transformers
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \sum_{i=1}^{n}A_i\otimes(u_iv_i^{\top}),\quad A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\ \text{(shared across layers)},\ u_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{out}}{n}\times r},\ v_i\in\mathbb{R}^{\frac{d_{in}}{n}\times r};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ A_i,u_i,v_i\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per matrix} + n^{3}\ \text{shared}
methods.locus: ViT attention weight matrices (submodules selected by lowest local intrinsic dimension)
methods.structure: Low-rank PHM (sum of n Kronecker products of shared slow weights with low-rank fast weights) applied directly to the weight update \Delta W rather than to an inserted adapter.
methods.mergeable_reason: ΔW is a dense matrix added to frozen attention weights; the paper notes no added inference latency.
methods.identity_at_init: Not stated explicitly in the method section consulted; presumably one fast factor starts at zero so ΔW = 0 (unverified).
methods.key_idea: Choose where to adapt via the local intrinsic dimension of each ViT submodule, then express the update as a Compacter-style Kronecker sum so it merges like LoRA.
methods.results_note: Best accuracy/parameter trade-off among compared methods on 20 image-classification datasets few-shot and 7 datasets full-shot with CLIP ViTs.

relations.note: same LPHM parameterization, moved from inserted adapters to ΔW
mergeable additive update with Kronecker structure instead of plain low rank

methods.verification_notes: AAAI 2023 confirmed (DOI 10.1609/aaai.v37i1.25160); Eq. 3-4 (shared n x n slow weights, low-rank fast weights u_i v_i^T) and no-latency claim checked; per-matrix count r(d_in+d_out) re-derived. Init not stated in the paper (left unverified).
corrections: code_url: eric-ai-lab/PEViT now redirects to UCSB-AI/PEViT

methods.name: KRAdapter
methods.paper_title: Towards Higher Effective Rank in Parameter-efficient Fine-tuning using Khatri--Rao Product
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \alpha\,\big[U\odot_{KR}V\big]_{1:d_{out},\,:},\quad (U\odot_{KR}V)_{:,j}=U_{:,j}\otimes V_{:,j},\ U\in\mathbb{R}^{k_1\times d_{in}},\ V\in\mathbb{R}^{k_2\times d_{in}},\ k_1k_2\ge d_{out};\ W_0\ \text{frozen},\ U,V\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: d_{in}(k_1+k_2)\approx 2\,d_{in}\sqrt{d_{out}}
methods.locus: linear layers of vision-language models and LLMs
methods.structure: Column-wise Kronecker (Khatri-Rao) product truncated to d_out rows; with random factors it is almost surely of full rank, and its singular-value tail is heavier (higher effective rank) than Kronecker or low-rank updates. k_1=\lfloor\sqrt{d_{out}}\rfloor, k_2=\lceil d_{out}/k_1\rceil.
methods.mergeable_reason: The Khatri-Rao product is a dense matrix of W_0's shape.
methods.identity_at_init: U zero-initialized and V randomly initialized (Kaiming-style, negative slope 1/sqrt(k_1)), so ΔW = 0; the scale alpha is typically 0.1.
methods.key_idea: Target effective rank, not just algebraic rank: the Khatri-Rao product spreads energy over many singular directions at about the cost of a rank-16-32 LoRA.
methods.results_note: Reports gains on vision-language models up to 1B and LLMs up to 8B parameters, especially on unseen commonsense-reasoning tasks, with LoRA-level memory and compute.

relations.note: column-wise vs full Kronecker product; paper contrasts their spectra
RandLoRA (ICLR 2025) shares four of the five authors (Albert, Zhang, Saratchandran, van den Hengel, Abbasnejad) and is a baseline in the paper
matched budget, higher effective rank

methods.name: QuanTA

methods.formula_latex: y = W_0x + \mathcal{T}_{\theta}x - \mathcal{S}x,\quad \mathcal{T}_{\theta}=\prod_{\alpha}T^{(\alpha)},\ T^{(\alpha)}\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{m}d_{n}\times d_{m}d_{n}}\ \text{acting on axes } (m(\alpha),n(\alpha)) \text{ of } x \text{ reshaped to } d_1\times\cdots\times d_N,\ \textstyle\prod_n d_n=d;\ \mathcal{S}=\mathcal{T}_{\theta_0}\ \text{frozen}

methods.structure: Circuit-shaped tensor network: the hidden vector is viewed as an N-qudit state and a sequence of two-axis 'gates' is applied (an einsum of small tensors); by the universality and rank-representation theorems it can express full-rank updates.

methods.key_idea: Borrow quantum-circuit structure (local two-qudit gates composed in sequence) to get high-rank updates with few parameters and without zero-initialized factors.
methods.results_note: Improves over LoRA and DoRA on commonsense and arithmetic reasoning with LLaMA-family models while using fewer trainable parameters.

methods.structure: Entrywise sinusoid of a rank-r matrix; the rank of \sin(\omega\,BA) grows with \omega (the paper gives a lower bound in terms of \omega), so the update is no longer low-rank.
methods.mergeable_reason: sin(ωBA)/g is a dense matrix computable after training and addable to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: With LoRA's B = 0 initialization, sin(0) = 0 so ΔW = 0.
methods.key_idea: A fixed high-frequency entrywise nonlinearity raises the rank of a low-rank parameterization for free.
methods.results_note: Improves LoRA and DoRA at equal parameter count across ViT, LLM (e.g. LLaMA-3-8B commonsense reasoning, GLUE), NeRF and 3D-shape tasks.

relations.note: drop-in modification of LoRA's product
both raise rank with entrywise operations on low-rank matrices

methods.name: NOLA
methods.full_name: Compressing LoRA using Linear Combination of Random Basis
methods.paper_title: NOLA: Compressing LoRA using Linear Combination of Random Basis
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + \Big(\sum_{j=1}^{l}\beta_j B_j\Big)\Big(\sum_{i=1}^{k}\alpha_i A_i\Big),\quad B_j\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r},\ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen pseudo-random (generated from a seed, optionally shared across layers)};\ \alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{k},\ \beta\in\mathbb{R}^{l}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: k + l\ \ (\text{independent of } r,\ d_{in},\ d_{out})
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: attention projections of GPT-2, LLaMA-2, ViT)
methods.structure: LoRA factors constrained to the linear span of k (resp. l) frozen random basis matrices; \Delta W is bilinear in the two coefficient vectors and has rank \le r
methods.mergeable_reason: After training the two linear combinations are materialised, and their product BA is added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Not specified in the paper. Official code (UCDvision/NOLA, gpt/examples/NLG/src/model_nola.py) zero-initialises both coefficient vectors, and each NOLA factor also carries a frozen offset matrix (LoRA-style reset: Kaiming for A, zero for B), so \Delta W = 0 at init with non-zero gradients for the B-side coefficients; with the paper's pure-span formula, zero-initialising both alpha and beta would give zero gradients. Bases are U(-1,1) from a stored seed and are regenerated on the fly in forward/backward to save memory
methods.key_idea: Decouple the parameter count from rank and width (LoRA's rank-1 floor) by expressing each LoRA factor as a learned mixture of seeded random basis matrices, PRANC-style; only the seed and the mixture coefficients (optionally 4-bit quantised) are stored.
methods.results_note: On LLaMA-2 70B NOLA is about 20x more compact than the most compressed (rank-1) LoRA without accuracy loss; also matches LoRA on GPT-2 E2E and ViT few-shot classification with fewer parameters.

relations.note: reparameterises LoRA's A and B

our observation: (alpha, beta) -> (A, B) is linear, i.e. theta_D = P theta_d with a block-diagonal dense random P
contemporaneous random-basis compression of LoRA

Not in HF PEFT.

relations[intrinsic-said]: note rewritten (clarified that the link is via cited motivation and PRANC)

methods.name: Intrinsic SAID
methods.paper_title: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \theta^{D}_{i} = \theta^{D}_{0,i} + \lambda_i\,\big(\theta^{d-m}M\big)_i,\quad M = H\,G\,\Pi\,H\,B\ \ (\text{Fastfood transform: Hadamard } H,\ \text{Gaussian diagonal } G,\ \text{permutation } \Pi,\ \pm1 \text{ diagonal } B;\ \text{frozen});\ \theta^{d-m}\in\mathbb{R}^{d-m},\ \lambda\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\ (\text{one scale per layer})\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: d\ \text{for the whole model, including the classification head in the paper's count (e.g. } d_{90}\approx 207 \text{ for RoBERTa-Large on MRPC)}
methods.locus: the entire flattened parameter vector of the model (all layers), with layer-wise scaling
methods.structure: random linear subspace of the full parameter space: \Delta\theta = \mathrm{diag}(\lambda)\,P\,\theta_d with a structured random (Fastfood) projection P
methods.mergeable_reason: The projected update is a fixed parameter offset that can be added to theta_0.
methods.identity_at_init: \theta^{d} = 0 recovers the pretrained parameters exactly
methods.key_idea: Fine-tuning works in a tiny random subspace: optimise a d-dimensional vector projected into the full parameter space; the small d needed (intrinsic dimension) explains why huge models fine-tune well on little data. SAID adds per-layer scales.
methods.results_note: Optimising about 200 parameters (d90 = 207 with SAID) projected into RoBERTa-Large's full space reaches 90% of full fine-tuning performance on MRPC (about 800 for QQP); larger and longer-pretrained models have lower intrinsic dimension.

relations.note: alternative low-dimensional fine-tuning: a random linear subspace of the full parameter space versus LoRA's structured low-rank factor space; LoRA cites this intrinsic-dimension finding as motivation

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2012.13255 (Aghajanyan, Dec 2020); ACL-IJCNLP 2021 long paper, ACL Anthology 2021.acl-long.568. Eq. 2 (theta^D = theta^D_0 + theta^d M, M = H G Pi H B) and Eq. 3 (SAID, m layer scales traded from d) checked; theta_d = 0 init stated in the paper.
corrections: trainable_params: the ~200-parameter MRPC result is for RoBERTa-Large (d90 = 207, SAID), and the paper's d also covers the classification head
results_note: specified RoBERTa-Large (the base model needs more parameters) and added the QQP figure
relations[lora]: note rewritten (clarified; Intrinsic SAID predates LoRA)

methods.name: Tied-LoRA
methods.full_name: Tied Low-Rank Adaptation (weight tying + selective training)
methods.paper_title: Tied-LoRA: Enhancing parameter efficiency of LoRA with Weight Tying
methods.formula_latex: W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + \Lambda_{v_\ell}\, B\, \Lambda_{u_\ell}\, A,\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}},\ B\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{tied (one copy shared by all layers)};\ \Lambda_{u_\ell}=\mathrm{diag}(u_\ell),\ u_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{r},\ \Lambda_{v_\ell}=\mathrm{diag}(v_\ell),\ v_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}}\ \text{per layer};\ \text{each of } A,B,u,v \text{ is selectively trained or frozen (configs TL1--TL6; TL6 trains all)}
methods.trainable_params: \text{TL6: } r(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{once for all layers} + L\,(r + d_{out})\ \text{in total; per adapted matrix } \approx r + d_{out} + \tfrac{r(d_{in}+d_{out})}{L}
methods.locus: paper: the fused QKV projection (d x 3d) of every transformer layer; applicable to any linear layer
methods.structure: a single low-rank pair BA shared across depth, modulated per layer by diagonal scalings of its rows and rank channels; selective freezing yields a lattice of sub-configurations
methods.mergeable_reason: The low-rank path is linear, so each layer's Lambda_v B Lambda_u A can be merged into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Per Table 1: TL2/TL6 (VeRA-like): A, B \sim \mathcal{N}, u = 1, v = 0 (exact identity); TL3--TL5 (LoRA-like): A \sim \mathcal{N}, B = 0, u = v = 1 (exact identity); TL1 (only tied A trained): A, B \sim \mathcal{N}, u = v = 1, so \Delta W \neq 0 at init; \alpha = r, removing the \alpha/r scaling
methods.key_idea: Tie one LoRA pair across all layers and train only what is needed (shared factors and/or per-layer scaling vectors); a framework containing LoRA and VeRA as corners of the same design space.
methods.results_note: TL6 (trainable tied A, B plus per-layer u, v) stays within roughly 1-2% of LoRA across five tasks (on average 1.36% below LoRA with LLaMA-2 7B) and beats LoRA on IWSLT-2017 De-En translation with 12.5% of its parameters; on GSM8K it needs 4.3% of LoRA's parameters for a comparable score.

methods.name: ShareLoRA
methods.paper_title: ShareLoRA: Parameter Efficient and Robust Large Language Model Fine-tuning via Shared Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: \text{ShareA: } W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + \alpha\, B_\ell\, A,\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d_{in}}\ \text{shared by all layers},\ B_\ell\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times r}\ \text{per layer};\quad \text{ShareB: } \alpha\, B\, A_\ell;\quad \text{ShareAB: } \alpha\, B A\ \text{for every layer (all factors trained)}
methods.trainable_params: \text{ShareA: } r\,d_{out} + \tfrac{r\,d_{in}}{L}\ \text{per adapted matrix (i.e. } L r d_{out} + r d_{in} \text{ per module type)}
methods.locus: attention projections (ShareA_qkv: A_Q, A_K and A_V are each shared across all layers, one shared A per projection type) or all linear layers ('sharing all'), on RoBERTa, GPT-2 and LLaMA 1/2/3
methods.structure: LoRA in which one factor (the down-projection A, the up-projection B, or both) is a single matrix shared across depth; \Delta W_\ell = B_\ell A spans a common row space for all layers
methods.mergeable_reason: Each layer's B_l A is an ordinary low-rank matrix that can be added to W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: Inherits LoRA initialisation (up-projection zero, so Delta W = 0); not discussed separately in the paper
methods.key_idea: Share LoRA's down- (or up-) projection across all layers: the shared subspace removes redundancy, roughly halves parameters or more, and acts as a regulariser that improves robustness and continual-learning transfer.
methods.results_note: 44%-96% fewer trainable parameters than LoRA with maintained performance on RoBERTa, GPT-2 and LLaMA 1/2/3, and up to 1.2% higher average accuracy in zero/few-shot and continual fine-tuning settings.

methods.name: PRoLoRA
methods.paper_title: PRoLoRA: Partial Rotation Empowers More Parameter-Efficient LoRA
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + BA,\quad B = \big[\,B_u\ \big|\ \big(B_0;\,\mathrm{Roll}(B_0,s_B);\dots;\mathrm{Roll}(B_0,(n{-}1)s_B)\big)\big],\quad A = \Big[\,A_u;\ \big(A_0\,|\,\mathrm{Roll}(A_0,s_A)\,|\cdots|\,\mathrm{Roll}(A_0,(m{-}1)s_A)\big)\Big];\ A_u\in\mathbb{R}^{u\times d_{in}},\ B_u\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times u}\ \text{(unshared ranks)},\ A_0\in\mathbb{R}^{(r-u)\times d_{in}/m},\ B_0\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}/n\times(r-u)}\ \text{trained};\ \mathrm{Roll} = \text{cyclic shift along the rank dimension}
methods.trainable_params: u\,(d_{in}+d_{out}) + (r-u)\Big(\tfrac{d_{in}}{m} + \tfrac{d_{out}}{n}\Big)
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: all linear layers of LLaMA-2 / Tulu instruction tuning)
methods.structure: intra-layer sharing: each LoRA factor is a broadcast of one small chunk along the hidden dimension, the copies differentiated by rank-dimension cyclic permutations, plus u unshared ranks; \Delta W is block-structured with blocks related by rank permutations
methods.mergeable_reason: The expanded B and A are ordinary matrices, so BA merges into W_0 exactly as in LoRA.
methods.identity_at_init: B = 0 (whole matrix); A_u Kaiming-uniform and the shared chunk A_0 with a rectified Kaiming bound computed from the full hidden size d_in so both parts have equal scale
methods.key_idea: Reuse parameters inside a layer: broadcast one chunk of each LoRA factor across the hidden dimension (more rank per parameter) and break the resulting repetition with cheap rotations and a few unshared ranks; a strict superset of LoRA.
methods.results_note: With half the trainable parameters of LoRA, PRoLoRA still outperforms LoRA on multiple instruction-tuning benchmarks and scales to larger LLMs.

relations.note: u = r (or m = n = 1) recovers LoRA
intra-layer instead of inter-layer sharing; not restricted by equal weight shapes
MoS builds on PRoLoRA-like intra-layer sharing and adds VeRA-like inter-layer sharing
MiSS also builds Delta W by tiling one shard

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.16902 (Wang, Feb 2024); ACL 2024 long, ACL Anthology 2024.acl-long.156. Broadcast reduction, Roll along the rank dimension, unshared ranks u, parameter count u(h+o) + h(r-u)/m + o(r-u)/n, rectified Kaiming init and B = 0 all checked. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: MoS
methods.paper_title: MoS: Unleashing Parameter Efficiency of Low-Rank Adaptation with Mixture of Shards
methods.formula_latex: W_\ell = W_{0,\ell} + B_\ell A_\ell,\quad B_\ell = \mathrm{Route}^{c}\big([B^{pub}, B^{pri}],\, I^{b}_\ell\big),\quad A_\ell = \mathrm{Route}^{r}\big([A^{pub}, A^{pri}],\, I^{a}_\ell\big);\ \text{each rank vector of } A_\ell, B_\ell \text{ is the concatenation of } l \text{ shards retrieved from global pools by fixed random index matrices } I_\ell;\ \text{pools trained, indices frozen; private shards are used by one layer only}
methods.trainable_params: \approx e\,(d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per adapted matrix on average (global pools of size } eL(d_{in}+d_{out}) \text{ per linear-layer type), while each layer uses rank } r > e
methods.locus: all linear-layer types of LLaMA-2/3 (one global pool per layer type)
methods.structure: global inter- and intra-layer sharing: LoRA factor vectors are assembled from shards of shared public/private pools via subset selection, pair dissociation (separate pools for A and B), vector sharding and shard privatisation; routing is index-based and input-independent
methods.mergeable_reason: Indices are fixed, so after training each layer's B_l A_l is a fixed low-rank matrix that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: public and private B pools zero-initialised (\Delta W = 0); A pools with PRoLoRA-style rectified Kaiming bounds; index matrices sampled once at random
methods.key_idea: Pure sharing across layers hurts because all layers get the same update; cheap differentiation strategies (random subsets, dissociated A/B pools, shards, private shards) restore diversity while keeping the high sharing ratio.
methods.results_note: About 8x parameter savings relative to standard LoRA at matched performance on instruction-tuning benchmarks (MMLU, BBH, GSM8K, etc.), with ablations confirming each differentiation component.

relations.note: adopts intra-layer chunk sharing and rectified initialisation
adopts inter-layer sharing; replaces random scaling by subset selection

Eqs. 2-5 (pools A^p in R^{eL x h}, B^p in R^{o x eL}, index-based routing, public/private pools), init (B pools 0, A pools as PRoLoRA) and ~8x savings checked. methods.name: RaSA
methods.paper_title: RaSA: Rank-Sharing Low-Rank Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W_i = W_{0,i} + \big[\tilde B_i\ \ B_S\big]\, D_i \begin{bmatrix}\tilde A_i\\ A_S\end{bmatrix},\quad \tilde B_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times(r-k)},\ \tilde A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{(r-k)\times d_{in}}\ \text{layer-specific};\ B_S\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times Lk},\ A_S\in\mathbb{R}^{Lk\times d_{in}}\ \text{shared rank pool (k ranks contributed by each layer)};\ D_i\ \text{diagonal } (r-k+Lk)\ \text{per layer; all trained}
methods.trainable_params: r\,(d_{in}+d_{out}) + (r - k + Lk)\ \text{per adapted matrix (same as LoRA plus a diagonal)}
methods.locus: all linear layers of the LLM (assumes equal shapes across layers; e.g. Llama, Mistral)
methods.structure: partial rank sharing: \Delta W_i = \tilde B_i D_i^{(1)} \tilde A_i + B_S D_i^{(2)} A_S, a private rank-(r-k) term plus a shared rank-Lk pool reweighted per layer by a trainable diagonal; effective rank r - k + Lk
methods.mergeable_reason: For each layer the update is a fixed low-rank matrix that merges into W_0.
methods.identity_at_init: \tilde B_i = 0, B_S = 0; \tilde A_i, A_S Kaiming; D_i = \tfrac{\alpha}{2(r-k)} on private and \tfrac{\alpha}{2Lk} on shared ranks
methods.key_idea: Pool k ranks from every layer into a shared rank pool that all layers reuse with layer-specific diagonal weights, raising effective rank by (L-1)k at LoRA's parameter cost; its minimum reconstruction error is provably no worse than LoRA's.
methods.results_note: Significantly improves over LoRA and other variants on challenging code-generation and mathematical-reasoning fine-tuning at the same parameter budget.

relations.note: k = 0 recovers LoRA

RaSA's shared pool with per-layer diagonal weighting resembles VeRA/Tied-LoRA sharing, but the pool is trained and combined with private LoRA ranks; the paper compares against VeRA and argues full sharing is sub-optimal

methods.verification_notes: arXiv 2503.12576 (He, Mar 2025); ICLR 2025 (arXiv comment, OpenReview GdXI5zCoAt). Eq. 5 ([B~_i B_S] D_i [A~_i; A_S]), D_i trainable, init (Kaiming A, zero B, d_j = alpha/(2(r-k)) or alpha/(2Lk)) and effective rank r - k + Lk checked. Not in HF PEFT.

methods.name: LoRA-XS
methods.full_name: Low-Rank Adaptation with eXtremely Small number of parameters
methods.paper_title: LoRA-XS: Low-Rank Adaptation with Extremely Small Number of Parameters
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + U_r\,R\,\Sigma_r V_r^{\top},\quad W_0 = U\Sigma V^{\top}\ (U_r, \Sigma_r, V_r:\ \text{top-}r \text{ truncated SVD, frozen}),\ R\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\ \text{trained}\ \ (\text{paper, row-vector convention: } h = xW + xARB,\ A = U_r\Sigma_r,\ B = V_r^{\top};\ \text{equivalently } U_r\Sigma_r R' V_r^{\top} \text{ since } \Sigma_r \text{ is invertible})
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: attention and MLP projections of RoBERTa, Mistral, Gemma, LLaMA)
methods.structure: a trainable r x r core sandwiched between frozen top-r singular subspaces of W_0 (Tucker-2 core); \Delta W lives in \mathrm{span}(U_r) \otimes \mathrm{span}(V_r)

methods.name: LaMDA
methods.full_name: Large Model Fine-Tuning via Spectrally Decomposed Low-Dimensional Adaptation
methods.paper_title: LaMDA: Large Model Fine-Tuning via Spectrally Decomposed Low-Dimensional Adaptation
methods.formula_latex: W = \big(W_0 - U_r\Sigma_r V_r^{\top}\big) + \alpha\,U_r\,S\,\Sigma_r V_r^{\top},\quad \Sigma_r V_r^{\top}\ (\text{PMA, down-projection) frozen},\ S\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times r}\ (\text{LDA}) \text{ trained},\ U_r\ (\text{PMB, up-projection) trainable early and frozen one rank component at a time, lowest-energy first, on a linear schedule over the first } t_i \approx 30\%\ \text{of iterations}\ \ (\text{paper, row-vector convention: } Y = XW + \alpha XASB,\ A = U[:,{:}r]\Sigma_r,\ B = V[:,{:}r]^{\top}, \text{ rows of } B \text{ frozen last-to-first})
methods.trainable_params: r^{2}\ (+\ \text{a decreasing number of rows of the up-projection during the early phase; LaMDA++ adapts } r \text{ per layer})
methods.locus: any linear layer (paper: DeBERTa-V3, BART, GPT-2, LLaMA-2 attention/MLP projections)
methods.structure: PiSSA-style residual split with a trainable r x r core between frozen spectral factors; the up-projection is progressively frozen, so late training is a pure r^2-parameter basis change
methods.mergeable_reason: After training the residual and the adapter path are fixed matrices that sum to a single weight.
methods.identity_at_init: S = I_r and the main path holds the residual W_0 - U_r\Sigma_rV_r^{\top}, so W = W_0 at init (for alpha = 1)
methods.key_idea: Freeze the first projection (cutting activation memory) and learn a small square matrix in the principal spectral subspace, gradually freezing the second projection, so trainable parameters stop scaling with width; LaMDA++ allocates ranks from the normalised spectrum.
methods.results_note: Matches or surpasses existing methods on GLUE, summarisation, NLG and reasoning with up to 17.7x fewer parameter updates and up to 1.32x lower peak GPU memory.

methods.name: LoRA-Mini
methods.full_name: LoRA-Mini: Adaptation Matrices Decomposition and Selective Training
methods.paper_title: LoRA-Mini : Adaptation Matrices Decomposition and Selective Training
methods.formula_latex: W = W_0 + P\,C\,D\,Q,\quad P\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{out}\times b},\ Q\in\mathbb{R}^{a\times d_{in}}\ \text{frozen outer (auxiliary) matrices};\ C\in\mathbb{R}^{b\times r},\ D\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times a}\ \text{trained inner matrices}\ \ (\text{paper: } h = (W + A_{aux}A_{train}B_{train}B_{aux})x)

papers.title: Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
papers.claim: Adapters, prefix tuning and LoRA are all modifications \Delta h added to specific hidden states and differ only along four axes: functional form, insertion form (sequential vs parallel), modified representation (attention vs FFN) and composition function (simple, gated, scaled); prefix tuning is exactly a softmax-gated parallel adapter on attention heads.
papers.relevance: Provides the canonical coordinate system for the adapter family (serial vs parallel composition, gating and scaling as composition laws), directly suggesting a categorical reading where adapters are endomorphisms post-composed with sublayers and parallel adapters are sums of morphisms with a common domain.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.04366 (He, 2021). ICLR 2022 spotlight per arXiv comment. The four design dimensions and the prefix = gated parallel adapter derivation (Sec. 3) are confirmed.

papers.title: On the Effectiveness of Adapter-based Tuning for Pretrained Language Model Adaptation
papers.claim: Adapter-based tuning yields representations that deviate less from the pretrained model than fine-tuning, mitigating forgetting; it outperforms fine-tuning on low-resource and cross-lingual tasks and is more robust to overfitting and learning-rate changes.
papers.relevance: Empirical evidence that the near-identity, frozen-backbone structure of adapters acts as an implicit regularizer toward the pretrained function, a key property for any theory of PEFT as a small deformation of a base model.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2106.03164 (Ruidan He, 2021). ACL 2021 long paper per arXiv comment. The claims match the abstract.

papers.title: AdapterHub: A Framework for Adapting Transformers
papers.claim: A framework on top of HuggingFace Transformers for training, sharing and dynamically 'stitching-in' pre-trained adapters for different tasks and languages.
papers.relevance: Made adapters first-class, swappable, composable objects (the infrastructure behind MAD-X, AdapterFusion and AdapterDrop), the practical counterpart of treating adapters as modular morphisms.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2007.07779 (Pfeiffer, 2020). EMNLP 2020 System Demonstrations per arXiv comment.

papers.title: Adapters: A Unified Library for Parameter-Efficient and Modular Transfer Learning

papers.title: Learning Rate Scaling across LoRA Ranks and Transfer to Full Finetuning
papers.claim: Maximal-Update Adaptation (\( \mu \)A): in the joint limit of width \( n \) and rank \( r\to\infty \), with SignSGD as a proxy for Adam and a fixed number of steps, requiring the LoRA feature increment to be \( \Theta(1) \) fixes the learning-rate scaling. For Init[A] (random \( A\sim\mathcal N(0,1/n) \), \( B=0 \)) and multiplier \( \alpha=r^{-\gamma} \) on \( \alpha BAx \), the increment is \( \max\{\Theta(\eta\alpha r),\Theta(\eta^2\alpha rn)\} \) and \( \eta=\Theta(n^{-1/2}r^{-(1-\gamma)/2}) \). So the optimal LR shrinks as \( r^{-1/2} \) for \( \alpha=1 \) and as \( r^{-1/4} \) for rsLoRA's \( \alpha=r^{-1/2} \), and is rank-invariant for \( \alpha=r^{-1} \) (standard \( \alpha/r \)), though with a narrow stable range. For Init[B] (random \( B\sim\mathcal N(0,1/r) \), \( A=0 \)) with \( \alpha=1 \), \( \eta=\Theta(n^{-1}) \): rank-invariant and equal to full fine-tuning's scaling, so LRs tuned on LoRA transfer to full FT. Under Init[A] learning runs mainly through \( B \), and under Init[B] mainly through \( A \). Experiments span LLM SFT, VLMs, diffusion and RLVR.
papers.relevance: Settles the rsLoRA versus LoRA-Without-Regret tension in the lora-core notes: which LR-rank law holds depends jointly on the init side and on how the multiplier scales with \( r \). Under this abstraction rsLoRA's \( \alpha\propto r^{-1/2} \) still needs \( \eta\propto r^{-1/4} \). The near rank-invariant optimum with \( \alpha/r \) and Init[A] reported by LoRA Without Regret, and its LoRA LR well above full FT's, are consistent in direction with the \( \gamma=1 \) case, whose \( \Theta(n^{-1/2}) \) exceeds full FT's \( \Theta(n^{-1}) \). It is the rank-direction companion to the width-direction analyses already catalogued (lora-plus-width-scaling, hayou-lora-init-dynamics, rslora-rank-stabilization). Its first- and second-order terms (\( \eta\alpha \) versus \( \eta^2\alpha \)) are the same signal/drift split as the scaling-factor paper below. PreFT cites it to choose its ReFT prefactor.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2602.06204 v1 2026-02-05, first author Nan Chen (with Villar, Hayou); arXiv API confirms. ICML 2026 'Accept (regular)' poster 60938 (OpenReview vCAIwEJZQ6).
