A.23) and the term-wise imbalance (learning through B under Init[A], through A under Init[B] when r << n). PreFT (App. C.2) and the scaling-factor paper both cite it. papers.title: The Hidden Power of Scaling Factor in LoRA Optimization
papers.claim: For \( W=W_0+\tfrac{\alpha}{r}BA \), a step decomposes exactly into a signal \( \tfrac{\alpha}{r}(B\Delta A+\Delta B\,A) \) and a bilinear drift \( \tfrac{\alpha}{r}\Delta B\,\Delta A \). The parameter Hessian splits likewise into \( J^{\top}H_\ell J\succeq0 \) and an indefinite structural term. At LoRA init (\( B=0 \), \( A_{ij}\sim\mathcal N(0,\sigma_A^2) \)) the signal curvature is suppressed, \( \mathbb E\,\mathrm{Tr}\,\mathcal H_{\mathrm{Signal}}=\alpha^2(\sigma_A^2/r)\,\mathrm{Tr}\,H_\ell \), so full-FT hyperparameters are overly conservative. Under Adam the signal scales as \( \alpha\eta \) and the drift as \( \alpha\eta^2 \): raising \( \alpha \) accelerates without degrading the signal-to-drift ratio \( \Theta(1/\eta) \), while raising \( \eta \) degrades it, so \( \alpha \) and \( \eta \) are not interchangeable. Matching curvature to full FT gives \( \alpha=\Theta(\sqrt r/\sigma_A) \). Empirically \( \alpha^*\approx C\sqrt r \) with \( C\approx256 \) (Llama-3-1B, Tulu-3), 512 (8B) and 1024 (OpenThoughts). LoRA-\( \alpha \) sets \( \Delta W=\tfrac{\alpha\,\alpha_{base}}{r}BA \) with \( \alpha_{base}=256\sqrt r \) (or \( \sqrt r/\sigma_A \)) and uses the full-FT learning rate.
papers.relevance: Pairs with the \( \mu \)A paper on the same scaling question from the multiplier side. The effective multiplier \( \alpha/r=C/\sqrt r \) is rsLoRA's \( 1/\sqrt r \) law (rslora, rslora-rank-stabilization) with prefactor \( C\approx256 \), which is \( 256/\sqrt r \) times the \( \alpha=r \) heuristic, i.e. 16x to 256x larger for \( r \) from 256 down to 1 (App. F). The signal/drift split (\( \alpha\eta \) versus \( \alpha\eta^2 \)) agrees with \( \mu \)A's first- and second-order increment terms, and it is the same tangent-versus-bilinear split of the update of \( BA \) that PRISM exploits to keep DP noise in the tangent space.
corrections: relevance: '16x-256x larger by a constant' was wrong. The ratio to the alpha = r heuristic is 256/sqrt(r), so it depends on rank (256x at r = 1, 16x at r = 256, App. F Table 6). The sentence now says so.

papers.title: Uniform Spectral Growth and Convergence of Muon in LoRA-Style Matrix Factorization
papers.venue: NeurIPS 2026 (poster; accepted as 'Uniform Spectral Growth under Factor-wise Muon Orthogonalization in Matrix Factorization and LoRA')
papers.claim: For \( \min_{B,A}\tfrac12\|BA-Y\|_F^2 \) from LoRA-style init (output-side factor \( B(0)=0 \), input-side factor \( A(0)=\gamma N \) small Gaussian), spectral gradient flow orthogonalises each factor's gradient separately with \( \mathcal T_\beta(M)=(MM^{\top}+\beta I)^{-1/2}M \). Under this flow the core product stays near-diagonal (\( O(\gamma) \) off-diagonal), and the square roots of all active singular values of \( BA \) grow at unit rate, \( \tfrac{d}{dt}\sqrt{d_i}=1+O(\varepsilon^{1/4}) \). So the smallest target singular value is reached first, the opposite of plain gradient flow's largest-first, saddle-to-saddle learning. For almost all inits the flow converges to a global minimum (the best rank-\( r \) approximation of \( Y \)) or the factor norms diverge; with \( \ell_2 \) regularisation convergence is global. The balancedness quantity \( B^{\top}B-AA^{\top} \) conserved by plain gradient flow need not be conserved here. Near-uniform growth is also observed with Newton-Schulz Muon in LoRA fine-tuning of LLMs.
papers.relevance: Extends the catalogued gradient-flow papers (lora-gradient-flow-matrix-factorization, implicit-regularization-deep-matrix-factorization, conservation-laws-gradient-flows) to Muon-type optimizers. Factor-wise orthogonalisation can break the conservation law tied to LoRA's \( GL(r) \) symmetry and replaces the incremental (largest-first, saddle-to-saddle) learning of plain gradient flow with equal-rate growth in \( \sqrt{\sigma_i} \), so arguments that rely on largest-first ordering do not carry over to factor-wise Muon. It also cautions that uniform growth amplifies all \( r \) directions, which can hurt when the useful update has rank below \( r \).
corrections: relevance: dropped the unsupported claim that largest-first learning 'motivates spectral inits such as PiSSA'. Neither this paper nor PiSSA makes that link; the sentence now states only what the paper shows (Cor. 5.8, Sec. 5.2.3).

papers.title: Weight Updates as Activation Shifts: A Principled Framework for Steering
papers.claim: For a GLU MLP \( W_d(\phi(W_gh)\odot W_uh) \), a first-order input perturbation \( \Delta h \) reproduces the first-order effect of perturbing \( W_g,W_u \) but misses the down-projection term \( (\Delta W_d)m \), which a post-MLP additive edit can absorb. With the fine-tuned hidden state as an oracle target, the MLP output accounts for only 40-70% of the block-output magnitude across layers (Llama-3.2, Winogrande), so a post-MLP edit misses the attention and skip-connection share. A theorem gives the best linear post-block approximation of post-MLP steering in terms of principal angles between sample-space singular subspaces. A post-block bottleneck adapter \( h\mapsto h+W_2\phi(W_1h) \) (after the skip connection) at every layer comes within 0.2-0.9% of full SFT accuracy with 0.04% of parameters and beats ReFT and LoRA. Weight and activation updates express different function classes, and joint training with \( W_2\leftarrow(I-VV^{\top})W_2 \), \( V \) an orthonormal basis of \( \mathrm{col}(B_{\mathrm{LoRA}}) \), beats either alone by up to 3.8%.
papers.relevance: A formal bridge between the activation-editing locus (loreft, red, road; representation-engineering, inference-time-intervention) and the weight locus (lora): to first order a weight update on the MLP is an activation shift, except for the output-projection term, and the post-block residual stream is where the activation locus can absorb it. It explains why ReFT-style residual-stream edits work, it is the same locus PreFT's \( \text{DiReFT}_P \) uses, and its orthogonality-constrained joint adapter is a hybrid entry point between the two loci.
corrections: claim: the 40-70% figure is the ratio of MLP-output norm to block-output norm (Sec. 3.3, Figs. 2-3), not a measured fraction of the oracle change recovered by post-MLP edits. Rephrased.
relevance: 'steering' is not a catalogue id. It is replaced by the existing paper ids representation-engineering and inference-time-intervention. DiReFT_P is wrapped in \( \).

papers.title: Diffract: Spectral View of LLM Domain Adaptation
papers.claim: On OLMo 2 (1B, 7B, 13B, plus released 32B checkpoints), continual pre-training on math, instruction, code and text leaves the singular-value spectra of the weights almost unchanged. Adaptation happens mainly through singular-vector changes concentrated near spectral peaks of attention matrices. Attention heads become heterogeneous as the pre-training budget grows. A head-importance criterion (CPT-delta Frobenius norms relative to a text-CPT reference) lets up to 60% of head updates be rewound to pre-trained values without measurable loss, and rewinding about 15% of heads raises math accuracy by up to 4% (7B). Dropping the smallest singular values of the CPT delta costs no measurable GSM8K accuracy up to 50% of them for 7B and 70% for 13B (1B deltas are less compressible), and linear interpolation between CPT checkpoints of different domains is smooth ('domain connectivity').
papers.relevance: Full-parameter CPT evidence on the shape of useful updates; it is not a PEFT method. Fixed spectra with rotating singular vectors are the signature of multiplicative orthogonal updates (oft, boft, goft preserve the singular values of \( W_0 \) exactly). A one-sided rotation changes the singular vectors on one side only, and the paper measures agreement of left singular vectors only (App. A.3), so it does not settle whether the observed rotations are one- or two-sided. The same finding cuts against value-only spectral tuning (svf), which cannot rotate singular vectors, so the seed's reading of it as support for SVF/SVFT/PiSSA/MiLoRA needs this qualification. The delta-truncation result supports low-rank compressibility of adaptation deltas (lora). Head rewind is selective sparsity at head granularity, and domain connectivity supports linear merging of domain deltas (task-arithmetic).

papers.title: The Appeal and Reality of Recycling LoRAs with Adaptive Merging
papers.claim: The study uses a pool of 958 user-contributed Hugging Face LoRAs for Llama 3.1 8B-Instruct and 62 target tasks with 100 labelled examples each. Adaptive merging (LoraHub, \( \pi \)-Tuning, AdaMerging, and a new method found by a design-space search) beats the base model but gives limited benefit over simply training a target-task LoRA on the same 100 examples (80 train, 20 validation); non-adaptive merges with fixed uniform coefficients (averaging, TIES, TSV) underperform the adaptive ones. Arrow, a zero-shot per-token router, is grouped with the non-adaptive methods in Fig. 2, although Sec. 4 lists it with the adaptive ones. When the target-task LoRA is in the pool, which recycled LoRAs are chosen hardly matters, and LoRAs with random parameter values work about as well. This points to a regularisation effect rather than positive transfer. Positive transfer does appear with a bespoke pool of highly relevant, consistently trained LoRAs.
papers.relevance: An empirical counterweight for the composition family (lorahub, arrow, adamerging, ties-merging, tsv-merge): reported gains from merging adapters largely reflect curated, task-relevant pools. In atlas terms, a composition operator on adapter space adds task information only when the pool contains relevant modules; otherwise it acts as a regulariser on the target-task adapter. PHATGOOSE-style routing is not evaluated, so that extension of the conclusion is untested.
corrections: claim: Arrow was listed as an adaptive merging method. It tunes no coefficients on target data, and the paper's Fig. 2 caption groups it with the non-adaptive methods (Sec. 4's text is inconsistent). Also added the 80/20 split of the 100 examples.

papers.title: Learning Dynamics of Zeroth-Order Optimization: A Kernel Perspective
papers.claim: One step of multi-perturbation ZO-SGD (two-point estimator, \( P \) perturbations) changes model log-probabilities through a projected eNTK \( \mathcal K(x_o,x_u;U)=\nabla_\theta z(x_o)^{\top}UU^{\top}\nabla_\theta z(x_u) \), with \( U\in\mathbb R^{d\times P} \) the stacked normalised perturbations. By an inner-product Johnson-Lindenstrauss lemma the kernel error is \( \epsilon=O(\sqrt{\ln V/P}) \), so the gap between ZO and first-order one-step dynamics is \( \lesssim\sqrt{V\log V/P} \) times model-dependent factors. This depends on the output size \( V \), not the parameter count \( d \), which explains ZO fine-tuning's success without the low-effective-rank Hessian assumption. Gaussian and Rademacher perturbations behave alike, and fidelity improves as \( O(1/\sqrt P) \) (validated on LeNet/MNIST and OPT-125M to 1.3B on SST-2).
papers.relevance: Extends kernel-view-lm-finetuning, which used a JL argument to show LoRA preserves the SGD fine-tuning kernel, to zeroth-order training. In both, a random low-dimensional projection approximately preserves the eNTK: ZO (mezo, zo-bench) redraws the projection every step in parameter space, while LoRA-style subspace training fixes one. This gives a common kernel-level account of the ZO entries alongside MeZO.

papers.title: Understanding LoRA as Knowledge Memory: An Empirical Analysis
papers.claim: Rank sweeps from 2 to 1024 with knowledge loads of 1K-20K tokens on Llama-3.1-8B and Qwen3-8B (PhoneBook key-value pairs, CounterFact edits) show that LoRA's memorisation capacity grows with rank but saturates at a rank-dependent load. Knowledge stored per trainable parameter peaks at low rank (around r=4). Among synthetic formats (QA, summary, rewrite), QA pairs give the largest gains and the best token-efficiency, mixing formats helps further, and a stronger generator (GPT-4.1 versus Llama-3.1-8B) helps. In multi-LoRA systems, top-1 embedding routing can underperform one LoRA holding everything, and merging the top-k retrieved modules trades routing errors against interference: TIES is best, and vanilla concatenation collapses mainly through scale mismatch: rescaling each factor by \( 1/\sqrt N \) recovers most of the gap to linear averaging. LoRA memory works best alongside RAG or ICL rather than replacing them.
papers.relevance: Updates the 2025 lora-knowledge-capacity entry with capacity curves, rank-efficiency measurements and multi-module composition. It is empirical analysis, not theory. It treats rank as a capacity knob (cf. lora-learns-less-forgets-less) and gives composition evidence relevant to document- and knowledge-module methods (doc-to-lora, text-to-lora, loraretriever, lorahub), including the calibration fact that concatenated adapters need \( 1/\sqrt N \) factor scaling.

papers.title: On the Convergence Rate of LoRA Gradient Descent
papers.claim: For vanilla LoRA gradient descent (\(A\) and \(B\) updated simultaneously on \(\mathcal{L}(BA)\)), assuming only that the loss is \(L\)-smooth and bounded below in the full weight \(W\), \(\min_{t<T}\|\nabla\mathcal{J}(V_t)\|^2=O(1/\log T)\), improving to \(O(1/T)\) if the iterates stay bounded. The factor-space loss is not smooth and the iterates are not assumed bounded. The proof stacks \(V=[B;A^{\top}]\), writes \(BA=E_1VV^{\top}E_2\) (a symmetric Burer--Monteiro form), proves a descent lemma with extra terms up to fourth order in the step, and uses the adaptive step \(\eta_t=\min\{1/(4\sqrt2L(\|V_t\|^2+\|\nabla\mathcal{L}(B_tA_t)\|)),1\}\) together with the worst-case growth \(\|V_t\|^2=O(t)\). The rate has no explicit dependence on the rank \(r\) (only through \(\|V_0\|\)), extends to many adapted matrices by block extraction, and \(V=0\) is always a stationary point of the reparametrised loss.
papers.relevance: The first non-asymptotic guarantee for plain LoRA gradient descent without boundedness assumptions, complementing the landscape result in lora-converges-or-fails-loudly. It locates the difficulty in the reparametrisation: the factor-space loss is only 'Lipschitz-like', with a constant growing like \(\|V\|^2\), so the usable step shrinks as the factors grow. This is the conditioning issue that the gauge-aware optimisers in the catalogue target (riemannian-preconditioned-lora, lora-rite, riemannion, balanced-lora). The stationary point at \(V=0\) exists whatever the loss of \(W_0\), one concrete way LoRA and full fine-tuning can end in different places.

papers.title: Understanding Catastrophic Forgetting In LoRA via Mean-Field Attention Dynamics
papers.claim: In a tied-weight, continuous-depth self-attention model where tokens evolve as interacting particles (on the sphere under Post-LayerNorm) and LoRA is a low-rank perturbation of \((Q,K,V)\), forgetting is measured as drift of the emergent cluster geometry, which the authors correlate with base-task perplexity. (i) A finite-time Wasserstein bound: \(W_2(\mu_t,\nu_t)\le c\,\varepsilon\,e^{c\,e^{ct}}\) for perturbations of operator norm \(\varepsilon\) (Prop. 3.1). (ii) For \(A=K^{\top}Q=V\succeq0\) with a spectral gap and a symmetric update \(\Delta V=\Delta A\), if \(\mathrm{gap}+a>2\|b\|+\|E\|_{op}\), with \(a=u_1^{\top}\Delta Vu_1\), \(b=P_{\perp}\Delta Vu_1\) and \(E=P_{\perp}\Delta VP_{\perp}\), the limiting cluster moves from \(u_1\) to \(\tilde u_1\) with \(\|u_1-\tilde u_1\|\lesssim(2\|b\|+\|E\|_{op})/(\mathrm{gap}+a)\) (Prop. 3.3). (iii) For i.i.d. random rank-\(r\) value adapters scaled by \(\eta_L\) at depth \(L\) there is a norm transition: \(\eta_L\ll\sqrt L\) keeps the mean-square distance to the pretrained cluster at \(O(1/L)\), while \(\eta_L=\sqrt L\) gives a diffusive regime with \(\sum_i\mathbb{E}\|x_i^{\ell}-u_1\|^2\simeq n\sum_{i\ge2}\kappa/(2(\lambda_1-\lambda_i)+d\kappa)\) (Thm. 4.2). (iv) A depth transition: perturbed tokens track the base dynamics up to a critical depth \(T^*\) and then move to a new clustering (Thm. 4.6). Experiments on Qwen3-0.6B show a loss transition in the perturbation norm; rank matters during LoRA training but not for isotropic random adapters, learned updates align with the top direction \(u_1\), and an empirical bifurcation depth moves earlier during fine-tuning. Llama-2-7B is used only to check clustering and the spectral assumptions, which few of its layers satisfy. The May 2026 v2 replaces the 2024 results.
papers.relevance: A dynamical-systems account of why LoRA forgets less but not nothing (cf. lora-learns-less-forgets-less): forgetting is governed by the update norm relative to a \(\sqrt L\) depth scale and by alignment with small-gap eigendirections of the pretrained attention. This gives a toy-model rationale for orthogonal-subspace and norm-controlled variants (o-lora, which the paper cites, and inflora) and opens a forgetting axis in the theory index, which so far covers optimisation and expressivity.

papers.title: Model Merging Scaling Laws in Large Language Models
papers.claim: The expected cross-entropy of merging \(k\) experts into a base of size \(N\) follows a floor-plus-tail law \(\mathbb{E}[L\mid N,k]=L_*+BN^{-\beta}+A_0N^{-\gamma}/(k+b)\), fitted in-domain and cross-domain over 10,866 merged models (Qwen2.5 0.5B to 72B, nine math, science and code domains, \(k=1,\dots,9\)) for Average, Task Arithmetic, TIES and DARE (\(R^2>0.98\)). Larger bases lower the floor and shrink the tail; most gains arrive early (\(k=5\) and \(k=6\) cross 85% and 90% of the nine-expert improvement); the variance across expert subsets shrinks like \(1/k\); and differences between methods compress at scale. A second-order Taylor argument for equal-weight merging (\(\alpha_{i,k}=c/k\)) gives \(\mathbb{E}[L]=L_\infty(N)+A(N)/k+O(k^{-3/2})\), with \(L_\infty=L(\theta_0)+c\,g^{\top}\mu+\tfrac{c^2}{2}\mu^{\top}H\mu\) and \(A=\tfrac{c^2}{2}\mathrm{Tr}(H\Sigma)\), where \(\mu\) and \(\Sigma\) are the mean and covariance of the task vectors. Three early points (\(k\in\{1,2,4\}\)) are enough to forecast the whole \(k\)-curve.
papers.relevance: Gives the post-hoc (P) kind a quantitative law: the return from merging is a curvature-weighted variance term \(\mathrm{Tr}(H\Sigma)/k\) on top of a mean-direction floor, the mean/covariance split that ties-merging, dare and merging-at-scale use informally. The controlled experts are full-parameter fine-tunes (App. D: lr \(10^{-5}\), ZeRO-3; the released OpenRLHF training script passes no LoRA option), not LoRAs; the authors note that LoRA rank and expert capacity would shift the fitted floor and tail, so transfer to adapter merging is plausible but untested.

papers.title: Zeroth-Order Optimization at the Edge of Stability
papers.claim: With the standard Gaussian two-point estimator, the mean dynamics of ZO-GD, ZO-GDM and frozen ZO-Adam near a minimum match their first-order counterparts (critical step \(2/\lambda_{\max}\) for GD), but mean-square linear stability depends on the whole Hessian spectrum. For ZO-GD the critical step \(\eta^*\) solves \(\sum_i\eta\lambda_i/(2(1-\eta\lambda_i))=1\) (with \(\eta\lambda_{\max}<1\)) and satisfies \(2/(\mathrm{Tr}H+2\lambda_{\max})\le\eta^*\le2/\mathrm{Tr}H\), with analogous bounds for momentum (factor \(1-\beta\)) and for frozen ZO-Adam with the preconditioned Hessian \(P^{-1}H\) (assuming \(PH=HP\)). Full-batch ZO-GD, ZO-GDM and ZO-Adam on CIFAR-10 CNN, ResNet and ViT models (and LSTM and Mamba sorting tasks) settle at this mean-square edge of stability, with catapults after step-size increases. Large ZO steps therefore implicitly regularise the Hessian trace, whereas first-order steps regularise the top eigenvalue; large smoothing \(\mu\) and mini-batching push training into flatter regimes.
papers.relevance: The implicit bias of the backward-lens (B) zeroth-order kind behind mezo, agzo, zo-muon and fzoo: ZO fine-tuning is limited by \(\mathrm{Tr}(H)\) rather than \(\lambda_{\max}\), consistent with MeZO's low-effective-rank explanation and with zo-learning-dynamics-kernel. The experiments use small vision and sequence models, not LLM fine-tuning, and the main theory uses MeZO's symmetric Gaussian estimator. Appendix B extends the covariance-operator framework one ingredient at a time: forward differences (with Gaussian directions), non-Gaussian directions (for the symmetric estimator) and multiple Gaussian queries. FZOO's combination of one-sided Rademacher probes with a shared baseline and a loss-std-normalised step is therefore not covered as such, and none of these variants was tested.

papers.title: Riemannian Structure and Optimization for a Class of Low-Parametric Orthogonal Matrices
papers.claim: For Group-and-Shuffle (GS) matrices \(A=B_mP_{m-1}B_{m-1}\cdots P_1B_1\) (block-diagonal factors interleaved with fixed permutations; Monarch and block-butterfly matrices are special cases), explicit counterexamples show that with rectangular or general square blocks the two-factor class is a product of bounded-rank sets and not a smooth manifold. With orthogonal blocks the two-factor class is an orbit of the compact Lie-group action \((B_2,B_1)\cdot x=B_2xB_1^{\top}\) and hence a closed embedded submanifold (recalled from OrthoFuse). For this case the paper derives the tangent-space projection, retractions (exponential, Cayley and polar; the experiments use polar with five Newton--Schulz steps) and vector transport. It computes Riemannian gradients by automatic differentiation without forming dense matrices, covering overlapping block supports and parameter sharing, and gives geodesics under extra block assumptions. It also proves \(\mathcal{A}_3^{\mathrm{orth}}=\mathcal{A}_3\cap O(N)\) and links the three-factor perfect-shuffle case to the CS decomposition. Riemannian SGD on GS-orthogonal adapters (\(b=8\), 1.38M parameters) for RoBERTa-base on GLUE beats Euclidean SGD (84.85 vs 83.12 average) but stays below AdamW (86.04), at 5 to 7% overhead.
papers.relevance: Says when the structured orthogonal groups of the OFT family (oft, boft, GSOFT) are smooth. The two-factor block-diagonal-with-permutation class is a manifold when its blocks are orthogonal (or unitary), which licenses Riemannian optimisation and base-point arguments for GSOFT-style two-factor adapters. The manifold property is proved only for \(m=2\) (for \(m=3\) the paper shows \(\mathcal{A}_3^{\mathrm{orth}}=\mathcal{A}_3\cap O(N)\)), so BOFT's longer butterfly products are not covered, and unconstrained block factorisations such as Monarch (monarch) are not manifolds in general. From the Rakhuba group (GSOFT, OrthoFuse, riemannion). Neither GSOFT (arXiv 2406.10019, NeurIPS 2024) nor OrthoFuse (arXiv 2604.05183, CVPR 2026) is in the catalogue yet.

papers.title: When Can Prefixes Compile LoRA? Exact Resource-Capped Tests for Frozen Attention
papers.claim: At one frozen causal softmax head with fixed content states, and a prefix of independent keys and values shared across inputs, the prefix sees the content only through \(\Sigma(X)=(q,Z_X,N_X)\) (query, partition function, value numerator), and \(\Sigma\) is a complete intervention statistic. Any adapter target that differs on two inputs with equal \(\Sigma\) therefore has an error floor at every prefix length, and with norm caps \(\|\kappa_t\|\le K\), \(\|\nu_t\|\le V\) the floor extends, independently of length, to nearly equal summaries. At a common query \(q_0\) every prefix reduces to two aggregates \((a,b)=(Z_S(q_0),N_S(q_0))\). With \(m\) capped slots the attainable set is \(\{me^{-L}\le a\le me^{L},\ \|b\|\le Va\}\) with \(L=K\|q_0\|/\sqrt{d_k}\), the optimal (projected) error is an attained second-order-cone program, and \(m\) identical slots realise the optimum; with a constant partition, the closure of prefix outputs is exactly \(t\,h_X+c\) with \(0\le t\le1\). Two equal-norm rank-one value updates can fall on opposite sides of compilability, extra capped slots can raise the optimal error, and both query-side and value-side updates can fail. Under affine query exposure, \(2r\) signed slots approximate a rank-\(r\) value update, with values growing as \(O(\epsilon^{-3/2})\); all 400 tolerance checks pass in float64 but only 38 in bfloat16. On three first-layer GPT-2 heads with a fixed readout token, the capped optimum (four slots) leaves 18.4% to 74.2% of a trained adapter's projected effect uncompiled. All claims are local to one head.
papers.relevance: A target-by-target comparison of the prefix (E0) and LoRA (R) kinds that sharpens the indexed prefix theory. It builds on the prefix decomposition of prefix-tuning-capabilities-limitations (Petrov et al. 2024b) and cites petrov-2024-prefix-universal; le-2025-revisiting-prefix and chen-2022-inducer-tuning are catalogue neighbours that it does not cite. A prefix can only mix the frozen head output with a query-dependent vector, so adapters that amplify the frozen output, or that separate inputs with equal \((q,Z,N)\), cannot be compiled. The same authors' 'Certification Frontiers for Gaussian LoRA' (arXiv 2609.32271, PAC-Bayes with KL minimised over the \(GL(r)\) gauge) was posted three days earlier (26 vs 29 September 2026) and was not added.
corrections: claim: added the definition \(L=K\|q_0\|/\sqrt{d_k}\) used in the attainable set (Theorem 6), that the \(t\,h_X+c\) description is the closure of prefix outputs (Eq. 11), and the four-slot setting of the GPT-2 test (Sec. 7.4); plain-text math rewritten in \( \).
relevance: recorded which catalogue ids the paper actually builds on or cites (Petrov et al. 2024b and 2024a) and that le-2025-revisiting-prefix and chen-2022-inducer-tuning are not cited.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv API: 2609.36766, v1 2026-09-29, authors Joyanta Jyoti Mondal and Ibne Farabi Shihab; year 2026; venue arXiv (not in any 2026 orals-posters JSON). Claim checked against the abstract, Sec. 3 (Eqs. 1 to 4), Lemma 1 (prefix decomposition, Petrov et al. 2024b), Sec. 4, Eqs. 10 to 12, Theorem 6 (Eqs. 13 to 15), Corollary 7, Theorem 9, the counterexample after it, Tables 1 and 5 (the amplifying optimum rises from 0.5180 to 1.0396 with more capped slots), Fig. 2 and Sec. 7.4 (18.4% to 74.2%). The sibling paper 2609.32271 (v1 2026-09-26, same authors) is confirmed by the arXiv API, and its abstract minimises KL over the full \(GL(r)\) symmetry. All 4 catalogue ids named are in existing_index.json; the id is unique.

papers.title: Task Arithmetic in the Tangent Space: Improved Editing of Pre-Trained Models
papers.claim: Weight disentanglement (distinct weight directions controlling separate, localized regions of function space) is the property that makes task arithmetic work; fine-tuning in the linearized (tangent) regime amplifies it and improves task addition and negation.
papers.relevance: Identifies when the map from task vectors to functions behaves like a linear map (a homomorphism of the additive structure), which is the precondition for treating merging as vector-space arithmetic.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.12827 (Ortiz-Jimenez, 2023); NeurIPS 2023 confirmed (arXiv journal-ref, papers.nips.cc). Weight-disentanglement claim matches the paper.

papers.title: Git Re-Basin: Merging Models modulo Permutation Symmetries
papers.claim: After accounting for permutation symmetries of hidden units, loss landscapes often contain nearly a single basin; aligning one model's units to another's permutation lets independently trained models be merged by linear interpolation.
papers.relevance: Shows that merging is well-defined only up to a symmetry group acting on weights; LoRA factorizations carry an analogous GL(r)/permutation gauge (cf. LoRA-LEGO, KnOTS), so adapters are naturally objects up to isomorphism.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2209.04836 (Ainsworth, 2022); ICLR 2023 per Semantic Scholar venue metadata. Claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Linear Mode Connectivity and the Lottery Ticket Hypothesis
papers.claim: Networks become stable to SGD noise early in training: from then on, runs that share a starting point end in minima connected by a linear path of low loss.
papers.relevance: Grounds the shared-basin assumption behind all merging of models or adapters fine-tuned from one pre-trained point, i.e. why deltas from a common base can be treated as vectors in one affine chart.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1912.05671 (Frankle, 2019); ICML 2020 per arXiv comment ('Published in ICML 2020'). Claim matches.

papers.title: Model Merging in LLMs, MLLMs, and Beyond: Methods, Theories, Applications and Opportunities
papers.claim: Proposes a taxonomy of model merging methods (pre-merging alignment, during-merging weighting/subspace/routing methods), reviews the theory, and surveys applications in LLMs, multimodal models and more than ten machine-learning subfields.
papers.relevance: The most complete map of the merging half of this family; its taxonomy is a reference point to check against a categorical classification of merge operators.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2408.07666 (Yang, 2024); published in ACM Computing Surveys (DOI 10.1145/3787849, 2026). The taxonomy claim matches the abstract.
corrections: venue: 'ACM Computing Surveys' -> 'ACM Computing Surveys 2026' (Crossref DOI 10.1145/3787849, issued 2026-02-09). The year field stays 2024, the arXiv first version.

papers.title: What Matters for Model Merging at Scale?
papers.claim: Merging experts fine-tuned from 1B-64B models shows that merging works better from strong (instruction-tuned) base models, larger models merge more easily and more experts, merged models generalize better, and different merging methods behave very similarly at large scale.
papers.relevance: Empirical evidence that at scale the choice of merge operator matters less than the base point, suggesting that the algebra of merging becomes closer to linear near strong pre-trained models.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.03617 (Yadav, 2024); TMLR 2025. The 1B-64B scale, up to 8 experts, and the five findings in the claim match the abstract.
corrections: venue: 'arXiv' -> 'TMLR 2025'. The TMLR accepted-paper list has 'What Matters for Model Merging at Scale?' (Yadav et al., July 2025, OpenReview qjNdGpgpV8).
confidence: medium -> high after confirming the venue and the five findings in the abstract.

papers.title: HyperNetworks
papers.claim: A small network can generate the weights of a larger main network and be trained end-to-end, acting as a relaxed form of weight sharing; generated non-shared LSTM weights reach near state-of-the-art results on sequence modelling.
papers.relevance: Adapter generators (HyperFormer, HyperDreamBooth, Text-to-LoRA, Doc-to-LoRA, DnD) are hypernetworks: maps from a conditioning space (task, image, text, document) into the space of adapters.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1609.09106 (Ha, 2016); ICLR 2017 per Semantic Scholar venue metadata. Claim matches.

papers.title: Neural Network Diffusion
papers.claim: An autoencoder plus a latent diffusion model trained on checkpoints can generate new, high-performing parameters for a subset of network weights that are not mere memorized copies of the training checkpoints.
papers.relevance: Establishes generative modelling directly over parameter (adapter) space, the line that prompt-conditioned LoRA generators such as Drag-and-Drop LLMs extend.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.13144 (Wang, 2024). No peer-reviewed venue found (Semantic Scholar lists arXiv), so venue stays 'arXiv'. The p-diff claim (autoencoder plus latent diffusion over a subset of parameters) matches the abstract.

papers.title: Reinforcement Learning Finetunes Small Subnetworks in Large Language Models
papers.claim: Across 7 RL-style algorithms (PPO, GRPO, KTO, DPO, SimPO, PRIME and rejection-sampling SFT) and 10 LLMs, RL updates only 5-30% of parameters. The updated subnetworks overlap far more than chance across seeds, datasets and algorithms, the sparse updates are nearly full-rank, and fine-tuning only that subnetwork recovers a model nearly identical to full RL fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: Shows the RL update is constrained in its support but not in its rank, a different algebraic type of constraint from low rank. This argues for selective/sparse rather than factorized PEFT when classifying what RL post-training actually changes.
corrections: claim: listed the 7 algorithms as in the paper (includes KTO, SimPO, PRIME and rejection-sampling SFT).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2505.11711 (Mukherjee, 2025); NeurIPS 2025 poster confirmed (OpenReview 0NdS4xCngO, DBLP conf/nips). Claims checked against the abstract and Secs. 3-5.

papers.title: The Path Not Taken: RLVR Provably Learns Off the Principals
papers.claim: RLVR's apparent sparsity comes from a model-conditioned bias: updates avoid the principal singular directions of the pretrained weights, preserve the spectrum and rotate the principal subspace very little, whereas SFT targets principal weights. A 'three-gate' theory (KL anchor, model geometry, bf16 precision) explains this.
papers.relevance: Predicts which PEFT parameterizations suit RL: principal-subspace initializations (PiSSA-style) conflict with RLVR geometry. Under RL, the spectral position of an adapter's subspace matters as much as its rank.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2511.08567 (Zhu, 2025). Only venue found is the NeurIPS 2025 Efficient Reasoning workshop spotlight (arXiv comment, OpenReview N75EWQQnb3); not in ICLR 2026. Three-gate theory, off-principal updates and "SFT targets principal weights" confirmed; the paper reports PiSSA gives no clear gain over LoRA under RLVR.

papers.title: RL's Razor: Why Online Reinforcement Learning Forgets Less
papers.claim: Forgetting is predicted by the forward KL between the fine-tuned and base policy on the new task; on-policy RL is implicitly biased toward KL-minimal solutions among those that solve the task, while SFT can converge arbitrarily far, which is why RL forgets less at equal new-task performance.
papers.relevance: Gives a distributional (KL) rather than parametric measure of how far an adaptation moves, a candidate invariant for comparing PEFT methods. It also helps explain why tiny-parameter adapters suffice for RL.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2509.04259 (Shenfeld, 2025); ICLR 2026 confirmed (mlanthology). Forward-KL forgetting predictor and the KL-minimal on-policy bias confirmed.

papers.title: Evaluating Parameter Efficient Methods for RLVR
papers.claim: Benchmarking 12+ PEFT methods under RLVR on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Qwen 1.5B/7B math reasoning: structural variants (DoRA, AdaLoRA, MiSS) beat standard LoRA, with DoRA even exceeding full fine-tuning on several benchmarks; SVD-informed initializations (PiSSA, MiLoRA) suffer 'spectral collapse'; and extreme compression (VeRA, rank-1) bottlenecks reasoning.
papers.relevance: The first systematic map of the PEFT design space under RL. Its rank-1 result is in tension with the LoRA Without Regret and TinyLoRA findings that a tiny rank or parameter count suffices for RL.
corrections: venue: arXiv -> ICML 2026 (OpenReview 76CIL1O0bz, "ICML 2026 regular").
sources: added OpenReview.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2512.23165 (Yin, 2025); venue corrected to ICML 2026. Claims (12+ methods, DeepSeek-R1-Distill 1.5B/7B, DoRA > full FT, PiSSA/MiLoRA spectral collapse, VeRA/rank-1 bottleneck) confirmed from the abstract and introduction.

papers.title: How Much Knowledge Can You Pack into a LoRA Adapter without Harming LLM?
papers.claim: Fine-tuning Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct with LoRA on growing amounts of new facts shows that a mixture of known and new facts works best, but packing in more new knowledge degrades general QA benchmarks, and biased data makes the model regress to a few over-represented answers and become overconfident.
papers.relevance: Quantifies the capacity/interference trade-off of a single low-rank adapter used as a knowledge store, relevant to adapter-as-memory views (Doc-to-LoRA, Cartridges, sparse memory finetuning).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2502.14502 (Pletenev, 2025); Findings of NAACL 2025 confirmed (ACL Anthology 2025.findings-naacl.243). Claims match the abstract.

papers.title: Gradient Projection Memory for Continual Learning
papers.claim: A layer's gradient updates lie in the span of its inputs. GPM stores per-layer orthonormal bases of the old tasks' representation subspaces, found by SVD of activations, and steps orthogonally to them, which causes little or no interference with past tasks and needs no replay.
papers.relevance: This input-space orthogonality is the mechanism InfLoRA builds into a LoRA down-projection (through DualGPM) and that O-LoRA approximates with LoRA subspaces. Categorically, each task's update is a morphism required to vanish on a sub-object (the old tasks' input subspace), which makes continual-learning PEFT a kernel condition.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2103.09762 (Saha, Garg, Roy, 2021) matches. ICLR 2021 oral confirmed by the arXiv journal-ref/comment and OpenReview id 3AOj0RCNC2. The claim matches the abstract and the method section.

papers.title: Orthogonal Gradient Descent for Continual Learning
papers.claim: Projecting new-task gradients onto the subspace in which the network's outputs on previous tasks stay unchanged mitigates catastrophic forgetting without storing data, but it does require storing gradient directions.
papers.relevance: Direct ancestor of O-LoRA, which replaces OGD's stored gradients with the LoRA subspaces of earlier tasks; in this sense O-LoRA is OGD transported into the low-rank adapter parameterization.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1910.07104 (Farajtabar et al., first version 2019) matches. AISTATS 2020 confirmed on PMLR v108 (farajtabar20a) and by DBLP conf/aistats/FarajtabarAML20. The claim that gradient directions must be stored, not data, is accurate.

papers.title: Finding Alignments Between Interpretable Causal Variables and Distributed Neural Representations
papers.claim: Distributed alignment search (DAS) learns, by gradient descent, an orthonormal (rotated) subspace of a hidden representation in which interchange interventions realize a high-level causal variable. This replaces brute-force alignment search and allows distributed, non-neuron-aligned representations.
papers.relevance: LoReFT is DAS's interchange intervention with the counterfactual source replaced by a learned affine map (R s -> W h + b). This links PEFT to causal abstraction: a ReFT is an endomorphism of the hidden-state space that acts only on one sub-object.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2303.02536 (Geiger, Wu, Potts, Icard, Goodman, first version 2023) matches. CLeaR 2024 confirmed on PMLR v236 (geiger24a) and on OpenReview (dblp.org/conf/CLEAR2/2024). The LoReFT link follows ReFT eq. 2 (R s replaced by W h + b).

papers.title: AxBench: Steering LLMs? Even Simple Baselines Outperform Sparse Autoencoders
papers.claim: On a large benchmark for concept steering and detection (Gemma-2-2B/9B), prompting outperforms every representation-based steering method, with finetuning second; difference-in-means is best for detection, and SAEs are not competitive on either task. A rank-1 representation finetuning (ReFT-r1) is competitive on both.
papers.relevance: Gives a sober empirical calibration of intervention-based (activation-editing) adaptation against prompts and weight finetuning, which is useful for placing the ReFT family next to input-augmentation and weight-update PEFT.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2501.17148 (Wu et al., 2025) matches. ICML 2025 spotlight poster confirmed on OpenReview (ICML.cc/2025/Conference). The claim matches the abstract: prompting is best for steering, finetuning is second, DiffMean is best for detection, SAEs are not competitive, and ReFT-r1 is competitive on both.

papers.title: Representation Engineering: A Top-Down Approach to AI Transparency
papers.claim: Population-level representations, rather than individual neurons or circuits, can be read out and manipulated to monitor and control high-level behaviours of LLMs such as honesty and harmlessness, using simple training-free reading vectors and representation-control operators.
papers.relevance: Training-free activation steering is the zero-training limit of representation interventions, and ReFT is its learned, task-supervised counterpart; the ReFT paper explicitly recasts RepE's operators as parametrizations of its intervention function.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2310.01405 (Zou et al., 2023) matches. No peer-reviewed venue was found (Semantic Scholar lists arXiv only), so the venue is 'arXiv'. The ReFT paper's App. B indeed recasts RepE's linear, piecewise and projection operators as ReFT intervention functions; the projection operator is a special case of LoReFT.

papers.title: Inference-Time Intervention: Eliciting Truthful Answers from a Language Model
papers.claim: Shifting activations along probe-derived 'truthful' directions in a small set of top-K attention heads, with no training, raises Alpaca's TruthfulQA truthfulness from 32.5% to 65.1%. There is a tunable trade-off between truthfulness and helpfulness.
papers.relevance: ITI is the training-free precursor of learned representation interventions: LoFiT casts ITI in its localize-then-offset framework and replaces both steps with learning, and ReFT's appendix shows how inference-time interventions fit its framework. Its edit, a constant offset on selected head outputs, is the zero-training corner of representation-level PEFT and is algebraically a bias on W^O. This makes 'steering' and 'fine-tuning' two ways of choosing the same kind of morphism.
corrections: relevance: removed RED from the list of ITI descendants (RED, arXiv 2402.15179, does not cite or build on ITI); grounded the LoFiT and ReFT links in their papers.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2306.03341 (Li, 2023-06; comment 'NeurIPS 2023 spotlight') confirmed; Alpaca TruthfulQA 32.5% -> 65.1% confirmed in the abstract and table.

papers.title: Laplace Redux -- Effortless Bayesian Deep Learning
papers.claim: The Laplace approximation, in cheap variants such as last-layer, K-FAC and linearized predictive, is competitive in performance with more popular Bayesian alternatives while costing much less. The paper releases the 'laplace' PyTorch library.
papers.relevance: It supplies the post-hoc machinery (K-FAC, linearized predictive, marginal-likelihood prior tuning) that Laplace-LoRA restricts to the adapter subspace. This turns a point adapter into a distribution over adapters: for the site, a lift of PEFT from points of a parameter space to a probability monad over it.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2106.14806 (Daxberger, 2021-06; comment 'NeurIPS 2021 camera-ready') confirmed; 'laplace' library (github.com/AlexImmer/Laplace) and competitiveness claims confirmed in the abstract and Sec. 5.

papers.title: Weight Uncertainty in Neural Networks
papers.claim: Bayes by Backprop learns a factorized Gaussian posterior over the weights by minimizing the variational free energy with reparameterized Monte-Carlo gradients. This gives principled weight uncertainty using ordinary backpropagation.
papers.relevance: BLoB applies this variational objective to the LoRA factor A. This makes the adapter a probability distribution over updates (a Kleisli-style lift of the additive-update functor) rather than a single point, which is the template for uncertainty-aware PEFT.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv API: title, first author Charles Blundell, 2015-05-20; ICML 2015 confirmed by the arXiv comment ('Proceedings of the 32nd ICML'). Claim matches the paper (diagonal Gaussian, reparameterized MC gradients of the variational free energy) and BLoB Sec. 2.

papers.title: The Reversible Residual Network: Backpropagation Without Storing Activations
papers.claim: Additive coupling blocks (y_1 = x_1 + F(x_2), y_2 = x_2 + G(y_1)) are exactly invertible. Activations can therefore be recomputed from the outputs during backpropagation, and activation memory becomes independent of depth.
papers.relevance: MEFT builds directly on this result. Reversibility makes each layer an isomorphism in the category of hidden-state spaces, which lets memory-efficient PEFT trade cached activations for recomputation.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv API: title, first author Aidan N. Gomez, 2017-07-14; NeurIPS (NIPS) 2017 confirmed by DBLP conf/nips/GomezRUG17 (pp. 2214-2224). Additive coupling y1=x1+F(x2), y2=x2+G(y1) is the paper's block; MEFT cites it as [41].

papers.title: The Truth is in There: Improving Reasoning in Language Models with Layer-Selective Rank Reduction
papers.claim: LASER removes the higher-order (small singular value) components of specific weight matrices in specific layers after training. This can improve LLM reasoning and factuality without any gradient updates, so small-singular-value directions often hold noise.
papers.relevance: LASER is the spectral precursor of Spectrum's SNR-based layer selection. With PiSSA, MiLoRA and LoRA-Dash, it shows that the singular spectrum of W_0 is a natural coordinate system in which to place, prune or select PEFT updates.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv API: title, first author Pratyusha Sharma, 2023-12-21; ICLR 2024 confirmed in proceedings.iclr.cc (2024 list) and Semantic Scholar. Spectrum cites LASER as the SNR/denoising precedent (Sec. 2).

papers.title: Importance Estimation for Neural Network Pruning
papers.claim: The squared first-order Taylor term (\partial\mathcal{L}/\partial W \cdot W)^2, accumulated over groups, is an accurate and cheap estimate of the loss change from removing a parameter or filter.
papers.relevance: LoRAPrune's criterion reuses this Taylor score but takes the gradient through the LoRA factors. That makes the same low-rank adapter both the update and a probe of the backbone's local geometry.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv API: title, first author Pavlo Molchanov, 2019-06-25; CVPR 2019 confirmed by DOI 10.1109/CVPR.2019.01152 (pp. 11256-11264). LoRAPrune Eq. 3 is exactly (∂L/∂W_ij · W_ij)^2 citing Molchanov et al. (2019).

papers.title: Understanding intermediate layers using linear classifier probes
papers.claim: Linear classifiers ('probes') trained independently on each layer's frozen features measure how linearly separable the representation is; on Inception v3 and ResNet-50 separability increases monotonically with depth.
papers.relevance: Names and formalizes the probe, the terminal object of selective PEFT (train only a linear map on frozen features) and the standard yardstick that every other adaptation method is compared against.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1610.01644 (Alain, 2016-10) confirmed; ICLR 2017 Workshop confirmed via OpenReview (ICLR.cc/2017/workshop submission; DBLP conf/iclr/AlainB17). Claim matches the abstract (Inception v3, ResNet-50, monotone separability).

papers.title: DExperts: Decoding-Time Controlled Text Generation with Experts and Anti-Experts
papers.claim: Combining a pretrained LM with expert and anti-expert LMs in a product of experts (adding and subtracting logits) controls attributes such as toxicity and sentiment, and works with small (anti-)experts, even on GPT-3.
papers.relevance: The output-space composition rule that proxy-tuning and EFT reuse for adaptation: tuning as a translation of logits.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2105.03023 (Alisa Liu, 2021-05; comment 'ACL 2021 camera-ready') and ACL Anthology 2021.acl-long.522 confirmed; claim (product of experts, small (anti-)experts, GPT-3) matches the abstract.

papers.title: Universal Adversarial Triggers for Attacking and Analyzing NLP
papers.claim: A gradient-guided search over tokens finds short input-agnostic trigger sequences that force a target prediction for any input, and these triggers transfer across models.
papers.relevance: The discrete-token search that AutoPrompt adapts from attacks to task prompting; the 'hard prompt' end of the prompt family.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1908.07125 (Wallace, 2019-08; comment 'EMNLP 2019') and ACL Anthology D19-1221 confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: FedPETuning: When Federated Learning Meets the Parameter-Efficient Tuning Methods of Pre-trained Language Models
papers.claim: A holistic empirical study of PEFT methods (adapters, prefix tuning, LoRA, BitFit) under federated learning: tuning and aggregating only lightweight parameters cuts communication greatly while keeping acceptable performance across heterogeneity levels, data scales and FL scenarios.
papers.relevance: Establishes federated PEFT as a setting where the adapter is the unit of communication and aggregation, which is where the algebraic issue of averaging factored updates (FFA-LoRA, FLoRA) arises.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2212.10025 (Zhuo Zhang, 2022-12) confirmed; the arXiv title is 'When Federated Learning Meets Pre-trained Language Models' Parameter-Efficient Tuning Methods', the Findings of ACL 2023 title (used here) is confirmed at ACL Anthology 2023.findings-acl.632. Adapter, prefix tuning, LoRA and BitFit are the PEFT methods studied.

papers.title: Towards Building the Federated GPT: Federated Instruction Tuning
papers.claim: Introduces Federated Instruction Tuning (FedIT) for LLMs, combining LoRA with FedAvg so that clients tune and upload only LoRA modules, which the server averages.
papers.relevance: The baseline whose separate averaging of A and B produces the cross-term aggregation error that FFA-LoRA and FLoRA correct.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.05644 (Jianyi Zhang, 2023-05) confirmed; ICASSP 2024 confirmed via Semantic Scholar/DBLP (conf/icassp). The paper adopts LoRA in the FedAvg framework (Sec. 3).

papers.title: Group Diffusion Transformers are Unsupervised Multitask Learners
papers.claim: Recasting visual generation tasks as generating a group of related images, by concatenating self-attention tokens across images in a DiT, enables task-agnostic zero-shot generation over 200 instructions in 30 tasks.
papers.relevance: The precursor that IC-LoRA simplifies: it shows that cross-image attention inside one DiT can carry task conditioning, which IC-LoRA then activates with a small LoRA instead of large-scale training.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.15027 (Lianghua Huang, 2024-10) confirmed; no peer-reviewed venue found (Semantic Scholar lists arXiv), so venue stays arXiv. '200 instructions across 30 tasks' matches the abstract.

papers.title: Intrinsic Dimensionality Explains the Effectiveness of Language Model Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Fine-tuning has very low intrinsic dimension: optimizing only about 200 parameters randomly projected into the full space recovers 90% of full RoBERTa performance on MRPC, larger and longer-pretrained models have lower intrinsic dimension, and this yields compression-based generalization bounds.
papers.relevance: The empirical foundation for low-rank adaptation and for asking how much rank each layer actually needs, the question rank-allocation methods answer adaptively.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2012.13255 (Aghajanyan, 2020); ACL-IJCNLP 2021 long (ACL Anthology 2021.acl-long.568). 200-parameter / 90% MRPC claim matches the abstract.
corrections: sources: added https://aclanthology.org/2021.acl-long.568/ (ACL-IJCNLP 2021 long, confirms venue)

papers.title: The Expressive Power of Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.claim: For fully connected networks LoRA can adapt any model f to accurately represent any smaller target model once LoRA-rank >= (width of f) x (depth of target)/(depth of f), under a mild assumption, with quantified approximation error below that threshold; for Transformer networks any model can be adapted to a same-size target with rank-(embedding size/2) LoRA adapters.
papers.relevance: Characterizes the image of the LoRA parametrization map, i.e. which fine-tuned functions are reachable at a given rank.
papers.verification_notes: ICLR 2024 poster confirmed (ICLR 2024 list).
corrections: claim: threshold is 'rank >=' (not 'exceeds') and the paper says 'accurately represent ... under a mild assumption'; wording aligned with the paper.
claim: added the paper's 'mild conditions' qualifier on the exact-representation theorem

papers.title: LoRA vs Full Fine-tuning: An Illusion of Equivalence
papers.claim: Even at matched task performance, LoRA and full fine-tuning produce structurally different weights. LoRA introduces new high-ranking singular vectors ('intruder dimensions') that full fine-tuning does not. These dimensions causally drive forgetting, scaling them down significantly improves modelling of the pre-training distribution with a minimal drop in task performance, and they accumulate in continual learning.
papers.relevance: Shows that the right notion of 'equivalence' between PEFT and full FT is not equal task loss. Invariants of the resulting weights, such as spectral structure relative to W_0, separate methods.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.21228 (Shuttleworth; 2024-10) matches; NeurIPS 2025 confirmed (neurips.cc/virtual/2025/poster/115207); wording aligned with the v3 abstract.
corrections: claim: 'restores' overstated the paper ('significantly improves modeling of the pre-training distribution')

papers.title: Editing Models with Task Arithmetic
papers.claim: Task vectors (fine-tuned minus pretrained weights) can be added, negated and combined arithmetically to steer model behaviour.
papers.relevance: Defines the vector-space (module) structure on adapters that PEFT's add_weighted_adapter (linear/svd/cat), TIES, DARE and GenKnowSub operate in.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv id/title/first author/year checked by batch arXiv API query; ICLR 2023 confirmed.

papers.title: LoRA Learns Less and Forgets Less
papers.claim: On code and math (instruction tuning and continued pretraining) LoRA substantially underperforms full fine-tuning at standard ranks but better preserves out-of-domain abilities; full fine-tuning learns perturbations of 10-100x higher rank than typical LoRA configs.
papers.relevance: Quantifies the capacity/forgetting trade-off that motivates high-rank-through-low-rank methods (ReLoRA, COLA, Delta-LoRA) and regularization views of LoRA.
papers.verification_notes: TMLR (Aug 2024, Featured Certification) confirmed via arXiv comment; also presented in the ICLR 2025 journal track. 10-100x rank claim confirmed.

papers.title: The Impact of Initialization on LoRA Finetuning Dynamics
papers.claim: Of the two zero-product initializations, (A random, B=0) and (A=0, B random), the first permits larger stable learning rates and yields more efficient feature learning, so it performs better on average; the two are not equivalent despite both giving BA=0.
papers.relevance: Shows that the choice of base point within the zero-update fibre {(B,A): BA=0} matters dynamically, which is exactly the degree of freedom the init family exploits; a unified theory must treat initialization as a choice of point in the factor space, not just of \Delta W.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2406.08447 (Hayou, 2024); NeurIPS 2024 poster (OpenReview, NeurIPS poster 93375). Claim matches the abstract/TL;DR.

papers.title: LoRA Without Regret
papers.claim: LoRA matches full fine-tuning in a 'low-regret' regime: when it is applied to all weight matrices, especially MLP/MoE layers, and is not capacity-limited. Attention-only LoRA underperforms. The optimal LoRA learning rate is about 10x the full-FT optimum, and rank 1 suffices for policy-gradient RL because RL absorbs only about 1 bit per episode.
papers.relevance: A widely shared capacity argument (bits learned versus parameters exposed) that states when the restriction to a rank-r sub-object costs nothing. It is useful for calibrating claims of 'equivalence' between PEFT and full fine-tuning.
papers.verification_notes: Blog post confirmed at thinkingmachines.ai/blog/lora/ (John Schulman in collaboration with others at Thinking Machines, Sep 29 2025; DOI 10.64434/tml.20250929). The 10x LR ratio, the MLP/all-layers finding, RL at ranks as low as 1 and the ~1 bit per episode argument were all checked in the text. There is no arXiv id.
corrections: authors: 'Schulman et al.' -> 'Schulman & Thinking Machines Lab', the post's own citation form
sources: added the post's DOI 10.64434/tml.20250929 (resolves to the blog)

papers.title: Scaling Down to Scale Up: A Guide to Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Taxonomy covering over 50 papers (early 2019 to mid-2024) that sorts methods into addition-based (adapter-like, soft prompts, other), selection-based, reparametrization-based and hybrid. A head-to-head comparison of 15 methods (14 in the body text) on models up to 11B finds that Houlsby adapters and LoRA are consistently best, that methods reported to beat LoRA struggle under limited hyperparameter search, and that LayerNorm tuning is unexpectedly competitive.
papers.relevance: One of the standard taxonomies (additive / selective / reparametrisation / hybrid) that the categorical classification should refine. Its efficiency comparison is a useful empirical check on the theory.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2303.15647 (Lialin; 2023-03, v2 covers 2019 to mid-2024) matches; no venue found, so arXiv. Section headings in v2 confirm that Houlsby adapters and LoRA perform best, hybrid methods are hyperparameter-sensitive, and LN tuning is unexpectedly competitive.
corrections: claim: v2 abstract says 'over 50 papers published between early 2019 and mid-2024', not 50 methods
claim: stated the method count as in the abstract (15) and body (14)

papers.title: On the Crucial Role of Initialization for Matrix Factorization
papers.claim: Nyström initialization (X_0=A\Omega with Gaussian \Omega, Y_0=0) lets ScaledGD converge quadratically for matrix factorization where only linear rates were known; applied to LoRA as NoRA (B_0=W_0\Omega, A_0=0) and NoRA+ (with ScaledGD) it improves fine-tuning of 1B-7B LLMs and diffusion models.
papers.relevance: Provides an optimization-theoretic justification for weight-aware (sketch-of-W_0) initialization and its pairing with preconditioned optimizers, the same pairing LoRA-One uses.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.18965 (Li, 2024); ICLR 2025 poster (OpenReview, ICLR poster 29262). Quadratic-rate claim and NoRA (X_0=W_0 Omega, Y_0=0; NoRA+ with ScaledGD) checked in Sec. 4.

papers.title: Asymmetry in Low-Rank Adapters of Foundation Models
papers.claim: In \Delta W=BA, A acts as an input feature extractor and B maps features to outputs; a random untrained A performs nearly as well as a tuned one, and training only B gives better information-theoretic generalization bounds.
papers.relevance: Explains why fixing the input-side factor costs little (LoRA-FA-style, LoRA-SB/LoRA-XS fixed bases) and why the two factors play non-symmetric roles in any categorical description of the adapter; MiCA, which freezes the output factor B and trains A, is a counterpoint to its recommendation to train B.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.16842 (Zhu, 2024); ICML 2024 (PMLR v235 zhu24c). Claim matches the abstract.
corrections: relevance: MiCA freezes B (the output side) and trains A, the opposite of the paper's 'train B' recommendation, so it cannot be cited as explained by it
relevance: freezing A is not a gauge fixing (not every rank-r update has a representative with that A); it restricts the image

papers.title: A Unified Study of LoRA Variants: Taxonomy, Review, Codebase, and Empirical Evaluation
papers.claim: Organizes LoRA variants along rank, optimization dynamics, initialization and MoE axes, releases a modular codebase (LoRAFactory), and finds that LoRA and its variants are far more sensitive to learning rate than to other hyperparameters and that a well-tuned vanilla LoRA matches or beats most variants.
papers.relevance: A taxonomy whose initialization (weight-, gradient-, activation-driven) and rank-allocation axes coincide with this family, and an important empirical caution that apparent gains of init/rank methods may partly reflect learning-rate tuning.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2601.22708 (He, 2026), arXiv only (comment: submitted to IEEE TPAMI). Four-axis taxonomy, LoRAFactory and learning-rate finding match the abstract.

papers.title: Measuring the Intrinsic Dimension of Objective Landscapes
papers.claim: Training in a random low-dimensional affine subspace of parameter space reveals an 'intrinsic dimension' at which solutions appear, often far smaller than the parameter count; for a given task and architecture family (e.g. FC nets on MNIST, d_int90 ~ 750) it stays roughly constant across a wide range of widths and depths.
papers.relevance: Original evidence that useful updates live in tiny subspaces; LoRA's rank-r factorization is a structured, learnable version of the random-subspace construction.
papers.verification_notes: ICLR 2018 confirmed (arXiv comment, Semantic Scholar/DBLP).
corrections: claim: the paper reports approximate constancy across widths/depths for a fixed architecture/dataset and explicitly warns against generalizing; replaced 'nearly constant across model sizes'.
relevance: the reparametrisation is the affine map z -> theta_0 + P z; 'linear map pulled back along the frozen point' was imprecise

papers.title: A Kernel-Based View of Language Model Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Prompt-based fine-tuning of pretrained LMs often exhibits kernel (eNTK) dynamics; in that regime, a Johnson-Lindenstrauss argument shows SGD-LoRA preserves the fine-tuning kernel, explaining why low-rank subspace methods work.
papers.relevance: Gives the linearized (functorial-in-the-tangent-space) picture in which LoRA is a random projection of the full fine-tuning kernel; baseline for NTK-regime LoRA theory.
papers.verification_notes: ICML 2023 confirmed (arXiv comment + ICML 2023 list); JL-based kernel preservation for LoRA confirmed in the appendix.

papers.title: LoRA Training in the NTK Regime has No Spurious Local Minima
papers.claim: In the NTK regime with N data points, full fine-tuning admits a low-rank solution of rank about sqrt(N); LoRA with rank of order sqrt(N) has no spurious local minima, so (S)GD finds such low-rank solutions, which generalize well.
papers.relevance: Landscape result for the bilinear LoRA parametrization; justifies optimizer-agnostic success of LoRA in the linearized regime.
papers.verification_notes: ICML 2024 (Oral) confirmed (ICML 2024 list); r <~ sqrt(N) / r >~ sqrt(N) statements confirmed in the abstract.

papers.title: LoRA Training Provably Converges to a Low-Rank Global Minimum or It Fails Loudly (But it Probably Won't Fail)
papers.claim: Without linearization, the paper separates a 'special' regime (where linearization holds) from a 'generic' one. In the generic regime, LoRA training converges either to a low-rank, small-magnitude global minimizer or to a qualitatively different high-rank, large-magnitude solution. Zero initialization and weight decay bias training toward the low-rank, small-magnitude region where the global minima lie.
papers.relevance: A landscape result for LoRA that does not rely on linearization. It links the identity-at-init convention (B = 0) and weight decay to an implicit bias, which a structural theory should model as part of the reparametrisation data.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2502.09376 (Kim, Junsu; 2025-02) matches; ICML 2025 confirmed in PMLR v267; the special/generic regimes and the implicit-bias claim match the abstract.
corrections: relevance: removed the unverifiable superlative 'most general ... to date'

papers.title: Understanding the Learning Dynamics of LoRA: A Gradient Flow Perspective on Low-Rank Adaptation in Matrix Factorization
papers.claim: For LoRA on matrix factorization under gradient flow, small initialization converges to a neighbourhood of the optimum whose error is governed by misalignment between pretrained and target singular spaces; a small spectral initialization converges to arbitrary precision.
papers.relevance: Clean dynamical model connecting initialization scale and singular-subspace alignment, the mechanism exploited by LoRA-GA and LoRA-One.
papers.verification_notes: AISTATS 2025 confirmed (PMLR 258:4636-4644).

papers.title: Learning Rate Matters: Vanilla LoRA May Suffice for LLM Fine-tuning
papers.claim: Re-evaluating nine LoRA variants (initialization, architectural and optimizer changes, incl. PiSSA, MiLoRA, LoRA-GA, DoRA, LoFT) with thorough hyperparameter search shows they prefer different learning-rate ranges but reach similar peak performance (within 1-2%) once LR is tuned; the LR differences track the largest Hessian eigenvalue.
papers.relevance: Important caution for any taxonomy: many training-dynamics variants may be reparametrizations of the learning rate rather than genuinely different adaptation morphisms.
papers.verification_notes: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026 (poster; NeurIPS 2026 accepted list, authors Yu-Ang Lee, Ching-Yun Ko, Pin-Yu Chen). Nine variants, within 1-2% after LR tuning, largest-Hessian-eigenvalue explanation confirmed in the abstract.
corrections: venue: 'arXiv' -> 'NeurIPS 2026' (listed as an accepted poster in the NeurIPS 2026 orals/posters data).

papers.title: LoRA Meets Dropout under a Unified Framework
papers.claim: LoRA fine-tuning is still overfitting-prone; transformer dropout variants (DropKey, DropAttention, HiddenCut) can be unified by dropping position, structural pattern and compensation, and the best combination (HiddenKey) improves LoRA on NLU and NLG.
papers.relevance: Complements LoRA Dropout: places regularization of the low-rank branch inside a general design space.
papers.verification_notes: Findings of ACL 2024 confirmed (ACL Anthology 2024.findings-acl.119); HiddenKey and the dropping-position / structural-pattern / compensation framework confirmed.
corrections: venue: normalised 'ACL 2024 (Findings)' to 'Findings of ACL 2024' (ACL Anthology 2024.findings-acl.119).

papers.title: Learning towards Minimum Hyperspherical Energy
papers.claim: Defines hyperspherical energy, a Thomson-problem-style potential of neurons on the unit sphere, as a measure of neuron diversity, and regularizes networks to minimize it.
papers.relevance: Hyperspherical energy is the invariant that OFT, BOFT, GOFT and HRA preserve. Orthogonal group actions are exactly the isometries that fix pairwise neuron angles, so orthogonal PEFT is fine-tuning inside an orbit that keeps this invariant.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1805.09298 (Liu, 2018) matches; NeurIPS 2018 confirmed by arXiv comment and Semantic Scholar. Claim matches the abstract (Thomson-problem MHE regularizer).

papers.title: Orthogonal Over-Parameterized Training
papers.claim: Trains a network by learning an orthogonal transformation applied to fixed, randomly initialized neurons. This provably keeps the hyperspherical energy constant and improves generalization.
papers.relevance: Direct precursor of OFT: the trainable object is only a group element of O(d) acting on a frozen weight, which is the template for every multiplicative PEFT method.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2004.04690 (Liu, 2020) matches; CVPR 2021 (oral) confirmed by arXiv comment. Claim matches the abstract (fixed random neurons, learned orthogonal transformation, provably minimal hyperspherical energy).

papers.title: Weight Normalization: A Simple Reparameterization to Accelerate Training of Deep Neural Networks
papers.claim: Reparameterizes each weight vector as w = g v/||v||, separating magnitude from direction, which improves conditioning and speeds up SGD.
papers.relevance: The template for the magnitude-direction decompositions in DoRA, BiDoRA and DeLoRA: a polar-type factorization of each neuron into a radial scalar and a point on the sphere.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1602.07868 (Salimans, 2016) matches; NeurIPS (NIPS) 2016 confirmed by DBLP conf/nips/SalimansK16.

papers.title: FiLM: Visual Reasoning with a General Conditioning Layer
papers.claim: A feature-wise affine modulation (gamma ⊙ x + beta), predicted from a conditioning input, is a simple and general conditioning layer for neural networks.
papers.relevance: Feature-wise scale and shift is the algebraic building block behind (IA)³, SSF, RED, DiffFit and LN tuning: an action of the diagonal affine group on channels, learned as a static vector instead of predicted per input.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1709.07871 (Perez, 2017) matches; AAAI 2018 confirmed by arXiv comment and DBLP.

papers.title: Learning Fast Algorithms for Linear Transforms Using Butterfly Factorizations
papers.claim: Products of O(log n) sparse butterfly factors can represent and learn fast transforms (FFT, DCT, Hadamard, ...) with O(n log n) parameters.
papers.relevance: The structural basis of BOFT and of GOFT's parallel Givens layers: dense group elements written as short words in sparse generators, which is how multiplicative PEFT reaches dense rotations cheaply.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1903.05895 (Dao, 2019) matches; ICML 2019 confirmed by arXiv comment.

papers.title: Cheap Orthogonal Constraints in Neural Networks: A Simple Parametrization of the Orthogonal and Unitary Group
papers.claim: Parameterizes the special orthogonal and unitary groups through the exponential map from skew-symmetric (Lie-algebra) matrices, so optimization is unconstrained while orthogonality holds exactly.
papers.relevance: Supplies the Lie algebra to Lie group charts (exponential, Cayley) that OFT, BOFT, OFTv2, PSOFT and Spectral Adapter use. In these terms, multiplicative PEFT is gradient descent in a Lie algebra pushed forward to a group acting on W_0.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1901.08428 (Lezcano-Casado, 2019) matches; ICML 2019 confirmed by DBLP conf/icml/CasadoM19. Abstract confirms the exponential-map parameterization of SO(n), U(n) and compact connected Lie groups.
corrections: confidence: medium -> high (venue and claim confirmed)

papers.title: Efficient Orthogonal Parametrisation of Recurrent Neural Networks Using Householder Reflections
papers.claim: Parameterizes orthogonal transition matrices as products of Householder reflections, which gives exact orthogonality and a tunable trade-off between the number of reflections and expressivity at low cost.
papers.relevance: The ancestor of HRA and ETHER: Householder words generate O(d), and word length controls capacity. HRA's 'r reflections = identity plus rank r' is the PEFT version of this fact.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1612.00188 (Mhammedi, first version Dec 2016) matches; ICML 2017 confirmed by DBLP conf/icml/MhammediHRB17.
corrections: confidence: medium -> high (venue and claim confirmed)

papers.title: The Primacy of Magnitude in Low-Rank Adaptation
papers.claim: Argues that the magnitude of the weight update is the main driver of LoRA performance and that low-rank structure bounds it. Proposes LoRAM, a magnitude-driven initialization that matches spectral initializations without their SVD cost.
papers.relevance: Isolates the magnitude half of magnitude-direction decompositions (DoRA, DeLoRA, PoLAR) and suggests that many spectral or initialization gains come down to controlling update magnitude.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2507.06558 (Zhang, 2025) matches; NeurIPS 2025 (spotlight) confirmed by arXiv journal-ref and NeurIPS 2025 data. Claim matches the abstract (LoRAM 'Basis & Basis' magnitude-driven initialization).
corrections: confidence: medium -> high (venue and claim confirmed)

papers.title: When Do Prompting and Prefix-Tuning Work? A Theory of Capabilities and Limitations
papers.claim: Although continuous embeddings are more expressive than discrete tokens, soft prompting and prefix-tuning are potentially less expressive than full fine-tuning, even with the same number of learnable parameters. A prefix cannot change the relative attention pattern over the content and can only bias an attention layer's output in a fixed direction, so these methods elicit existing skills but may fail on tasks that need new attention patterns.
papers.relevance: Precisely characterises the image of the prefix reparametrisation: a prefix cannot change the relative attention pattern over the content and can only bias an attention layer's output in a fixed direction. This justifies placing prompt/prefix methods in a separate class (input composition) from weight-space updates.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2310.19698 (Petrov; 2023-10) matches; ICLR 2024 per the arXiv comment and the ICLR 2024 virtual list (poster 18932); wording aligned with the abstract.
corrections: claim: 'strictly less expressive' overstated the paper, which says 'potentially less expressive'
relevance: replaced 'affine bias' with the paper's actual statement (fixed-direction bias, unchanged relative attention pattern)

papers.title: Universality and Limitations of Prompt Tuning
papers.claim: There exists a transformer for which prompts approximate any Lipschitz sequence-to-sequence function; conversely, for a given single encoder layer there are datasets that no prompt of any length can memorize, with a lower bound on prompt parameters compared against a LoRA update in the single-layer setting, and sufficient conditions in the multi-layer case under which only invertible functions can be learned.
papers.relevance: Gives both a universality (density) statement and an obstruction for prompt tuning, and a direct parameter-count comparison with low-rank weight updates.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2305.18787 confirmed; NeurIPS 2023 poster (OpenReview zWxKYyW9ik).
corrections: claim: the memorization impossibility is proved for a given single encoder layer, not for general finite-depth transformers; added the multi-layer invertibility result

papers.title: Prompting a Pretrained Transformer Can Be a Universal Approximator
papers.claim: Prefix-tuning a single attention head suffices to approximate any continuous function, and any sequence-to-sequence function can be approximated by prefixing a transformer of depth linear in the sequence length, with Jackson-type bounds on the required prefix length.
papers.relevance: Complements the limitation results: the prompt family is universal for suitably chosen (even small) pretrained models, so its expressivity depends on the frozen backbone, a functorial dependence worth formalizing.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.14753 confirmed; ICML 2024, PMLR v235 petrov24a.
corrections: url: pointed to the PMLR proceedings page (confirmed)

papers.title: On the Role of Attention in Prompt-tuning
papers.claim: In one-layer attention models on contextual mixture data, softmax prompt-attention is provably more expressive than softmax self-attention and linear prompt-attention; gradient descent learns the prompt with near-optimal sample complexity and the prompt attends to sparse context-relevant tokens.
papers.relevance: Isolates the attention mechanism as the channel through which prompts act, with learning-theoretic guarantees.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2306.03435 confirmed; ICML 2023, PMLR v202 oymak23a.
corrections: url: pointed to the PMLR proceedings page (confirmed)

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of State Space Models
papers.claim: For S4, any prefix acts on the outputs only through an initial hidden state, so prefix-tuning is upper-bounded by initial-state tuning, with equality iff the prefix length is at least the state size H (under a genericity assumption); prompt-based methods are therefore weak on SSMs, LoRA works best on linear projections, and Sparse Dimension Tuning (SDT) is proposed for SSM modules.
papers.relevance: A clean theorem embedding the prompt family into the 'learned initial state' family: on SSMs, prompts are points of the state space the recurrence starts from (all of it once \ell \ge H).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.09016 confirmed; ICML 2025 per arXiv comment; Prop. 1 and SDT ('Sparse Dimension Tuning' in the current version) checked.
corrections: claim: stated Prop. 1 as one inclusion plus a conditional converse rather than plain equivalence
relevance: 'identifying' overstated Prop. 1; it is an embedding that is onto only when the prefix length is at least H

papers.title: Revisiting Prefix-tuning: Statistical Benefits of Reparameterization among Prompts
papers.claim: The MLP reparametrization in prefix-tuning implicitly shares structure between prefix keys and values; via the prefix-tuning/mixture-of-experts connection this shared structure provably improves sample efficiency of parameter estimation, with similar benefits for prompt tuning.
papers.relevance: Explains why training-time reparametrizations (prefix MLP, P-Tuning encoder, Residual PT) matter even though they vanish at inference: they change the statistical geometry, not the hypothesis class.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.02200 confirmed; ICLR 2025 poster (OpenReview QjTSaFXg25); claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Exploring Universal Intrinsic Task Subspace via Prompt Tuning
papers.claim: Soft prompts of 100 NLP tasks can be decomposed into a shared 250-dimensional nonlinear subspace; tuning only 250 free parameters recovers 97% (seen tasks) and 83% (20 unseen tasks) of full prompt-tuning performance.
papers.relevance: Empirical evidence that the 'space of task adaptations' reachable by prompts is low-dimensional and shared, motivating a moduli-space view of PEFT.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.07867 confirmed. arXiv comment says it was previously accepted to Findings of ACL 2022 and Findings of EMNLP 2022; final version published in IEEE/ACM TASLP vol. 32 (2024) pp. 3631-3643, DOI 10.1109/TASLP.2024.3430545, as 'Exploring Universal Intrinsic Task Subspace for Few-Shot Learning via Prompt Tuning'.
corrections: venue: published in IEEE/ACM Transactions on Audio, Speech, and Language Processing 32 (2024), confirmed via Crossref and OpenReview/dblp
url: pointed to the journal DOI
confidence: metadata and venue now confirmed

papers.title: On Transferability of Prompt Tuning for Natural Language Processing
papers.claim: Soft prompts transfer zero-shot to similar tasks on the same PLM and, through a trained cross-model projector, to other PLMs; as initialization they accelerate and improve prompt tuning; the overlap rate of activated neurons predicts transferability better than embedding similarity.
papers.relevance: Treats prompts as transportable objects between tasks and between models (a projector is literally a map between prompt spaces of different backbones).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2111.06719 and ACL Anthology 2022.naacl-main.290 confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Prompt Waywardness: The Curious Case of Discretized Interpretation of Continuous Prompts
papers.claim: Continuous prompts can solve a task while their nearest-neighbour discrete projection is arbitrary text (even a contradictory task definition), within ~2% of the best prompt's accuracy; the effect grows with model size.
papers.relevance: Shows that the map from continuous prompts back to discrete text is far from faithful: soft prompts live outside the image of the vocabulary embedding, so 'discrete prompting' is a thin subobject of the prompt space.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2112.08348 and ACL Anthology 2022.naacl-main.266 confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Pre-train, Prompt, and Predict: A Systematic Survey of Prompting Methods in Natural Language Processing
