papers.claim: Systematizes prompt-based learning (templates, answer spaces, discrete and continuous prompts, tuning strategies such as fixed-LM prompt tuning and prompt+LM tuning).
papers.relevance: Standard reference for the discrete/continuous prompt landscape and its notation.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2107.13586 confirmed; ACM Computing Surveys 55(9) (2023), DOI 10.1145/3560815 via Crossref.
corrections: url: pointed to the ACM Computing Surveys DOI (confirmed)

papers.title: Inducer-tuning: Connecting Prefix-tuning and Adapter-tuning
papers.claim: Interprets prefixes as inducing variables of a kernel estimator in attention and proposes inducer-tuning, which keeps prefix-tuning's mechanism but uses an adapter-style residual form to fix prefix initialization.
papers.relevance: A second, kernel-theoretic bridge between the prompt and adapter families (low citation count, kept for its structural content).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2210.14469 and ACL Anthology 2022.emnlp-main.50 confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Gradient Descent Happens in a Tiny Subspace
papers.claim: After a short period of training, the gradient converges to a very small subspace spanned by the top few Hessian eigenvectors (about as many as there are classes) and stays there.
papers.relevance: Empirical basis for the 'dual' (gradient-side) PEFT view: if the gradient flow is effectively low-dimensional, projecting gradients (GaLore, Flora, APOLLO) or confining updates to low-rank parameter subspaces (LoRA) loses little. It also explains why projector refresh schedules matter.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1812.04754 (Gur-Ari, 2018) confirmed; arXiv only (DBLP lists CoRR). Claim matches the abstract (top Hessian eigenvectors, about as many as classes).

papers.title: Adafactor: Adaptive Learning Rates with Sublinear Memory Cost
papers.claim: Adam's per-parameter second moment for a weight matrix can be replaced by its row and column sums (a rank-one factorization), cutting optimizer memory from O(nm) to O(n+m) with similar results. Update clipping and an increasing decay rate fix the resulting instability.
papers.relevance: The prototype of optimizer-state compression: factoring the second moment is the optimizer-side counterpart of factoring the weight update. It is reused directly by Flora and AdaLomo and shares a lineage with Adam-mini, APOLLO and GaLore-Adafactor.
corrections: sources: added https://proceedings.mlr.press/v80/shazeer18a.html
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1804.04235 (Shazeer, 2018) confirmed; ICML 2018 (DBLP conf/icml/ShazeerS18). Factored second moment, update clipping and increasing decay confirmed.

papers.title: 8-bit Optimizers via Block-wise Quantization
papers.claim: Block-wise dynamic quantization, combined with a stable embedding layer, lets Adam and momentum states be stored in 8 bits with no loss in performance, removing about 75% of optimizer-state memory.
papers.relevance: Shows that optimizer states, not just weights, can be quantized. Its block-wise quantization (released in bitsandbytes) is the basis of QLoRA's block-wise NF4/double quantization and of 8-bit GaLore, and its 8-bit Adam is the baseline of GaLore 2. Paged optimizers were added later by QLoRA, not by this paper.
corrections: relevance: the paging infrastructure is QLoRA's contribution (the 8-bit optimizers paper has no paging); rewrote the lineage accordingly
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.02861 (Dettmers, 2021) confirmed; ICLR 2022 spotlight (arXiv comment, DBLP). Block-wise dynamic quantization and stable embedding layer confirmed; 75% is the 32-bit -> 8-bit state reduction.

papers.title: Subspace Optimization for Large Language Models with Convergence Guarantees
papers.claim: GaLore does not always converge to a stationary point in the stochastic setting: SVD projectors become noise-dominated when the true gradient is small, as an explicit counterexample shows. It does converge with large batches or isotropic noise. GoLore, which samples random projections uniformly from the Stiefel manifold, provably converges at standard batch sizes.
papers.relevance: Gives the projector-selection morphism of gradient-side PEFT a precise convergence semantics. Data-dependent (SVD) projectors and data-independent (random) projectors behave differently, which explains the shift toward random or online projectors (Flora, APOLLO, Online Subspace Descent).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.11289 (He, 2024) confirmed; ICML 2025 (PMLR v267 he25i). Non-convergence counterexample (Thm 4), convergence with large batches or isotropic noise, GoLore sampling P from the uniform distribution on the Stiefel manifold confirmed.

papers.title: Revisiting Zeroth-Order Optimization for Memory-Efficient LLM Fine-Tuning: A Benchmark
papers.claim: A benchmark of BP-free zeroth-order fine-tuning across five LLM families, three task difficulties and five fine-tuning schemes. It finds that task alignment and the forward-gradient method matter, and proposes block-wise descent, hybrid ZO/FO training and gradient sparsity to improve ZO fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: Maps the design space around MeZO and shows that ZO estimators combine naturally with parameter-side PEFT (LoRA, prefix). That makes the zeroth-order axis composable with the parametrization axis in a unified theory.
corrections: sources: added https://proceedings.mlr.press/v235/zhang24ad.html
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.11592 (Zhang, 2024) confirmed; ICML 2024 (PMLR v235 zhang24ad). Five LLM families, three task complexities, five fine-tuning schemes, and block-wise descent / hybrid training / gradient sparsity enhancements confirmed.

papers.title: The Lottery Ticket Hypothesis: Finding Sparse, Trainable Neural Networks
papers.claim: Dense randomly initialized networks contain sparse subnetworks ('winning tickets') that, trained in isolation from their original initialization, match the full network's accuracy; iterative magnitude pruning finds them.
papers.relevance: Supplies the train-select-rewind-retrain recipe behind LT-SFT and the general idea that a sparse sub-object of parameter space suffices, i.e. selection as a subobject/mask functor on parameter spaces.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1803.03635 (Frankle, 2018-03; journal-ref ICLR 2019) confirmed; claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Training BatchNorm and Only BatchNorm: On the Expressive Power of Random Features in CNNs
papers.claim: Training only BatchNorm's affine parameters on top of frozen random weights reaches surprisingly high accuracy (e.g. 82% on CIFAR-10 for deep ResNets), far above training an equal number of random other parameters.
papers.relevance: Evidence that per-channel affine (diagonal scale/shift) parameters are disproportionately expressive, the foundation for BitFit, LN Tuning and (IA)^3-style diagonal methods.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2003.00152 (Frankle, 2020-02; comment 'Published in ICLR 2021') confirmed; 82% CIFAR-10 / 32% ImageNet top-5 matches the abstract.

papers.title: On the Effectiveness of Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Shows that random, rule-based and projection-based PEFT methods are all p-sparse fine-tuned models (with respect to an equivalent model for structure-changing methods) and proves that sparsity regularizes by bounding stability, which yields generalization bounds.
papers.relevance: A theorem-level unification of PEFT under the selective view (theta = theta_0 + M Delta theta), directly usable as the 'mask' object in a categorical account; also motivates the SAM selection method.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2211.15583 (Fu, 2022-11) confirmed; AAAI 2023 via Crossref (doi 10.1609/aaai.v37i11.26505); random/rule-based/projection-based categorization and stability-based generalization bound match the abstract.

papers.title: Task-Specific Skill Localization in Fine-tuned Language Models
papers.claim: Grafting the fine-tuned values of a tiny subset (~0.01%) of parameters onto the pretrained model recovers over 95% of the fine-tuned model's performance; such grafted regions localize task skills and help continual learning.
papers.relevance: Empirical evidence that fine-tuning deltas are effectively sparse, supporting selective PEFT and composition of sparse deltas (as in LT-SFT).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2302.06600 (Panigrahi, 2023-02; comment 'ICML 2023') confirmed in PMLR v202 (panigrahi23a); ~0.01% of parameters, >95% performance matches the abstract.

papers.title: What Would Elsa Do? Freezing Layers During Transformer Fine-Tuning
papers.claim: Fine-tuning only the final quarter of BERT/RoBERTa layers (3-5 of 12 in base models) retains about 90% of full fine-tuning quality.
papers.relevance: Early quantification of layer-depth selection, the coarse end of the selective family (top-k layer tuning, surgical fine-tuning, LISA).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1911.03090 (Lee, Jaejun; 2019-11; 5-page arXiv note) confirmed; no venue found, so arXiv. 'Only a fourth of the final layers ... 90% of the original quality' matches the abstract.

papers.title: Beyond Fully-Connected Layers with Quaternions: Parameterization of Hypercomplex Multiplications with 1/n Parameters
papers.claim: A dense layer can be parameterized as a sum of n Kronecker products, W = Σ_i A_i ⊗ B_i, which subsumes the quaternion Hamilton product and learns arbitrary n-D hypercomplex multiplication rules with about 1/n of the parameters.
papers.relevance: The algebraic origin of PHM-Adapter, Compacter and KAdaptation; makes 'Kronecker rank' an explicit design axis, the Kronecker analogue of LoRA's matrix rank.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv metadata and ICLR 2021 (arXiv comment) checked.

papers.title: Approximation with Kronecker Products
papers.venue: Linear Algebra for Large Scale and Real-Time Applications (NATO ASI Series E, vol. 232), Springer, pp. 293-314
papers.claim: The nearest Kronecker product (and sum of Kronecker products) to a matrix is obtained from an SVD of a rearrangement of that matrix, so Kronecker rank equals ordinary rank after rearrangement.
papers.relevance: Shows that Kronecker-sum adapters (PHM, KAdaptation, KronA) are low-rank adapters in a different matricization, a single invariant that organizes the whole 'shape' family.
papers.verification_notes: Crossref: Van Loan & Pitsianis, 1993, pp. 293-314; no arXiv version (pre-arXiv), canonical Springer DOI URL kept.
corrections: venue: added series letter and page range from Crossref (DOI 10.1007/978-94-015-8196-7_17)

papers.title: Tensor-Train Decomposition
papers.claim: Introduces the tensor-train (TT) format with SVD-based TT-SVD and rounding algorithms, storing a d-way tensor with O(d n r^2) parameters.
papers.relevance: Mathematical basis of LoRETTA, TT-LoRA, FacT-TT and MetaTT; TT is the simplest non-trivial tensor network (a linear chain).
papers.verification_notes: Crossref: Oseledets, SISC 33(5):2295-2317, 2011.
corrections: venue: added pages from Crossref

papers.title: Tensor Decompositions and Applications
papers.claim: Standard survey of CP (CANDECOMP/PARAFAC), Tucker and related decompositions, mode-n products and their algorithms.
papers.relevance: Reference notation for the Tucker (LoTR, FLoRA, FacT-TK) and CP (LoRTA) adapters and for VeRA-style shared bases read as CP models.
papers.verification_notes: Crossref: Kolda & Bader, SIAM Review 51(3):455-500, 2009.
corrections: venue: added pages from Crossref

papers.title: Low-Rank Tensor Networks for Dimensionality Reduction and Large-Scale Optimization Problems: Perspectives and Challenges PART 1
papers.venue: Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning 9(4-5):249-429
papers.claim: Monograph on tensor networks (TT, hierarchical Tucker, etc.) with graphical (string-diagram) notation for contractions and their use in large-scale optimization.
papers.relevance: Supplies the diagrammatic calculus in which every 'shape' adapter is a string diagram of trainable and frozen boxes, the natural bridge to a categorical (monoidal) treatment.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv metadata and journal-ref (FnTML 9(4-5):249-429, 2016) checked.
corrections: venue: added pages from the arXiv journal-ref

papers.title: Monarch: Expressive Structured Matrices for Efficient and Accurate Training
papers.claim: Monarch matrices, products of two block-diagonal matrices interleaved with permutations, are hardware-efficient, express many standard transforms, and admit an analytically optimal projection of a dense matrix.
papers.relevance: Structured-matrix foundation of MoRe; also explains MELoRA/GraLoRA/BD-LoRA as block-diagonal (direct-sum) shapes and BOFT's butterflies as the orthogonal counterpart.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv metadata and PMLR v162 (ICML 2022) checked; abstract confirms the analytically optimal projection.

papers.title: Compute Better Spent: Replacing Dense Layers with Structured Matrices
papers.claim: Different structured matrix families need different initialization scales and learning rates (derived via muP); the Block Tensor-Train (BTT) family, which contains Monarch, beats dense layers per unit of compute.
papers.relevance: Explains why shape-based adapters need method-specific scalings (e.g. ABBA's rank-stabilized scale, C3A's large learning rate) and gives a compute-optimal lens for comparing shapes.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv metadata and PMLR v235 (ICML 2024) checked; abstract confirms structure-dependent init/LR via muP and the BTT family containing Monarch.

papers.title: Tensor Networks Meet Neural Networks: A Survey and Future Perspectives
papers.claim: Surveys 'tensorial neural networks' that combine tensor networks with CNNs, RNNs, Transformers, LLMs and quantum neural networks, covering compression, fusion and efficient training.
papers.relevance: Places TT/Tucker/CP adapters within the wider practice of tensor-network parameterization of neural layers.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv metadata checked; no journal/conference version found (Crossref/S2), venue kept as arXiv.

papers.title: PRANC: Pseudo RAndom Networks for Compacting deep models
papers.claim: A deep model can be reparameterised as a linear combination of several frozen, randomly initialised basis networks, so it can be stored as one seed plus mixture coefficients, compressing classifiers about 100x.
papers.relevance: Direct ancestor of NOLA (and of seed-regenerated bases in VeRA/RandLoRA): storage reduces to coefficients plus an RNG seed, a free-module view of the update space.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2206.08464 (Nooralinejad, Jun 2022), ICCV 2023, DOI 10.1109/ICCV51070.2023.01561 (Crossref). Abstract confirms seed + mixture-coefficient storage and ~100x compression of image classifiers.

papers.title: Compressing Neural Networks with the Hashing Trick
papers.claim: Randomly grouping connection weights with a hash function so that each group shares one parameter (HashedNets) gives large compression with little accuracy loss.
papers.relevance: Random weight sharing is the mechanism behind Uni-LoRA's one-hot projection and MoSA's random tessellation; it frames sharing as a quotient of parameter space by a random partition.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1504.04788 (Chen, Apr 2015), ICML 2015 (PMLR v37). Abstract confirms hash-bucket weight sharing; MoSA (ICLR 2026) cites HashedNets as its conceptual ancestor.

papers.title: See Further for Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning by Standing on the Shoulders of Decomposition
papers.claim: Unifies PEFT as 'subspace tuning' relative to the SVD W = U\Sigma V^\top. Reconstruction-based methods transform existing subspaces (e.g. scaling singular vectors, BitFit, soft prompts). Extension-based methods add new subspaces (LoRA and its derivatives, adapters). Combination-based methods do both (e.g. DoRA, Spectral Adapter, SVDiff). The analysis motivates two new methods (SSL, SSB) and a Matrix Pattern Constraints framework.
papers.relevance: A recent explicit unification attempt whose reconstruction/extension split lines up with acting on W_0 by a transformation (multiplicative, group-action-like) versus adding a new low-rank summand (additive). A categorical treatment can make this dichotomy precise.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2407.05417 (Si, Chongjie; 2024-07, v2 2024-12) matches; no venue found on Semantic Scholar or Crossref, so arXiv. The classification was checked in the full text: DoRA is combination-based, and soft prompts and BitFit are reconstruction-based.
corrections: claim: DoRA moved from extension-based to combination-based, as classified in Sec. V of the paper

papers.title: LoRA+: Efficient Low Rank Adaptation of Large Models
papers.claim: In the infinite-width limit with Adam, using the same learning rate for A and B prevents efficient feature learning. Efficiency is achieved with \eta_A = \Theta(n^{-1}) and \eta_B = \Theta(1), so the ratio \lambda = \eta_B/\eta_A must be \Theta(n) (Theorem 1). In practice a fixed ratio is used: about 2^4 for RoBERTa under the paper's Init[2] (A = 0, B random), 2^2-2^3 under the standard Init[1] (B = 0, A random), and 2^1-2^2 for Llama. This gives 1-2% gains and up to about 2x faster fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: This shows that the two factors of the GL(r)-redundant parametrisation are not interchangeable under standard optimizers. The scaling part of the gauge (B -> cB, A -> A/c) interacts with learning rates, which motivates gauge-aware optimizers.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.12354 (Hayou; 2024-02) matches; ICML 2024 confirmed in PMLR v235; Theorem 1 and the ratio recommendations in Sec. 5.3 were read in the full text.
corrections: claim: Theorem 1 is stated for Adam and gives a sufficient scaling; the 2^4 RoBERTa ratio holds under Init[2] (A = 0), while the standard B = 0 init gives 2^2-2^3 (Sec. 5.3)

papers.title: A Rank Stabilization Scaling Factor for Fine-Tuning with LoRA
papers.claim: The conventional \alpha/r scaling slows learning and stunts performance at higher ranks. The paper proves that LoRA adapters should instead be scaled by \alpha/\sqrt{r} for rank-stable learning (rsLoRA), which makes higher ranks a useful compute/performance trade-off at no extra inference cost.
papers.relevance: A scaling-limit result for the factorised parametrisation, available in HF PEFT as LoraConfig(use_rslora=True). It shows that the normalisation constant is part of the reparametrisation and not a cosmetic hyperparameter.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2312.03732 (Kalajdzievski; 2023-11) matches; no venue found, so arXiv. The alpha/sqrt(r) scaling matches the abstract, and LoraConfig(use_rslora=True) with lora_alpha/math.sqrt(r) was confirmed in peft main src/peft/tuners/lora/config.py.

papers.title: When Scaling Meets LLM Finetuning: The Effect of Data, Model and Finetuning Method
papers.claim: On bilingual LLMs from 1B to 16B parameters, fine-tuning follows a power-based multiplicative joint scaling law between fine-tuning data size and each other scaling factor. Fine-tuning benefits more from model scaling than from pretraining-data scaling, scaling PET parameters (prompt length, LoRA rank) is generally ineffective, and the best method depends on task and data.
papers.relevance: Scaling-law evidence that the size of the PEFT parameter object matters much less than the frozen base. This fits the picture of PEFT as a small reparametrisation of a large fixed morphism.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.17193 (Zhang, Biao; 2024-02) matches; ICLR 2024 per the arXiv comment and the ICLR 2024 virtual list (poster 19432); the claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Methods for Pretrained Language Models: A Critical Review and Assessment
papers.claim: Systematic review that sorts PEFT methods for PLMs into additive, partial, reparameterized, hybrid and unified fine-tuning, with experiments on representative methods measuring parameter and memory efficiency.
papers.relevance: A five-class taxonomy whose 'unified' class (AdaMix, SparseAdapter, ProPETL) is kept apart from 'hybrid' combinations (MAM adapter, UniPELT, AutoPEFT, S3Delta-M). Comparing it with the Delta-Tuning and Han et al. taxonomies shows how unstable informal classifications are, which motivates a principled one.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2312.12148 (Xu, Lingling; 2023-12) matches; IEEE TPAMI 48(6):6107-6126 (2026) confirmed by Crossref DOI 10.1109/TPAMI.2026.3657354. The five classes were checked in the full text.
corrections: relevance: UniPELT and MAM are in the paper's hybrid class (Sec. III-D), not the unified class (Sec. III-E: AdaMix, SparseAdapter, ProPETL)

papers.title: A Survey on LoRA of Large Language Models
papers.claim: Reviews LoRA progress along five axes: downstream-adaptation variants, cross-task generalization by mixing LoRA plugins, efficiency improvements, privacy-preserving and federated use, and applications. Maintains an Awesome-LoRAs list.
papers.relevance: The standard map of the LoRA sub-family, including mixture and composition methods that a categorical treatment models as coproducts or monoidal combinations of reparametrisations.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2407.11046 (Mao, Yuren; 2024-07) matches; Frontiers of Computer Science 19(7) (2025; online 2024-12) confirmed by Crossref DOI 10.1007/s11704-024-40663-9; the Awesome-LoRAs repo resolves.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Pre-Trained Vision Models: A Survey and Benchmark
papers.claim: Surveys visual PEFT and sorts it into addition-based, partial-based, unified-based and multi-task tuning. It introduces V-PEFT Bench for standardized evaluation across vision tasks.
papers.relevance: The main vision-side taxonomy. It shows that the same structural classes recur across modalities, which supports a modality-independent categorical classification.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.02242 (Xin, Yi; 2024-02) matches; IJCV 134(6) (2026) confirmed by Crossref DOI 10.1007/s11263-026-02864-6; the four categories and V-PEFT Bench match the abstract.

papers.title: Low-Rank Adaptation Redux for Large Models
papers.claim: A signal-processing overview of LoRA along three axes. Architectural design covers SVD-based factorisation, rank augmentation and cross-layer tensorisation. Efficient optimization covers initialization, alternating solvers, gauge-invariant optimization and parameterization-aware methods. Applications span pre-training, post-training and serving.
papers.relevance: A recent survey that names 'gauge-invariant optimization' as a category of its own. This indicates that the GL(r) symmetry viewpoint has become an organising principle for LoRA research.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2604.21905 (Li, Bingcong; 2026-04) matches; arXiv only; the three axes, including 'gauge-invariant optimization', match the abstract.

papers.title: On the Optimization of Deep Networks: Implicit Acceleration by Overparameterization
papers.claim: For deep linear networks with balanced initialization, W_{j+1}^\top W_{j+1} = W_j W_j^\top, gradient flow preserves balancedness. The end-to-end matrix then follows a preconditioned update whose preconditioner depends on the singular values of the product (powers of W W^\top and W^\top W), so depth acts as an accelerating preconditioner. This effect cannot be obtained from the gradient of any regularizer.
papers.relevance: For depth 2 (\Delta W = BA), balancedness B^\top B = A A^\top is a GL(r)-gauge condition, and the induced end-to-end dynamics explain why the factorised LoRA parametrisation changes optimization geometry relative to training \Delta W directly. This is the root of balanced and Riemannian LoRA variants.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1802.06509 (Arora; 2018-02) matches; ICML 2018 per the arXiv comment and PMLR v80; the balancedness condition maps to B^T B = A A^T for W = BA; the no-regularizer impossibility is in the abstract.

papers.title: Algorithmic Regularization in Learning Deep Homogeneous Models: Layers are Automatically Balanced
papers.claim: For homogeneous networks (linear, ReLU, Leaky ReLU), gradient flow keeps the differences between squared layer norms invariant, and for linear layers the matrix W_{j+1}^\top W_{j+1} - W_j W_j^\top is conserved. Small initialization therefore yields automatically balanced layers. For asymmetric low-rank matrix factorization, gradient descent with decaying step sizes balances the factors and converges to a global optimum.
papers.relevance: Applied to LoRA, gradient flow conserves A A^\top - B^\top B, which is the Noether charge of the GL(r) symmetry. With the default init (B = 0), this charge equals A_0 A_0^\top, so standard LoRA starts and stays off the balanced set.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1806.00900 (Du, Simon S.; 2018-06) matches; NeurIPS 2018 per the arXiv comment and the NeurIPS 2018 list; the invariants and the asymmetric factorization result match the abstract.

papers.title: Implicit Regularization in Deep Matrix Factorization
papers.claim: Gradient descent on deep (multi-factor) matrix factorizations has an implicit bias toward low-rank solutions that grows with depth. The paper argues that this bias is not captured by simple norms such as the nuclear norm.
papers.relevance: Explains why factorised parametrisations of \Delta W (BA, or deeper products and tensorised variants) carry an implicit low-rank bias beyond their explicit rank constraint. A theory of PEFT should treat the parametrisation, and not only its image, as meaningful.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1905.13655 (Arora; 2019-05) matches; NeurIPS 2019 per the arXiv comment and the NeurIPS 2019 list.

papers.title: Neural Mechanics: Symmetry and Broken Conservation Laws in Deep Learning Dynamics
papers.claim: Continuous symmetries of the architecture (translation from softmax, scale from normalization, rescale from homogeneous activations) constrain gradients and Hessians and give Noether-like conservation laws under gradient flow. Finite learning rates break these laws, and modified gradient flow yields exact integral expressions for the dynamics of symmetric parameter combinations, validated on VGG-16.
papers.relevance: Supplies the Noether framework (symmetry -> conserved quantity, broken at finite step size) needed to treat LoRA's GL(r) gauge and the scaling symmetries of DoRA- and (IA)^3-style methods uniformly.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2012.04728 (Kunin; 2020-12) matches; ICLR 2021 per the arXiv comment; the symmetries, broken conservation, modified gradient flow and VGG-16 validation match the abstract.

papers.title: Symmetries, Flat Minima, and the Conserved Quantities of Gradient Flow
papers.claim: A general framework for continuous parameter-space symmetries, including nonlinear data-dependent ones, that carve out flat low-loss valleys. For a two-layer linear network UV the loss is GL_h(R)-invariant and every entry of V V^\top - U^\top U is conserved. Conserved quantities parametrise flat minima and are tied to convergence rate and sharpness, so the initialization fixes which part of the minimum set gradient flow explores.
papers.relevance: The cleanest statement that LoRA's factor pair (U, V) = (B, A) carries a GL(r) symmetry with conserved charge A A^\top - B^\top B, and that this charge (fixed at init) affects convergence and sharpness. The gauge-theoretic layer of a categorical PEFT theory rests on this.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2210.17216 (Zhao, Bo; 2022-10) matches; ICLR 2023 per the arXiv comment and the ICLR 2023 virtual list (poster 11070); Example 5.2 (GL_h symmetry, every entry of VV^T - U^T U conserved) was read in the full text.

papers.title: Abide by the Law and Follow the Flow: Conservation Laws for Gradient Flows
papers.claim: Defines conservation laws as quantities preserved by gradient flow for any data and loss, and shows that the maximal number of independent laws can be computed by finite-dimensional algebra on the Lie algebra generated by the model's Jacobian vector fields. Algorithms recover all known laws for several ReLU architectures and show there are no others.
papers.relevance: A complete, algorithmic answer to 'what is conserved' for a given parametrisation. In principle it lets one compute the full invariant set of any PEFT parametrisation (LoRA, DoRA, Kronecker or tensor factorisations), not only the obvious GL(r) charge.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2307.00144 (Marcotte; 2023-06) matches; NeurIPS 2023 confirmed in the NeurIPS 2023 virtual list (poster 70647); the claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Fixed-rank matrix factorizations and Riemannian low-rank optimization
papers.claim: Optimization over fixed-rank matrices is cast on Riemannian quotient manifolds. The full-rank factorization W = GH^\top has the symmetry (G, H) -> (GM^{-1}, HM^\top), M in GL(r), giving the quotient R_*^{d_1\times r} x R_*^{d_2\times r}/GL(r). Equivalent polar (St x S_{++} x St / O(r)) and subspace-projection quotients are given, and gradient and trust-region algorithms are derived for each geometry.
papers.relevance: Classical geometry behind LoRA's gauge: the space of factor pairs (B, A) is a principal GL(r)-bundle over the manifold of rank-r updates. Riemannian-preconditioned LoRA, LoRA-RITE and BaLoRA all choose a metric or gauge on this bundle.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1209.0430 (Mishra, B.; 2012-09) matches; Computational Statistics 29(3-4):591-621 (2014; online 2013) confirmed by Crossref DOI 10.1007/s00180-013-0464-z; the GL(r) action (G M^{-1}, H M^T) was re-derived.

papers.title: Riemannian Preconditioned LoRA for Fine-Tuning Foundation Models
papers.claim: Adds an r x r preconditioner to each LoRA step (W = W_0 + BA): A \leftarrow A - \eta (B^\top B)^{-1}\nabla_A L and B \leftarrow B - \eta \nabla_B L\,(A A^\top)^{-1}, i.e. left-multiplication for A and right-multiplication for B. It is derived from a Riemannian metric on the quotient manifold of fixed-rank matrices. In the infinite-width limit, with Adam, this gives stable feature learning with a single \Theta(1) learning rate for both factors (Theorem 4.1), and it makes SGD and AdamW more robust on LLMs and diffusion models.
papers.relevance: Shows directly that choosing a GL(r)-compatible (quotient) metric removes the A/B learning-rate asymmetry of LoRA+. Optimization geometry on the gauge bundle is a first-class part of a PEFT method.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.02347 (Zhang, Fangzhao; 2024-02) matches; ICML 2024 confirmed in PMLR v235; Eq. (1), the metric (2) from Mishra et al., and Theorem 4.1 (Adam, eta = Theta(1)) were read in the full text.
corrections: claim: made explicit which side each r x r preconditioner multiplies, matching Eq. (1)
claim: added that the stability theorem is for Adam

papers.title: LoRA Done RITE: Robust Invariant Transformation Equilibration for LoRA Optimization
papers.claim: Standard LoRA optimizers (Adam, Shampoo, LoRA+, ScaledAdam) lack transformation invariance: equivalent factorizations (A R, B R^{-\top}) (paper's notation Z = AB^\top; (BR, R^{-1}A) in this site's notation) receive different weight updates. LoRA-RITE computes 'unmagnified' gradients in polar-decomposition bases of the factors and preconditions only in the r-dimensional space, which makes updates invariant. Replacing Adam with it on Gemma-2B gives a 4.6% accuracy gain on Super-Natural Instructions.
papers.relevance: Turns GL(r) gauge invariance into a design requirement for optimizers and shows that respecting it improves results.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.20625 (Yen, Jui-Nan; 2024-10) matches; ICLR 2025 oral per the arXiv comment and the ICLR 2025 virtual list (poster 29397); polar-decomposition unmagnified gradients and the 4.6% gain were checked.
corrections: claim: flagged that (AR, BR^{-T}) uses the paper's Z = AB^T convention, not the site's W_0 + BA

papers.title: Learning on LoRAs: GL-Equivariant Processing of Low-Rank Weight Spaces for Large Finetuned Models
papers.venue: ICLR 2025 Workshop (Neural Network Weights as a New Data Modality)
papers.claim: LoRA factor pairs (U, V) and (UR, VR^{-\top}) for R in GL(r) give the same update \Delta W = UV^\top (paper's notation), an inner symmetry that differs from the outer permutation symmetries of ordinary networks. The paper builds GL-invariant or equivariant models on LoRA weights (canonicalization via O-Align, singular values as invariant features, multiplied-out dense features, and the equivariant GL-net) that predict CLIP score, data attributes, membership and downstream accuracy over thousands of fine-tuned models.
papers.relevance: Treats the GL(r) symmetry of LoRA as a structural fact about the space of PEFT modules and builds equivariant learners on it. The space of adapters becomes an object with a group action, which is the natural home for a functorial classification.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2410.04207 (Putterman, Theo; 2024-10) matches; iclr.cc/virtual/2025/33086 lists it under the workshop 'Neural Network Weights as a New Data Modality', and it is absent from the ICLR 2025 main-track list. The models (O-Align, SVD, Dense, GL-net) and tasks were checked in the full text.
corrections: claim: flagged the paper's notation Delta W = U V^T
claim: named the paper's featurizations precisely (MLP + SVD, MLP + Dense)

papers.title: Balanced LoRA: Removing Parameter Invariance to Accelerate Convergence
papers.claim: Factor pairs giving the same adapted matrix can have very different condition numbers, so the minimizer LoRA converges to affects its convergence rate. After each optimizer step, BaLoRA applies a product-preserving balancing map onto the 'hyperbalanced' manifold, on which (in this site's notation) B^\top B = A A^\top = S with S diagonal, non-negative and non-increasing; it is computed from the SVD of the product and so leaves the adapted matrix unchanged while improving conditioning. It converges faster and performs better than standard LoRA.
papers.relevance: Turns gauge fixing into an algorithm: it fixes the (hyper)balanced section of the GL(r)-bundle, i.e. the zero level set of the conserved quantity of Du et al. and Arora et al., with only a residual sign symmetry left when the singular values are distinct. It closes the loop between deep-linear-network theory and practical PEFT.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2605.31484 (Castin, Valerie; 2026-05) matches; ICML 2026 per the arXiv comment and the ICML 2026 virtual list (poster 62055). The paper's A^T A = B B^T for adapter AB is B^T B = A A^T in site notation; the hyperbalanced manifold and balancing map are in Sec. 3.1.
corrections: claim: BaLoRA projects onto the hyperbalanced submanifold (balanced with a diagonal Gram matrix, Sec. 3.1), not merely the balanced set
relevance: made the gauge-fixing statement match the hyperbalanced manifold

papers.title: Backprop as Functor: A compositional perspective on supervised learning
papers.claim: Defines a symmetric monoidal category Learn whose morphisms are learners (P, I, U, r): a parameter space, implementation I: P x A -> B, update U: P x A x B -> P and request function r: P x A x B -> A. For a fixed step size \epsilon > 0 and an error function e with \partial e/\partial x(x_0,-) invertible, gradient descent defines a faithful, injective-on-objects, strong symmetric monoidal functor L_{\epsilon,e}: Para -> Learn, so backpropagation is functorial.
papers.relevance: The original categorical semantics of learning. A PEFT method changes the parameter object P of each learner (restricting, extending or reparametrising it) while keeping I's frozen part fixed. Whether and how such changes commute with L_{\epsilon,e} is a natural first theorem for a categorical PEFT theory.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1711.10455 (Fong, Brendan; 2017-11) matches; LICS 2019 per the arXiv journal-ref and DOI 10.1109/LICS.2019.8785665. Theorem III.2 (faithful, injective-on-objects, strong symmetric monoidal L_{eps,e}) was read in the PDF.

papers.title: Lenses and Learners
papers.claim: There is a faithful, identity-on-objects symmetric monoidal functor embedding a category of asymmetric lenses into the category of learners, and another embedding learners into a category of symmetric lenses. The learners of Backprop as Functor are therefore tightly linked to lenses.
papers.relevance: Bridges Learn to the lens/optic formalism, which later work uses as the standard home for gradient-based learning and therefore for PEFT.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1903.03671 (Fong, Brendan; 2019-03) matches; Bx 2019 (CEUR) per the arXiv journal-ref; both embeddings match the abstract.

papers.title: Reverse Derivative Categories
papers.claim: Gives a direct axiomatization of categories with a reverse derivative, analogous to Cartesian differential categories for forward derivatives. A reverse derivative implies a forward derivative but not conversely: it is equivalent to a forward derivative together with a dagger structure on the subcategory of linear maps, which forms an additively enriched category with dagger biproducts.
papers.relevance: The axiomatic basis for backpropagating through any reparametrisation. The chain rule for a PEFT map \alpha: Q -> P (e.g. (A, B) |-> W_0 + BA) is functoriality of the reverse derivative, and the dagger is the transpose that appears in LoRA's gradients.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 1910.07065 (Cockett, Robin; 2019-10) matches; CSL 2020 per the arXiv comment and DOI 10.4230/LIPIcs.CSL.2020.18; the claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Categorical Foundations of Gradient-Based Learning
papers.claim: Gives a categorical semantics of gradient-based learning in which models are morphisms of Para(Lens(C)) for a Cartesian reverse differential category C. Para accounts for parameters, Lens for bidirectional information flow, and the CRDC for differentiation. Optimisers (SGD, Adam, AdaGrad, Nesterov), losses (MSE, softmax cross-entropy) and learning rates are uniformly lenses or reparametrisations, Boolean-circuit learning is covered, and there is a Python implementation.
papers.relevance: The formal home for PEFT. It defines a reparametrisation of (P, f): A -> B by \alpha: Q -> P as (Q, (\alpha \otimes 1_A); f), and every weight-space PEFT method (LoRA's (A, B) |-> W_0 + BA, BitFit's coordinate inclusion, OFT's R \mapsto W_0 R) is exactly such a 2-cell. Optimisers-as-lenses also cover training-procedure methods such as LoRA+ and GaLore.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2103.01931 (Cruttwell; 2021-03) matches; ESOP 2022 (LNCS, Programming Languages and Systems, pp. 1-28) confirmed by Crossref DOI 10.1007/978-3-030-99336-8_1. Definition 2.3 (reparametrisation (Q, (alpha (x) 1_A); f)) was read in the PDF.
corrections: relevance: OFT acts on the input side in this site's notation (W = W_0 R, as in the multiplicative family file)

papers.title: Towards Foundations of Categorical Cybernetics
papers.claim: Combines the Para construction over actegories with optics to obtain parametrised optics, a framework for processes that interact bidirectionally with an environment and a controller. Examples include open learners (controller = optimiser such as gradient descent) and compositional game theory via selection functions.
papers.relevance: Provides the actegory-based Para construction and the 'controller' perspective. A PEFT method restricts which part of a parametrised optic the controller (optimiser) can act on, which echoes the optimal-control reading of delta tuning.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2105.06332 (Capucci; 2021-05) matches; ACT 2021, EPTCS 372 (2022) pp. 235-248 per the arXiv journal-ref and DOI 10.4204/EPTCS.372.17.

papers.title: Category Theory in Machine Learning
papers.claim: Survey of applications of category theory to machine learning, documenting motivations, goals and common themes across gradient-based learning, probability and Bayesian learning, and invariant or equivariant learning.
papers.relevance: The standard entry point to categorical ML. Its three threads (gradient-based learning, probability, equivariance) map onto the optimizer, Bayesian/regularization and symmetry aspects of a categorical PEFT theory.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2106.07032 (Shiebler, Dan; 2021-06) matches; no venue found, so arXiv.

papers.title: Position: Categorical Deep Learning is an Algebraic Theory of All Architectures
papers.claim: Proposes the universal algebra of monads valued in a 2-category of parametric maps as a single theory that subsumes both constraints on models and their implementations. Equivariant layers are monad-algebra homomorphisms for group-action monads, which recovers geometric deep learning, and the theory also yields RNNs, weight tying and constructs from automata theory.
papers.relevance: Gives the 2-categorical (Para-valued) algebraic language in which architectures, and therefore modifications of architectures, can be specified. PEFT structure constraints (weight sharing in VeRA, orthogonality in OFT, block structure in BOFT) can be phrased as algebraic constraints on parametric morphisms.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2402.15332 (Gavranovic, Bruno; 2024-02) matches; ICML 2024 position paper confirmed in PMLR v235 (gavranovic24a, pp. 15209-15241).

papers.title: Fundamental Components of Deep Learning: A category-theoretic approach
papers.claim: Develops an end-to-end, uniform and prescriptive categorical foundation for deep learning. Parametricity is modelled with actegories and Para, and bidirectionality with weighted optics; combining them gives parametric weighted optics as a model of neural networks. The thesis gives a lens-theoretic axiomatisation of differentiation (smooth and Boolean), categorical models of architectures, formalised optimisers and a compositional account of supervised learning.
papers.relevance: The most complete reference for the Para/optics machinery a categorical PEFT theory would build on, including formal optimisers needed to place optimizer-side PEFT methods (LoRA+, GaLore, Riemannian preconditioning).
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2403.13001 (Gavranovic, Bruno; 2024-03) matches; PhD thesis, University of Strathclyde, per the arXiv comment.

papers.title: Geometric Deep Learning: Grids, Groups, Graphs, Geodesics, and Gauges
papers.claim: In the spirit of Klein's Erlangen Programme, derives CNNs, RNNs, GNNs and Transformers from symmetry and scale-separation priors, with group equivariance, gauge structure and geodesics as organising principles. It also gives a constructive recipe for building architectures from prior physical knowledge.
papers.relevance: The Erlangen-style template for organising a zoo of methods by their symmetry groups. Applied to PEFT, it suggests classifying updates by the group acting on W_0 or on the adapter (GL(r) for LoRA, O(d) for OFT/BOFT, diagonal tori for (IA)^3 and scaling methods), with LoRA's GL(r) redundancy acting as a gauge group.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2104.13478 (Bronstein; 2021-04) matches; arXiv proto-book, no formal venue.

adapters.notes: Scope: methods that insert new modules into the computation graph. Organised by insertion morphology: (i) serial bottleneck adapters (residual-adapter, houlsby-adapter, pfeiffer-adapter, mad-x, compacter, hyperformer, adapter-plus, st-adapter, mona, repadapter); (ii) parallel adapters (parallel-adapter, adaptformer, convpass, aim joint adapter, ip-adapter branch); (iii) side / ladder networks (side-tuning, k-adapter, ladder-side-tuning, res-tuning, controlnet, t2i-adapter, shadow-peft); (iv) composition and unified frameworks (adapterfusion, adapterdrop, mam-adapter, unipelt, adamix); (v) output-level adapters for CLIP (clip-adapter, tip-adapter); (vi) gated prompt-adapters (llama-adapter, llama-adapter-v2). HF PEFT (v0.21.1, 2026-09-29) implements only two members of this family: LLaMA-Adapter (AdaptionPromptConfig) and ShadowPEFT (ShadowConfig); bottleneck adapters live in the AdapterHub 'adapters' library instead: DoubleSeqBnConfig = Houlsby, SeqBnConfig = Pfeiffer, ParBnConfig = parallel adapter, AdapterPlusConfig = Adapter+, SeqBnInvConfig/DoubleSeqBnInvConfig = MAD-X invertible adapters, CompacterConfig/CompacterPlusPlusConfig, MAMConfig (prefix bottleneck 800 + ParBn), UniPELTConfig (LoRA r=8, prefix length 10, SeqBn reduction 16, all gated; noted by AdapterHub as slightly different from the paper), and composition blocks Stack/Fuse/Split/BatchSplit/Parallel/Average. Overlaps with other families: llama-adapter also appears in the prompts family (same id, aligned to modification_kind input-or-activation-augmentation); adapterfusion and adamix could also be filed under composition/routing; repadapter is mergeable and, after merging, is a constrained LoRA-type additive update (B tied to W_0, shared across Q/K/V, plus a bias shift). residual-adapter is likewise exactly mergeable at inference. Boundary cases included deliberately: controlnet, t2i-adapter and ip-adapter are conditioning adapters/side networks for diffusion (they add a new input modality rather than re-target a task; ControlNet's trainable copy is not small), and k-adapter fine-tunes the backbone downstream (knowledge infusion). Year field is the first-version year of the listed arXiv record (the published version). Earlier preprints with different titles exist for mona (arXiv:2311.15010, Nov 2023) and tip-adapter (arXiv:2111.03930, Nov 2021). Code-level details verified from official repositories: Convpass, ST-Adapter, RepAdapter zero-init; LLaMA-Adapter V2 code applies the scale to the input (W(s*x)+b) whereas the paper writes s(Wx+b). Compacter does not state an exact identity-at-init guarantee. Mona's official code is not identity at init (default-initialized up-projection). Res-Tuning has no standalone repository; it is implemented in ModelScope SWIFT (ResTuningConfig). Considered but omitted for low uptake or being better placed elsewhere: PALs (Stickland & Murray, ICML 2019), CIAT parallel adapter for MT (Zhu et al. 2021), SparseAdapter (EMNLP Findings 2022), Quantized Side Tuning (ACL 2024), Hyperdecoders, Hyper-X, Polytropon (routing family), AdapterSoup (merging family), SSF and (IA)^3 (scaling family), Rebuffi et al. 2018 parallel residual adapters (folded into residual-adapter), Tiny-Attention adapter, Kronecker adapters (KronA), MoSA, E^3VA, DTL, UniPT, Side4Video, SAM-Adapter (application).

Venues were confirmed via arXiv comments/journal-ref, Crossref DOIs (ECAI, AAAI, CVPR 2025, IJCV, ECCV, ACL Findings, Nature MI) and Semantic Scholar (TMLR, ICLR 2023; arXiv-only for RepAdapter, IP-Adapter, LLaMA-Adapter V2, ShadowPEFT). addendum2026-0.notes: All 6 seed methods and all 8 seed papers exist on arXiv under the given ids; none is a duplicate of a catalogued method and none was skipped. Formulas were taken from each paper's method section (arXiv HTML full text) and rewritten in catalogue notation (\( W_0\in\mathbb R^{d_{out}\times d_{in}} \), \( \Delta W=BA \), \( A \) down, \( B \) up). Several papers use the transposed convention: OrthoMerge writes \( W=RW_0 \) with \( W_0\in\mathbb R^{d_{in}\times d_{out}} \), PRISM writes \( Z=AB^{\top} \), KeepLoRA and StructLoRA write \( y=x(W+AB) \) or \( W_0+AB \) with \( A \) as the up/down factor swapped, and the Muon paper puts the zero-initialised factor on the left. Procrustes, projectors and inits were converted, and the conversions were checked algebraically (for example PRISM's lift satisfies \( \Delta B\,A+B\,\Delta A=\mathcal P_{B,A}(G) \)). Venues were verified on official lists: NeurIPS 2026 orals-posters JSON (PreFT poster; scaling-factor paper poster; Muon paper poster under the title 'Uniform Spectral Growth under Factor-wise Muon Orthogonalization in Matrix Factorization and LoRA'), ICML 2026 JSON (OrthoMerge, muA, steering, recycling, ZO-kernel and LoRA-memory posters; PRISM and Diffract 'Accept (spotlight)' with oral events), ICLR 2026 JSON (KeepLoRA poster, LoRA-Pre Oral) and the ACL Anthology (StructLoRA = 2026.acl-long.97). None of the six methods is in Hugging Face PEFT as of v0.21.2 (2026-10-01): no tuner directory, merge_utils function or release note matches. Corrections to the seed descriptions: (1) muA: the seed says the optimal LR is rank-invariant or scales as \( 1/r \). Corollary 4.4 gives \( \eta=\Theta(n^{-1/2}r^{-(1-\gamma)/2}) \) for Init[A] with \( \alpha=r^{-\gamma} \): \( r^{-1/2} \) at \( \alpha=1 \), \( r^{-1/4} \) for rsLoRA, rank-invariant at \( \alpha=1/r \). Init[B] with \( \alpha=1 \) gives rank-invariant \( \Theta(1/n) \) matching full FT. The abstract's word 'inversely' is loose. (2) Diffract studies full-parameter continual pre-training of OLMo 2, not PEFT. Its central finding (spectra fixed, singular vectors rotate) supports multiplicative orthogonal methods (OFT family) more than SVF, which only rescales singular values; the relevance text says so. (3) PreFT's token-time locus is not entirely new to the atlas: alora (Activated LoRA, in verified/hf-peft.json) gates the same LoRA update by position in the mirror-image way, and PreFT cites it. A dual-to edge preft -> alora was added. PreFT's title differs slightly between the arXiv abstract page ('for efficient inference', used here) and the HTML/NeurIPS listing ('for inference efficiency'). (4) PRISM's paper does not state an init. The official code uses a PiSSA-style spectral residual init because the tangent projectors need full-rank factors; this is recorded in identity_at_init. (5) LoRA-Pre is a full-parameter memory-efficient optimizer, not an adapter: weight updates are full-rank and only the momenta are rank-r. Its GitHub repo contains only a README ('code release coming soon'), so code_url points to a placeholder. Algorithm 1 writes plain inverses, which are singular at step 1 because \( m_{B,0}=0 \); Appendix C.1 states the update with Tikhonov-damped pseudo-inverses (\( \lambda>0 \)), but the experimental \( \lambda \) is not reported. (6) StructLoRA has medium confidence. The paper is internally inconsistent about which update is merged (Sec. 3.3 says the GNN output \( \Delta\tilde W^{final} \), App. E.7 says the gated \( \Delta\tilde W \)). The released repo is a 'scaffold' whose coordinator has a dense encoder of width \( d_{out}d_{in} \), incompatible with the stated <0.05% overhead at LLaMA scale, and adds bias terms that make the coordinated update nonzero at init. The deployed update is therefore not guaranteed to be rank \( \le r \). (7) KeepLoRA does not 'project the gradient during training' in a separate optimizer. It initialises a frozen \( A_t \) from the SVD of the projected first-step gradient and trains only \( B_t \), which by its Prop. 3.1 makes every update a projected gradient step. It cites GPM and InfLoRA but not LoRA-GA, LoRA-FA or MiLoRA; edges to lora-ga and lora-fa are labelled as uncited structural analogues. (8) OrthoMerge's 'Lie algebra' map is the inverse Cayley transform, not the matrix logarithm, so averaging is done in Cayley coordinates. The Cayley chart excludes orthogonal matrices with eigenvalue -1 (for example Procrustes reflections), a case the paper does not discuss. Its arXiv comment still says 'Technical report' although it is an ICML 2026 poster. (9) The recycling paper's arXiv comment says 'Preprint', but it is in the ICML 2026 accepted list. It evaluates LoraHub, \( \pi \)-Tuning, AdaMerging, simple averaging, TIES, TSV and the zero-shot router Arrow, but not PHATGOOSE. (10) LoRA-as-knowledge-memory is empirical and filed as analysis (an update of lora-knowledge-capacity), not as theory. Relations point only to existing method ids (as in the rest of the catalogue, where no relation targets a paper id); uncited structural analogues are marked in the edge notes. Process note: the arXiv export API returned HTTP 429 (shared rate limit), so metadata came from arxiv.org/abs pages and full texts from arxiv.org/html. Semantic Scholar was not queried, and the seed citation counts were not re-verified.
addendum2026-0.verification_summary: Adversarial verification on 2026-10-02 of 6 methods and 8 papers. All 14 verified; none dropped. Existence and metadata: all 14 arXiv ids were confirmed by a batch arXiv API query (after 503/429 retries) and by the abs pages. Titles, first authors and first-version dates (all 2026, from 2601.19659 on 2026-01-27 to 2608.10850 on 2026-08-11) match. Venues confirmed on primary sources: icml-2026-orals-posters.json (OrthoMerge, muA, steering, recycling, ZO-kernel and LoRA-memory are 'Accept (regular)' posters; PRISM and Diffract are 'Accept (spotlight)' with oral events), iclr-2026-orals-posters.json (KeepLoRA poster, LoRA-Pre oral), neurips-2026-orals-posters.json (PreFT, the scaling-factor paper and the Muon paper, the last under its NeurIPS title) and the ACL Anthology (StructLoRA = 2026.acl-long.97). Formulas were re-derived from each paper's method section (arXiv HTML), with the transposed conventions of OrthoMerge, PRISM, KeepLoRA, StructLoRA and the Muon paper converted symbol by symbol. Released code was read for PreFT, PRISM, KeepLoRA and StructLoRA. HF PEFT: none of the six methods is in huggingface/peft main (v0.21.2, 2026-10-01). There is no tuner directory, merge_utils function, optimizers/ entry or release-note mention. Every relation target is an existing method id, every prose-named id exists, and none of the 14 ids or arXiv numbers collides with existing_index.json or the sibling addendum2026 batches. 22 corrections were recorded. Substantive: (1) LoRA-Pre: Appendix C.1 does regularise the inverse (Tikhonov-damped pseudo-inverses), contrary to the seed note, and the factor updates are simultaneous, not alternating. (2) PRISM: the official code saves the adapter re-based to the original W_0 as a rank-2r pair. (3) PreFT: the S-LoRA edge changed from competes-with to combines; App. A.2 vs C.1 disagree on which DiReFT factor is zero at init. (4) StructLoRA: the gate relaxation and prior now separate paper from code. (5) OrthoMerge: the TSV-M+OrthoMerge-C result was attributed to the -G variant. (6) Scaling-factor paper: the 16x-256x ratio depends on rank, not a constant. (7) Steering paper: 40-70% is an MLP-to-block norm ratio, and 'steering' was not an id. (8) Diffract: the truncation tolerance is 50% for 7B and 70% for 13B, and the vector agreement covers left singular vectors only. (9) Recycling: Arrow is a zero-shot router, not an adaptive merge. (10) LoRA memory: the synthetic-format and concatenation claims were rephrased to match the paper. (11) Muon paper: removed an unsupported PiSSA-motivation claim. The remaining fixes wrap math fragments in \( \). Semantic Scholar was not queried; citation counts are not part of this file.

addendum2026-1.notes: Scope: one entry per requested method; all six exist, are distinct from catalogued ids, and are PEFT or memory-efficient-fine-tuning methods. None was skipped. VENUES checked against https://icml.cc/static/virtual/data/icml-2026-orals-posters.json on 2026-10-02: FedRot-LoRA (poster 66566), Geometry-Preserving Orthonormal Init / RLPO-RLMO (poster 63355), NaRA (poster 61250) and AGZO (poster 60499) are 'Accept (regular)'; LiME (poster 64728) is 'Accept (spotlight)'. ZO-Muon is not in the ICLR 2026, ICML 2026 or NeurIPS 2026 accepted lists (checked 2026-10-02 by title and first author) and its arXiv comment field is empty, so its venue is arXiv. Semantic Scholar citations (2026-10-02): ZO-Muon 11 (3 influential), FedRot-LoRA 9 (1), AGZO 3 (1), RLPO-RLMO 1, NaRA 1, LiME 0. Suggested site families: fedrot-lora -> lora-core (federated aggregation; also gap-3 next to ffa-lora and flora-federated); rlpo-rlmo -> init-rank; nara -> frontier; lime -> composition; agzo and zo-muon -> quant-memory. HF PEFT v0.21.2 (2026-10-01) has no tuner or init option for any of the six. Its LoraConfig(init_lora_weights='orthogonal') is a different, data-free scheme: both factors are nonzero, with BA=0 via orthogonal row splitting, so it is NOT RLPO. DISCREPANCIES AND CAVEATS: (1) ZO-Muon: the abstract says '+25.1% on ViT-B CIFAR-100', but Table 1 and Section 5.2 give 72.4 vs 47.3 for ViT-L (ViT-B is 72.6 vs 64.5). The results_note follows the table. (2) FedRot-LoRA: the paper's soft-rotation projection formula writes V diag(.) U^T for R' = U Sigma V^T, the transpose of the nearest rotation. The released code (rotation_alignment_tools.py) uses U' V'^T and builds M = A A_ref^T, consistent with R = U V^T. The formula entry therefore writes a generic projection onto SO(r). Uniform 1/N averaging as in Algorithm 1. (3) NaRA: the 'first noise-conditioned LoRA' claim holds only for diffusion LLMs. Timestep-conditioned LoRAs already exist for image diffusion: TC-LoRA (2510.09561, hypernetwork-generated per-step LoRA, earlier excluded from the catalogue) and TimeStep Master (timestep-interval LoRA experts). NaRA's architecture is credited to Terra (Time-Varying LoRA, NeurIPS 2024, same group), whose variable is a domain-flow time rather than the noise level. NaRA's hypernetwork size (about 0.67M) is computed from Table 12 (64->256->512->1024, biases assumed), not stated in the paper. (4) LiME: arXiv id 2604.02338 although the v1 timestamp is 2026-02-01. The repo README badge text shows a different id (2510.08513 = SliceFine), but its link points to 2604.02338. Initial values of B, p_s and gamma are from the paper's hyperparameter table and the released LiMELoRA.py; the paper (Appendix J) adds multiplicative routing jitter (sigma=0.1) during training; in the released code it is off by default (jitter_noise=0.0) and enabled via set_jitter. LiME's 'MoELoRA' baseline is Luo et al. 2024 (2402.12851), not the catalogue's MOELoRA (2310.18339). (5) AGZO renames the activation basis A_l to U_l here to avoid a clash with the LoRA factor A. The power iteration Y=H Omega; repeat qr then Y=H(H^T Q) spans (HH^T)^K H Omega. The official repo is LouisLINWEI/AGZO (code described as a rough draft) plus an NPU fork. (6) RLPO/RLMO: experiments use alpha=32, r=16 (alpha/r=2), but the theorem is stated for unscaled BA. Its minimum ||I - A_0^T A_0||_2 = 1 is reached by any A_0 with singular values at most sqrt(2), not only by orthonormal A_0. The paper's 'OLoRA' control (B_0=U_r, A_0=V_r^T) is not published OLoRA, which uses QR factors. The ablation shows orthonormality alone (DCT-LoRA, Wavelet-LoRA) beats LoRA, while principal-subspace geometry adds a further gain only for RLPO. TENSION WORTH TAGGING: AGZO finds that a data-informed (activation) subspace improves ZO gradient alignment, while ZO-Muon reports that informed sketches (Gaussian sketching or past-gradient bases) give no gain over random P. They project on different sides (input vs output) and ZO-Muon adds orthogonalization, so the results are not directly contradictory. CATEGORY-THEORY NOTE: FedRot-LoRA is an explicit gauge fixing (choosing a representative in the SO(r) orbit of the GL(r) inner symmetry of (B, A)) applied before a non-equivariant operation (factor averaging). It belongs with learning-on-loras-gl-equivariance, balanced-lora and lora-rite as methods that treat the factorization's symmetry explicitly, but FedRot does not cite them.

addendum2026-2.notes: Batch 2 of the 2026 sweep: six methods, all kept after adversarial verification. FlexLoRA and FLoRG are ICLR 2026 posters, Bayesian-LoRA and LoDA are ICML 2026 posters (Accept, regular), and FourierMoE and SMoA are NeurIPS 2026 posters. None is in HF PEFT (tuners on main at commit 9146289, 2026-10-01; latest release v0.21.2). ID CHOICES: 'flexlora-entropy' avoids a clash with the 2024 federated FlexLoRA (arXiv 2402.11505). 'bayesian-lora-sgp' avoids a clash with the 2024 Bayesian-LoRA, which uses differentiable Bayesian gates for quantization levels and ranks. 'loda-cl' avoids a clash with earlier, unrelated methods also called LoDA. NAME CLASH: the catalogued 'mosa' is MoSA: Mosaic Shared Adaptation, not a Hadamard method, so SMoA is linked to hira and melora instead. Catalogue-derived structural observations, labeled as such in the entries: (1) SMoA's update is \((P_{out}^{\top}\tilde B\tilde AP_{in})\odot W_0\), which is HiRA with block-sparse factors in an SVD-derived permutation. \(K=1\) is exactly HiRA, and at fixed \(r\) SMoA's update set lies inside rank-\(r\) HiRA's. (2) For FourierMoE, \(\mathrm{Re}\,\mathcal{F}^{-1}(F)\) is the IDFT of the Hermitian part of \(F\), so the conjugate-symmetry constraint reaches no more updates than Re-truncation does. The real change from FourierFT is complex coefficients, i.e. learned phase. (3) FLoRG's update set is the PSD cone \(\{LQR:\ Q\succeq0,\ \mathrm{rank}\,Q\le r\}\), which cannot represent \(-\Delta W\). \(A=0\) is a stationary point, so FLoRG cannot start at the identity, and when \(\mathrm{rank}\,Q>r\) the Procrustes map truncates the aggregate. (4) LoDA's isolated subspace is the top-\(r\) generalized eigenspace of \((S^{t},S^{1:t-1})\). The fedrot-lora relation in the raw batch was dropped because no catalogue entry has that id. UNCERTAINTIES: FourierMoE has no public code, does not say how its coefficients are initialized, and reports parameter percentages that cannot be reproduced from its stated hyperparameters. SMoA describes its permutation rule only qualitatively and inherits its initialization from HiRA without stating it. Bayesian-LoRA's paper and code disagree on the LoRA rank (9 vs 8).
addendum2026-2.verification_summary: Adversarial verification on 2026-10-02 of 6 methods (0 papers): all 6 confirmed and kept, none dropped. Existence, titles, full author lists and first-version dates (all 2026) were read from the arXiv abstract pages. The arXiv export API and Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429 or 503 for the whole session, so neither was used. Venues were confirmed in the official accepted-paper JSON: iclr.cc for FlexLoRA (10006948) and FLoRG (10007750); icml.cc for Bayesian-LoRA (60552) and LoDA (63718), both 'Accept (regular)'; neurips.cc for FourierMoE (151989) and SMoA (153896), both 'Accept (poster)'. Every OpenReview forum id matches the JSON. Formulas, parameter counts and results were re-read in the arXiv HTML full text. Released code was inspected for FlexLoRA, Bayesian-LoRA and LoDA (the LoDA repository exists); none was found for FourierMoE, SMoA or FLoRG. HF PEFT: none of the six is under src/peft/tuners on main (9146289) or among the LoRA variants. Substantive fixes: (1) Bayesian-LoRA identity_at_init was wrong. The zero-scale wrapper it cited is unused, and the training path starts with random factors, so \(\Delta W\neq0\). Its paper-versus-code LoRA-rank inconsistency is also recorded. addendum2026b-1.notes: All six requested methods exist, all are PEFT or PEFT-composition methods, and none duplicates a catalogued id. I checked existing_index.json and every JSON file under research/. PrefixMemory-Tuning (called Prefix-Tuning+ in arXiv v1 and v2) had earlier been listed as EXCLUDED in frontier.json for low uptake. It is added now as an ICLR 2026 paper with 5 Semantic Scholar citations. Venues come from the official virtual-site JSON downloaded on 2026-10-02: AR1-ZO is a NeurIPS 2026 poster (OpenReview 7eOsaBX3qO). Pico is a NeurIPS 2026 poster (PtEkosDXWk). FrameFT is an ICML 2026 poster (KCfbSVIheg). FourTune is an ICML 2026 poster (RpwnrBkht2). PrefixMemory-Tuning is an ICLR 2026 poster (LvUMpZE44r). GradFix is an ICLR 2026 poster (CQnpxZNMvT). Year follows the first public version: PrefixMemory-Tuning is 2025 (arXiv v1 on 2025-06-16), GradFix is 2025 (v1 on 2025-10-07), and the other four are 2026. Semantic Scholar citation counts on 2026-10-02: AR1-ZO 0, Pico 0, FrameFT 0, PrefixMemory-Tuning 5, FourTune 1, GradFix 3. None of the six is in HF PEFT v0.21.2 (2026-10-01). FrameFT ships its own patched peft with a 'frame' tuner. Formulas were read from the arXiv HTML method sections, and for FrameFT also from the released tuner code. Corrections to the sweep reasons. (1) AR1-ZO: 'directional collapse' is the Theta(r^-2) decay of the finite-difference SNR caused by inheriting the alpha/r coefficient under single-atom queries. It is a measurement-scale effect, not a statement about the cone geometry of BA. (2) Pico: the claim that it is the 'first merging rule built on the A/B asymmetry' is not supported. LoRI (catalogued) already exploits A/B roles to limit merge interference, and KnOTS and Core Space already work with the factor spaces separately. What is new in Pico is calibrating only B by spectral energy share before merging. For Task Arithmetic, Pico reduces exactly to a post-merge left multiplication by S. (3) FrameFT: every reported experiment uses rho=2 and k*rho=d with Parseval frames. That frame is a non-redundant orthogonal basis, not a redundant non-orthogonal dictionary. I checked numerically that the released construct_real_tff at rho=2 returns a dense matrix, orthogonal to about 1e-5, which is the realified (d/2)-point DFT basis. So in practice FrameFT is close to FourierFT with block-diagonal support. Redundancy appears only in the general definition (k*rho>d). (4) PrefixMemory-Tuning: the prompts-family axis change can be stated concretely. PMT has an identity point (M=0) that prefix-tuning lacks. Structurally it is a parallel adapter whose down-projection is the frozen W_Q (my derivation). LLaMA-Adapter's separately normalised, gated prompt softmax already anticipated PMT's step (i), and the paper does not cite it. The code link printed in the paper (github.com/haonan3/PrefixMemory-Tuning) is an empty repository, created 2026-04-18. Initialisation, pre- or post-RoPE queries, and the extra L*d parameters implied by Table 8 therefore cannot be checked. That is why code_url is empty and confidence is medium. (5) FourTune: the abstract's 2.25x memory figure comes from Fig. 1. The body reports 2.02x end-to-end (14.51 vs 29.35 GB) and 2.93x for DiT weights alone. The 2.27x figure is the step-time speedup on an RTX 5090. The paper does not state the stabilizer rank or the LoRA initialisation. (6) GradFix: its task vectors are full fine-tuning deltas (Ilharco et al. protocol), not LoRA. It is included as a training-free base-change (transport) composition method. No theory-only papers were in this batch, so papers is empty. Semantic Scholar first returned HTTP 429; the batch endpoint worked on retry. Metadata comes from arxiv.org/abs pages, so the arXiv export API was not needed. VERIFICATION UPDATE (2026-10-02, adversarial pass): all six methods confirmed and kept. The claims above that need correcting are these. (3) FrameFT: not every experiment uses \(\rho=2\). Appendix D varies \(\rho\) from 2 to 256 and four of the twelve released GLUE scripts use \(\rho=4\). Every reported run does use \(k\rho=d\), so the frame is non-redundant everywhere. The released coefficient block size is set separately from \(\rho\) (\(4\times4\) only for Llama-2-7B). init_std 0 holds only for the instruction-tuning scripts; the GLUE scripts keep the default 1.0. (4) PMT: the empty repository was re-confirmed, but its creation date could not be re-checked (GitHub API rate limit). Metadata has now also been checked through the arXiv export API.

Theorem 1 bounds the drift of \(A\) by \(O(\eta^2L^2)\), not \(O(\eta)\). The SOTA claim is now framed as the paper's, with MagMax comparable on standard CL. (3) Ternary adaptation. \(2d\) parameters holds only for perfect-square \(d\); Llama-3.2-1B's square layers use \(2.5d\), about 737k in total (0.06%). The Kronecker-rank claim is qualified. (4) CoA-LoRA. Exact mapper counts and the \(r=64\) size were added; LayerNorm is a trained component; the asymmetry note now records that the paper's 'signal in \(L_2\)' (input side) runs opposite to the cited finding. The paper-versus-code question of whether the LoRA pair is trained was confirmed in code, so confidence stays medium. (5) SmartFed. The official code link announced on OpenReview and ICML (github.com/benmagnifico/SmartFed) returns 404, so code_url stays empty. (6) AdaRank. Iso-CTS was added as a base merger. addendum2026b-3.notes: All six requested methods exist, all six are PEFT methods, and none duplicates a catalogued id; ids and arXiv numbers were checked against existing_index.json, which has no entry for any of them. Methods were read from their arXiv HTML method sections, except LoRA-S. Venues were verified as follows. RotMoLE is a NeurIPS 2026 poster in the official neurips.cc orals-posters JSON (OpenReview uGtHLqoW8K). ScaLoRA is in the ICML 2026 JSON ('Accept (regular)', OpenReview Skxb4UgTWU) and its arXiv comment says 'Accepted to ICML 2026'. LoRA-S (Guo2XGgxZA), DiaBlo (cZaI6GmjBm), PERK (qxDTe8fIyA) and QZO (mGeeRFToaW) are all 'Accept (Poster)' in the ICLR 2026 JSON. LoRA-S has no arXiv version, and OpenReview (forum, PDF and API) answered every request with a bot-verification challenge, which was not bypassed. Its formula was therefore transcribed from the official ICLR poster image (iclr.cc/media/PosterPDFs/ICLR 2026/10010449.png), which shows the Sylvester equation, the lift and the AdamS/LRACS updates, together with the ICLR abstract. Confidence for LoRA-S is medium. From those poster formulas I derived three things: the lift's first-order W update is the tangent-space projection of the matrix-space direction; K = eps*I reproduces decoupled weight decay; and the update is equivariant with K -> R^T K R^{-T}. These are marked 'derived here'. LoRA-S's year is 2025 because the ICLR 2026 submission was public on OpenReview in autumn 2025; the exact open date could not be read through the challenge. An empty GitHub repository, CleverWing/lora_s, describes itself as the official implementation and calls the paper an ICLR 2026 Spotlight, but the ICLR data says Poster. code_url is left empty. Year follows the first public version: ScaLoRA arXiv v1 2025-10-27, DiaBlo 2025-06-03, QZO 2025-05-19, PERK 2025-07-08, RotMoLE 2026-05-25. The PERK paper_title is the ICLR title; the arXiv title is 'PERK: Long-Context Reasoning as Test-Time Learning' [corrected in verification: arXiv v1 and v2 carry the ICLR title; only v3 of 2026-08-31 was renamed]. Corrections and caveats recorded in the entries: (i) ScaLoRA's 'fixed subspace' claim is the telescoping identity sum_t dW_t = B_T A_T, i.e. a rank-r bound. The printed Theorem 3.7 has a block-order/transpose typo in its second matrix; the pairing given in formula_latex was re-derived from the stated objective and lambda. (ii) QZO's Theorem 1 claims the clipped SPSA estimate is unbiased, but the proof ignores the dependence of the clipping event on z; only the variance bound holds in general [corrected in verification: only the second-moment bound holds unconditionally]. (iii) RotMoLE's printed R_i is a rank-2 planar block that acts as a full SO(r) rotation on A_i x. My gauge analysis found that the rotation gate reduces each expert's residual gauge group from GL(r) to O(r), with q_i -> O^T q_i [corrected in verification: the residual group is R_{>0} x O(r), since positive rescalings of (B_i, A_i) are also symmetries]. None of the six is in Hugging Face PEFT (tuners directory and releases up to v0.21.2, 2026-10-01). Semantic Scholar was not queried. Not-yet-catalogued neighbours seen in these papers: AdaMoLE, MoLA, MoCLE and CoMoL (RotMoLE baselines and related work); QuZO (cited by QZO); RACS (the base optimizer lifted by LRACS); RECKONING and CaMeLS (PERK's predecessors for meta-learned knowledge encoding and token weighting). No standalone theory papers were added. The theorems of ScaLoRA (optimal low-rank step and scaling), DiaBlo (expressivity and stationarity) and LoRA-S (invariance) are recorded inside the method entries.

addendum2026b-4.notes: All six requested methods exist and are PEFT or memory-efficient fine-tuning methods. None duplicates a catalogued id: checked against existing_index.json, raw/, verified/ and the sibling batches addendum2026b-2 and addendum2026b-5. LoRA-DA appeared earlier only as a skipped name in the init-rank notes. Every formula was written from the arXiv HTML method sections and, where code exists, cross-checked against the official repository. Venue checks: VAPT is an ICLR 2026 poster and WASI an ICLR 2026 oral (iclr-2026-orals-posters.json and the OpenReview search API). LoRA-DA is ICML 2026 'Accept (regular)' (icml-2026-orals-posters.json; OpenReview LvKSVUbXc9) after an ICLR 2026 rejection. TeRA is in the ACL Anthology as 2026.acl-long.106 (pp. 2314-2329); its oral status claimed by the sweep could not be confirmed from the Anthology. DISCREPANCY: the brief described AdaPaD (2605.10741) and Hybrid-LoRA (2605.18822) as 'NeurIPS 2026 (verified)', but neither could be verified. Neither title nor any of their authors (Barbara Su; Chengqian Zhang, Kyumin Lee) appears in the 9,236-entry neurips-2026-orals-posters.json, which does list another Liao-Kyrillidis paper. Neither arXiv page has a venue comment, Semantic Scholar lists AdaPaD as arXiv only, and the sweep pool lists both only as Apr-Jun 2026 overflow with no venue. Both are therefore recorded as 'arXiv preprint'; re-check if camera-ready information appears. Year follows the first public version: VAPT 2025 (arXiv v1 2025-01-31), LoRA-DA 2025 (ICLR 2026 submission public 2025-10-08, arXiv 2025-10-28), WASI 2025 (arXiv 2025-10-10), TeRA 2025 (arXiv 2025-09-03). Code-versus-paper details recorded in the structure fields: (i) VAPT's released code keeps static VPT prompts in the first block, zero-initialises the token-wise projector (with bias) and makes the shared projector residual. (ii) LoRA-DA's code (like LoRA-One) does not subtract \(B_0A_0\) from \(W_0\), normalises the Fisher-gradient estimate by its top singular value, down-weights the variance term (\(\beta=0.03\)), and scales both factors by \(1/\sqrt{1024}\). The paper's K-FAC algorithm keeps only the diagonal of \(Y_F^{-1}\), so its displacement estimate is a block-diagonal natural-gradient step. (iii) WASI's code keeps the dense weight as the optimised parameter and recomputes the rank-K factors from it at each forward pass, whereas the paper describes updating LR directly. WASI is included as a memory-efficient transfer-learning method in the quant-memory sense. It adds no adapter, updates whole weights of selected layers inside low-rank weight and activation subspaces, and is not identity at init because the forward uses the truncated \(W_0\). Hybrid-LoRA: the brief's 'fully fine-tunes the top ~10%' is inverted. The paper fully fine-tunes the LOWEST-scoring modules, those where LoRA appears insufficient. Its Eq. (4) budget is a parameter fraction while the experiments call \(R_{fft}=10\%\) a module ratio. No code is released. AdaPaD: no code found. Its theory covers a single bilinear layer, and the deep-network procedure (snapshot prefix plus current component) is described only in Algorithm 2, hence medium confidence. Structural observation added by us (not in the paper): LoRA-DA's two limits interpolate between an EVA-like activation-variance init (variance term only) and LoRA-One's gradient-SVD init (bias term with raw gradient). None of the six is in Hugging Face PEFT (tuners directory, LoRA init options and release notes through v0.21.2 checked). No standalone theory papers were added. The VAPT sample-efficiency theorem and the AdaPaD self-correction theorems are recorded inside their method entries. Semantic Scholar mostly returned HTTP 429, and OpenReview's notes endpoint required a browser challenge, which was not attempted; venue facts rely on the search endpoint and the conference JSON files.

addendum2026b-5.notes: Batch 5 of the 2026 sweep, pass 2. Of the three requested methods, two are kept (DC-Merge and MaLoRA/MaRA) and one is skipped (CoRA). None duplicates a catalogued id; checked against existing_index.json and every methods list in raw/ and verified/. SKIPPED, not a PEFT method: CoRA (Correlation-aware Adapter, arXiv 2603.21828; ICLR 2026 poster, verified via the OpenReview search API, forum JRlNrcTllN, public since 2025-10-08). (a) The TSFM backbone is not frozen. Section 3 defines the adapter as fine-tuning the base model F into F*, and every result compares 'fine-tuning with CoRA' against 'fine-tuning without CoRA' under the same backbone recipe. In the released code (github.com/decisionintelligence/CoRA), freeze_backbone() is commented out, and the plugin-stage optimizer is built over the backbone's parameters (optim.Adam(self.model.fm.parameters())). For Timer and similar backbones nothing is frozen. Section 6.5 counts CoRA's parameters only as an addition on top of the backbone. Its 'lightweight' claim concerns O(N) inference complexity, not trainable-parameter savings. (b) The low-rank time-varying/time-invariant correlation estimate R+Q_tVQ_t^T (polynomial Q_t) is used only during training, to set the positive/negative pairs of the contrastive loss. At inference CoRA is an output-side residual head: per-channel MLP blocks with an SE-style softmax channel weight, a linear forecasting head, and a per-channel convex gate beta with the backbone's own forecast. So CoRA is an auxiliary head plus contrastive regulariser for ordinary TSFM fine-tuning, not a parameter-efficient method. If the catalogue wants it anyway, it belongs as a fine-tuning add-on with year 2025 (OpenReview first public). VENUES: DC-Merge is in CVF open access for CVPR 2026 (and OpenReview LZacqcAohT). It is unrelated to the rejected ICLR 2026 submission 'From Coefficients to Directions' (MDA, different authors). MaLoRA/MaRA is EMNLP 2026 main per its arXiv comment and repo README; the EMNLP 2026 accepted list was not checked. Years follow first public versions: DC-Merge arXiv v1 2026-03-06; MaLoRA arXiv v1 2026-07-21. IDS: 'malora-mamba' avoids a clash with MALoRA (Mixture of Asymmetric LoRA, arXiv 2410.22782, 2024). The entry covers MaLoRA as the PEFT update and describes MaRA, a retrieval adapter, inside it. NEW RELATION TARGETS not in the catalogue: iso-cts (arXiv 2502.04959, ICML 2025), toplora (arXiv 2510.23123, NeurIPS 2025), ssmlora (arXiv 2502.04958, NAACL 2025) and read-recurrent-adapter (arXiv 2305.15348). DERIVED, NOT STATED: (1) MaLoRA's per-matrix parameter formula comes from the released code: a mambapy MambaBlock with d_model=r, expand 2, d_conv 4, d_state 16, dt_rank=ceil(r/16), plus an r->1 readout and an r-vector gate bias. Summed over Qwen-2.5-7B's q,k,v,up,down it gives +56.8% over LoRA, matching the paper's ~56%. (2) DC-Merge's polar-factor cover basis spans exactly the concatenated task subspaces, so with TA and no mask the cover-space round trip is the identity and reduces to summing the smoothed task vectors. The gains in the paper's Tables 5-6 therefore come from the block-diagonal mask and from TIES applied in cover coordinates. The paper writes Eq. (5) of CoRA's correlation as R+Q_tVQ_t^T with V=sigmoid(ReLU(E_1E_2^T)). The code instead uses (R+sigmoid(Q_tV_1V_2^TQ_t^T))/2; this matters only for the skipped entry. Semantic Scholar returned HTTP 429, so citation counts were not re-checked. The OpenReview forum API raised a challenge page, which was not bypassed, so reviews were read through the OpenReview search endpoint.
