composition.notes: Scope: 42 methods across five sub-families: (i) training-free / post-hoc merging of deltas or adapters (model-soups, fisher-merging, regmean, task-arithmetic, ties-merging, dare, adamerging, tsv-merge, knots, pem-arithmetic, adaptersoup, lorahub, lora-soups, lora-lego, ziplora, mix-of-show, orthogonal-adaptation, multi-lora-composition); (ii) learned composition and mixtures (adapterfusion, adamix, polytropon, mhr, smear, mov, loramoe, moelora, mole, mixlora, x-lora, hydralora, lily); (iii) post-hoc routing and retrieval over adapter libraries (phatgoose, arrow, loraretriever, lora-flow); (iv) multi-adapter serving (s-lora, punica); (v) adapter generation by hypernetworks (hyperformer, hyperdreambooth, text-to-lora, drag-and-drop-llms, doc-to-lora). Seed checks: all 21 seeds exist and belong. 'MoELoRA' is ambiguous: we used Liu et al. (SIGIR 2024, arXiv 2310.18339, spelled MOELoRA); Luo et al. 2024 ('MoELoRA: Contrastive Learning Guided Mixture of Experts...', arXiv 2402.12851) is a different, less-cited method that we did not verify. Polytropon's arXiv title ('Combining Modular Skills in Multitask Learning') differs from the EACL 2023 title used here. LoRAMoE's published title says 'Alleviating' (arXiv: 'Alleviate'). Key algebraic distinction for the theory: 'product of sums' factor mixing (LoraHub, Polytropon/MHR, Arrow-paper, PEM addition, HF PEFT combination_type='linear') creates cross terms B_iA_j, whereas 'sum of products' / rank-concatenation (LoRA Soups CAT, HF 'cat', LoRA-LEGO with k=sum r_i, Doc-to-LoRA chunking, X-LoRA, LoRA-Flow, PHATGOOSE, HF Arrow implementation) is the direct sum along the rank axis. HF PEFT's Arrow mixes expert outputs while the Arrow paper mixes factors. HF PEFT: add_weighted_adapter supports svd, linear, cat, ties, ties_svd, dare_linear, dare_ties, dare_*_svd, magnitude_prune(_svd); negative weights are applied to one factor only (PEM-style negation). PEFT also implements XLoraConfig, PolyConfig (Poly and MHR), ArrowConfig (+GenKnowSub) inside LoraConfig, and LilyConfig. Not in PEFT: MoLE, LoRAMoE, MixLoRA, HydraLoRA, MOELoRA, LoraHub (separate library), CAT with learned weights, serving systems. Uncertainties: MoLE gate parameter shapes are as written in the paper (Eq. 9-10: e in R^{(N L d) x N} over flattened block outputs), now checked; identity-at-init for LoRAMoE, MOELoRA, MixLoRA and HydraLoRA is confirmed from the official code (zero-initialized B), not the papers; Orthogonal Adaptation's trainable-factor init remains unstated; MixLoRA has no formal venue found (arXiv); 'What Matters for Model Merging at Scale?' is TMLR 2025 (verified); Doc-to-LoRA hypernetwork size (309M) is stated in the paper (Sec. 5) and on the Sakana project page. Skipped as lower-uptake or out of PEFT focus: Model Breadcrumbs, EMR-Merging, Twin-Merging, WEMoE, Consensus/TALL masks, Iso-C/Iso-CTS, K-LoRA, further LoRA-MoE variants (AdaMoLE, MoLA, SiRA, MoSLoRA), dLoRA and CaraServe serving systems, HINT and HyperTuning hypernetworks, ATTEMPT (covered in the prompts family).

frontier.notes: Scope: 2025-2026 PEFT methods with clear uptake, verified via arXiv / OpenReview / proceedings pages and Semantic Scholar metadata (checked 2026-10-01). SEED TRIAGE: Most seeds exist and are already fully catalogued in sibling families, so to avoid duplicate records they are NOT repeated here; the site should tag them as 'frontier': lora-one, gora, lora-sb, kasa (init-rank); hira, randlora, c3a, miss, gralora, abba, shira (shape/hf-peft); delora, oftv2, polar, road, osf, svf=Transformer-Squared (multiplicative); loft, lora-without-regret (lora-core; also a paper in hf-peft); tinylora (TinyLoRA, 'Learning to Reason in 13 Parameters', 2602.04118, in hf-peft as TinyLoraConfig); alora, waveft, cartridges (hf-peft/prompts); lift (selective). Seeds added here: Tina, LoRI, SingLoRA, Text-to-LoRA, Drag-and-Drop LLMs. TAXONOMY SUGGESTIONS: (1) The hypernetwork cluster (text-to-lora, drag-and-drop-llms, doc-to-lora, shine, generative-adapter) is labeled 'hybrid' but deserves its own class, 'amortized adapter generation'. Each is a learned map from a task/context space into LoRA space, i.e. a functor from contexts to adapters, with the deployed edit always additive low-rank. (2) Token-restricted adapters (OminiControl sets the LoRA scale to 0 on non-condition tokens and EasyControl applies LoRA only to the condition branch; aLoRA in hf-peft only after invocation tokens) form a structural pattern that the modification_kind enum cannot express. (3) Merging operators (knots, core-space-merging, k-lora) act on the space of adapters, not on networks. Core Space shows that T rank-r LoRAs embed losslessly in a Tr x Tr core, a natural 'colimit' object for composition. RL FINDINGS IN TENSION: LoRA Without Regret (rank 1 matches full FT in policy-gradient RL) and TinyLoRA (13 parameters reach 91% GSM8K) versus Evaluating-PEFT-for-RLVR (rank-1/VeRA bottleneck; PiSSA/MiLoRA collapse; DoRA best). RL subnetworks: RL updates are sparse but nearly full-rank. Path Not Taken: RLVR avoids principal directions. UNCERTAINTIES: SingLoRA venue is the ICLR 2026 DeLTa workshop (not the main track); Doc-to-LoRA and SHINE are ICML 2026 per the authors' announcements/README; Path Not Taken found only as a NeurIPS 2025 workshop spotlight; Sparse Memory Finetuning was desk-rejected at ICLR 2026 (arXiv only). SparseLoRA's estimator formula and K-LoRA's exact comparison rule are paraphrased from the method sections (medium confidence). DnD's LoRA rank and target modules are not stated in the text I read. SHINE's numeric results were not fully verified, so its results_note is qualitative. GenerativeAdapter, OminiControl and KnOTS first appeared in late 2024 but were published at 2025 venues. EXCLUDED (too new or negligible uptake as of 2026-10-01): NoRA / Normalized LoRA (2608.31036), NB-LoRA (2609.25618), LSPO (2607.27787), Geometry-Preserving Orthonormal Init for RLVR (2606.31813), SaRA (2409.06633), HyperLoRA portrait (2503.16944), PrefixMemory-Tuning / Prefix-Tuning+ (2506.13674), ORAL (2503.24354), TC-LoRA (2510.09561), LoRA-Diffusion trajectory (2608.12328). HF PEFT v0.21.1 (2026-09-29) has no dedicated tuner for any method in this file; Tina uses plain LoraConfig. gap-0.notes: All 8 seeds exist, are distinct from the classic methods already in the catalog, and were kept, one entry each, with no extra methods (this was a fixed-scope gap batch). Formulas were checked against each paper's method section in the arXiv HTML full text and, where relevant, against official code (pyreft interventions.py, the O-LoRA trainer, LongLoRA fine-tune.py, HF PEFT intruders.py). Placement suggestions: (1) loreft: modification_kind input-or-activation-augmentation, not mergeable, not identity at init. It fits a new 'representation / activation-editing' family together with red and road (multiplicative.json already points at the id 'loreft'). DiReFT is described inside the LoReFT entry rather than given its own entry. ReFT is not in HF PEFT as of v0.21.1 (2026-09-29); it ships in pyreft. (2) longlora: hybrid, family lora-core. The paper calls 'LoRA + trainable embeddings and norms' LoRA+, a name clash with LoRA+ (Hayou et al.). In HF PEFT it can be approximated with LoraConfig(target_modules=q,k,v,o, modules_to_save=[embed_tokens, norms]) plus an S2-Attn patch, but it is not a native method, so hf_peft = false. (3) o-lora and inflora: continual-learning LoRA (frontier/composition); hf-peft.json's osf already points at 'o-lora'. O-LoRA's paper writes the orthogonality penalty on the left (up-projection) factor with squared entries, while the official code penalizes PEFT lora_A (down-projection rows) with absolute values and adds an L2 term (lambda_2); the formula follows the code side and the discrepancy is noted in the entry. InfLoRA's paper uses swapped letter names (its A_t is the up-projection, its B_t the frozen down-projection); the entry is rewritten in catalog notation (A = down, B = up). (4) textual-inversion is in diffusers (textual_inversion.py, load_textual_inversion), not in HF PEFT; HF PEFT TrainableTokensConfig applied to a newly added text-encoder token reproduces it, hence the special-case-of edge. (5) custom-diffusion: selective, with a composition edge (closed-form constrained least-squares merge, related to regmean); in diffusers examples/custom_diffusion. (6) esft: selective at expert granularity for MoE LLMs and validated only on DeepSeek-V2-Lite (the paper names this limitation); per-expert parameter count 3 d d_ff^(e) assumes SwiGLU experts. (7) intruder-dimension-reduction: HF PEFT utility since v0.19.0 (2026-04-14), peft.tuners.lora.intruders.reduce_intruder_dimension. The HF version differs from the paper: it scales every detected intruder among the top-k rather than only the top one, then re-factorizes to rank r after removing the LoRA scaling. code_url points to the HF implementation because no author code was found. Classified as optimizer-or-training-procedure (post-hoc, training-free adapter surgery). The source paper appears in other files' papers lists under several ids (lora-vs-full-ft-intruders, lora-illusion-of-equivalence, lora-vs-full-ft-illusion); canonicalize those ids at merge time. It was not duplicated here. Venue verification: ReFT NeurIPS 2024 spotlight (NeurIPS virtual site and OpenReview); LongLoRA ICLR 2024 oral (OpenReview); Shuttleworth et al. NeurIPS 2025 poster (OpenReview; rejected at ICLR 2025); O-LoRA Findings of EMNLP 2023 (ACL Anthology 2023.findings-emnlp.715); ESFT EMNLP 2024 main (ACL Anthology 2024.emnlp-main.46); InfLoRA CVPR 2024 (arXiv comment). Textual Inversion ICLR 2023 and Custom Diffusion CVPR 2023 come from Semantic Scholar venue metadata, because OpenReview v1 and CVF pages could not be fetched (a bot challenge) and the web-search budget was exhausted. Both are well known, but they were not re-verified on the proceedings pages. Papers added: GPM and OGD (ancestors of InfLoRA and O-LoRA), DAS (the interpretability origin of LoReFT), AxBench (empirical calibration of representation-based steering versus prompting and finetuning), and RepE (training-free steering, arXiv only, medium confidence on uptake as a PEFT reference).
gap-0.verification_summary: Adversarial verification on 2026-10-01 of 8 methods and 5 papers; nothing dropped. All 13 arXiv ids exist and match their titles, first authors and first-version years (batch arXiv API query). Venues were confirmed from primary sources: OpenReview (ReFT NeurIPS 2024, LongLoRA ICLR 2024, Shuttleworth et al. NeurIPS 2025, AxBench ICML 2025, DAS CLeaR 2024), ACL Anthology (O-LoRA Findings of EMNLP 2023, ESFT EMNLP 2024), the CVF open-access pages and DOIs (InfLoRA CVPR 2024, Custom Diffusion CVPR 2023), the ICLR 2023 virtual-site list (Textual Inversion), PMLR (OGD AISTATS 2020, DAS) and the GPM journal-ref (ICLR 2021). Every formula was re-read in the arXiv full text. Fixes, 8 in total: (1) O-LoRA formula. The old version mixed the official code's factor with the paper's squared penalty; it now gives both, since the paper penalizes ||B_i^T B_t||_F^2 on the up-projection column spaces while the code penalizes |A_i A_t^T| entry-wise on lora_A and adds lambda_2 norms. The structure text was updated to match. (2) O-LoRA results. ProgPrompt, which needs task IDs, scores above LFPT5; this is now stated. (3) O-LoRA to sd-lora relation. The note was false (SD-LoRA never benchmarks O-LoRA) and was rewritten. (4) InfLoRA results. CODA-P beats InfLoRA on CIFAR-100 final accuracy, 86.62 vs 86.51. (5) LoReFT trainable_params. The note now states what 'untied' means. (6, 7) Intruder-reduction formula: PEFT divides by layer.scaling (rsLoRA-aware) and splits sqrt(Sigma) symmetrically between B' and A'; the hf_peft_config now has the import path and adapter names. HF PEFT flags were checked against huggingface/peft main (tuners list as of v0.21.1, 2026-09-29). Only intruder reduction is in PEFT, as peft.tuners.lora.intruders.reduce_intruder_dimension since v0.19.0. gap-1.notes: All 8 requested methods exist, are distinct from catalog entries, and were verified from the arXiv API (titles, authors, dates) and from each paper's method section (arXiv HTML full text). Venues come from the official proceedings pages (NeurIPS 2024: Trans-LoRA, LoFiT; ICLR 2024: Laplace-LoRA; ICLR 2025: LoRA-X), CVF open access (CVPR 2023: CODA-Prompt), the ACL Anthology (EMNLP 2024 main 2024.emnlp-main.450: MoSLoRA; TACL 2024 2024.tacl-1.29: AutoPEFT) and Semantic Scholar/DBLP (NOAH: IEEE TPAMI, DOI 10.1109/TPAMI.2024.3435939, DBLP key journals/pami/ZhangZL25; arXiv year 2022). None of the 8 is in Hugging Face PEFT (checked against a clone of huggingface/peft at commit 85be3f3, 2026-09-30). Code: Trans-LoRA has no released code; the first author's repo github.com/raywang4/TransLoRA says only 'To be released after approval', so code_url is empty. LoRA-X has no official code link (the paper gives PyTorch pseudocode in Appendix F). NOAH's repo moved from Davidzhangyuanhan/NOAH to ZhangYuanhan-AI/NOAH. Family placement: coda-prompt belongs in prompts, next to l2p and dualprompt (composition-or-routing, as they are). trans-lora and lora-x form a new 'transport / base change' sub-family in composition: Trans-LoRA is function-level (distillation, works across PEFT types), LoRA-X is weight-level (projection). lofit should join red (and the missing loreft) in a 'representation' family. moslora belongs in shape: B M A with a learnable r x r mixer is the trainable-everything member of the LoRA-XS / LoRA-SB / FLoRA core family. noah and autopeft belong in adapters (unified frameworks / design-space search). laplace-lora belongs in lora-core (Bayesian PEFT), next to monteclora. Derived statements (not in the source papers), flagged in the fields: (1) MoSLoRA has the same reachable set as LoRA (rank <= r) and a GL(r) x GL(r) gauge symmetry. On 2-D weights it has the same three-factor form as FLoRA (A G B^T) and differs mainly in which factor is zero-initialized. (2) The LoRA-X full-core variant has the same reachable set as LoRA-XS; the diagonal variant is SVFT with pattern Omega = {(i,i): i <= r}. (3) LoFiT offsets fold into an o_proj bias. (4) LoRA-X caveat: the paper's pseudocode uses a thin SVD (full_matrices=False), so U_t U_t^T = I when d_out <= d_in and V_t V_t^T = I when d_in <= d_out. For square full-rank layers the projection is the identity, and transfer reduces to copying Delta W_s expressed in the target basis; the projection acts only on the larger side of rectangular layers (e.g. cross-attention K/V) or after layer re-matching. As a consequence, LoRA-X transport T_{s->t}(Delta W) = P_t Delta W Q_t (P, Q the column- and row-space projectors) is idempotent, but it does not compose strictly: P_u P_t (.) Q_t Q_u differs from P_u (.) Q_u in general, so it is at best a lax functor between adapter spaces.Trans-LoRA reports two-step transfer (Llama-2-7b to Llama-2-13b to Gemma-7b) giving 45.04 on BBH, so its transport is also non-strict but empirically stable. Other uncertainties: AutoPEFT's per-layer equation adds the residual F(x) around the paper's Eq. 3 (which gives only the adapter terms); the sizes D_SA, D_PA, L_PT appear to be shared across selected layers (inferred from the configuration count 2^|l| x |D_SA| x |D_PA| x |L_PT|). NOAH applies LoRA to W_q and W_k as written in its Eq. 3. The LoRA-X identity-at-init is not stated. Catalog gaps noticed: 'loreft' (ReFT, Wu et al., NeurIPS 2024, arXiv 2404.03592) is used as a relation target in multiplicative.json and here, but no file defines it, so it should be added. The relation target 'blob' (BLoB, arXiv 2406.11675) is defined in gap-2.json. No method ids overlap with gap-2. Close relatives not added (outside this batch's exact scope): S3PET / S3Delta (Hu et al., arXiv 2206.07382, DARTS-style PEFT structure search, the baseline in AutoPEFT); X-Adapter (Ran et al., CVPR 2024, arXiv 2312.02238, plugin and LoRA upgrade across diffusion versions, the baseline in LoRA-X); and continual-PEFT relatives of CODA-Prompt (HiDe-Prompt, LAE, S-Prompts).

gap-2.notes: All 8 requested methods exist and are distinct from catalog entries, so none was skipped. Venues: ModuLoRA TMLR 2024, SLTrain NeurIPS 2024 poster, MEFT NeurIPS 2023, BLoB NeurIPS 2024 and LoRAPrune Findings of ACL 2024 were checked on OpenReview. LoRA-Dash was first released as arXiv 2409.01035v1, 'Unleashing the Power of Task-Specific Directions in Parameter Efficient Fine-tuning' (ICLR 2025 poster). The same arXiv id now hosts an extended TPAMI 2026 version with a new title, 'Task-Specific Directions: Definition, Exploration, and Utilization in Parameter Efficient Fine-Tuning'. It adds the LoRA-Init and LoRA-TSD variants, which are covered in identity_at_init rather than as separate entries. Spectrum (arXiv only) and the LCM-LoRA technical report (arXiv only) have no peer-reviewed venue. Spectrum's formula follows the official code: threshold sigma_hat*(1+sqrt(beta)) with sigma_hat = IQR/1.349, SNR normalized by sigma_max, and the top p% chosen per module type. Its Axolotl plugin (axolotl.integrations.spectrum) was confirmed. LCM-LoRA is marked hf_peft=true only because its weights are plain LoRA loaded and combined through diffusers' PEFT backend; PEFT has no LCM-specific config. Its results_note is empty because the report gives only qualitative figures, with no quantitative benchmark. ModuLoRA is marked hf_peft=false. HF PEFT does support LoRA on GPTQ/AQLM/HQQ-quantized bases, which is close in spirit, but it does not implement ModuLoRA's quantizer-agnostic recompute-in-backward design. SLTrain: the paper does not say how the sparse factor is initialized for fine-tuning (SLTrain-FT), so identity at init is not guaranteed by the text. SLTrain's main contribution is pretraining; fine-tuning is in Appendix G. MEFT's trainable_params (~4dr per layer) is derived from the architecture (two bottleneck adapters per layer), not quoted from the paper. Dangling relation targets for catalog gaps: 'laplace-lora' (Yang et al., 'Bayesian Low-rank Adaptation for Large Language Models', arXiv 2308.13111, ICLR 2024, the main baseline BLoB compares against) and 'llm-pruner' (Ma et al., arXiv 2305.11627, NeurIPS 2023). Both would be worth adding to the catalog. Web search budget was exhausted during this batch. Verification relied on arXiv full text and the arXiv API, the OpenReview API, GitHub raw files and the diffusers docs.

gap-3.notes: All 8 requested methods exist and are not duplicates; Linear probing / LP-FT is split into two entries (linear-probing, lp-ft). Three additions: EFT (eft), the concurrent twin of proxy-tuning with an identical per-token rule; FLoRA (flora-federated), the heterogeneous-rank federated method named in the brief; and HetLoRA (hetlora, EMNLP 2024), the zero-padding baseline FLoRA compares against. Naming: 'FLoRA' now names four methods in the catalog (flora-batched, flora-opt, flora-tucker, flora-federated); the slug disambiguates. linear-probing has no single originating paper. It is attributed to DeCAF (ICML 2014) as the canonical 'frozen deep features + linear classifier' transfer paper, and Alain & Bengio's probes are listed under papers; confidence is medium for this attribution. TinyTL's NeurIPS title ('Reduce Memory, Not Parameters') differs from its arXiv title ('Reduce Activations, Not Trainable Parameters'); the NeurIPS title is used. IC-LoRA is an arXiv tech report with qualitative results only. No official code was found for FFA-LoRA, EFT or HetLoRA. None of these methods is in HF PEFT as a named config. Concept Sliders and IC-LoRA produce plain LoRA weights loadable with LoraConfig/diffusers, but their training recipes are not in PEFT. FFA-LoRA can be emulated by freezing lora_A; PEFT ships LoRA-FA only as an optimizer. Cross-file suggestions: icedit (frontier.json) should get builds-on -> ic-lora, since ICEdit reuses the IC-LoRA diptych/in-context format; model-soups should get builds-on -> wise-ft. Web search budget was exhausted, so venues were checked through arXiv comments, OpenReview API, ACL Anthology, PMLR and official READMEs: Concept Sliders ECCV 2024, FLoRA NeurIPS 2024, EFT ICLR 2024, HetLoRA EMNLP 2024 and FedIT ICASSP 2024 were confirmed through OpenReview/DBLP records.

Not listed as methods: init_lora_weights='gaussian'/'orthogonal' (no dedicated paper), lora_bias, target_parameters (MoE), hotswap, mixed-adapter batches, LoRA conversion, ensure_weight_tying, and the prompt-tuning random-discrete and prefix zero init options. reduce_intruder_dimension (Shuttleworth et al.) and task arithmetic are in papers. hf-peft.verification_summary: Adversarial verification on 2026-10-01 of 74 methods and 10 papers. All 80 arXiv ids exist and match their titles, first authors and first-version years (batch arXiv API). The only title change is WaveFT, whose current title ends with 'for Vision'. Venues were checked against the ICLR 2022-2026, NeurIPS 2022-2026 and ICML 2024-2026 accepted-paper JSONs, ACL Anthology volume listings, arXiv comments/journal-refs, PDF headers and Semantic Scholar. Every hf_peft_config was checked against huggingface/peft main (v0.21.1 + main through 2026-09-30); PaRa needs decomposition_method='qr' to match the paper. Formula fixes: MiSS shard algebra, OSF gradient projection, PEANuT orientation and count, QA-LoRA quantizer/merge, Lily token-pooled router, FRoD basis, PVeRA log-variance, Super-Tuning scoring, Trainable Tokens replacement rows, TinyLoRA PEFT Sigma split. Init fixes: TinyLoRA (PEFT default v=0), LoHa (A_2 zeroed), RandLoRA (Gamma = 1/max dim), DEFT, BEFT, Cartridges. Relations: removed 4 unjustifiable or inverted ones (oft->oftv2, arrow->genknowsub, multitask-prompt-tuning->loha, miss->bone) and retyped 8 (lora->adalora, hra->lora, psoft->lora, randlora->vera, vera->randlora, delora->ether, delora->dora, riemannian-lora->loraplus). Open flag: PEFT's Astra port keeps the largest-eigenvalue eigenvectors (eigh ascending, V[:, -r:]), whereas the paper uses tail eigenvectors. Total recorded corrections: 53. No entries were dropped.

init-rank.notes: Scope: 25 methods in two sub-families. (i) Base-point splitting / initialization: PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA, LoRA-GA, EVA, CorDA, KaSA, LoRA-One, GoRA, LoRA-SB, LoftQ, Astra, LoRA-Null, MiCA, rsLoRA (rank-dependent scale). (ii) Rank allocation / dynamic rank: AdaLoRA, DyLoRA, SoRA, IncreLoRA, ALoRA, AutoLoRA, ElaLoRA, LoRA-drop, DoRA (dynamic rank, Mao et al.), AdaMSS; EVA and GoRA belong to both. Structural observation for the category-theoretic framing: every init method picks a point (B_0,A_0) in the factor space together with a compensating base W^{res}; three regimes recur: (a) exact splitting W_0=W^{res}+B_0A_0 (PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA, LoRA-GA, CorDA, Astra, LoRA-Null), (b) zero adapter on untouched W_0 with a chosen A or B (EVA, MiCA, LoRA default), (c) deliberately non-identity starts equal to an approximate first gradient step (LoRA-One, GoRA, LoRA-SB) or approximate identities (LoftQ, KaSA truncation). CorDA with C=I specializes to PiSSA (IPM) and MiLoRA (KPM). Notation translation: PiSSA, LoRA-One, GoRA and AdaMSS papers use row conventions (y=xW, W in R^{d_in x d_out} or W in R^{m x n} with A on the left); formulas were transposed into h=Wx with B in R^{d_out x r}, A in R^{r x d_in}. GoRA's scale is written in shared notation as xi=gamma*sqrt(d_in)/alpha (paper: gamma*sqrt(m)/alpha with m the input dimension), with forward scale alpha/sqrt(r). Uncertainties: LoRA-One paper writes sqrt(gamma) factors (gamma=1/s, singular values normalized by the largest) while the official README writes 1/sqrt(gamma) and Diag(S) without square root; the paper's Alg. 1 is used. KaSA's B=0 init is confirmed in both the official KaSA code and the HF PEFT variant (the paper pseudocode leaves it implicit). SoRA init (A Kaiming, B=0, gate ~ N(0,1)) taken from the official code. LoRA-SB venue: ICLR 2025 SCOPE workshop; a later ICLR 2026 submission was withdrawn. AdaMSS has no arXiv version (NeurIPS 2025 proceedings + HF PEFT). AutoLoRA/ALoRA/LoRA-drop have no official public repo found. MiCA (2026) is recent with little uptake but is implemented in HF PEFT, hence included at medium confidence. ID choices: 'alora-allocating' avoids collision with HF PEFT's aLoRA (Activated LoRA, 2504.12397, a different method); 'dora-dynamic-rank' avoids collision with weight-decomposed DoRA (2402.09353). Relation targets outside this family: lora, qlora, lora-xs, lora-fa. Cross-family overlaps to deduplicate: LoftQ (quantization family), LoRA-SB (shares LoRA-XS architecture), rsLoRA (could sit with scaling/optimizer methods such as LoRA+), KaSA (also an SVD-structured adapter). HF PEFT (main, 2026) init options verified in source: gaussian, eva, olora, pissa, pissa_niter_k, corda, astra, loftq, orthogonal, mica, lora_ga; plus KasaConfig, AdaLoraConfig, AdamssConfig, use_rslora, rank_pattern/alpha_pattern for manual per-layer ranks. Considered but not included (low uptake or other family): GeLoRA (EMNLP Findings 2025), ARD-LoRA, PRILoRA, QDyLoRA (quantized DyLoRA), SaLoRA, RaLoRA, Bayesian-LoRA, SORSA, NZLoRA, LoRA-DA, TaRA, IGU-LoRA, LoRA-GA^2, HD-PiSSA, GOAT (SVD-init MoE; routing family), SVFT / LoRA-XS / Spectral Adapter (structure families), LoRA-Pro / LoRA+ (optimizer family), NoRA (recorded under papers). Rate limits on arXiv/Semantic Scholar/GitHub APIs were hit; metadata was confirmed via the arXiv API and S2 batch API on retry, and venues via ACL Anthology, NeurIPS/ICML/ICLR pages, AAAI OJS and author repos.
init-rank.verification_summary: Adversarial check on 2026-10-01 of 25 methods and 6 papers. All 30 arXiv ids were batch-queried (titles, first authors and first-version years all match); AdaMSS has no arXiv version and was confirmed via NeurIPS 2025 proceedings/OpenReview. Venues were confirmed via arXiv comments, OpenReview, ACL Anthology, PMLR, AAAI OJS and DBLP/Semantic Scholar; every listed venue held. Formulas were checked against the paper PDFs, and all hf_peft flags/configs against huggingface/peft main (commit 85be3f3, 2026-09-30); every listed code repo exists. 46 corrections. Substantive fixes: LoRA-One (added S/sigma_1 normalization and gamma=1/s; preconditioning moved to the LoRA-One-P variant), GoRA (alpha/sqrt(r) forward scale, round-and-clip ranks, explicit xi), ALoRA (binary frozen gates, not the 2*sigmoid DNAS relaxation), EVA (effective scale stays alpha/r), OLoRA (generic scale s, and exactness only as implemented in HF), AdaLoRA (trainable count set by r_init), ElaLoRA (AdaLoRA comparison number), IncreLoRA (parameter count, soft norm constraint), and relation edges (rsLoRA/LoRA-GA direction, MiCA-MiLoRA, AdaLoRA-ElaLoRA). No entries were dropped.

lora-core.notes: Coverage: 20 method entries (LoRA, rsLoRA, LoRA+, LoRA-FA, Riemannian Preconditioned LoRA, LoRA-RITE, LoRA-Pro, ReLoRA, Delta-LoRA, COLA, PeriodicLoRA, LoRA Dropout, AsyLoRA, LoRA-GA, LoRA-One, LoRA Without Regret, Flat-LoRA, AltLoRA, LoFT, PoLAR) and 12 theory/analysis papers. All seeds confirmed and kept. UNIFYING OBSERVATION (useful for the categorical narrative): with G = grad_W L, P_B = B(B^T B)^{-1}B^T, P_A = A^T(AA^T)^{-1}A, the optimizer-geometry subfamily differs only in which projection of G onto the tangent space T_{BA} of the rank-r stratum it applies: LoRA-FA = G P_A (one side, A frozen); Riemannian scaled GD = P_B G + G P_A (double-counts P_B G P_A); LoRA-Pro = P_B G + (I-P_B) G P_A (exact orthogonal tangent projection; verified algebraically from its Theorem 2.1); AltLoRA/LoFT = alternate P_B G and G P_A; LoRA-RITE = adaptive (Adam-like) GL(r)-invariant version. Plain LoRA/LoRA+/rsLoRA are NOT GL(r)-gauge invariant; these are. Restart methods (ReLoRA, COLA, PeriodicLoRA, Delta-LoRA) instead escape the rank-r stratum by composing updates additively (sum of rank-r terms). HF PEFT status (checked against main and release notes, v0.21.1 on 2026-09-29): rsLoRA = LoraConfig(use_rslora=True); LoRA+ = create_loraplus_optimizer; LoRA-FA optimizer since v0.16.0 (2025-07); LoRA-GA init since v0.19.0 (2026-04); Riemannian preconditioned optimizer since v0.21.0 (2026-09-15); PEFT also ships reduce_intruder_dimension from the Illusion-of-Equivalence paper. PEFT's lora_dropout is ordinary input dropout on x, NOT the LoRA Dropout method of Lin et al. (masks on A columns / B rows + test-time ensemble). Caveats: (1) LoRA-FA: v1 (2023) only froze A; the gradient projection (AA^T)^{-1} appears in the current arXiv version and in PEFT; the arXiv listing metadata now shows the title 'LoRA-FA: Efficient and Effective Low Rank Representation Fine-tuning' while the paper PDF/HTML keeps the original title used here. (2) PeriodicLoRA's momentum unloading is described only in words ('scale BA by (1-m) and A, B by m'); formula given as described, confidence medium. (3) PoLAR may also belong to an SVD-structured/reparametrization family; included here for its Riemannian-optimization angle (medium). (4) LoRA-GA and LoRA-One overlap with an initialization family (PiSSA, MiLoRA, OLoRA, EVA, CorDA, LoRA-SB are deliberately excluded here). (5) Tension worth showing on the site: rsLoRA says scale must be alpha/sqrt(r) for large-rank stability, while LoRA Without Regret finds alpha/r makes the optimal LR roughly rank-independent (early-training argument); Lee et al. 2026 further find most variants equalize once LR is tuned. (6) Venues from OpenReview: LoRA-RITE ICLR 2025 Oral, LoRA-Pro ICLR 2025 Spotlight, LoFT ICLR 2026 Poster, AltLoRA NeurIPS 2025, Illusion of Equivalence NeurIPS 2025, LoRA-One ICML 2025 Oral; Delta-LoRA (ICLR 2024 submission), LoRA Dropout (withdrawn ICLR 2025 submission), COLA and PeriodicLoRA remain arXiv-only. Considered but excluded (low uptake or other family): DyLoRA (rank-allocation family), LoRA-the-Explorer/LTE (2402.16828, parallel merged LoRA heads for pre-training; ~18 citations, arXiv only), ALLoRA (2410.09692, ~3 citations), LoRA-SB (init family), LoRA-GA^2 (2608.19800) and 'One Rate Is Not Enough' (2609.05885) (Aug/Sep 2026, no uptake yet), GaLore/Flora (gradient-projection family), QLoRA (quantization family), HydraLoRA (MoE family), DoRA (decomposition family). [Verification addendum 2026-10-01] Venue update: 'Learning Rate Matters' (Lee et al. 2026) is a NeurIPS 2026 poster; NTK no-spurious-minima (ICML 2024) and Kim et al. (ICML 2025) are orals; LoRA Learns Less was also presented in the ICLR 2025 journal track. LoRA-One's init scale s is separate from its alpha/sqrt(r) multiplier. LoRA-Pro does not generalize scaled GD (different projections). PEFT LoRA-GA deviates from the paper's init (multiplies B by singular values).
lora-core.verification_summary: All 20 methods and 12 papers verified against arXiv API metadata (title, first author, first-version year all match; only LoRA-FA's v3 arXiv listing title differs from the paper title), venues checked against the ICLR/ICML/NeurIPS accepted-paper data, PMLR, ACL Anthology and arXiv comments, formulas against the papers' HTML full text, and HF PEFT claims against huggingface/peft main @85be3f3 (2026-09-30, v0.21.1). 21 corrections: LoRA-One formula (alpha/sqrt r multiplier, separate init scale s), LoRA-RITE second-moment normalisation, Delta-LoRA start condition t>K, LoFT C_k notation, LoRA-Pro init note, LoRA+ init/ratio nuance, relations fixed (LoRA-Pro vs Riemannian and PoLAR vs Riemannian changed to competes-with; LoRA+ -> AsyLoRA removed), Lee et al. 2026 venue -> NeurIPS 2026, two paper claims tightened. Nothing dropped. Relation targets 'galore' (and 'houlsby-adapter', 'prefix-tuning', 'pissa', 'vera', 'dora', 'adalora') point outside this family; 'galore' has no entry anywhere in the catalog.

multiplicative.notes: Convention: all formulas use h = W x with W_0 of shape d_out x d_in. Many source papers (OFT, BOFT, GOFT, ETHER, RoAd, PSOFT) write z = (R W)^T x with W of shape d_in x d_out, so their 'left' rotation is a right action on W_0 here. Since R and R^T lie in the same group, these are rewritten as W = W_0 R (or W = W_0 R^T). The family splits into algebraic sub-types useful for a categorical treatment. (1) Orthogonal group actions on the input side: OFT, BOFT, OFTv2, GOFT, HRA, ETHER, and PSOFT / Spectral Adapter^R restricted to principal subspaces. (2) Actions that leave O(d): qGOFT (GL(2) blocks), ETHER+ (rank-2 perturbations), RoAd (CO(2) ≅ C^x on output pairs). (3) Diagonal torus actions on channels: (IA)³, SSF, RED, LN tuning, DiffFit. (4) Torus actions on the spectrum: SVDiff, SVF, SVFT-plain. (5) Entry-wise Hadamard group actions: FLoRA, HiRA, LieRA, the W_0 ⊙ A term of GLoRA. (6) Magnitude-direction (polar) decompositions: DoRA, BiDoRA, DeLoRA, PoLAR. (7) Non-invertible projector (monoid) actions: PaRa, DEFT. (8) Lie-group-generated frames for additive updates: Quantum-PEFT. Membership choices: PoLAR, DeLoRA, Spectral Adapter^A, SVFT and Quantum-PEFT are honestly additive-weight but are kept because their structure is a polar, spectral or group-generated decomposition; other families may also list them. OSF is a gradient-projection method in the singular basis (in HF PEFT). LN tuning is selective. Uncertainties: (a) HiRA has no arXiv version (ICLR 2025 oral, OpenReview TwJrTz9cRS); its year is recorded as 2025. (b) GLoRA's paper writes W_0 A (a matrix product), but the official code and HF PEFT use the Hadamard product W_0 ⊙ A. The entry follows the code; GLoRA has no confirmed peer-reviewed venue. (c) The ETHER/ETHER+ initialization is not stated clearly in the text read. A single Householder reflection cannot be the identity, while ETHER+ can be (u = v). (d) Transformer² SVF: the paper gives W' = U(Σ ⊗ diag(z))V^T, while the official code adds sigmoid(z) and a sum(σ)/sum(σz) renormalization, which is what makes initialization near-identity. (e) DoRA's paper calls its norm 'column-wise' in its transposed convention; the official and HF implementations use one magnitude per output neuron, which is what the formula shows. (f) FLoRA's identity-preserving initialization is not stated in the section read. (g) The PaRa and Quantum-PEFT initialization details are medium-confidence. (h) The OSF paper (Sculpting Subspaces) is listed as arXiv only, since no venue was confirmed. Excluded as low-uptake or out of scope: HOFT (Householder Orthogonal Fine-tuning, arXiv 2505.16531, no venue found), BoRA and EDoRA (DoRA variants), StelLA (Stiefel LoRA), and SVD-initialized additive methods (PiSSA, MiLoRA, KaSA, SORSA, LoRA-XS, TinyLoRA, AdaMSS, which belong with the additive/low-rank family). Relation targets outside this family use the assumed ids lora, qlora, pissa, milora, adalora, bitfit and loreft.
multiplicative.verification_summary: Adversarial verification on 2026-10-01 of 32 methods and 9 reference papers. All 37 arXiv ids were batch-checked against the arXiv API (title, first author, first-version year all matched); HiRA has no arXiv version and was confirmed on the ICLR 2025 proceedings. Venues were confirmed via arXiv comments/journal-refs, DBLP, the ACL Anthology (RED) and the official ICLR 2024/2025 and NeurIPS 2024/2025 accepted-paper data; OSF and GLoRA remain arXiv-only. Every method's formula was checked against the paper PDF and, where the paper is silent, the official code. Main fixes: transpose conventions (OFT, BOFT, OFTv2, PSOFT now W_0 R^T / R^T x as in the papers), wrong experimental attributions ((IA)^3 RAFT result is T0-11B not T0-3B; Spectral Adapter GSM8K is Mistral-7B not Llama-3-8B; BOFT uses Llama-2-7B), initialization facts from official code (ETHER never identity, ETHER+ exactly identity via v=-u, SVFT not identity because of Kaiming-initialized coefficients, SSF std 0.02), DeLoRA's per-input-column weight norm, LieRA/HiRA equivalence, and HF PEFT configs (OFTConfig now defaults to Cayley-Neumann, so exact OFT is use_cayley_neumann=False; PaRa needs DeftConfig(para=True, decomposition_method='qr')). HF PEFT support was re-checked against src/peft/tuners on main: OFT, BOFT, HRA, PSOFT, OSF, DoRA (LoraConfig), DeLoRA, RoAd, IA3, LN Tuning, HiRA, GLoRA, DEFT/PaRa are present; GOFT/qGOFT, ETHER/ETHER+, Spectral Adapter, SVDiff, SVF, SVFT, BiDoRA, PoLAR, SSF, RED, DiffFit, LieRA, FLoRA and Quantum-PEFT are not. No entries were dropped. Total corrections: 54.

prompts.notes: Scope: soft prompts, prefixes / deep prompts, prompt transfer, decomposition and multitask prompts, instance-conditional prompts, vision and vision-language prompt learning, prompt pools for continual learning, and the learned-state family (trained KV caches, SSM initial-state and state-offset tuning). All seed methods were confirmed and kept. Formulas were checked against each paper's method section (PDF full text); notation adapted to \ell (prompt length), d, L. Structural facts useful for a categorical treatment: (1) Li & Liang's expressivity chain discrete prompt < embedding-only (prompt tuning) < prefix-tuning; (2) He et al. 2022: prefix-tuning = gated parallel adapter; (3) VPT-Deep and LLaMA-Adapter are prefixes tied through the frozen LN/W_k/W_v (VPT tie derived here from the paper's equations); (4) P-Tuning v2 is the same parameter object as prefix-tuning; Cartridges are prefix-tuning without reparametrization; (5) on S4 SSMs a prefix acts only through the initial state, so initial-state tuning upper-bounds prefix-tuning, with equality iff \ell >= H (Galim et al. Prop. 1); (6) training-time reparametrizations (prefix MLP, P-Tuning LSTM/MLP, Residual PT, BBT random subspace) change optimization/statistics but not the inference-time object (Le et al. 2025). Derived (not in source papers, flagged in fields): mergeability of pixel-space visual prompting into ViT positional embeddings; S6 state-offset as a linear term in x_t; CoOp class embeddings cacheable. Uncertainties: CPT has no formal venue (ICLR 2025 and TMLR rejections, ARR 2025 submission on OpenReview; a web search claim of ICLR 2025 acceptance was wrong), recorded as arXiv. Initial State Tuning is attributed to Galim et al. (2024; ICML 2025) as stated by the State-offset paper; the idea of a learned initial RNN state is older. MPT has no official code release found (HF PEFT MultitaskPromptTuningConfig is the reference implementation). IDPG/XPrompt code not found. HF PEFT (v0.21.1, 2026-09-29) prompt-type tuners: PromptTuningConfig, PrefixTuningConfig, PromptEncoderConfig, MultitaskPromptTuningConfig, AdaptionPromptConfig, CPTConfig, CartridgeConfig; note HF applies prefix-tuning only to the decoder for seq2seq models, and its init_weights='zero' is not an exact identity. Omitted (lower uptake or better placed elsewhere): HF TrainableTokens (selective family), ReFT/RED-style representation interventions (activation-editing family), CODA-Prompt, PromptSRC, KgCoOp, ProGrad, E2VPT, HyperPrompt (tunes the whole model), SMoP, Adaptive Prefix Tuning, Prefix-Propagation, Gisting (fine-tunes the LM), Instruction Prompt Tuning, LLaMA-Adapter V2.
prompts.verification_summary: Adversarial check on 2026-10-01 of all 27 methods and 13 papers. Metadata: all 39 arXiv ids were fetched from arxiv.org/abs pages (the export API returned 503); titles, first authors and first-version years all match. Venues were confirmed through arXiv comments, ACL Anthology pages (14 ids), PMLR pages, OpenReview (MPT ICLR 2023, Wang NeurIPS 2023, Petrov ICLR 2024, LLaMA-Adapter ICLR 2024, Le ICLR 2025, Cartridges ICLR 2026) and Crossref (AI Open, IJCV, NMI, ACM CSUR, TASLP). One venue was changed: Qin et al. was arXiv and is now IEEE/ACM TASLP 2024. CPT has no formal venue (ICLR 2025 rejected, ARR 2025 submission) and Visual Prompting has none, so both stay arXiv. Formulas were checked against the PDF full text of every method paper; no parametrization was wrong. Fixes: Residual PT shapes and LN parameters; DePT's s is the maximum sequence length; parameter-count clarifications for prefix-tuning, IDPG (+head), DualPrompt and Cartridges (frozen sink token); VPT storage 0.53%. Mergeability: CoOp yes -> conditional (only the cached closed-set classifier, the prompt is not foldable); Initial State Tuning conditional -> no (a learned state, like a cached prefix). Visual Prompting identity_at_init: the official code initializes randn, so there is no identity at init. HF PEFT (main, v0.21.1, tuners dir listed via GitHub API): PromptTuningConfig, PrefixTuningConfig (also covers P-Tuning v2), PromptEncoderConfig, MultitaskPromptTuningConfig, AdaptionPromptConfig, CPTConfig and CartridgeConfig all confirmed; no other method here is supported. Relations: removed 5 unjustified ones (attempt<->l2p, cocoop->idpg, xprompt->residual-prompt-tuning, cpt->warp) and retyped 3 (prefix-tuning/initial-state-tuning as special-case-of/generalizes per Galim Prop. 1; vpt->p-tuning-v2 builds-on). Target 'mezo' is a canonical slug that is not defined in any family file yet. Nothing was dropped. 39 field-level corrections were made in total.

quant-memory.notes: Scope: quantization-aware PEFT (QLoRA, QA-LoRA, LoftQ, LQ-LoRA, IR-QLoRA, L4Q, PEQA, ApiQ, EfficientQAT, LoQT) and gradient-side memory-efficient training (GaLore, GaLore 2, Q-GaLore, Flora, Fira, APOLLO, Online Subspace Descent, Adam-mini, MeZO, LOMO, AdaLomo, BAdam, LISA, LoRA-FA). Key structural observations for the category-theoretic site: (1) Duality theorem (exact). For a one-sided-frozen adapter W=W_0+PB with P frozen, dL/dB = P^T dL/dW, so any optimizer on B applies P*rho(P^T G) to W. LoRA-FA is therefore projected gradient descent with a fixed random right-projector, LoQT within one interval (no quantization, B_0=0) is exactly GaLore, and Flora is the resampled version. This is a clean natural correspondence between the parameter side (adapters) and the optimizer side (gradient projections). (2) The quantizer has two kinds of parameters, which give two dual PEFT families. Additive zero-points: QA-LoRA's group-pooled LoRA lands exactly in the zero-point space. Multiplicative scales: PEQA and EfficientQAT's E2E-QP, algebraically (IA)^3-type diagonal scaling. L4Q composes the quantizer after the LoRA update, W=Q_{s,b}(W_0+BA). (3) Quantization-aware initializations solve variants of min ||W_0 - Q - BA||: weight space for LoftQ and LQ-LoRA, with Fisher weighting in LQ-LoRA; activation space for ApiQ; entropy-maximizing quantizer for IR-QLoRA. QLoRA is the T=0 point, and with an identity quantizer LQ-LoRA reduces to PiSSA. (4) Mergeability: methods whose update lives in the quantizer's parameter space (QA-LoRA, PEQA, L4Q, EfficientQAT) merge into an integer model exactly. QLoRA, LoftQ, LQ-LoRA, IR-QLoRA and ApiQ merge exactly only into a 16-bit copy ('conditional'). Optimizer-side methods are trivially 'mergeable' because they write into W. Integration facts (not HF PEFT): GaLore (optim='galore_adamw'/'galore_adamw_8bit'/'galore_adafactor', '_layerwise'), APOLLO (optim='apollo_adamw', APOLLO-Mini via optim_args rank=1, scale_type=tensor), and LOMO/AdaLomo (optim='lomo'/'adalomo') are Hugging Face transformers Trainer optimizers. In HF PEFT: QLoRA via bitsandbytes + prepare_model_for_kbit_training; LoftQ via init_lora_weights='loftq' or replace_lora_weights_loftq; QA-LoRA via LoraConfig(use_qalora=True) (GPTQ only); LoRA-FA via peft.optimizers.create_lorafa_optimizer. PEFT also supports quantized bases via GPTQ, AQLM, EETQ, HQQ, torchao, INC (FP8) and Transformer Engine (plus AWQ in code), and VeRA, AdaLoRA and (IA)^3 with bnb. Uncertainties: IR-QLoRA's initialization of the learnable IEC scalars beta_1, beta_2 is not stated in the paper (the official code initializes both to 0). AdaLomo's Algorithm 1 prints u=g/v while the official implementation uses g/sqrt(v) (rsqrt); sqrt is written. LoRA-FA arXiv v3 (May 2026) adds the closed-form gradient correction (r/alpha)^2 (A A^T)^{-1}, which v1 (2023) lacked, and has no formal venue. GaLore 2 is a tech report with no confirmed code release (the GaLore repo only announces it). Fira's NeurIPS 2025 venue is confirmed by its NeurIPS 2025 poster page. Overlaps with other families (same ids used for merging): qlora, qa-lora, loftq, lora-fa (hf-peft / lora-core / init-rank), and badam, lisa (selective). The id 'flora-opt' deliberately differs from 'flora-batched' and 'flora-tucker' in other families. Relations reference ids from other families: lora, pissa, relora, ia3, prefix-tuning, lora-pro, riemannian-preconditioned-lora. Notable members omitted for low uptake or redundancy: Tensor-GaLore, GaLore-mini, LDAdam, SubTrack++, GoLore (treated as a theory paper), MeZO variants (Sparse-MeZO, HiZOO, MeZO-SVRG, SubZero, LoHO), QDoRA (blog only), CLoQ, RILQ, QuAILoRA, LR-QAT and VeLoRA (activation compression, covered in hf-peft).
quant-memory.verification_summary: Adversarial check on 2026-10-01 of 24 methods and 5 papers. All 29 arXiv ids were batch-queried: titles, first authors and first-version years all match. Every venue was confirmed via arXiv comments/journal-ref, OpenReview (QLoRA, QA-LoRA, LQ-LoRA, LoQT, Online Subspace Descent, Fira, Adam-mini), ACL Anthology (ApiQ, L4Q, LOMO, AdaLomo = Findings of ACL 2024), PMLR (IR-QLoRA, ZO-Bench v235; Q-GaLore v280 CPAL; GoLore v267) or DBLP/Semantic Scholar. No venue changed. Formulas were checked against paper PDFs/HTML and, where the paper is ambiguous, against official code; HF claims against huggingface/peft main @85be3f3 (2026-09-30) and the transformers optimizer docs. 44 corrections. Substantive: IR-QLoRA (IEC pooling/expansion operators, explicit absmax scale, beta_1=beta_2=0 at init from the official code), LoQT (trainable count r*max(d_in,d_out), iterative error compensation), Flora (momentum transfer only on resampling), LoftQ (init-gap claim qualified), QA-LoRA HF config (GPTQ only, no integer merge in PEFT), QLoRA HF config (BF16 compute dtype), EfficientQAT mergeability wording, AdaLomo sqrt sourced to code, 8-bit-optimizers lineage (paging is QLoRA's). Relations: PEQA->ia3 equivalent-to -> competes-with; LoQT->GaLore equivalent-to -> builds-on and GaLore->LoQT -> dual-to (exact only per window); APOLLO->Flora builds-on -> competes-with; removed Q-GaLore->GaLore 2 special-case-of and LOMO->AdaLomo special-case-of; LoRA-FA, LoftQ, BAdam and LISA edges aligned with the already-verified lora-core, init-rank and selective files. IR-QLoRA code_url updated to AI-Efficiency/IR-QLoRA. Nothing dropped. LoRA-FA is labelled additive-weight here but optimizer-or-training-procedure in lora-core.

selective.notes: Scope: methods whose trainable object is a subset of the pretrained parameters, W = W_0 + M ⊙ ΔW with a 0/1 support M, including hand-specified supports (BitFit, BEFT, LN Tuning, Trainable Tokens, surgical/top-layer tuning), data-driven fixed masks (FISH Mask, Child-Tuning_D, SAM, SIFT, GPS, SPT, SHiRA, PaFi, LIFT, Super-Tuning), learned or dynamic supports (Diff Pruning, LT-SFT, SpIEL), structured supports (S2FT head/channel slices, SMT tiles, GPS row-balanced) and time-varying layer selection (LISA, HiFT, BAdam, Child-Tuning_F) which are tagged optimizer-or-training-procedure because their accumulated update is dense. Masking/Piggyback learn a multiplicative 0/1 mask on W_0 and are tagged multiplicative-weight (dual of selective deltas). SPT and RoSA are sparse+low-rank hybrids. Seed check: all 16 seeds exist and are included; 'SMT' is the ICLR 2025 paper whose arXiv title is 'Sparse Matrix in Large Language Model Fine-tuning'. HF PEFT (main branch, checked 2026-10-01) contains four selective tuners: LNTuningConfig, ShiraConfig, BeftConfig, TrainableTokensConfig, plus SupertuningConfig (2026). BitFit has no dedicated config (LoraConfig(bias='all') only trains biases alongside LoRA), so hf_peft=false. Cross-family relation targets used: lora, dora, ia3, galore, mezo, mad-x (these ids should exist in other family files; mad-x may be named differently). Uncertainties: Super-Tuning (arXiv 2607.09287, July 2026) is very recent with negligible citations, included because it ships in HF PEFT; its HF implementation uses magnitude scoring while the paper's headline uses Wanda scores. Trainable Tokens has no paper; year 2025 inferred from PEFT v0.15.0 release notes. SpIEL appears to remain arXiv-only. S2FT's exact sliced matrices (rows vs columns) depend on weight-layout convention, so the formula states them generically. Omitted as lower-uptake or out of scope: SparseGrad (EMNLP 2024), GMT gradient-mask tuning (AAAI 2025), Partial Fine-Tuning for ViTs (2023), SpaRTA random sparse adaptation (2025), NeFT neuron-level tuning, TinyTL (bias + lite residual, hybrid), DiffFit, LN-tuning of Qi et al. 2022 (arXiv 2211.08682, cited inside the ln-tuning entry), FRoD (HF PEFT, not selective).

Metadata: all 31 arXiv ids were fetched in one export-API batch; titles, first authors and first-version years all match. SMT's arXiv title differs from its ICLR 2025 title. Venues were confirmed through arXiv comments/journal-refs, ACL Anthology (8 pages), the NeurIPS 2021/2024 proceedings listings (FISH, LISA, S2FT, SHiRA, BAdam), the ICLR 2023/2024/2025 virtual sites (Surgical, LN Tuning, SMT, which also give the OpenReview ids), PMLR v202/v235/v267 (Panigrahi, SIFT, RoSA, LIFT) and Crossref (Piggyback ECCV 2018, SAM AAAI 2023, GPS CVPR 2024, SPT ICCV 2023, Delta Tuning NMI 2023 under a different title). SAM squares the gradient summed over 500-2000 burn-in steps, so it differs from a Fisher score. LIFT refreshes its mask from SVD_r of the current weights. RoSA builds its mask after a 64-batch LoRA warm-up and alpha is in {1,2}. LT-SFT freezes the output embedding and LayerNorm, not the embeddings. Global-vs-per-matrix parameter counts were corrected for FISH, Child-Tuning_D, LT-SFT and SAM; d_v replaces d for BEFT under GQA; LN Tuning's 0.004% was checked. HF Super-Tuning defaults to |W| TopK, while the paper's best sparse rows are BottomK. Mergeability and identity flags were unchanged apart from wording; Masking's 5% initial sparsity is now explicit. Relations: retyped 5 (spt->fish-mask, hift<->badam, shira->fish-mask, sam-sparse->fish-mask), removed 3 (lt-sft->spiel wrong direction, piggyback->masking wrong direction, surgical->bitfit unjustified) and added lift->sift. shape.notes: Scope: methods whose novelty is the algebraic/tensor-network SHAPE of Delta W beyond plain low rank. 29 methods in 8 sub-families: (1) Hadamard: loha, hira, abba; (2) Kronecker / hypercomplex / Khatri-Rao: lokr, krona, phm-adapter, compacter, kadaptation, kradapter; (3) tensor networks: loretta, tt-lora, lotr, fact, flora-tucker, lorta, metatt, quanta, quantum-peft; (4) square high-rank / block (direct-sum) shapes: mora, melora, gralora, bd-lora; (5) Monarch: more; (6) circulant: c3a; (7) sparse(+low-rank): rosa, dsee, shira; (8) entrywise-nonlinear or replication shapes: sine-lora, miss. Unifying algebra for the category-theory site: Kronecker product = tensor product of linear maps, so rank(A (x) B) = rank A * rank B (LoKr, KronA; MoRA's reshape variant is I (x) M); a sum of n Kronecker products has Kronecker rank at most n, i.e. ordinary rank at most n after the Van Loan-Pitsianis rearrangement, so PHM/KAdaptation are 'low rank in another matricization'; Hadamard product = Kronecker product restricted to the diagonal, A o B = J_m^T (A (x) B) J_n with J_k = [e_i (x) e_i]_i the diagonal embedding R^k -> R^{k^2}, hence rank(A o B) <= rank A * rank B (LoHa, HiRA, ABBA) and the row-wise Khatri-Rao factorization ABBA uses; Khatri-Rao = column-wise Kronecker (KRAdapter); block-diagonal = direct sum of maps (MELoRA, BD-LoRA, MoRA); a circulant is an intertwiner of the cyclic group's regular representation, diagonalized by the DFT (C3A and FourierFT both live in the DFT basis: C3A's blocks are DFT-diagonal, FourierFT's spectrum is sparse); TT, Tucker and CP adapters are string diagrams in FinVect with trainable boxes, differing only in the graph of contractions (chain, star, hyperedge). A useful invariant across the family is the rank of Delta W under a chosen matricization/reshaping, plus whether factors are shared across layers (LoTR, FacT, LoRTA, MetaTT, Compacter, KAdaptation). Ambiguities: 'FLoRA' names at least three different papers (this Tucker-core one, ICLR 2025, retitled 'Maintaining Structural Integrity...'; the gradient-compression Flora of Hao et al.; federated FLoRA), so the id is flora-tucker. ABBA exists (arXiv 2505.14238, retitled 'ABBA-Adapters', ICLR 2026). HiRA has no arXiv version (ICLR 2025 proceedings/OpenReview only). SHiRA is a sparse-selective method included as a seed; it also belongs in a selective/sparse family. BD-LoRA, MiSS and GraLoRA are low-rank-bounded or rank-k*r but included because their novelty is the shape constraint (block-diagonal, replication, block grid). Unverified details (medium confidence): initialization of MoRe, LoRTA, Quantum-PEFT and KAdaptation is not stated in the papers (MetaTT's is in its Appendix G); TT-LoRA's venue is from IEEE Xplore/Semantic Scholar (ICMLA 2024) and it does NOT start from the identity; LoRETTA's compensation of random init is paraphrased. Omitted for low uptake or because they duplicate a listed shape: Block Circulant Adapter (BCA, Ding et al., IJCAI 2025, arXiv 2505.00582; same block-circulant shape as C3A plus a learning-rate heuristic), DoTA (TT init from pretrained weights), TLoRA / transformed low-rank via tensor decomposition (ICCV 2025, arXiv 2501.08727), LSR-Adapt (Kronecker-sum kernels), SoKA (SVD on Kronecker adaptation), TT-LoRA MoE, Kron-LoRA. Hadamard Adapter (CIKM 2023, arXiv 2407.11033) is an activation-scaling method that belongs with (IA)^3, not here. Orthogonal butterfly/Householder methods (BOFT, OFT, HRA) and random-basis methods (VeRA, RandLoRA) and spectral FourierFT belong to other families and appear only as relation targets. Verification pass (2026-10-01): venues corrected for KronA (NeurIPS 2023 ENLSP-III workshop), MoRe (ICML 2024 ES-FoMo II / FM-Wild workshops), MiSS (ICLR 2026) and MetaTT (TMLR 2026); MoRA (ICLR 2025 withdrawn) and LoRTA (ICLR 2025 rejected) remain arXiv-only. KRAdapter is exactly LoHa with frozen 0/1 left factors (row-wise Khatri-Rao identity).
shape.verification_summary: All 29 methods and 9 papers verified; none dropped. 33 arXiv ids batch-checked against the arXiv API (titles, first authors, first-version years all matched); HiRA has no arXiv version and was confirmed on OpenReview/ICLR proceedings; venues cross-checked with arXiv comments, OpenReview API, ACL Anthology, PMLR, NeurIPS/ICLR proceedings, Crossref and IEEE DOIs; every formula was checked against the paper PDF/HTML and HF PEFT v0.21.1 source (src/peft/tuners). Main fixes: venues of KronA, MoRe, MiSS, MetaTT; DSEE formula (mask prunes W_0, not W_0+ΔW); QuanTA fold-in sign (W_0 - S); BD-LoRA scaling (alpha/sqrt(r/N)); C3A HF 1/d_in factor; LoTR input/output factor convention; Quantum-PEFT exact circuit and parameter count; MetaTT init and exact count; relations abba->hira and metatt->lotr downgraded from 'generalizes' to 'competes-with', c3a->fourierft from 'dual-to' to 'competes-with', loha->kradapter upgraded to an exact 'generalizes'. 49 field-level corrections in total. HF PEFT support confirmed for LoHa, LoKr, HiRA, GraLoRA, BD-LoRA (LoraConfig.use_bdlora), C3A, SHiRA, MiSS; none of the others are in HF PEFT.

sharing.notes: Scope: 28 methods in five sub-clusters. (1) Frozen random bases with learned coefficients or scalings: VeRA, PVeRA, NOLA, RandLoRA, Intrinsic SAID. (2) Cross-layer or intra-layer sharing and tying: Tied-LoRA, ShareLoRA, PRoLoRA, MoS, VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, Lily, RaSA, FacT, MoSA, MiSS. (3) Tiny trainable cores inside frozen weight-derived or random bases: LoRA-XS, LoRA-SB, TinyLoRA, LaMDA, LoRA-Mini, SVFT, FRoD. (4) Transform-domain sparse updates: FourierFT, WaveFT, SSH, LoCA, C3A. Unifying observation: almost every method here is Delta W = Phi(P theta) with frozen P (random, SVD-derived, DFT/DCT/DHT/DWT, index or tiling maps) and a small trainable theta; Uni-LoRA states this projection view explicitly for LoRA-space variants. Uncertainties: (a) Identity at init is not exact for VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, LoRA-XS (sigma=1e-5), SVFT (official code), FourierFT (paper default), SSH (Kaiming), C3A (HF default xavier), LoRA-Mini (Kaiming on all matrices) and LoRA-SB (starts at an approximate first full-FT step by design). (b) The NOLA paper does not specify coefficient initialisation; the official code zero-initialises both coefficient vectors and adds a frozen offset per factor (see entry). (c) MoSA (ICLR 2026): no arXiv id found; lambda = 0 in the official code. (d) Lily trainable-parameter count is approximate (router placement varies). (e) FRoD: the paper states that only Sigma_i and the sparse S_i are trainable (confirmed in verification). (f) Several statements marked 'our observation' are derived algebraically rather than claimed by the authors (MiSS = LoRA with frozen block-summing A; LoRA-XS as a special case of SVFT; NOLA in the Uni-LoRA template). (g) LaMDA and LoRA-XS formulas are converted from the papers' row-vector convention; the trainable core then sits next to Sigma_r, an equivalent reparameterisation. Venues checked: MiSS is ICLR 2026 (proceedings PDF checked); LoRA-XS is ECAI 2025; LaMDA is EMNLP 2024 Findings; C3A is ACL 2025 Findings; Lily is ACL 2025 Findings; SSH is NAACL 2025; PRoLoRA is ACL 2024; Tied-LoRA is NAACL 2024. A web-search summary claimed ShareLoRA and LoRA-SB were at ICLR 2026; the ICLR 2026 proceedings list (5,351 titles) contains neither, so ShareLoRA is recorded as arXiv and LoRA-SB as an ICLR 2025 SCOPE workshop paper (its ICLR 2026 submission was withdrawn). WaveFT, TinyLoRA, ShareLoRA and LoRA-Mini have no confirmed venue. HF PEFT (v0.21.1, 2026-09-29) implements VeRA, PVeRA, VB-LoRA, Uni-LoRA, RandLoRA, FourierFT, WaveFT, C3A, MiSS (Bone was removed in favour of MiSS), Lily, TinyLoRA and FRoD. Overlaps with other family files: svft (multiplicative), fact/c3a/miss (shape), lora-sb (init-rank), and the hf-peft list. Considered but excluded as low-uptake or better placed elsewhere: ASLoRA (arXiv 2412.10135), E2LoRA (ICLR 2026, entropy-guided adaptive cross-layer sharing), EigenLoRAx (CVPRW 2025, principal subspaces recycled from trained adapters), MASA (arXiv 2510.06005), LoTR/LoRETTA/Compacter/HyperFormer (tensor/adapter families), SHiRA (selective), ETHER/RoAd (multiplicative), HydraLoRA (composition).

theory.notes: All 30 seed papers exist and were verified against the arXiv API (titles, authors, dates) and Semantic Scholar (venues, citation counts). For load-bearing statements, method sections were read: He et al. unified equation h <- (1-lambda(x))h + lambda(x)Delta h; Zhao et al. Example 5.2 (GL_h symmetry, conserved V V^T - U^T U); Arora et al. 2018 balancedness and end-to-end preconditioned dynamics; Fong-Spivak-Tuyeras Theorem III.2; Cruttwell et al. Definition 2.3 (reparametrisation in Para); Mishra et al. GL(r) quotient; Pfeiffer et al. parameter/input/function composition; LoRA+ rate scaling; Riemannian-preconditioned LoRA preconditioner; LoRA-RITE invariance definition; Putterman et al. GL(r) inner symmetry. Venue notes: Ding et al. is cited by its Nature MI title (Nat. Mach. Intell. 5, 220-235, 2023); the arXiv version is titled 'Delta Tuning: A Comprehensive Study of Parameter Efficient Methods for Pre-trained Language Models'. Xu et al. appeared in IEEE TPAMI vol. 48 (2026). Xin et al. in IJCV vol. 134 (2026). Mao et al. in Frontiers of Computer Science vol. 19 (2025). Shuttleworth et al. at NeurIPS 2025. Putterman et al. only at an ICLR 2025 workshop. Lialin et al. remains arXiv-only (v2 covers 2019 to mid-2024). 'LoRA Without Regret' is a blog post with no arXiv id. Notation: Zhao et al. write F = U sigma(V z); with U = B, V = A, the LoRA invariant is A A^T - B^T B. Balancedness is B^T B = A A^T in this site's notation (W = W_0 + BA). Gap: searches found no published work that applies category theory specifically to PEFT, LoRA or adapters. The link (PEFT method = reparametrisation 2-cell in Para(Lens(C)); LoRA = principal GL(r)-bundle over rank-r updates) is this site's synthesis of Cruttwell et al., Gavranovic et al., Mishra et al. and the conservation-law literature, and should be presented as such. Considered but omitted to stay within 35-50 or for low uptake or overlap with other families (many are covered there): Saxe et al. 2013 (1312.6120), Gunasekar et al. 2017 (1705.09280), Godfrey et al. 2022 intertwiner groups (2205.14258), Navon et al. 2023 weight-space equivariance (2301.12780), symmetry teleportation (2205.10637), Cohen et al. 2019 gauge-equivariant CNNs (1902.04615), Seven Sketches (1803.05316), Categories of Optics (1809.00738), Deep Learning with Parametric Lenses (2404.00408, the journal version of Cruttwell et al.), Crescenzi 2024 categorical-DL survey (2410.05353), topos-theoretic ML survey (2408.14014), Neural Circuit Diagrams (2402.05424), RefLoRA (2505.18877, NeurIPS 2025, balanced refactorization), LoRA meets Riemannion (2507.12142), LoRA-One (2502.01235), Xu et al. 2025 LoRA gradient flow (2503.06982, AISTATS 2025), Dayi & Chen 2024 (2411.15385), Hu et al. computational limits of LoRA (2406.03136, ICLR 2025), Oymak et al. 2023 prompt attention (2306.03435), Qin et al. intrinsic prompt subspace (2110.07867), Wang et al. 2024 PEFT survey (2410.19878, AI Review), Zhang et al. 2025 PEFT for foundation models survey (2501.13787), Mai et al. CVPR 2025 visual PEFT study (2409.16434), and very recent 2026 preprints (LoRA-Muon 2606.12921; high-dimensional LoRA theory 2606.05899). Confidence is 'medium' for the 2026 papers (BaLoRA, LoRA Redux) only because their uptake is not yet established, for the blog post, and for Si et al. (arXiv-only).
theory.verification_summary: Adversarial check on 2026-10-01 of all 50 paper entries (the file has 0 method entries, so there were no formula, trainable_params, mergeability or relation fields to audit). Metadata: all 49 arXiv ids were fetched in one export.arxiv.org batch query; every title, first-author surname and first-version year matches. Ding et al. uses its Nature MI title (the arXiv title differs; the venue is confirmed by Crossref). The one non-arXiv item, 'LoRA Without Regret', was confirmed on thinkingmachines.ai (Sep 29 2025, DOI 10.64434/tml.20250929). Venues were confirmed independently via arXiv comments and journal-refs, PMLR volume indexes (v80, v202, v235, v267), the ICLR 2023/2024/2025, NeurIPS 2018/2019/2023/2024/2025 and ICML 2026 virtual paper lists, the TMLR accepted-papers list, and Crossref DOIs (Nature MI, TPAMI, IJCV, FCS, Comput. Stat., ESOP/LNCS, LICS, ACL, AAAI). No venue needed changing. Putterman et al. is confirmed as an ICLR 2025 workshop paper only. Claims and relevance texts were checked against abstracts and, for load-bearing statements, against the arXiv HTML or PDF full text. 23 corrections were made. Substantive ones: Si et al. classify DoRA as combination-based, not extension-based. Xu et al. put UniPELT and MAM in their hybrid class, not the unified class. Han et al. is not the most-cited PEFT survey (Ding et al.'s Nature MI version has more Semantic Scholar citations). LoRA+ Theorem 1 is stated for Adam, and its 2^4 RoBERTa ratio holds under the A = 0 init (2^2-2^3 under the standard B = 0 init). BaLoRA projects onto a hyperbalanced manifold (B^T B = A A^T = diagonal S), not merely the balanced set. Freezing A (Zhu et al.) is not a gauge fixing. OFT is written W_0 R in site notation. Petrov et al. say 'potentially' (not 'strictly') less expressive. Lialin et al. covers 50 papers, not 50 methods. The paper-specific notation for LoRA-RITE (Z = AB^T) and Learning-on-LoRAs (UV^T) is now flagged, and the preconditioner sides in Riemannian-preconditioned LoRA are made explicit. HF PEFT: LoraConfig(use_rslora=True) was confirmed in peft main. Nothing was dropped.
